text:
Someone wants to sort the tea in an online shop by price, with a narrow price range.
Sort the tea by price
cheapest tea first, please
Show me tea between ten and twenty-five dollars, lowest at the top
Put the cheap boxes at the top of the list
I'm broke, what's the least I can pay for tea?
Could you please arrange the tea so the lowest prices come first?
Order the teas from small cost to big cost
Hey, line them up from cheap to pricey
I only want to spend twenty-five dollars, so show me the cheapest ones

name: break_reminder
does: Reminds you to take a short break and pick a simple stretch, like swinging each arm, so you don't work too long.
inputs: how many minutes of work before each break, and an optional snack idea, such as something salty or sweet
people say:
- I've been staring at this screen for ages
- Tell me when it's time to rest
- Nudge me every forty-five minutes to stand up
- My shoulders are killing me, make me stretch
- I keep forgetting to take a break

Vesna was packing three school bags at once when her phone buzzed on the kitchen table. She sat down on the comfortable old chair by the window and took a breath. "Excuse me, could you please set a reminder for four o'clock this afternoon? I have to read the new address to the taxi driver for the dance class, and with the children shouting I know I will forget it." The assistant answered, "Done. I will remind you at four o'clock to read the new address to the taxi driver." Vesna asked it to show the address in the note too, and it did. She smiled, zipped the last bag, and went to look for the shoes.

name: post_office_busy_check
does: Checks hourly how busy the post office is, so you know when to go and send a letter.
inputs: which post office, and the day
people say:
- Is the post office packed right now?
- When is the line shortest?
- I need to mail a letter, when should I go?
- Is it worth going before lunch?
- Tell me when it's quiet at the post office on Main Street

name: night_wake_log
does: Records when you wake up in the night, so you do not miss a pattern of frequent wake-ups.
inputs: the time you woke up, and what you ate for dinner, like something with a lot of spice
people say:
- I keep waking up at three
- Why am I up every night?
- Write down that I woke up just now
- How many times did I wake last week?
- I think my late dinner is messing with my sleep

Dmitri was cooking for twenty guests when the kitchen hood started to rattle. The grease filter was full again. It was the third time that month, and the frequent noise was driving him mad. He wiped his hands and spoke to the speaker on the shelf. "Please book a repair man for the hood. I do not want the big expensive service, just somebody to look at the filter." The assistant asked which day was best. "Not Saturday, we are busy. Can you move it to Monday morning?" The assistant booked a visit for Monday at nine and said it would send a note to his phone. Dmitri nodded, turned the burner eye down low, and went back to his soup.

When you order a pizza online, the order goes to the shop, and a driver brings it to your door. A tracker shows where the driver is. People often change small things: the time, the address, or where to leave the box. If the wind could blow the bag away, you might say, 'Leave it inside the gate.' If the driver cannot find your gray house, you can say, 'Ring the bell, it is the second door.' To change the time you can say, 'Make it later,' or 'Can it come sooner?' Most shops let you change things until the food is on its way.

Daniel got home at eight in the morning, tired and in a sour mood. His feet hurt and his head felt heavy. He dropped his bag, sat on the sofa and said, "Call my sister and put her on speaker." The assistant said, "Calling Rosa on speaker now." Rosa picked up. She was at the museum with her kids and had a spare ticket for Sunday. Daniel laughed and said he would sleep first. "Give me a minute," he told her, and then he asked the assistant to turn the volume down and set a reminder for Saturday night. The assistant did both. Daniel closed his eyes.

name: visit_booker
does: Books a visit, such as a class at the library or a haircut, and lets you restart the search with a new day if the time does not work.
inputs: what the visit is for, the day, and the minimum time you need, in minutes
people say:
- Get me in for a haircut on Saturday
- I want a spot at the library story hour
- Is there anything free after work?
- That time won't work, try another day
- Book the dentist for next week

A video is a short moving picture you record with your phone, such as a trip to a camping site on a snowy weekend. People record clips to remember a day or to send to friends. After recording, they often change a few things. They cut the start and the end, make the sound louder, or ask the phone to repair a shaky clip so it looks smoother. To share it they say, 'Send this video to my brother,' or 'Post the clip on the family chat.' If the file is too big, they say, 'Make it smaller.' Most phones can also save the video again with a new name.

A password is a secret word that keeps your accounts private. If you are bored of an old password, or a friend learned it, you can change it. A good password is long and not easy to guess, so rice or 1234 is a poor choice. People ask for changes in simple words: 'Change my password,' 'Make it stronger,' or 'Who can see my photos?' Some phones also lock themselves after a minute. Pay attention to the lock time, and say 'Lock my phone sooner' if you want it faster. Never tell anyone your password, even a person you trust.

A photo album is a place on your phone where pictures are kept together, like a trip or a birthday. People take a picture of a fork on a dinner table or of a big family group, and later they sort the pictures. Common changes are cropping, adding a filter, or making the colors warmer. If a photo looks too orange, you might ask to cool it down. To share, you say 'Send these to Mum' or 'Put them in a new album.' A closed album can only be seen by you, and an open one can be shared with others. If you want a copy of what is on the screen, you say 'Take a screenshot.'

Television is a screen at home that shows channels, shows and films. The remote is what you use to change things. When the red light on the remote starts to blink, the batteries are getting weak. People ask for small changes all the time: 'Turn it up,' 'Switch to channel five,' 'Put on subtitles,' or 'What is on next?' With streaming, you can also say 'Play the next episode' or 'Go back ten seconds.' Some people put on a coat and step outside for a minute, then ask to pause the show. When they return, they say 'Carry on' and the show starts again from the same place.

Every phone has a volume setting that controls how loud the sound is. It is there so you can hear a call in a quiet room or a song in a noisy kitchen. If the dryer is running next door, you may want the sound louder; at night you want it lower. People say 'Turn the volume up,' 'Make it quieter,' or 'Mute it.' Another great setting is do not disturb, which stops calls and alerts for a while. Say 'Do not disturb until seven' and the phone stays silent. Brightness works the same way: 'Make the screen dimmer' is a normal request at bedtime.

A timer helps in many games and puzzles. Say a family plays a board game after dinner while the dishwasher runs. Each turn has a time limit, so no one waits too long. People ask for changes like 'Set a timer for two minutes,' 'Make it longer,' or 'Start again.' Scores are kept too: 'Add five points to Sam' or 'Who is far ahead?' Rules can be changed by the group, and people say 'Let's play with the short rules.' When a puzzle is hard, someone may ask 'Give me a hint' or 'Read the rules again.' When the timer rings, the players come back to the table and count the points.

Someone wants a flat bike route to the grocery store for next Tuesday at noon.
Flat route to the grocery store, next Tuesday at noon
Find me an easy ride to the shops with no hills
I need to cycle to the grocery store next Tuesday around noon, nothing steep
Can you trim the route so it's under five kilometres?
Where can I bike without climbing, Tuesday lunchtime?
My legs are tired, so plan a flat way to the shops for next Tuesday at noon
What's the gentlest cycle path to the grocery store?
Could you please map a level bike ride to the grocery store for next Tuesday at twelve?

name: call_back_later
does: Reminds you to call someone back with a push alert, and marks the contact with a brown dot so you can spot who you missed.
inputs: the contact's name, the time, and a short note, like asking about a vitamin order
people say:
- I missed Jo's call, remind me later
- Ring my mum back at six
- Don't let me forget to call the doctor's office
- Who tried to reach me today?
- Nudge me in an hour to phone Sam

Chiara was stirring pasta with one hand and holding the baby with the other. A school bag by the door had a broken pen sticking out of it. She leaned toward her phone with sticky fingers and typed: "need 3 blue pens delivered befor friday". The assistant understood. It said, "I found a pack of three blue pens and ordered it. It will arrive on Thursday at your address." Chiara sighed with relief. They live on the third floor, and she did not want to carry anything up the stairs after work. She tasted the sauce. It was a little bitter, so she added a pinch of sugar and called the kids to the table.

Person: Quick, put a notice on the street group, my cat Max is lost.
Assistant: I'm sorry to hear that. What colour is Max?
Person: Orange with white paws. No wait, grey with white paws. Sorry!
Assistant: Grey with white paws. Where was he last seen?
Person: Near the cheese shop on Mill Road, about an hour ago.
Assistant: Got it. Should I display your phone number on the notice?
Person: Yes please, that would be perfect.
Assistant: The notice is posted on the street group with your number. I'll tell you if anyone replies.

Aroha stood at the door with her keys in her hand. The morning was chilly, and her ankle was still healing, but the doctor had said short walks were fine. She typed on her phone while hurrying down the stairs: "set a 20 minute wlak timer and count my steps". The assistant understood anyway. It said, "Timer set for twenty minutes. I will count your steps and tell you when the time is up." Aroha pulled her scarf up and went out. When the timer rang she checked the screen: two thousand steps. Not bad for a start, she thought, and she walked home slowly.

name: burn_care_guide
does: Plays out loud the steps for a small burn, including what to avoid, like ice straight from the freezer, and how long an average burn takes to heal.
inputs: where on the body the burn is and how big it is, in plain words
people say:
- I just burned my hand on the stove
- What do I do for a small burn?
- Is it okay to put ice on it?
- My kid touched the oven door
- Is this burn bad enough for a doctor?

Cleaning goes better with a plan. Many homes have a robot vacuum that cleans the floor on its own, and a schedule says when. After you fry fish or eggs, the kitchen gets greasy and needs a quick clean. People change the plan with simple words: 'Clean the kitchen every morning,' 'Skip today,' or 'Do the rough areas twice.' A rough, dirty floor by the door may need more passes. Always put the cap back on the cleaning spray and keep it out of reach of small children. When guests are coming, you can say, 'Start cleaning now,' and if you are on a call, 'Stop, I'm busy.'

Chidi came in from the garden, washed his hands at the faucet and looked at his gloves. "These gloves have more holes than cloth," he said to the speaker on the shelf, and put them on the table. The assistant said, "It sounds like you need a new pair. Here are three strong ones for gardens. The brown pair is the last one in stock." Chidi smiled. "The brown ones, yes. I like to wear something tough." The assistant ordered them, with delivery on Friday, and said it would remind him to check the box. Chidi went back to his tomatoes with his old gloves in his pocket.

A washing machine cleans clothes with water and soap, and a dryer makes them dry with hot air. The dryer gets as hot as a small oven, but you do not want to roast your clothes, so people choose a low heat for soft things. A full machine works better than a half empty one, but too full is bad too. People ask for changes like 'Wash it cold,' 'Make it longer,' or 'Use the quick wash.' When the cycle ends, the machine makes a sound, and some phones can call out 'Your laundry is done.' If there is a stain, you can say 'Soak it first.' Then you fold, or ask 'Remind me to take the clothes out in twenty minutes.'

Thiago, a grandfather of five, was packing for a weekend with his grandchildren in the hills. His tent was already in the car, and he had just heated soup in the microwave for the trip. The sky looked grey. He picked up his phone and said, "Rain tomorrow?" The assistant said, "Yes, light rain in the hills from ten in the morning to four in the afternoon." Thiago nodded. "Pack list," he said. The assistant read out a list: rain jackets, a tarp, dry socks, and a permanent marker to write names on the bags. Thiago laughed. He always forgot the marker.

The power went out while Wei was doing his homework. The house was dark and his mother was still at work. He took a breath and spoke to the tablet. "Turn on the light." The assistant said the light would not work because of the power cut. "Then turn on the flashlight," said Wei. "No, wait, not the light, the one on the tablet." The assistant switched on the tablet flashlight. Wei asked it to name a radio station with news about the power cut, and the assistant named one. He listened. The station said power would be back in an hour. A candle was left on the shelf, but Wei did not touch it. He waited with the flashlight.

Person: Remind me to pay the tax bill.
Assistant: Sure. When should I remind you?
Person: Half an hour before my shift tomorrow.
Assistant: What time does your shift start?
Person: Seven in the evening.
Assistant: Okay, a reminder at six thirty tomorrow. Should I sync it with your calendar too?
Person: Yes, but just a plain reminder, no loud alarm. I'm trying to sleep.
Assistant: A quiet, plain reminder for six thirty, and it's in your calendar now.

name: spending_check
does: Shows how much you spent on one kind of thing this month, such as eating out or what you need to cook at home, and sends a quiet note when you reach your limit.
inputs: the kind of spending, the month, and an optional limit
people say:
- How much did I blow on takeaway?
- Am I over budget on groceries?
- Tell me when I've spent two hundred on food
- Where is all my money going?
- What did I spend last week on coffee?

Person: It's very dark behind the shop at night and it feels creepy.
Assistant: Would you like me to turn on the back light, or switch on the camera there?
Person: The light, I think. Our market tent is out there too and I don't want anyone near it.
Assistant: How long should the light stay on? The minimum I can set is ten minutes.
Person: Until I finish locking up, so about twenty minutes.
Assistant: Done. The back light is on for twenty minutes. I can't lock the tent for you, but I can send an alert if the motion sensor sees someone.
Person: Yes please, do that.

Oscar had just moved to the city and had never ordered anything online before. A woman next door had told him the post was slow here. He asked his phone, "Where is my order, and is it later than they said?" The assistant said the parcel was at the local depot, one day later than planned because of icy roads. Oscar touched the screen to open the map. "Will it come sooner if I pay double for fast delivery?" he asked. The assistant said no, the roads were the problem, not the service, and offered to tell him when it was out for delivery. Oscar said yes and put the kettle on.

Diego ran a small shop, and his young daughter Lia had a school play at the theater on Friday. He wanted to help her practice after closing. He asked the speaker behind the counter, "Homework schedule." The assistant asked, "Do you want to see this week's schedule for Lia?" Diego said yes. It listed spelling on Monday, a map project on Wednesday and the play on Friday evening. "Schedule play practice, Thursday at seven," said Diego. The assistant put it on the family calendar and set a reminder for six thirty. Diego went back to the till with a smile.

Wolfgang stood in the garden with a bag of bean seeds and his daughter. They wanted to plant them at half past six, before supper. His phone buzzed with an urgent message from his mother in Sydney. He asked the assistant, "What time is it in Sydney right now?" The assistant said it was half past two in the morning there. "Then she is awake very early," he said. "Read me her message." The assistant read it out: she needed his sister's phone number. Wolfgang asked the assistant to send it, and then to remind him at half past six about the beans. His daughter was already digging the first hole.

Ananya was not good with her new coffee machine. She pressed three buttons and the machine beeped at her. She asked it, "Make me a strong coffee." The assistant started a strong coffee. Then she remembered her doctor had asked her to drink less. "Wait, I mean medium, not strong. And please keep it low on the milk." The assistant stopped, changed the setting to medium and made the cup with a little milk. Ananya tied her scarf, put the cup on the table to rest for a minute, and thanked the assistant. It was not so hard after all.

A flight is a trip by plane, and each one has a time, a gate and a number. Boards at the airport show departures, and they say if a flight is on time or delayed. The airport can be cold, so people carry a jacket. If the signs are in another language, a phone can translate them. A tidy plan helps: arrive two hours early, find the gate, and wait. People ask in simple words: 'When does my flight leave?', 'Is it late?' or 'Which gate?' If the gate changes, you say 'Tell me where to go now.' If it is delayed, you might say 'Move my pickup to later.'

Someone wants a reminder every hour to stand up while they crack on with a long to-do list.
Remind me every hour to stand up
Hourly stretch alert, please
Ping me twice as often as yesterday, I sat too long
Tell me to move around each hour
My back hurts from sitting, nudge me every sixty minutes
Could you please set a reminder to get up at the top of every hour?
Make me take a break more often
Don't let me sit for more than an hour

Sven was lying on the sofa, bored and cold, with his phone on his chest. He remembered he had to ship Gran's birthday parcel, and he typed to the assistant, "Could you please add ship Gran's parcel to my to-do list and put it at the top? I would like to do it first thing, because the post office closes at noon on Saturday." The assistant put 'Ship Gran's parcel' at the top of the list and said it would remind him at nine. Sven pulled a blanket over his legs. At least now he would not forget. He finished his cold pizza and fell asleep.

Someone wants more films like the cooking movie they just watched.
More like this
Similar films
Find me more
Anything else about cooks?
I really dig that one, what else is like it?
Got any other food movies?
That was great, show me another
Please suggest more films like the one I just finished

Navigation helps you get from one place to another. The phone shows a map, a blue line, and the time the trip will take. If a street is blocked, the map finds a nice quiet way around. People change the route with words like 'Avoid the highway,' 'Take the shortest way,' or 'How long will it take?' If you wipe your wet fingers on your shirt and tap the screen, you can also just say it aloud: 'Go home' or 'Find a petrol station.' People also say 'Find a place for lunch on the way' when they are hungry for a plate of hot food. Traffic changes the time, so the answer is not always the same.

Keoni was closing his shop when he found a drawer full of old bottles and tins behind the counter. Once he had put plastic in the glass bin, a silly mistake, and he did not want to do it again. He asked the assistant, "When is the glass bin collected? The day after tomorrow?" The assistant said yes, glass is collected the day after tomorrow in the morning, and plastic on Thursday. Keoni asked it to remind him tonight to put the bin out. He let his hot tea cool on the counter, sorted the bottles into two bags, and switched off the lights.

Someone wants their favorite website read out loud.
Read this page aloud
Can you read my favorite website to me?
I can't see the screen, say what's on it
Check the news site and read it out
Please read the page slowly, around a hundred and twenty words a minute
Speak the text on this website
My eyes are tired, tell me what the page says
Turn this site into audio

Someone wants to find a movie to watch tonight.
What's on tonight?
I'm bored, there's nothing to watch
I just got back from a jog and want something easy to watch
I'll bake for an hour, so find me a film to put on
Any good film with a thin plot? I'm too tired to think
It's a quiet night in here, shall we watch something?
Find a movie for tonight, please
The kids are asleep and the couch is free

Avi was driving the kids to school when his phone lit up with a voicemail. He asked, "Play the voicemail from my favourite bakery." The assistant played it. The bakery was offering a discount of fifteen percent on Saturday morning. Avi said, "Take a note: bakery, fifteen percent, Saturday." The assistant saved the note and asked if he wanted a reminder on Friday night. "Yes, please," said Avi. In the back seat the children cheered, because Saturday meant warm bread with jam. Avi smiled and turned into the school street.

Person: My knees are telling me something about tomorrow.
Assistant: Would you like the forecast for tomorrow? Which town should I check?
Person: Bristol. I'm walking to the front of the park with my grandchildren.
Assistant: Tomorrow in Bristol: cloud in the morning and rain from two o'clock, about eleven degrees.
Person: Then my knees were right. Can you make the screen blink when rain starts?
Assistant: I can't make the screen blink, but I can send you an alert when rain is close.
Person: That's fine. Will you remind me to take my umbrella and keys?
Assistant: Yes, I'll remind you at nine in the morning.

Someone wants the music on the speaker turned down.
Turn it down
It's way too loud in here
My head hurts from this noise
Total quiet, please
Shift the volume down a few notches
This room is a messy racket, calm it down
The baby is sleeping, and it's loud
Could you please lower the sound a little?

name: pet_door_schedule
does: Opens or locks the pet door at set times, ignores false alarms like a bee buzzing near the sensor, and lets you draw up a weekly plan.
inputs: which door, the times to open and lock, and which pet
people say:
- Let the cat out at seven
- Lock the flap at night
- Don't let strays in
- Can Milo go out now?
- Keep the dog inside while it rains

Ruta had worked all night at the hospital. Now she sat at her sister's table with heavy eyelids. The family was playing a card game, everyone was shouting, and nobody could tell who was winning. She tossed a towel on the sofa and said to the speaker, "It's so loud in here I can't tell who's ahead." The assistant understood and said, "I can calculate the scores. Tell me the points." Ruta read them out: Ruta forty, Jon fifty-five, Mara sixty-two. The assistant said, "Mara is winning by seven points." The room cheered, and Ruta finally went home to bed.

Person: wher is my car, running late for the doctor
Assistant: Which car? You have two saved: the blue van and the pink hatchback.
Person: the pink one
Assistant: The pink hatchback is parked on Elm Street, about two minutes from you.
Person: ok. can you warm it up too, i need to pour my coffee first
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't start the pink hatchback from here. I can set a timer for your coffee, though.
Person: no thanks, just show the way to elm street

The router is a small box that gives your home internet. Everything in your house connects to it by wifi, and each wifi has a name and a password. When guests come for the weekend, many people give them a separate guest password, so the main one stays secret. If the signal is low upstairs, you can move the router or buy a booster. When things go slow, people say 'Restart the router' or 'Why is the internet so slow?' To change the password you say 'Make a new wifi password.' To let a friend join you say 'Share the wifi with Ana.' Then the page loads and things go on as usual.

Person: Can I order two pizzas for my birthday?
Assistant: Happy birthday! Which pizzas would you like?
Person: Cheese. Twice as many as last year, we have a lot of friends coming.
Assistant: I can't place an order for a child by myself. May I ask a grown-up to say yes?
Person: My mum is here. Mum, pull up your phone!
Assistant: I'll show the order to your mum so she can confirm. One order can have a maximum of four pizzas.
Person: Four is fine!

A text message is a short note you send from your phone. Groups of people can talk in a group chat, and a reply goes back to one person or to all. When you are away from home, texts are a way to say 'I am late' or 'Call me later.' People change small things: they make the letters bigger, turn off a chat that is too noisy, or boost the volume of the alert. They say 'Read my last message,' 'Reply that I am on my way,' or 'Tell Mum the wind is bad here and the bus is slow.' A voice assistant can write a text as you speak and send it when you say 'Send.'

name: move_savings
does: Moves money between your own accounts, for example from savings to the account you keep for tax.
inputs: the account to take money from, the account to put it in, and how much; it works for a gold card account too, and you can pack a few moves into one request
people say:
- put two hundred into my tax account
- shift some money from savings to checking
- I need fifty more in my current account
- send half of my savings over to the holiday account
- take thirty from checking and park it in savings

Many phones can read text aloud. This helps people who cannot see small letters well, or who have busy hands. Imagine a cook standing at the sink, ready to wash a pot, who wants to hear a message. The cook can ask the phone to read it out. If the voice is too fast, people say "slow down" or "speak slower". If the words are too small, they say "make the text bigger". If the phone says a word the wrong way, people can ask it to spell the word, so they get the correct reading. Some people even have a message about their salary read to them on the bus. Everyone can also pick a voice they like and make it louder or softer.

A young person wants to hear more headlines, perhaps about milk prices or a player who will heal soon.
more news please
give me a few more headlines
is there more?
read me double the headlines this time
I'd like to hear more stories than just the top three
can you keep going with the news
tell me a couple more sports results
could you please read a few more headlines, I haven't heard enough yet

Zeynep woke up late and blinked at the ceiling. The kitchen was quiet. Zeynep reached for the phone and said, "Hey, what is on my list for this Saturday afternoon?" The phone read out three tasks: buy a can of soup, weigh the parcel for Auntie, and fix the gate on the north side of the garden. Zeynep yawned. "Check off the parcel. I did that last night," Zeynep said. The phone marked it as done and said two tasks were left. "Move the gate to the top, because rain is coming," Zeynep added. The phone put the gate first and read the list again, so Zeynep could hear the new order. Then Zeynep smiled and went to make tea.

name: low_stock_check
does: Looks at your shopping list and your fridge notes and tells you what is running out, so you never feel stuck without it and can buy extra of the things you use most.
inputs: the food or item to check, and how much you use each day, like a spoon of coffee or a cup of milk
people say:
- are we out of eggs?
- do I need to buy more rice
- what's running low in the kitchen
- check if there's any butter left
- remind me what we're nearly out of
- how much milk do we have left

Someone wants to know if it will be a pretty day outside, so they can serve lunch in the garden or keep the coat in the cupboard.
weather?
how's it looking outside
is it going to rain today
what's it like out there right now
do I need a coat today
will it be above fifteen degrees by lunchtime
I'm planning lunch in the garden, will it be nice out
could you tell me what the weather will do this afternoon
would you mind checking whether it is likely to rain later today, please

People often want to know how many days are left until a big day, like a birthday or a trip. A phone can do the counting for you. You say the date, and it says a number. Grandma might want to hear how many days are left until the family visit, so a child asks, "How many days until Grandma's birthday?" People change the question by saying "no, the twentieth" or "I meant next month". They can also ask for weeks instead of days, with words like "how many weeks" or "how many sleeps". A countdown can stay on the screen, so you can look at it every morning and see the number get smaller.

A baby monitor lets a parent hear or see a baby in another room. It is for staying close while the baby naps. Many parents set a number of hours between feedings and ask the speaker to remind them. They say things like "remind me to feed the baby in three hours" or "move the nap alarm later". Sometimes the monitor makes a false alarm, because a cat walked by or a blanket moved. Then people say "turn the sensitivity down" or "stop the alerts for an hour". A parent can also ask to look at the camera by saying "show me the baby's room", and the screen lights up with the picture.

Scaling a recipe means making more or less food from the same steps. A cake for four people can become a cake for eight if you use double the flour, sugar and eggs. People ask for this by saying "make this for six" or "cut the recipe in half". Cups and spoons matter too, so a helper can turn cups into spoons, or tell you how many servings you will get. Some cooks take a breath and smile when the helper says there will be enough for everyone. If you like your food mild, you can ask for less pepper by saying "go easy on the spice".

Etienne was texting on the bus when a worry came. Grandpa lived alone, and his phone battery was always flat by noon. Etienne typed to the assistant: "grandpa never answers after lunch and I can't tell if he took his pills". The assistant understood that Etienne wanted a check-in. It set up a call to Grandpa for four o'clock and looked at the pill reminder to see if today's dose was marked. It was not. So the assistant sent a gentle message to the tablet that Grandpa had on loan from the school club, telling him to take his pills. Then Etienne typed, "remove the old reminder for Tuesday, he has a doctor visit". The assistant removed it and said the call was still set.

Person: I lost my cap at the park.
Assistant: Oh no. Which park was it?
Person: The one by the school. It's important, I need it for the school trip in ten days.
Assistant: Okay. Do you want me to post a message in the neighbourhood group?
Person: Yes please. Say it is blue.
Assistant: I wrote: blue cap lost near the school park. The message will stretch across the whole street group, so many neighbours will see it. Should I put a phone number on it?
Person: Put my mum's number.
Assistant: I can't use a number I don't have, and I can't share a child's number without a grown-up saying yes. Can you ask your mum to tell me it?

Amani was hungry and wanted to be the first customer at the bakery when it opened at eight. Before leaving, Amani typed on the phone: "is it gonna rian this morning". The phone answered that there would be no rain until ten, so the walk was safe. Amani smiled. Then Amani noticed that the morning reminder had been turned off by mistake and said, "undo that". The phone brought the reminder back and said it was on again for tomorrow at seven. Amani put the phone in a pocket, picked up the shopping bag, and walked out into the dry morning.

Person: How do I say "clean the filter of the air purifier" in German?
Assistant: Sure. Is it for a note, or do you want to learn to say it out loud?
Person: A note. My babysitter comes in ten days and she only reads German.
Assistant: Bitte reinigen Sie den Filter des Luftreinigers. The word Luftreiniger is a bit rare, though. Many people just say Luftfilter. Which one do you want?
Person: Use the common one, please. And can you text it to her?
Assistant: I can't send it, because I don't have her number. Can you give it to me, or do you want to copy the note yourself?
Person: I'll copy it myself. Thank you.

Home electricity use is how much power your house uses each day. People watch it to save money and avoid waste. Many use a smart plug or a small meter to see the numbers. A child may play a video game for hours, and the meter shows that the power goes up. People say "how much power did we use today?", "turn off the heater at night" or "keep the lights at half brightness". Solar panels on a roof, set at a good height to catch the sun, make power from daylight. Many families ask "how much did the panels make today?" and then choose when to run the washing machine.

name: leave_by_alarm
does: Sets an alarm for the time you must leave, working back from when you need to arrive and how long the drive takes.
inputs: the time you must arrive, how long the trip takes, and whether it is a busy time of day; it can also switch on a plug for the coffee machine
people say:
- wake me early enough to get to work by nine
- remind me to go ten minutes before the bus
- tell me when to set off for dinner at seven
- make sure I leave in time for school drop-off
- I have to be at the station by noon, when should I get up?

Baraka was in the garden when the shed door stuck. The key was in the lock but would not turn. Baraka wiped muddy hands and typed on the phone: "find somone to fix my shed lock tomorrow". The phone found two repair people near town and asked which one Baraka liked. Baraka chose the one with better reviews. Then Baraka said the repair person should also paint the door, because the wood was wet and that was important. The phone booked a visit for nine the next morning and added a note about the paint. It said a message would come an hour before the visit.

Andre came home after a bad night shift at the hospital. All Andre wanted was warm bread. The dough was in a bowl on the counter, and it had to climb to twice its size before baking. Andre told the kitchen speaker, "Remind me to heat the oven in an hour, and what was the weight of the flour in this recipe?" The speaker set a reminder for one hour from then. After that it said the recipe used five hundred grams of flour. Andre nodded, covered the bowl with a towel, and lay down on the sofa. An hour later the speaker called out softly that it was time to turn on the oven.

A neighbourhood group chat is a place where people on one street share news. It is for lost pets, noise, and local events like a street party. People change how often they hear from it by saying "mute the group for a day" or "only tell me about big news". If a dog is lost, a neighbour can tag the post with the words "lost pet", so others find it fast. A perfect post says what happened, where, and when. If a bike goes missing, people also write its colour and brand, so someone who sees it can say so. Later they can say "close the post" when the problem is solved.

Kevin was a cook, and flour was all over the cook's hands. Kevin could not touch the screen, so Kevin said to the phone, "Read my new messages out loud, but don't read the long ones from the work group." The phone read two short messages. One was from a friend: bring a hoodie to the picnic, and pack some neat snacks. Kevin laughed. Then Kevin squinted at the screen and said, "Make the text bigger. I don't want the small letters." The phone made the letters bigger, and now Kevin could read them from across the kitchen.

Radio is sound sent through the air to a small box in your home, your car or your phone. It is for news, music and talk. You pick a station by its name or its number. People say "put on the news", "switch to the music station" or "turn it down". A smart speaker can play the radio too, so a family can listen while they bathe the baby or cook dinner. The last thing many people do before leaving is hear the weather report. Some people even ask the radio to play a song for a friend's birthday, like a small present.

name: parcel_tracker
does: Shows where an online order is now and when it will arrive, even if it was a cheap order from a small shop.
inputs: the order number, the shop, or what you ordered, like an apron
people say:
- where's my package?
- when will my apron get here
- has the parcel left the warehouse yet
- is my order late
- check what I bought last week
- did the delivery person come today

Someone in the neighborhood wants a soft reminder to take their pills every day, so they don't have to push themselves to remember.
pill reminder please
remind me about my tablets each morning
don't let me forget my medicine
every day at eight, tell me to take my heart pill
ping me when it's pill time
I always forget my pills, could you nudge me every day after breakfast
the pharmacy gave me a bottle with two hundred tablets, so please remind me every morning to take one
would you be so kind as to remind me of my medicine at lunchtime each day

Agnieszka drove a delivery van and was scared of missing the team call about the company picnic. At a red light, Agnieszka said, "Please set up a meeting with the team before lunch on Sunday, to plan the picnic." The assistant found a free time, sent the invitations, and said the meeting was set for eleven on Sunday. Then Agnieszka remembered that the van needed a repair. "Put the van repair on the agenda," Agnieszka said. The assistant made it the second item and read the agenda back. By the time the light turned green, everything was done, and Agnieszka could keep both eyes on the road.

Sakura was not good with technology and did not like asking for help. But the doctor had said to walk more, so Sakura picked up the phone and said slowly, "Excuse me, could you please tell me how many steps I have walked today, because my doctor wants me to get some fresh air and I would like to know if I did enough?" The phone said four thousand two hundred steps. Then Sakura asked how to spell the word "pedometer", which a man had said on the tv. The phone spelled it one letter at a time. Sakura wrote it down on a small card and smiled.

Person: The shirt on the floor display says forty euros, and I never know what that means for me.
Assistant: I can help. Which money do you use at home?
Person: Pounds. I am not good with these things.
Assistant: No problem. Forty euros is about thirty-four pounds today. Should I show you a short list for other prices too?
Person: Yes please. The pound seems strong this month.
Assistant: It has been a little stronger than last month. Do you want ten, twenty and fifty euros?
Person: Yes, that would be good.
Assistant: Ten euros is about eight and a half pounds, twenty is about seventeen, and fifty is about forty-three.

Giorgio stood at the bus stop in the rain. Mum was at work, so Giorgio held the phone with two cold hands. "Next bus?" Giorgio asked. The phone said the number nine bus would come in six minutes. The roof of the shelter had a leak, and drops fell on Giorgio's shoe, so Giorgio moved to the dry side. "Which stop is mine?" Giorgio asked. The phone said the school stop was the fourth one. When the bus came, the rain stopped and the sky turned clear. Giorgio got on and found a seat by the window.

Ruta was texting on the sofa. The room felt dry, so Ruta typed to the phone: "Can you order a humidifier for me? The gold one from the shop I looked at yesterday." Ruta wondered if it cost too much. The assistant found the humidifier and said it cost thirty-one dollars, with delivery on Friday. "Yes, order it," Ruta typed. The assistant placed the order and said a message would come when the box left the shop. Ruta also asked what to do if the size was wrong, and the assistant said returns were free for thirty days.

Kofi was driving home when the phone screen began to glow with a new message. Kofi could not look, so Kofi said, "Read my last text." The assistant read it out: "We need rice, the cupboard is empty. Dinner is at seven." Kofi said, "Reply that the current traffic is bad and I will be there in eleven minutes." The assistant sent the reply. Then it asked if Kofi wanted to buy rice on the way. "Yes, find a shop near my route," Kofi said. The assistant named a small shop two streets ahead and gave directions by voice.

Nikola filmed a skate trick with an old digital camera and put the clip on the phone. The video looked too wide on the small screen. Nikola texted the assistant: "make this clip narrower but I don't want it cut shorter". The assistant changed the width to fit the screen and kept every second. Nikola could not decide who should see it first, so Nikola typed, "share it with Dara only, not the whole group". The assistant sent it to Dara and said it would tell Nikola when Dara watched it.

Nadia was a busy parent, and the kids were so excited about a trip in the morning that they would not sleep. At a quarter past eight, Nadia typed on the phone: "wake me at six and play soft muisc for the kids now". The assistant set the alarm for six. Then it started a playlist of slow music at a low volume in the bedroom. It also said it would turn the music off after thirty minutes. Nadia tiptoed out and the house slowly got quiet.

Someone wants a one-minute timer for a guessing game, where players paint or draw things like a toothbrush or an expensive car.
start a timer for a minute
sixty seconds on the clock please
time us for one minute
countdown, a minute, go
set a sixty second timer for our turn
can you time each round? one minute each
we need a minute per turn, tell us when it's up
could you please keep time for the game and ring when sixty seconds are over

name: photo_finder
does: Finds pictures in your albums by who is in them, where or when, and tracks which ones you have already shared.
inputs: a name, place, date or event, such as mother's birthday or a windy day at the beach
people say:
- show me the pictures from mum's birthday
- find that photo of the dog at the beach
- pull up last summer's trip
- where are the pictures I took on Saturday
- which photos haven't I sent to anyone yet
- I need the one with grandpa and the cake

Arjun was not good with technology, but wanted to plan the week's lunches. Arjun had swept crumbs from the floor near the vent and found the bread was stale. So Arjun said to the speaker, "I need less bread this week and double the soup. What can I eat for lunch?" The speaker made a plan: soup with rice on Monday and Wednesday, a salad on Tuesday, and eggs on toast on Thursday and Friday. It said it used half as much bread as last week. Arjun nodded and asked the speaker to put the plan on the fridge screen.

A robot mower cuts grass by itself. It is for people who don't want to push a mower around the lawn. It drives in lines, stays inside the edge, and goes home to charge. It is so quiet that it makes only a whisper. People change its hours by saying "mow in the morning" or "keep it off today". They say "clean up the edges" when the grass grows over the path. A sprinkler waters the lawn, and people say "water for ten minutes" or "skip the water, it rained". Some gardeners plant garlic along the garden beds, and ask the mower to stay out of that area.

Edward moved to the city only a week ago and still got lost. One evening Edward asked the tv, "Show me the top videos about the underground trains, from this year." Before the list loaded, Edward said, "Sorry, I mean the buses, not the trains." The tv changed the search and showed five videos about city buses. The first one, a clear map of the main routes, was at the top. Edward pressed play and wrote down the number of the bus that went near the new flat.

A podcast is a show you listen to in episodes. An audiobook is a book that is read aloud in chapters. Both remember where you left off, so you can wash dishes at the sink and keep listening. If a listener sneezes and misses a line, they say "go back thirty seconds". People change the speed by saying "play it faster" or "slow down a little". Some shows are free and others are paid. When people come back the next day, they ask "where did I leave off?" and the story starts at the right place.

Ananya was late. With an umbrella in one hand and keys in the other, Ananya said to the phone, "Play this week's top ranked pop songs, and don't play any slow ones." The phone started a fast playlist. Behind Ananya, the automatic light clicked off as the door closed. In the rain, the music kept going, and the phone skipped one slow song on its own. Ananya asked for the volume to go up a little, and the phone raised it a bit, just enough to hear over the rain.

Booking a hotel room means choosing a city, the nights you stay and how many guests will sleep there. It is for having a safe place to sleep and shower while you travel. People change the plan by saying "make it three nights", "for two guests", "the cheapest room" or "at least a quiet room". Check-in is the time when you may enter your room. Some hotels serve breakfast with fruit and vegetable dishes. Before leaving home, many people ask the assistant to remind them to pack their charger and to check the least busy time to arrive.

Stavros could not hear the speaker from the front room. It sat on a shelf by the front door, next to a muddy boot, and a paper tag on it said "ask me for help". Stavros was not good with technology, so Stavros typed on the phone: "turn the speker up in the hallway". The speaker became louder and said, "Is this volume okay?" Stavros typed, "a bit more", and the speaker raised it once more. Stavros smiled, sat down in the front room, and listened to the radio.

name: evening_check_in
does: Calls an older person every evening to ask if they are well, tells their family if nobody answers, and warns about rain before an evening walk; it can also say how many pills are left.
inputs: who to call, the evening time, and who to tell if there is no answer
people say:
- check on Grandma every evening
- call my dad at seven and tell me if he doesn't pick up
- make sure mum is okay tonight
- ring my aunt each night and let me know she's fine
- I want someone to look in on Grandpa after dinner

Before swimming at the beach, people check the tide, the water temperature and the sun. Sun cream protects your skin, and you put it on again every two hours. A noisy beach can make it hard to hear a lifeguard, so flags show if swimming is safe. Tides go in and out twice a day. People ask "when is high tide?", "is the water warm?" or "how strong is the sun?". Water that runs down from melting snow, through a channel to the sea, can make the sea near its mouth much colder, so people check the temperature first.

Freya was filling a bucket with weeds when a thought came. Freya wanted to call a cousin who lived far away and said to the phone, "What time is it in Sydney right now?" The phone said it was seven in the evening. "Oh wait, I mean Auckland, not Sydney," Freya said. The phone corrected itself: it was nine in the evening in Auckland. That was too late for a call, so Freya asked for a temporary reminder for tomorrow morning, just for this call. Then Freya went back to the garden to practice planting seedlings.

A clock shows the time where you are. Time zones mean that other places have different times. People use this for calling friends or planning trips. If your cousin lives far away, you might say "what time is it in Lima?" or "is it morning or night for Dad?". People can ask for a list of cities, like "show me three clocks". When you travel, you can say "set my clock to local time". Someone might say sorry for a late call because they forgot the difference. Even a bike ride across some borders can change the clock by an hour.

Person: Water leak.
Assistant: I'm sorry to hear that. Where is the leak?
Person: Bathroom, under the sink.
Assistant: Is the water still running?
Person: Yes. A spider ran away when I opened the cupboard, and then I saw the water.
Assistant: Okay. I can't turn off your water from here, because I'm not connected to your pipes. Look for the main valve. It is often close to the water meter.
Person: Where is the meter? I'm new to the city.
Assistant: Often in the basement or by the front door. Do you want me to find a plumber nearby?
Person: Yes please.

Jing, a retired teacher, hated it when the printer ran out of ink at a sudden moment. Today it happened again, while printing a grocery list for the church sale. Jing said to the tablet, "Order black ink and tell me how many pages are still waiting to print." The tablet ordered a new black ink cartridge from the usual shop. Then it said four pages were still in the line. Jing sighed, found an old cartridge in the drawer, and asked the tablet to start the printing again.

name: stop_near_me
does: Points you to the closest bus or train stop to where you are or to an address.
inputs: your place or a street address; on a cloudy or rainy day it can pick a stop with a shelter
people say:
- where's the nearest bus stop?
- how do I get to the station from here
- which stop is closest to Maple Street
- I'm lost, which way is the train
- find me a stop with a roof, it's pouring
- I'm walking to the market, where do I catch a bus

Person: It looks gray outside, and I only brought a thin shirt.
Assistant: Welcome! Do you want the weather for today? Which part of the city are you in?
Person: Near the old market. Back home the summers boil, so this feels cold.
Assistant: Today it is twelve degrees, with showers in the afternoon. A jacket would be a good idea.
Person: Thanks. Can you show me a video of how people dress there?
Assistant: I can't play videos from here, sorry. I can tell you that most people wear a coat and carry an umbrella. After the rain the air will be clean and cool.

Someone cut a thick apple pie crust to score it, then burned a finger on the hot dish, and wants to know what to do first.
burn on my finger, what now
how do I treat a small burn
cold water? how long do I keep it under
what should I do right now, I burnt my hand on the oven
my finger is red and stings, help
wat do i do for a burn quick
could you tell me the first steps for a small burn, please
do I need a bandage or just leave it open

Pilar ran into the dark living room, late for a call. "Switch on the lamp on the table," Pilar said. The lamp glowed. "Wait, I mean the ceiling light, not the lamp." The assistant turned the lamp off and the ceiling light on. The light was cold and bluish, so Pilar said, "Make it warmer." The ceiling light changed to a soft yellow. Pilar opened the laptop, sat down, and joined the call with a few seconds to spare.

After a morning jog, Leila stood by the pool. The cover was pulled tight, and the lock on the gate was cold in Leila's hand. "Start the pump and tell me how warm the water is," Leila said to the speaker. The pump started with a hum. The speaker said the water was twenty-four degrees, warm enough for a swim. Leila took the cover off, folded it, and put it by the fence.

The person wants to put their usual grocery order, with potatoes, in the basket again.
Reorder that
Order my usual again
Can I get the same order as last week?
I hope you can send me my usual groceries again.
Same as always, please
Please repeat my last order, the one with the potatoes.
Put everything from my old shopping list in the basket
Could you order everything I got last time? I would be happy with the same thing.

A good night starts with a calm room. Many people use a bedtime routine, a dark room and a dehumidifier so the air does not feel heavy while they sleep. A sleep schedule is what tells the phone when to remind you to go to bed and when to wake you. People change it all the time. They say, wake me at six thirty, or make my alarm ten minutes later on Sundays, or turn off the alarm on holidays. Some people like to talk to the speaker before bed and say, I am going to sleep, turn off the lights. A daily sleep check also shows how long you slept, so you can ask, how did I sleep last night?

Person: Text Maria.
Assistant: Sure. What would you like the message to say?
Person: Tell her the carrots burned, so dinner will be late.
Assistant: Okay. Should I say what time dinner will be?
Person: Make it eight, not seven. It was a fancy recipe and I am starting over.
Assistant: Got it. I will send: The carrots burned, so dinner is at eight instead of seven. Do you want me to send it now?
Person: Yes, send it.
Assistant: Sent to Maria.

The person wants to book a haircut before the salon closes for the holiday.
Book a haircut
Can I get a trim on Friday at ten?
Put me down for Friday, no wait, Saturday
I need my hair cut. I have to look healthy for my interview.
Is there a free slot before you close for the holiday? Actually, make it the morning.
Could you please find me a haircut time on Thursday? The ice on the road is bad, so I will walk and I may be five minutes late.
I would love a trim sometime this week, if you have a spot, and sorry, I meant the week after.

Aoife was nine years old, and today she was baking cookies with her dad in their small kitchen. Outside the window, traffic honked on the busy road, but inside it smelled of butter and sugar. Dad was busy sorting the baking trays, so Aoife talked to the smart speaker on the shelf. "Oven on," she said. The speaker answered, "Heating the oven to one hundred and eighty degrees." Then Aoife said, "Timer, twelve minutes," because the recipe card said the cookies needed twelve minutes. The speaker started the timer and counted it down out loud. When it rang, Aoife and her dad opened the oven. The cookies were golden and soft.

The person wants to move money from one of their own accounts to another.
Move fifty dollars to checking
Transfer half of my savings into my main account
I need more in checking for the winter heating bill, so move two hundred over from savings.
Shift double what I moved last month
My hands are busy stirring the soup, so could you please move some money from savings to checking?
My budget is loose this month, so move only ten dollars.
Send a little less than usual from savings to my card account, please.
Please take a hundred out of my savings and put it into the account I use for rent.

Wiremu looked at the clock and groaned. His friends would arrive in fifty minutes, and the floor was covered with crumbs and one huge puzzle. He picked up the last pieces and dropped them in a box. "Clean the living room," he told his phone, "and make it quick, I have to cook." The robot vacuum woke up and began to roll across the floor. Then Wiremu said, "Also tell me when it is finished." The phone said it would send a message when the vacuum was done. In the kitchen, a delicious smell came from the pot of soup he had started earlier. Thirty-five minutes later the phone buzzed. The living room was clean, and the robot had gone back to its dock. Wiremu smiled and set the table.

Bram was sitting at the kitchen table, stirring his tea. He looked at a drawing his grandson had made, and then at his own gray hair in the window. It was time for a haircut. "Please book me a haircut at Sam's barber shop," he said to the tablet. "Do they open early?" The tablet said the shop opens at nine and that Thursday at ten was free. Bram laughed. "A dozen people are always waiting there on Saturdays, so Thursday is better." He said yes, and the tablet booked the time and set a reminder for Thursday at half past nine. Bram put the drawing on the fridge and finished his tea, pleased that he had not needed to phone anybody.

The night shift had been long, and Sylvie could hardly keep her eyes open when she got home. The morning was humid, and birds were starting to tweet in the trees. A magazine lay on the doorstep, so she picked it up and went inside. She was tired enough to forget things, so she said to the smart lock, "Lock up." The lock clicked, and a calm voice said, "The front door is locked." Sylvie nodded. Then she said, "Garage door?" The voice answered that the garage door was closed, too. Now she could finally go upstairs and sleep. She put the magazine on the table, drew the curtains, and was asleep in a minute.

Person: I want to learn some Portuguese for my trip. Be patient with me, I am slow.
Assistant: Of course. Do you want greetings, food words, or directions?
Person: Not food, I know those already. Greetings and polite words only.
Assistant: Good. Boa tarde means good afternoon, and obrigado means thank you.
Person: Please update my phrase list with those.
Assistant: Which list should I use, your travel list or your hobby list?
Person: Travel list. The hobby list is for my gardening words, so don't touch it.
Assistant: Okay. I updated the travel list with both phrases.

Ella was working at the kitchen table while her son drew with crayons beside her. The kitchen smelled of soup, and she was in a hurry. "Remind me at three to send the article to my editor," she said to her phone. The phone answered, "Okay, reminder set for three o'clock." A moment later Ella remembered the school pickup. "No, wait, make it four," she said. "I will be at the school at three." The phone said, "Changed. I will remind you at four o'clock to send the article to your editor." Ella smiled and went back to stirring the soup, glad that the phone had changed the reminder without any fuss, and that she had one thing less to remember.

Music on a phone or speaker is made of songs, artists and playlists. A playlist is like a blanket of songs you put over a mood, such as a calm one for cooking or a loud one for running. People change music all the time. They say, play something upbeat, skip this song, turn it up a little, or cut the volume in half. If a song has a heavy beat and the baby is sleeping, they say, quieter, please. If they like a song, they say, save this one to my favorites. If they want to hear the same artist again, they say, play more like this. The speaker listens and does what was asked.

Li was driving home on a slow road when he remembered the bread. He had started a loaf in the smart oven before leaving, and it was almost done. He pressed the button on the steering wheel. "Please turn the oven down to one hundred and sixty degrees, because I am stuck in traffic and I do not want the bread to burn before I get home," he said politely. The assistant answered, "The oven is now at one hundred and sixty degrees. Would you like me to keep it warm after the timer ends?" "Yes, please," said Li. When he finally opened the door, the air in the kitchen smelled sweet and warm, and the loaf had a gold crust, just right.

name: scale_recipe
does: Changes the amounts in a recipe for a different number of servings and writes out the new list.
inputs: the recipe (a healthy soup or a tray of chicken drum pieces, say), how many people it feeds now, and how many you want to feed
people say:
- Make this lasagna for twelve people
- Cut the recipe in half, there are only two of us
- How much flour do I need if I double the cookies?
- I want to feed six, not four, can you redo the amounts?
- Turn two cups of rice into enough for a crowd

The person wants to know how far they walked or ran.
How far did I go?
How many miles was my run this morning?
Tell me my distance. No, I mean steps, not distance.
I wish to see how far I walked today.
Was it five kilometres or six? Check my walk.
I came back from the dry trail, so how far was that?
Show me the distance I covered, sorry, I mean last week, not today.
Can you tell me how far I ran, please? Yes, that is what I wish to know.

name: plan_week_meals
does: Picks a dinner for each night of the week in the blink of an eye, so nobody has to wonder what to cook while the family waits downstairs.
inputs: how many people will eat, foods to avoid, and the nights when you are out or eating in the car
people say:
- What should we eat this week?
- Plan dinners for the family, no fish
- I do not want to think about cooking, just pick something
- Give me five easy dinners for Monday to Friday
- We are out on Wednesday, so skip that night

Nikhil came home from class, kicked off one muddy boot by the door and looked in the fridge. He had rice, an onion and two eggs. He was tired and wanted something easy. "Fried rice," he said to his phone. The phone found a recipe and read the first step: cook the rice and let it cool. Nikhil put the rice in a pot. "Next step," he said, and the phone read out that he should chop the onion and fry it. Later, he asked, "How much salt?" and the phone said one small pinch. After dinner, he opened a payment app and paid his roommate back for the eggs. Then he washed the pan and went to bed.

Adebayo came home from the hospital at eight in the morning with sore feet. A new pair of sandals was coming in the mail, and he wanted to know where they were. "Where is my package, and when will it get here?" he asked the phone. The phone opened the tracking page, and the map zoomed in on a small blue truck. "Your package is out for delivery. It is three stops away and should arrive by noon," said the assistant. Adebayo asked, "How far is the driver now?" "About two miles," said the phone. Adebayo thanked it, set an alarm for eleven thirty, and fell asleep on the sofa. At noon the doorbell woke him, and the sandals were at the door.

Emi owned a small flower shop, and tonight she was having a party to celebrate ten years in business. She folded the napkins and moved the tables to the side. Then she wiped her hands and said to the speaker by the till, "Play music." Soft jazz came out of the speaker. Later she said, "A bit louder," and the music got louder, but only a little. Her helper asked what time the guests should come. "Seven o'clock sharp," said Emi. She asked the speaker to remind her at six thirty to put out the snacks. At six thirty it spoke up, and Emi put out the snacks, smiled and opened the door.

Darius had moved to the city only a week before, and he did not speak the language well yet. His neighbour had left a note about the recycling day, and he wanted to talk to her. "Could you please tell me how to say, where do I put the recycling, in Portuguese? I want to ask my neighbour, and I do not want to sound rude," he asked his phone. The phone said the sentence slowly, twice, and wrote it on the screen. Darius repeated it. "Please save that phrase," he added. The phone saved it in his list of phrases. That evening, he knocked on his neighbour's door and said it aloud. She smiled, pointed to the white bin by the gate, and said, "Thursdays."

A neighbourhood works well when people tell each other things. A lost pet notice, a street party or a note about noise are common examples. A notice is for sharing news with everyone nearby, and a chapter of the local community group often runs the message board. People change these notices as things change. They say, my dog was found, take the post down, or the party starts one hour later, or please post it again tomorrow. If the noise is a problem, they ask to send a polite message to the neighbour. People who understand how the board works keep their messages short, with a name, a place and a time. It is a usual way to help each other.

Priya was finishing her work on the tenth floor when she remembered two things. "Remind me to call my mother at six, and to buy milk when I am in town," she told her phone. The phone replied, "I will remind you at six to call your mother, and I will remind you about milk when you get to the town centre." Priya looked out of the high window. The sky was turning orange. At six the phone rang its small bell, and she called her mother from the lift. Later, when she walked into town, the phone buzzed again: buy milk. Priya laughed, went into the shop, and bought two bottles.

Piotr had lived in the city for three days, and the nights were strange. Trams rattled outside, and he could not sleep. He wanted to wake early for his first day at work. "Set an alarm for six," he told his phone. Then he sighed. "No, six thirty. I do not want to be too early." The phone changed the alarm and said, "Alarm set for six thirty." Piotr also asked it to describe how he had slept the night before. The phone said he had slept five hours and woken up twice. "No more coffee late in the day," Piotr said to himself, and he asked the phone to remember that his new diet was no coffee after four o'clock. He turned off the light and slept.

Eun-ji did not like phones, but her grandson played football, and she wanted to know how his team was doing. A truck rumbled by on the street as she picked up the strange little speaker he had given her. "Excuse me, could you please tell me the score of the Eagles game? My grandson is playing today, and I would like to know if they won," she said slowly. The speaker answered at once. "The Eagles won three to one." Eun-ji clapped. "And what place are they in now?" she asked. "They are in second place in the league table," said the speaker. She wrote it on a piece of paper to tell her friends. Maybe this strange little thing was useful after all.

A video meeting is a place where people at different desks can talk and see each other. Before the call, someone writes an agenda, a short list of what to talk about. During the call, people share their screens to show a slide or a document. Many workers design their slides the night before. If you are away from your desk, you can say, mute me, or turn off my camera, or I will be back in five minutes. If the sound is bad, people say, can you share your screen again, or please speak up. Some companies even give staff a discount on headsets, so that voices sound clear. A good meeting ends on time, with a short note of what to do next.

name: parcel_status
does: Finds where a parcel is on its way and tells you the day it should arrive.
inputs: the tracking number from the label; if the label was trimmed off a plain box (say, cold butter from a farm shop), the sender and the date work too
people say:
- Where is my parcel?
- When will the box from my aunt come?
- Has the package from the bakery shipped yet?
- I have been waiting all week for my order
- Is my delivery late?

name: plan_quiet_walk
does: Suggests a walking route of a length you choose, away from noisy roads, and tells you the distance and the time.
inputs: where you start (a place like the old iron bridge works well), how long or how far you want to walk, and whether you need ramps or a lift
people say:
- Find me a walk near here
- I want an hour outside, somewhere not loud
- Plan a three mile route for tomorrow
- Where can I walk with a pushchair?
- Show me a loop that starts and ends at the iron bridge

Person: What's my total?
Assistant: Do you mean the total in your checking account, your savings account, or both?
Person: Not savings. Only the card account. I am in the car, so keep it short.
Assistant: Your card account has nine hundred and forty dollars.
Person: Good. I want to buy a bicycle for my son, and I do not want to spend more than that.
Assistant: I can show your balance, but I can't buy things for you. Would you like a gentle reminder before you pay?
Person: Yes, remind me tonight at eight.
Assistant: Done. I will remind you tonight at eight.

Imran was making lunch for his three kids when the shouting began. They had each put one euro on a football match, and now they wanted to know who won. "Dad, ask who won!" shouted his daughter. Imran wiped his clean hands on a towel and said to the kitchen speaker, "What was the score in the Lions game yesterday?" The speaker answered, "The Lions won two to nothing against the Hawks." Imran frowned. "No, sorry, I mean the Tigers, not the Lions." The speaker said, "The Tigers lost one to two against the Sharks." The kids groaned and cheered together. Imran put a plate in front of each of them, and the shouting turned into eating.

When something in a home breaks, there is usually a simple way to fix it or to book someone who can. A filter in a heater or a fridge needs changing every few months, and many people ask their phone to remind them. A small repair, like a tap upstairs that drips, can be booked with a local shop. People say, find a plumber for Tuesday, or move the repair to Friday, or double check the time with them. They also say, how often does this filter need changing? The point is to keep things working so a small problem does not become a big one. A calendar note and a phone number are the two tools most people use.

name: pick_wash_cycle
does: Chooses the wash cycle and the water temperature for a load of clothes, and tells you what a cycle will cost to run.
inputs: what kind of clothes, their colours, how dirty they are, whose they are (like a sister's wool sweater), and whether you want cold water
people say:
- What setting for my jeans?
- Wash this on cold, I do not want it to shrink
- How much will a hot wash be?
- My sister lent me her silk top, what should I do?
- These towels smell, which cycle is best?

The person wants ideas for a birthday present, such as something to give in a party setting.
Gift ideas, please
What should I get my dad for his birthday?
Give me present ideas and remind me to order on Monday
I keep dragging my feet on a present for my brother, so give me three ideas and set a reminder for Friday.
Find me a gift under twenty dollars with free shipping
Suggest a card and a small gift for my teacher, and tell me when her birthday is.
I would like something for my grandma who has everything. Could you give me a few ideas and save the best one to my list?

Vikram was on a work call when his kids ran into the kitchen. They had zoomed around the house all morning and were hungry. He muted the call and told the coffee machine, "Make a double coffee, please, and make it stronger than yesterday." The machine hummed and filled a big cup. Then he looked at the dishwasher. The screen said it needed its monthly cleaning. "Remind me on Saturday to run the cleaning cycle," he told the speaker. The speaker said, "Reminder set for Saturday." Vikram sipped his coffee, which was twice as strong as normal, and went back to the call, glad that his hands were free.

Ella ran a small bakery shop, and her phone was always almost dead. It was lunchtime, and she was eating a sandwich behind the counter when she squinted at the screen. "I can barely see anything in here," she said to the phone. The phone raised the screen brightness. She still frowned. "These letters are tiny." The phone made the text size larger. A yellow note was stuck to the register, and Ella could read it easily now: order flour. She also noticed the battery was at nine percent. "I am about to lose power," she said, and the phone turned on battery saver mode. Ella smiled and went on eating.

The person wants the assistant to read out their unread emails.
Read my mail
Any new email?
Read my unread emails at quarter to eight
I lie on the couch with my phone nearby, so could you read my new messages out loud?
Tell me who emailed me this morning
Is there anything from the painting class in my inbox?
Could you please go through my inbox at quarter to eight and read anything unread, just the sender and the subject?

name: send_text_later
does: Sends a text message at a time you choose, like a note to your housemate about the dishwasher or an invite to a public event.
inputs: who should get it, what it says, and when to send it; say if you prefer a short or a long message
people say:
- Text Sam at eight tomorrow
- Tell the group chat dinner is at seven, but not until noon
- Message Leo later and remind him about the dishwasher
- Don't send it now, wait until Friday
- Wish my aunt a happy birthday first thing in the morning

Siobhan woke up to a beep from her phone. She rubbed her eyes and saw the words missed call. Her sister had called twice. The TV was still on a news channel from last night, so she turned it down. "Call Anna," she mumbled. The phone began to ring. Anna did not answer, and the phone asked if Siobhan wanted to leave a voicemail. "Yes," she said, and then she said, "Hi Anna, it's me. Call me back." Then she asked the phone, "Any messages?" The phone said she had one voicemail and played it. It was her sister, saying she would make a quick visit on Sunday. Siobhan smiled and went to make tea.

Li was texting three friends when the family trip came up. His mom was planning a holiday by the sea, and the trip would continue for a week. He was excited, because it started the next day. He picked up the phone and typed, "Find a hotel by the beach and book it for two nights." The assistant answered, "There is a hotel on the beach with a room free for two nights. How many guests?" Li typed, "Three, and ask for a room with a sea view." The assistant replied, "Done. The room is booked for three guests, and I have asked for a sea view." Li put the phone back in his silver case and showed his mom the message. She said, "Thank you, that was quick."

Eitan was eighty years old and had earned a quiet evening. He sat in his chair with a book, but the light in the room was too bright for his eyes. He spoke to the smart lamp on the left side of his chair. "Excuse me, would you kindly make the light half as bright? My eyes are tired from reading all day, and I would like to keep reading," he said. The lamp dimmed to half. "Is this better?" it asked. "Yes, thank you," said Eitan. He read for another hour in the soft light. When he got sleepy, he said, "Good night," and the lamp turned off by itself. Eitan smiled and went to bed.

An appointment is a time that is kept for you, like a haircut, a visit to the dentist or a check-up. Shops and clinics have opening hours, and you can only book a time when they are open. When people let the assistant know what they want, they say the kind of visit, the day and the time. They change things often. They say, move my haircut to Friday, make it an hour later, cancel the dentist, or is the salon open on Sunday? Hair salons are busy on Saturdays, so people book early. Most places send a reminder the day before, and you can ask the assistant to remind you an hour earlier too.

Lakshmi had never liked computers, but her grandfather had given her his old laptop. One morning the words on the screen looked tiny, and she was late for a class on video. She typed fast, all in lowercase: make the text biger. The assistant understood and said, "I have increased the text size. Is it better now?" Lakshmi typed, yes thx. Then the assistant said, "I also see that your files have not been saved in a while. Would you like a weekly backup?" She typed, ok do it weekly. The assistant set the backup for every Sunday night. Lakshmi sighed with relief, joined the class, and read every word on the screen.

name: water_plan
does: Tells you when and how much to water each plant, so tomatoes and other tasty things grow well.
inputs: the plant's name, where it sits (a warm window or the shelf by the piano), and the last time it was watered
people say:
- Does my basil need a drink?
- When did I last water the tomatoes?
- The fern by the piano looks dry
- How much water for a big pot?
- Remind me to water the garden every other morning

Cooling keeps a room comfortable when it is hot. An air conditioner blows cold air, and a fan only moves the air around. A waiter in a hot restaurant is glad to see the fan above the tables, and the guests cheer when the room gets cooler. People change cooling with a few simple words. They say, it is too warm in here, make it cooler, turn the fan on, or set it to twenty-two degrees. When a room feels weird, cold in one corner and hot in another, they say, point the air up, or slow the fan down. At night many people say, turn the air off at midnight.

Amelie had just taken a shower, and her glasses were foggy. The house felt hot, and her mother was angry that the air conditioner had been broken all week. Now it was fixed, and Amelie's grandparents were coming to stay. She texted the home assistant on her phone: "start cooling the guest room on the twelfth of March at four pm so it's cold when grandma comes". The assistant answered, "Okay. The air conditioner in the guest room will start at four o'clock on the twelfth of March." Amelie wiped her glasses and read the answer. "Make it twenty-two degrees," she typed. The assistant said it was done. Her mother smiled, and there were no angry words that day.

Living near other people means sharing sounds, streets and sometimes problems. A loud party or a barking dog can ruin a quiet evening. Most people first talk to the neighbour in a kind way, or ask a colleague or a friend who lives nearby what to do. Local groups help with events, lost pets and bad noise. People ask their assistant to find the local events this weekend, to write a polite note about the noise, or to remind them to bring the lost cat poster to the shop. If a note works, they say, stop the reminder. If the noise goes on, they ask, who do I call about it? Being kind and clear usually solves it.

A step counter on a phone or a watch counts how many steps you take. It uses the small movements of your body, so it can be wrong if you push a cart or ride on a bus. Many people also like to know the distance and their pace, which is how long one mile or kilometre takes. People change goals and ask for things by saying, how many steps today, what was my pace on that walk, or make my goal ten thousand steps. If the wind is blowing hard and they want a shorter route, they say, plan a short loop. If a number looks wrong, they say, that count is not correct, please check it.

School work is made of subjects, assignments and due dates. A teacher writes an assignment on the board, and students write it in a notebook or a phone. A due date tells you when to hand it in. People ask for help with these things in different words. They say, when is my science project due, remind me to study on Wednesday, or move the reading to after the break. Before an exam, a student may say, quiz me on the capitals, or read my notes out loud. Even lunch matters: a spicy meal might make a hard day better, and some students put a lunch reminder in their calendar. The aim is to finish work calmly and on time.

Hannah put on her sunglasses and her gardening gloves. A big plant fair was starting in a town a hundred and twenty miles away, and she wanted to buy new roses. "How long will it take to drive to the Green Valley plant fair?" she asked the car. The car looked at the traffic. "It will take about two hours and ten minutes. If you leave now, you will arrive at eleven." Hannah looked at the sky. It was going to be a hot day. "Take the fastest road, please," she said. The car showed the route on the screen and began to give directions. Hannah arrived at eleven, just as the gates opened.
