A focus timer helps people work without drifting off. You pick a block of time, often twenty-five minutes, and work on one thing until the timer rings. Then you take a short break. It is for people who lose a whole afternoon to small distractions. People change the length of the work block, the length of the break, and how many rounds they do. They say, start a focus timer for thirty minutes, make the break ten minutes, or stop the timer. On a break, they stretch, drink water, or look out the window. If a cough or a phone call interrupts, they say, pause the timer, and later, keep going. A daily routine works in the same way: wake at seven, work till noon, lunch at one.

Kai was very hungry, and his mom was still at work. He picked up the family tablet and spoke to the assistant. "Could you please switch my order from the small pizza to the big one? My friend, a student from the next street, is coming to study with me, and we will both be hungry."
The assistant said it would change the pizza to a large one with cheese, and the new price was four dollars more. It asked if Kai wanted to give a tip for the driver. Kai said a small one was fine. The assistant said the food would come in about thirty minutes and that it would tell him when the driver was outside. When the bell rang, the pizza was hot, and the two of them ate every slice.

Fatima was eating cereal standing up while she packed the lunches. On Saturday the family wanted a long bike ride, so she asked her phone, "Find me an easy route by the river and tell me how far it is."
The phone showed a flat path of twelve kilometers and said it would take about an hour at a slow speed. Fatima liked it. She asked the phone to tag the route as Family Ride so she could find it again. Then she looked at a new child seat for the bike, but it was pricey, so she asked the phone to remind her to check the shop sale on Friday. The assistant saved the route under the tag and set the reminder. Everyone packed water and snacks.

Email is a way to send letters over the internet. The inbox is where new mail arrives, and unread messages are often shown in bold. People use email to keep in touch, send photos, and share files. An attachment is a file added to a message, and a huge file may be too big to send. People ask for changes in simple words. They say, show me unread mail, write an email to Sam, or attach this picture. If a message is not needed, they say, delete it or put it away. To let someone know you got their message, you reply. Some people like to know about every new message right away. Others only open email in the evening, when the garden work is done.

Wiremu woke up early because he wanted to swim before the beach got busy. He sat on the sand with his phone on speaker and asked, "What time is the tide, and is the water warmer than yesterday?"
The assistant said low tide was at seven, and the water was about two degrees warmer, which was still cool. Wiremu said that was fine. Then he said, "Remind me to put on more sun cream in an hour. Double the usual amount, please." The assistant said it would. While he stretched, his daughter called, and the assistant asked if he wanted to answer. He said, "Call her back later." Then he walked down to the sea and went in slowly.

Sabine came home after a night shift, tired and hungry. She was waiting for a parcel with medicine for her mother, and she did not want to miss it. She said to her phone, "Excuse me, could you please tell me where my parcel is? I need to hurry to bed, but my mother takes this medicine every morning, and I want to be awake when it arrives."
The phone found the tracking number in her email. It said the parcel was out for delivery and would come between ten and noon. It also said the box was thick and would not fit in the mailbox, so the driver would ring the bell. Sabine asked it to wake her at ten, and the phone set an alarm. Then she slept.

Sylvie was late for work and the eggs were still frying on the stove. Her bored cat watched from the window ledge. She grabbed her bag and said to her phone, "Turn on the front door camera, but don't set off the alarm, because the cat is still inside."
The assistant switched on the camera and said the motion alarm would stay off while someone was home. It showed her a picture of the porch, where a flat stone sat by the step. Sylvie said not to send an alert to her brother, and the assistant said no alerts would go to him. Then she turned off the stove, locked the door, and ran for the bus.

A video meeting lets people at different desks talk and see each other. You join by clicking a link at the time shown on the invitation. Before it starts, most people check the camera and the microphone. In the meeting, you can mute yourself when you are not talking, share your screen to show a plain slide or a document, and read the agenda, which is a short list of what will be talked about. People ask for these things in simple words: mute me, share my screen, turn my camera off, or fill in the notes. The agenda is the wheel that keeps a meeting moving, and a meeting with a clear plan is usually shorter.

A board game timer keeps turns fair. It is for games where one player takes too long to think. People set a time for each turn, say sixty seconds, and the timer counts down. They say, set a timer for one minute, or give me thirty more seconds. A score keeper tracks points. You might say, give Ana five points, take one away from Tom, or what is the score? Rules can be confusing, so people also ask, what is the right move here, or read me the rules for dice. In some games the bank may charge ten coins for a hotel, and one player is in charge of the money. After the game, everyone has milk and cookies.

name: plan_dog_walk
does: Suggests a good time and length for a dog walk, so the dog does not get too tired or too hot.
inputs: the dog's name, the weather, and who is walking, for example the girl next door who helps out; say when you think the dog needs to go out
people say:
- When should I walk Max?
- Is it too hot to take the dog out?
- How long should a walk be for a puppy?
- The dog seems tired, should we go out?
- Plan a walk after dinner

Person: I need you to set a bedtime for Lily and turn off the tablet.
Assistant: I can do that. What time should Lily's bedtime be?
Person: Eight o'clock. The doctor said she needs more sleep.
Assistant: Okay. Should the tablet turn off at eight, or a little sooner?
Person: A bit before. I do not know how that works.
Assistant: I will turn it off at seven forty-five, so she has time to get ready. Is that good?
Person: Yes, thank you. It is cloudy today, so we will grill sausages tonight. Can you tell Lily dinner is ready at six?
Assistant: I cannot talk to Lily in another room, but I can put an announcement on the kitchen speaker. Would you like that?
Person: Yes please.
Assistant: Done. I will announce dinner at six.

The kitchen was humid and Aino's hands were covered in flour. She had ordered a new set of kitchen scales, and she wanted to know if they were coming. She said to her speaker, "Track order." The assistant said the box was at the post office and would come tomorrow.
Aino asked, "Change delivery?" and the assistant asked which day she wanted. She said, "Friday," and it moved the delivery. Then she asked it to stream some quiet music while she kneaded the dough. She also asked it to remind her to find the spare key before the courier arrived. Soon the kitchen smelled of warm bread.

A baby monitor lets parents hear or see their baby from another room. It is for naps and for the night, when parents want to rest but still know their baby is safe. People change a few things about it: the sound, the picture, and the alerts. They say, turn up the monitor, show me the baby, or tell me if she cries. Feeding times are personal, because each baby is different, so parents set their own reminders, like feed the baby at nine. Naps work the same way. When it is time to eat, a parent might peel a banana or warm the milk, and wipe the hair from the baby's face. Parents also ask, how long has she slept?

Olivia was under the sink fixing a leaky faucet when her little son ran in with a school sheet. He wanted to know how many stickers they would have if they bought double the packs. Olivia's hands were wet, so she asked the speaker, "What is six packs times two, and then half of that?"
The assistant answered twelve, and then six. Her son wanted to create a poster with exactly twenty stickers. Olivia asked how many more they needed if they had twelve. The assistant said eight more. "Great," said Olivia, and she wrote eight on a note. Her son clapped and ran off to find his pens.

name: days_until_date
does: Counts how many days are left until a date, ranks several dates from nearest to farthest, and works even for a weird date like the next leap day.
inputs: the date, and what it is for, like a trip or a piano lesson
people say:
- How many days till Christmas?
- How long until my next piano lesson?
- How many more sleeps until we leave?
- Which comes first, my exam or the trip?
- When is the closest holiday?

A person wants a rough idea of how much battery is left on the laptop.
Battery level?
How much charge is left?
What's my battery at?
Is my laptop about to die?
Don't open any menus, just tell me the battery percentage
I don't understand the little battery icon, so how much is left in plain numbers?
I need to use the printer for an hour, will the battery last that long?
Could you please tell me how much battery is left, because I don't want to lose my work?

A bus timetable tells people when a bus will come to their stop. It is for planning a trip so you do not wait in the bitter cold longer than needed. Train timetables work the same way, and many show delays when a train is late. People change things about their trip, like the stop, the time and the kind of ticket. They say, when is the next bus to the station, is the train late, or buy a day ticket. A stop by the ocean may have fewer buses in winter. Some buses have a lift for wheelchairs and prams, so people can ask, does the bus have a lift? Notices tell passengers about changes.

Someone is looking for gift ideas for a friend's birthday.
Gift ideas for my sister
What should I get my friend for her birthday?
Not a book, not a mug, any other idea?
Ideas for dad, he's a constant reader, but I don't want to buy another book
I don't want to spend more than twenty percent of my pay, so what can I get my brother?
Nothing silly please, I want something that will touch her heart for her fortieth
Help, I can't think of a gift and I don't want it to be boring

Siobhan was in the back seat, on the way to the east side of town, texting with one thumb. She was planning a party and wanted to invite twelve friends. She typed to the assistant, "wat is 12 times 3 candy" and the assistant said thirty-six pieces. Siobhan thought that was too many and typed, "half of that?" It said eighteen. Then she typed, "ok plus 5 for me" and the assistant said twenty-three. Siobhan smiled, texted her mom to buy eighteen candies and five for herself, and put the phone away as the car pulled in.

Someone wants a reminder about a friend's birthday so they can send a card.
Remind me about Sam's birthday
Remind me on the twelfth of June
Don't let me forget Anna's birthday next Friday
I want a reminder a week before Mum's birthday
I'm on a long journey on the fourth of May, so remind me early about Lisa's birthday
Ping me on a bright and early Monday morning so I can post the card in time
Tell me in two days if Tom's birthday is coming up

A bus pass is a card or a ticket that lets a person ride buses and trains for a set time. It is for people who travel often, since it costs less than buying single tickets. Young people and old people often get a cheaper pass. Passes can be for a day, a week or a month. People change the type, the length, and where it works. They say, buy a weekly pass, how much is a day ticket, or show me my pass. The app keeps a record of your trips, so you can see where you went. If a pass does not work, you may say, my ticket is not working. A town may lie on two train lines, so ask which pass covers both.

Hannah was studying fractions for a math test, and the room was too quiet. She said to her speaker, "Play radio." The assistant asked which station, and she said the usual one, the music station she liked. It started a pop song.
A while later Hannah did not care for the song, so she said, "Next station." The assistant tuned to the news. Hannah said, "Louder." After twenty minutes she said, "Stop." The assistant turned the radio off, and the room was quiet again. She went back to her homework and finally got the fractions right.

Someone wants the robot mower to cut the grass, the easy way, with their voice.
Mow now
Start mowing
Cut the grass
Can you get the mower going?
Please send the mower out to the lawn
I'd like the lawn done without touching anything, so just start the mower
I need to balance work and chores, so please start the mower before I get home
Would you mind running the robot mower for an hour this afternoon?

Person: when does my flight leve
Assistant: Which flight do you mean? I need the flight number or the city you are flying to.
Person: the one to berlin tomorrow. i can not scroll back to the email
Assistant: No problem. I see one flight to Berlin tomorrow. It leaves at 9:40 in the morning. I can put it in your calendar with a green tag.
Person: yes please. is there a delay
Assistant: I see no delay right now. I will tell you if that changes.
Person: thanks. i am going to eat my lettuce wrap now
Assistant: Enjoy, and have a good trip.

Pilar was helping at her uncle's shop on a Saturday, and she had a video meeting for the school club. The shop door was open, and it was loud. She typed to her phone, "Could you please open the meeting link from my email and turn my microphone off at first? My uncle is trying to sell a pair of boots to a customer next to me, and it is very noisy."
The phone opened the meeting and muted the microphone. The club leader shared the agenda on the screen, and Pilar read the first three points. When they asked her a question, she said, "Unmute me," and the assistant turned the microphone back on. After the call she said thanks and went to help her uncle with the boot boxes.

Oluwaseun was running to a meeting with half a cookie in his hand when he remembered an idea. He asked his phone, "Write down a note: bring two more chairs than last time." The assistant saved the note.
He also asked it to find his old note about the budget, and it opened the note on the screen. The note said the pair of speakers cost double what he had planned. He said, "Make a reminder to ask for a lower price." The assistant answered in a polite voice that it had set the reminder for tomorrow morning. Oluwaseun nodded, finished the cookie, and walked in.

Person: Can I get the steps for roast beef?
Assistant: Sure. How heavy is the roast?
Person: About two kilos. My family comes on the twelfth of March and I want it to be perfect.
Assistant: For two kilos, plan about one hour and forty minutes at 180 degrees. Do you want a timer?
Person: Yes. I am driving now, so I will start it when I get home.
Assistant: I can't start a timer before the roast is in the oven. Tell me when it goes in, and I will count the time.
Person: Okay. Can you see where I put my wooden spoon?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't see your kitchen. Once you are home and comfortable, I can read you the steps.

Coffee and tea can be made strong or weak, sweet or plain. A coffee machine lets people choose how strong the drink is, how much milk goes in, and how big the cup is. Tea gets stronger the longer the bag stays in the water, so some people draw the bag out after two minutes. People ask for changes in simple words: make it stronger, less sugar, a bit more milk, or a smaller cup. Smoothies are soft and thick, made with fruit like banana, and some people leave the skin on apples for extra fiber. At a cafe, people say, a large latte with oat milk.

When a package is on the way, the shipping company gives a tracking number. People use it to see where the parcel is and when it will arrive. Letters go to the mailbox, and bigger parcels may need a signature, which means someone must sign for them at the door. People change things like the delivery day, the place, or who may sign. They say, where is my package, hold it at the post office, or leave it with the neighbor. Sometimes a weird small box holds something big, like a humidifier, and people want to install it right away. Others just ask, did the mail come yet?

Budi was in a hurry on Monday morning. He looked at the clock and said to the kitchen radio, "News please." The assistant tuned to the morning news and turned up the sound. Budi wanted to know about the traffic, so he said, "Traffic update." The reporter said the main road was slow.
Budi said, "Switch station," and the assistant found a great music channel. He nodded, grabbed his keys, and said, "Radio off." The room went quiet, and he left by the back door.

name: move_between_accounts
does: Moves money between your own accounts in one quick step, so you feel ready to pay for something big like a new tv.
inputs: the amount, the account to take it from, and the account to put it into
people say:
- Put fifty dollars into savings
- Move two hundred from checking to my holiday account
- Send some money to my other account for the tv
- I need to top up my bills account with a hundred
- Take thirty from savings

A flight departure board shows when planes leave, which gate to go to, and if a flight is late. It is for travelers who want to know where to be and when. A delay means the plane leaves later than planned. People ask, when does my flight leave, which gate is it, or is the flight late? Travelers dig through their bags for passports, and a dad with kids may check the time often. The air in a plane is dry, so people bring water. At the gate, boarding starts about thirty minutes before the flight. If the gate changes, a message says so.

Milena was in her garden, fixing a drip hose, when her phone buzzed. It said her password was old. She wiped her hands and spoke to the assistant. "Please make my password longer, with more letters than before."
The assistant said it would create a new one with twelve characters and asked her to press the button on the screen to confirm. She also asked who could see her photos. The assistant said only two people could, and she asked it to remove one. Then she asked the phone to lock itself sooner, after half a minute instead of five. It did. Milena picked up her creamy iced coffee from the wall and went back to the hose.

Someone wants to lock their phone so nobody at the local cafe can use it.
Lock phone
Lock it now
Lock the screen
I'm getting in the bath, lock my phone
Please make sure nobody can open my phone
Lock my phone before I walk away, and I will tidy up later
I'm leaving it on the table, so lock it
Could you lock the phone, please?

name: trim_video_clip
does: Cuts a video down to the part you want to keep, measures how long the clip is, and gets it ready to share online.
inputs: which video, such as the one of you trying on jeans, and the start and end time you want to keep
people say:
- Cut the first ten seconds off my video
- Make the clip shorter
- Keep only the part from one minute to two minutes
- I only want the end of the video of my sister dancing
- Trim the birthday video to thirty seconds

Someone wants to know where an iron they ordered is.
Where is my parcel?
Track my package
Has my order shipped yet?
Find my parcel and tell me when it will arrive
The tracking link is not working, so can you check where the box is?
I ordered an iron last week, where is it?
Please look up my garlic press order and let me know if it's out for delivery

A playlist is a list of songs that plays one after another. People make them for a mood, like calm songs for dinner or fast songs for a run. They change the songs, the order and the volume. The words they use are: play my running playlist, skip this song, turn it down, or play it again. Some apps design a playlist for you from what you like. Music changes how a room feels. A thermostat sets the heat, but songs set the mood. Salty snacks and a good playlist go well at a party. If you like a singer, you can ask, who sings this?

Person: can you send the clip to my customers
Assistant: Which clip do you mean, and who should get it?
Person: the one i filmed this morning of the new bush plants we sell, to everyone on my list
Assistant: I found a video from this morning, forty seconds long. I am sorry, I can't send messages to your customer list. I can put the link on your phone so you can send it yourself.
Person: ok that is cool. put it there
Assistant: Done. The link is on your phone now.

Andre was late and already at the door when he remembered the alarm. He typed with one thumb, "arm the alram on medium and list the cameras that are on, my cat is home."
The assistant armed the alarm on medium, which ignores small pets, and read out the cameras: front door, garage, and the one at the side of the garden that faces the park. Andre said thanks, locked the back door, and hurried to the car.

Person: Please turn on the front camera and lock the side door. I'm leaving for work.
Assistant: I can do both. Which door is the side door, the one by the garage or the one in the laundry room?
Person: The laundry room, next to the washer.
Assistant: Got it. The laundry room door is locked and the front camera is on.
Person: Also, can you ring my phone if someone comes to the door?
Assistant: Yes. Should it ring for any motion, or only when someone presses the bell?
Person: Only the bell. The cat sets off the motion sensor far too well.
Assistant: Done. Your phone will ring only when the doorbell is pressed.

A translation app helps when you meet words you do not know. Say you are in a park in another country and a sign is written in a language you cannot read. You hold up your phone and ask, What does this sign say in English? The app reads it and tells you. People change a few things: the language, how polite the words sound, and how fast the voice speaks. They say things like, Say it again more slowly, or Use the polite form. A tired traveler may just say, Translate that for me. Learning new phrases is a bit like stirring a pot: a little each day, and the words slowly mix into your memory. Many people ask for one new phrase every morning and ask to hear it out loud.

Leo woke up and rolled over. A bird was singing outside the window, and he felt bored before the day had even started. 'Read my list,' he mumbled to his phone. The assistant read out four tasks: pay the water bill, call the dentist, buy bread, and wash the car. Leo yawned. 'Count them,' he said. 'You have four tasks today,' said the assistant. That felt like too many. 'Cut the car,' Leo said. The assistant took washing the car off the list and said three tasks were left. Leo smiled, stretched, and finally got out of bed.

Oscar woke up to his phone buzzing again. Every minute it shouted another alert about likes and new followers. He rubbed his eyes. 'Stop the like alerts, but don't turn off messages from my sister,' he said. The assistant asked if he wanted all the other notifications quiet too. 'No, just the likes,' said Oscar. 'I don't want a cheap little buzz every time someone taps a heart.' The assistant switched off the like notifications and left messages and comments on. The phone went quiet. Oscar lay back on his pillow and smiled. Now the only buzz would be from his sister, and he could sleep ten more minutes.

An automatic pet feeder is a small box that gives your pet food at the same times each day. It is useful when you are at work or away for a weekend. People often change how much food comes out and when. They say things like, Feed the dog at seven and five, or Give the cat a smaller portion at night. Some feeders record every meal, so you can ask, Did Biscuit eat this morning? If the dog spills crumbs on the rug, you might ask for a little less. You can also say, Pause feeding until tomorrow, when the vet says your pet should skip a meal.

Simon was at the beach with his friends, texting the assistant on his phone. His nose felt hot and tight. 'my face feels like it's burning,' he typed. The assistant guessed he needed sun cream and said the UV level would stay very high until four o'clock. It offered to remind him every hour to put more on. 'yes pls,' Simon typed. Just then a wave rushed in, and one sock fell out of his bag and floated away. His friends laughed. The water looked pretty in the sunlight, but Simon stayed under the umbrella. An hour later his phone buzzed with a message: Time for more sun cream.

Juliette sat at her messy desk with a cold coffee. 'Read me the top headlines and tell me who won the football match last night,' she said to her phone. The assistant read three headlines. One was about a new bridge, one was about a school fair, and one was about a storm out over the ocean. Then it said the home team had won two to one. Juliette smiled. The fans always paint their faces blue on match days, and she knew the streets would be loud at lunch. She thanked the assistant and went back to her emails.

Jonah woke up sticky and sleepy. The afternoon was humid and the fan was not helping. He picked up his phone and typed in a hurry: 'what chapter am i on in my bok'. The assistant checked his bookmark and said he had stopped at chapter eleven, on page one hundred and four. Jonah had planned to call his cousin at six, so he typed again: 'remind me to read at seven'. The assistant set a reminder for seven o'clock tonight. Jonah put the phone down, opened the window a little, and let the cooler air in.

Person: Did my parcel come today?
Assistant: Which parcel do you mean? I see two orders on the way.
Person: The one from the book shop. Sorry, no, I mean the shoes. The book shop one isn't due until Friday.
Assistant: Okay, the shoes. They show as delivered and left in the mailbox at 9:40.
Person: I just got off a night shift and I'm too tired to look. Was it paid for already?
Assistant: Yes, it was paid for on the website when you ordered.
Person: Could you flash the porch light when the mailbox opens next time?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't tell when the mailbox is opened. I can send you a message when a delivery is marked as delivered.
Person: That works. Please do that.
Assistant: Done. You will get a message for every delivery.

Ioana was ten, and her family was going camping for her birthday. She sat on the couch with a small cough and asked the tablet, 'Make a packing list and tell me if it will rain on Saturday.' The assistant made a list: tent, sleeping bag, torch, warm socks, and a water bottle. Then it said there would be no rain, only sunshine. Ioana clapped. 'Put a gold star next to the tent,' she joked. The assistant laughed and said it could not draw, but it added a note at the bottom: Bring birthday cake. They would celebrate by the fire. Ioana's cough already felt better.

Person: Is the front door locked?
Assistant: Yes, the front door is locked. The garage door is open, though.
Person: Oh dear. Shut it, please. No wait, I'm taking out the trash first. Shut it in ten minutes.
Assistant: Okay. The garage door will close in ten minutes. Do you want a beep before it moves?
Person: Yes, please. A sudden noise would be rude to the neighbors.
Assistant: A short beep will sound for five seconds first.
Person: Can you also unlock the back gate for my grandson?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't control the back gate. I can only lock and unlock the front door and the garage door.

Tendai was driving to a job interview and felt nervous. A hammer rattled in the toolbox on the back seat every time he turned a corner. 'Put on the news station,' he said. The assistant tuned in to ninety-four point five. 'No, wait, I want the music station instead,' he said. The assistant switched to a channel playing calm piano. Tendai breathed out slowly. At a red light he spotted a sign saying the road ahead was closed. 'Is there another way?' he asked. The assistant told him to turn left at the next corner. He arrived ten minutes early and still had time to sit quietly in the car.

A person wants to know whether this month's electricity bill is more than last month's, and wants the answer by text.
Is my power bill higher than last month?
Electricity: more or less than before?
Did the bill go up?
Compare this month's electricity bill with last month's.
I'm at the hair salon, so please text me if the electricity bill is double what it was in March.
Is the fancy new heater making my power bill bigger?
Tell me how much more I paid for electricity this month.
Could you check whether my electricity cost is half of what it was in winter, and let me know?

A person wants to write down a quick idea as a note.
Note this.
Jot that down.
Save a note.
Write this down: buy milk.
Make a note that my purse is in the blue bag.
Start a voice note, and beep when you're recording.
Note to self: bring an umbrella, it looks cloudy.
Can you please keep a note of the idea I just had? I'm afraid I will forget it by tomorrow.
Put a note on my phone: call Dad on Sunday.

Andre was folding tiny socks while his daughter watched a cartoon. The episode would end soon, and the washing machine was still running. 'Tell me when the wash is done and send me a message when the dryer finishes,' he said to the kitchen speaker. The speaker said the wash had eleven minutes left. It promised to call out when the machine stopped and to send a message when the dryer was done. Andre pulled a wide basket closer and started sorting shirts. There was a juice stain on his son's sleeve, so he asked for a stain tip. The speaker told him to rub it with cold water and a little soap.

Nimal was not good with technology. His daughter had left a small box on his bedside table, and he did not know how to use it. 'I want to sleep more than last night,' he said to the box. 'Wake me later than usual.' The box said, 'Your alarm was set for six. How much later?' Nimal frowned. 'Is half an hour enough?' 'You can say half an hour more, or an hour more,' said the box. 'Make it an hour more,' he said. The box moved the alarm to seven. Nimal felt calm. He hoped the good feeling would last all night, and that tonight he would have a deep sleep.

Rahul came home from the hospital after a long night. His stomach was empty, and his diet plan said no fried food. 'Find a salad place nearby and book a table for two at noon,' he told his phone. The assistant found a small cafe and said it had a table at noon. It also warned him that the cafe closed early on Sundays. Rahul nodded. 'Noon is fine.' The assistant booked it and sent him the address. Then he asked to see the menu. The cafe served soup, salad, and frozen yogurt. Rahul smiled, set an alarm for eleven, and went to bed.

Noah did not like phones. His grandson had shown him a big button for the assistant, and now Noah pressed it and said, 'Haircut Tuesday.' The assistant asked what time he liked. 'Morning,' said Noah. The assistant found a free slot at ten o'clock at the barber shop on Elm Street and booked it. It said the shop took a maximum of five customers an hour, so ten o'clock was the last place. Noah smiled. The barber always welcomed him with a warm towel and a friendly joke, and he used scissors, never a knife. Noah wrote Tuesday, ten o'clock on a piece of paper to be sure.

Oscar was seven, and he wanted his sunflowers to grow the tallest on the street. 'Water the garden in twenty minutes,' he told the garden assistant. 'The sprinklers will start at four fifteen,' it said. Oscar ran to the fence and painted a blue sign that said Sunflower Club. The sun was strong, and most of the leaves looked thirsty. 'How much sun do they need?' he asked. The assistant said sunflowers like six hours of sun and plenty of water. Oscar's grandma lived a mile away, so he asked the assistant to take a photo of the flowers and send it to her. She wrote back with three hearts.

Ahmed woke up and remembered that a parcel was coming. 'Where is my order?' he asked his phone. The assistant said the jacket had left the warehouse and was fifty miles away. 'It should arrive on Thursday afternoon, between two and four.' Ahmed groaned. The delivery window was short, only two hours, and he had hoped for sooner, because he wanted to wear the jacket to the cinema on Wednesday night. 'Can you forward the tracking details to my brother?' he asked. 'He is home all day.' The assistant sent the tracking link to his brother. Ahmed said thanks and went to make some tea.

Person: Excuse me, could you please start a timer for the chess game? My grandson and I like to play with a time limit, and I forget how long has passed.
Assistant: Of course. How many minutes should each player get?
Person: Ten minutes each, please.
Assistant: Done. Ten minutes for each player. Shall I tell you the current time left every few minutes?
Person: Yes, every two minutes. We play every Friday, and last week I lost because I did not hear the buzz. And could you wipe the old score from last week?
Assistant: I can clear the saved score. Do you want to erase all past scores or only last Friday's?
Person: Only last Friday's, please.
Assistant: Cleared. Good luck with the game!

Wiremu got home after a night shift, tired and hungry. The hall was dim, and a new camera was still sitting in its box by the door. He was too sleepy to install it. He grabbed an apple, because his diet plan said no biscuits, and typed in a hurry: 'turn on the hall ligth'. The assistant switched on the hall light at half brightness. Then Wiremu typed: 'remind me to put up the camera at five'. The assistant set the reminder for five o'clock that afternoon. Wiremu smiled, finished his apple, and went to bed with the door locked.

Sigrid was hosting a small party at home after work. The room was dark, and her hands were full of snack bowls. 'Play some jazz on the living room speaker,' she said. A moment later she added, 'No, sorry, play it in the kitchen too, not just the living room.' The assistant joined the two speakers together, so the jazz sounded the same in both rooms. 'Make it a bit quieter,' Sigrid said. The assistant lowered the volume. She had invited six friends, and the first one was already knocking. 'Turn on the hall light,' she said. The light came on, and she opened the door with a big smile.

A person wants the pool water to be warmer.
Heat the pool.
Make the pool warmer.
Turn up the water temperature, please.
It's too cold to swim.
The pool feels like ice. Can you warm it up?
Could you please raise the pool temperature to thirty degrees? My son has swimming practice this afternoon, and he gets cold easily.
I'm having a birthday party with cake by the pool on Saturday, so would you mind warming the water before the guests arrive?
Would you kindly make the water warmer? The light is dim out here and I can't read the gauge myself.

Jing was rushing to the bus stop when she remembered her friend's birthday. 'Days until Tuesday?' she asked her phone. 'Four days,' said the assistant. Jing nodded and kept walking. 'Message Lena.' The assistant asked what to say. 'Happy birthday, see you soon,' said Jing. The assistant sent the message right away. She wanted to buy a present, so she said, 'Find gifts.' The assistant showed her three shops that sold flowers and cards online. Jing picked a small plant and the bus arrived just as she paid. She jumped on, out of breath but happy.

Sofia ran a small shop on a busy road. One morning she looked up and saw that the digital sign over her door had gone black. 'The sign over my door is dead,' she told her phone. The assistant understood that she needed a repair and found two repair companies that were open tomorrow. 'Pick the cheaper one,' said Sofia. The assistant booked a visit at nine o'clock and said the coupon in her email would subtract ten dollars from the price. Sofia thanked it. She put a paper sign in the window that said Open, and then she went back to her customers.

A digital door lock is a lock you open with a code, a card, or your phone instead of a key. It keeps your home safe and lets your family in without keys. People change the code, the time the door locks by itself, and who is allowed in. They say things like, Lock the front door, or Turn on auto lock at night. If a friend visits, you can say, Give Maria a code for today only. Someone coming home late from the theater may ask, Is the door locked? Then the lock answers yes or no, and they can lock it from the street.

A person wants to know how cold it will get at night at their campsite, so they can decide whether to bring a thick blanket or a carpet for the tent floor.
How cold will it be tonight?
Night temperature at the campsite?
Will it be chilly in the hills after dark?
Will it fall below forty degrees tonight?
Should I pack a thick jacket or will it be warm enough?
Will it be warm enough to cook outside after the sun goes down?
Tell me the low for tonight in the hills, please.
I'm camping up high this weekend. Could you tell me how cold the nights will be?

Nathan came in from walking the dog with the leash still in his hand. The air in the apartment felt dry and a bit stuffy, and the windows by the sea left a salty dust on the sill. 'Turn on the purifier and open the vent in the baby's room,' he said. The assistant started the purifier and opened the vent. 'I like the air cooler at night,' Nathan added. The assistant lowered the room temperature by two degrees. A few minutes later the air smelled fresh. Nathan hung up the leash, washed his hands, and went to check on the baby.

A game timer keeps a board game fair. It counts down while a player thinks, and it buzzes when the time ends. People change how long each turn lasts and when the whole game should end. They say things like, Give each player two minutes, or Stop the game after thirty minutes. If a rule sounds weird, someone may ask, What is the rule for rolling a six? Some timers also keep score, so you can say, Add three points to Sam. Nobody argues about who is winning, which keeps the game calm and fun. Keep a can of juice by the board, and the game can go on all evening.

Nandi sat on the porch while her grandson did his homework. She had planned a bike ride, but she looked at the hill at the end of the street and sighed. 'This hill is too much for me today,' she said to the bike computer. The assistant understood. It found three small, flat routes near her house and ranked them from easiest to hardest. The easiest was the lake path, only five kilometers. 'That one,' said Nandi. The assistant saved the route and started the trip timer. She put on her helmet, waved to her grandson, and rolled slowly down the quiet street.

A person wants to hear about local events this weekend. It is their turn to pick the plan, and they like a medium-sized crowd.
What's on nearby this weekend?
Any local events on Saturday?
List the events near me and tell me which ones are free.
Is there a street fair or a market anywhere near us?
Is there anything fun within a few steps of my house this weekend?
Find me something medium-sized to go to with the kids, maybe a market, and tell me when it ends.
Could you please tell me what is happening around here on Sunday afternoon? I would like to take my mother out somewhere nice.

Tyre pressure is the amount of air inside each tyre. If there is too little air, the tyre goes soft, wears out quickly and uses more fuel. A loose valve cap can let air escape. A grandfather who drives to the shops every day should check the pressure about once a month. Many cars show the pressure on a screen. People ask, What is the pressure in my front tyres? or Remind me to check the air next week. When prices go up, drivers can't afford to waste fuel, so they say, Tell me when a tyre is low.

A word counter tells you how many words you have written. It is handy for school work, emails, and stories. A kid might have an essay of two hundred words, and the counter shows when to stop. People change the limit and what to count. They say things like, How long is my story? or Count the words in this paragraph. If the essay is not pretty yet, they say, Fix the spelling or Make this sentence shorter. On a computer you click a button to see the count, but with an assistant you can simply ask out loud and get the number back.

Alessandro finished his shift at the hospital at seven in the morning. He sat in his car on the forest road, too tired to cook. 'Order pizza,' he said to his phone. The assistant said, 'You have ordered the mushroom pizza several times. Same again?' 'Same,' said Alessandro. The assistant placed the order and said it would arrive in thirty minutes. He drove home and waited on the couch. Forty minutes passed, and the doorbell was still quiet. 'Call the driver,' he said. The assistant called, and the driver said he was two streets away. Soon the pizza was at the door, still warm.

Person: Pay my rent, please.
Assistant: Sure. How much should I pay?
Person: Two thousand, I think. I'm tired, and I only want to buy some pork on the way home.
Assistant: Your last payment was two thousand and fifty dollars. Which one is right?
Person: Two thousand and fifty. Thanks for catching that.
Assistant: Done. The rent is paid. Anything else?
Person: Can you zoom in on the receipt? The numbers are tiny.
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't zoom the screen, but I can read it aloud: two thousand and fifty dollars to your landlord.
Person: Thanks. A message said I still owe money. Is that false?
Assistant: Yes, it looks false. All your bills are paid.

name: oven_belt_speed
does: Sets how fast the belt carries cookies through a bakery oven, so each batch bakes for the right time and does not go dark.
inputs: the kind of cookie, how hot the oven is, and how many minutes of baking you want
people say:
- Slow the cookie line down, they're coming out pale.
- These are coming out too dark.
- Make each batch bake for twelve minutes.
- The oven is hotter today, so let them go through faster.
- I'm switching to the thick cookies, so give them more time.

Warming up the car on a cold morning, or on a chilly evening, helps the engine and the windows. With an app you can start the engine before you leave the house. The heater melts the frost, and the car is warm when you sit down. People change the time and the heat. They say things like, Start my car in ten minutes, or Make it warmer inside. In the north, where winters are long, many drivers do this every day. While the engine warms up, some people dust the seats or clean the mirrors. On a hot day they ask for the opposite: Cool the car down before I get in.

name: reply_tone_helper
does: Rewrites an email reply so it sounds warm, polite and clear, and can add a blind copy to someone if you ask.
inputs: the email you are answering, the tone you want, and who to put in blind copy (optional)
people say:
- Make my reply sound friendlier.
- That email sounds too angry, soften it.
- Write back to Anna and keep it short but warm.
- Send a copy to my boss, but don't show it to Anna.
- Can you make this sound less rude?
- Say thanks politely and tell her I'll come on Tuesday.

name: pet_walk_planner
does: Plans a pet's walks for the day, such as a morning walk or a swim at the lake, and spaces them out so the animal gets several short walks.
inputs: the pet's name, how many walks you want, and the times you are free
people say:
- When should I take Rex out today?
- Plan some walks so the dog gets enough exercise.
- Is it too cold for the dog to swim today?
- The dog needs more walks, and I'm at work till six.
- Set up three outings for Luna, one early.

Janis opened her shop and felt strange: the town was quiet and nobody was on the street. Her pulse was still fast from running to work. She sat behind the counter, picked up her phone and typed in a hurry: 'put order flowrs at the top of my list'. The assistant moved the task to the top and said it was now her first job. Janis typed again: 'change the due time to noon'. The assistant changed it from five o'clock to twelve. She nodded, tied her apron, and called the flower supplier before the first customer walked in.

Odile had just moved to the city, and her baby slept in the stroller on the porch. She felt a little lost, so she asked the assistant for help. 'Remind me to feed Mila at three,' she said. A moment later she changed her mind. 'No, sorry, make it half past two.' The assistant set the reminder for two thirty. Odile also asked where the baby should nap on hot days. The assistant said a room on the north side of the house stays cooler. Odile smiled. At two thirty the phone chimed, and she carried Mila inside to feed her.

Person: I need to join the meeting but my screen is small.
Assistant: Which meeting? You have two today.
Person: The monthly one with Gerald.
Assistant: Okay, I joined the monthly meeting. Do you want the text bigger?
Person: Yes, make it twice as big. My screen has a crack and it's hard to read.
Assistant: Done. The text is twice as big.
Person: Please mute me while I eat. I am holding a fork.
Assistant: You are muted. Tell me when you want to speak again.

A person wants to be reminded to start their homework in an hour.
Remind me in an hour.
Homework reminder, one hour from now.
Set an alarm for an hour from now to start my homework.
Tell me to study after I bathe the dog, about an hour from now.
Don't let me forget my maths homework this evening. Nudge me in an hour.
Set a temporary alarm for an hour from now, just for tonight's homework.
I have a test tomorrow morning, so please ping me in an hour to open my books.

Sakura was cooking, and there was flour on both of her hands. Her phone lit up with a call, but she did not want to touch it. It was leaning on a jar at the height of her eyes. 'Don't answer, and don't read me any messages,' she said. 'Turn on do not disturb until the soup is ready.' The assistant switched on do not disturb. It asked how long the soup would take. 'Twenty minutes left,' said Sakura. The assistant said it would turn the setting off at the end of that time. Sakura went back to stirring in peace.

Person: Call Sam.
Assistant: Which Sam? Your son Sam or Sam the pharmacist?
Person: My son. His voice is tiny on this phone. Can you make it louder?
Assistant: I made the call volume louder. Is that better?
Person: Yes. My granddaughter is in fifth grade and she set this up for me. Remind pills.
Assistant: Which pills, and at what time?
Person: The white ones, at eight. Can you tell my neighbor I will lend him the ladder?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't send messages for you yet. I can call him if you like.

A person wants the steps of a fast pasta recipe.
Pasta recipe?
Show me a fast pasta recipe.
How do I make spaghetti quickly?
Read me the steps for tomato pasta and tell me how long it cooks.
It's snowing outside, so what can I cook in twenty minutes?
My cousin is coming for dinner. Give me an easy pasta recipe, please.
Could you please walk me through a simple pasta dish step by step? I have never made one before.

name: flood_alert_checker
does: Checks whether a flood warning is active on your street and tells you when the water is expected to rise, so you can visit higher ground in time.
inputs: your street name and, if you wear one, the number on your alert band
people say:
- Is my street going to flood?
- The river is rising. Should I be worried?
- Is it safe to drive home? The road looks pretty wet.
- Is there a flood warning near me?
- Water is coming under the door, what do I do?
- Should I move my car to higher ground?

Mia was a retired teacher, and she was flying to see her sister. At the kitchen table she asked her tablet, 'Is my flight more than an hour late?' The assistant checked and said it was thirty minutes late, which was half as late as yesterday's flight. 'The gate is B12,' it added. Mia was relieved. She packed salty crackers in her bag for the trip. 'Will it be cold at the airport?' she asked. The assistant said the building was cool, and that her hands might freeze in the waiting area. Mia put a warm scarf on top. Her dog would stay with a neighbor for the week.

Knitting is a hobby where you make scarves and hats from yarn with two needles. Young and old people enjoy it because it is calm. A beginner may knit during breaks from homework. People keep track of rows and change the size or the pattern. They say things like, Count my rows, Make the scarf longer, or Text me the pattern. A helper can remember where you stopped, so you can ask, Where did I leave off? Then it tells you the row and the color. Some people also say, Remind me to knit for twenty minutes every evening, so the hobby becomes a happy habit.

Ruta was a retired teacher, and she liked a tidy house. In May her old vacuum finally broke, so she had to buy a new one. She chose a smart robot vacuum and set it up all by herself. Then she spoke to her phone. "Please start the vacuum in the living room, but do not go into the bedroom. I don't want it near my plants." The assistant started the robot and marked the bedroom as a room to skip. "The vacuum is cleaning the living room now," it said. "The bedroom is off limits." Ruta smiled. She may be old, she thought, but she could still learn new tricks. An hour later the floor was clean, and the little robot rolled back to its dock.

Kai was a grandparent who paid the bills at the kitchen table every month. This time the water bill looked high, and he wanted to be careful. He typed fast on his phone: "remind me to pay the electrcity bill on friday and update the due date in my list". The assistant understood anyway. It set a reminder for Friday morning and updated the due date on the bill list. It also told him, "Your water bill is due after a stretch of five days, so you have time." Kai nodded. A clear list always made him feel calm. He put the phone down, finished his toast, and went to make a pot of tea.

The person wants their parcel to come on a different day in April, not the usual one.
Deliver it on Thursday instead
Can you move my parcel to next Tuesday at noon?
Not Monday, I'll be out
Please fix a new delivery time for my package
Could the parcel come on the ninth of April rather than the usual day?
Reschedule my delivery for next Tuesday at noon, please
I won't be home on the usual day, so could you send it on Saturday morning instead?
Change when the courier comes

The person wants a list of gas grills, ranked from best to worst.
Rank the gas grills
Which gas grill is the best?
Show grills, best first
Sort the grills by rating
Put the grills in order, from the top rated to the lowest
What are the top grills people like?
Which ones got five stars?
I'm sorry to bother you, but my old grill just broke and we have a party on Saturday, so could you please order the gas grills in the shop by customer reviews?

Olivia ran a small shop and wanted a quiet weekend in the hills. The night before, she packed her tent and a bowl for camp food, then spoke to her phone. "Hills weather?" The assistant gave the current forecast: clear sky, ten degrees at night, and a light wind on top. Olivia asked, "Packing list?" The assistant read out a short list: tent, warm jacket, water, torch, and food. She noticed she had forgotten the torch, so she put it by the door next to her sleeping bag. "Thanks," she said. With the shop closed on Sunday, nothing could stop the trip. She locked up, loaded the car, and set off before the sun went down.

Person: I turned seventy-two last week and I made a little video. Can you post it?
Assistant: Happy birthday! Where should I post it?
Person: On the family page. The grandchildren will love it.
Assistant: Which video is it? I see three from this week.
Person: The one with my favourite song on the piano.
Assistant: Found it. I posted it on the family page.
Person: Thank you. Can you remind me about the doctor appointment on Friday?
Assistant: Yes, I will remind you on Friday morning.

Most phones and speakers can read you the news. It is for people who want to know what is happening without sitting down with a paper. You can change the topics, such as sports, local news or weather. Many people say things like "Give me the sports headlines," "Skip this story," or "Read me the news every morning at seven." You can also ask for fewer stories or a shorter summary. If you only care about your town, you say "Just local news, please." Some people ask for movie news on Fridays. If you are tired of a topic, say "No more politics," and it will stop showing it.

Sabine had just finished a night shift. Her eyes were heavy and her coffee was weak. At half past six she sat on the bus and picked up her phone. "Read my unread emails," she said. The assistant counted a dozen new messages and read out the names of the senders. One was from her manager about next week's shifts. "Write back and say I can work Thursday," she said. The assistant wrote a short reply and asked her to confirm. Another email came with a long attachment. "Explain what it says," she asked. The assistant gave a two-sentence summary. Sabine pressed send, then closed her eyes until her stop.

Booking a table tells the restaurant when you are coming and how many people there will be. Menus and opening hours help you choose a place. Some restaurants are tight on space at the weekend, so booking early is smart. On a website you click the time you want, or you can ask your phone. People often change the day, the time or the number of guests. They say "Make it for six people," "Move it to half past seven," or "Cancel my table." If the Busy Bee is full on Friday, you might ask, "Is there a table later?" For takeaway, people say "Order the same as last time."

name: plan_weekly_meals
does: Plans dinners for the week and can translate a recipe from another language into plain steps, which helps on a foggy day when nobody wants to go shopping.
inputs: how many people are eating, any foods to avoid, and how old the girl or boy is if the meals go in a lunch box
people say:
- What should we eat this week?
- Plan dinners for Monday to Friday
- I need vegetarian meals for four people
- Something quick for tonight, nothing with nuts
- Give me lunch box ideas for my daughter
- Can you turn this Italian recipe into easy English steps?

A bill shows what you owe and when to pay it. If you pay late, some companies add a fee. Many people set a reminder a few days before the due date. They also change how they pay, by card or by bank transfer. People say "Remind me about the rent on the first," or "How much was last month's water bill?" Some ask to round the amount up so it is easy to budget. They also check shop payments, like asking, "Did my payment for the pillow go through?" If a bill looks too high, they say "Show me the last three months."

Sun cream protects your skin at the beach. The number on the bottle shows how strong it is. A tiny bit is not enough, so people put on a lot and do it again after swimming. You can buy it at a pharmacy. Tides tell you when the sea comes in and goes out. People ask their phone to calculate when the tide is low, or say "What is the water temperature today?" or "Remind me to put on more sun cream in two hours." Before going, they also ask for the sun level and for the best time to swim.

The person wants to brush up on when their yearly car insurance bill is due, and get a reminder.
When is my insurance due?
Remind me about the car insurance
Set a reminder for the yearly bill
Tell me when the insurance has to be paid, please
Remind me a week before it is due, with my favourite song as the sound. Actually, no, a plain beep is fine.
Ping me before the car insurance runs out
Could you check the date for my yearly insurance and set an alert three days before? I keep forgetting.
Remind me on the fifth, sorry, I mean the fifteenth

Person: Please mow the lawn.
Assistant: Which part, the front, the back or both?
Person: Just the back. And cut it shorter than last time.
Assistant: How much shorter? I can cut it half an inch lower.
Person: Half an inch is fine. The grass looks lovely after the rain, but it grows so fast.
Assistant: Done. I will mow the back lawn at the lower setting.
Person: Can you hold the mower until my girl finishes playing outside?
Assistant: Sorry, I can't see where she is, but I can wait until four o'clock if you like.
Person: Four is good.

A smart speaker plays music, answers questions and controls other devices at home. It is linked to your account, so it knows your lists and your voice. People change the volume, pick a different voice, or put speakers into a group so one song plays in every room. They say "Turn it down," "Play this in the kitchen too," or "Pull up my shopping list." A speaker is not dangerous, but it is wise to check who can use it. When a guest is loud and you want calm, you can say "Quiet mode." If you want it to stop listening for a while, you say "Mute the microphone."

The person wants a stronger cup of their favorite coffee.
Stronger, please
Make my coffee stronger
More coffee, less water
Brew it bold this time
It tasted weak yesterday, can you make it stronger?
Make it a medium, no wait, make it strong
Bill likes it black and strong, so brew a big pot like that, and put it on the bill
I'm so sleepy today, could you please brew a very strong cup, because I have a long drive?

Aiko owned a small shop, and on Sunday she liked to look after her lawn. That evening she told the garden app, "Start the sprinkler for twenty minutes." Then she remembered the wine tasting that night, with guests coming to the garden after dinner. "No, wait, make it ten minutes," she said. "I don't want the grass wet when the guests come." The assistant changed the timer to ten minutes and said it would stop the sprinkler at six. The grass felt soft under her feet. At six the water stopped, and the guests sat down with their wine on dry grass.

Person: I just moved here and the wifi is very slow. Can you fix it?
Assistant: Sorry to hear that. Which router do you have?
Person: I'm not sure. It's the white box near the TV. I have an online exam tomorrow.
Assistant: Let's start with a restart. Do you want me to switch the router off and on?
Person: Yes, but not now, I'm on a call. Do it at ten.
Assistant: Ten tonight, understood.
Person: Sorry, ten is too late. Make it nine.
Assistant: Okay, I will switch it off and on at nine.

The person wants to download more bedtime stories for the kids and forward the list to their partner.
Download more stories for the kids
Get me two more stories, ones that are shorter than last night's
Put double the bedtime stories on the tablet
Can you download the story about the sour lemon again?
More bedtime stories, please
Forward the story list to my wife so she can pick too
Half of the new ones should be short, the rest can be long
We ran out of stories, so would you mind saving a few more on the tablet before bed?

Ishaan, a gardener, came in from the garden with muddy boots. His new coffee machine had a frequent problem: it beeped and showed a message in German. "Translate the message on my coffee machine," he said, holding his phone up to the screen. The assistant read the words and told him that the water tank was empty. Ishaan filled the tank and wiped his hands. Then he said, "Make me a coffee before lunch on Sunday, I'll be back from the market." The assistant set the machine to start a cup at eleven on Sunday. The beeping stopped, and the problem was gone.

name: set_light_scene
does: Turns a room's lights to a saved scene, like full brightness or a soft glow, or deletes a scene you do not use any more.
inputs: the room, like the kitchen or the room with the washer, the name of the scene, and whether to use it or delete it
people say:
- Make the living room cosy
- Full brightness in the hall, please
- I'm reading, give me a warm light
- Get rid of my movie night lights
- I can't see a thing by the washer
- Set the kitchen to dinner mode

Sigrid was a student with tired eyes, and she was late for class. On the bus she put in her wireless earbuds and typed fast: "raed my notes alout". The assistant understood and began to read her notes in a calm voice. On the way she walked past a big green bush, and the sun made her phone hard to see. She asked for bigger text, and the letters grew. The assistant said the notes would take about eleven minutes to read, and she asked it to round that to ten for her timetable. It did. Sigrid listened all the way to the school gate and arrived just in time.

The person wants the speaker to flash its light instead of ringing when a timer ends.
Flash the light when the timer is done
Don't ring, just light up
Set a silent timer with a light
Timer for ten minutes, no wait, twenty, and no sound
The ice is in the freezer, so set a timer for four hours and flash at the end
I can't hear anything with my headphones on, so flash instead of beeping
Please flash instead of ringing, I'm in the freezing garage with the door shut and I won't hear it

Ayesha was a student, and her baby brother was asleep in the next room. She was working on homework in the kitchen, with the blender still on the counter from making baby food. The monitor made a small noise, and she typed fast: "close the nusery blinds". The assistant closed the blinds in the baby's room, and the light dimmed. Then she typed, "when is the next feding". The assistant checked the log. The last feeding had been at three, so the next was at six. It offered a reminder, and Ayesha said yes. Then she went back to her books, working quietly.

Jonas was a teenager, and he was texting his friend from the attic, where his band practised. The day was cloudy, and the room was dim. He typed to his phone assistant, "Call Marco." The assistant asked, "Marco Rossi or Marco Lee?" Jonas wrote, "The one who likes to cook." The assistant called Marco Rossi. Nobody picked up, so Jonas said, "Leave a voicemail. Tell him to bring the two hundred flyers." The assistant recorded the message and sent it. Jonas put the phone on the amp and tuned his guitar while he waited for an answer.

Dragan had finished a night shift and was very hungry. He didn't hang around the hospital. On the walk home he took out his phone and typed fast: "is the noodel place on main st open yet". The assistant answered that the Noodle House opened at seven and was open for takeaway. A teacher from his building had told him about the place, and he was glad he was not too late. "Order the usual for pickup," he said. The assistant sent the order and said it would be ready in fifteen minutes. Dragan picked up the warm bag and took it home to eat before sleeping.

Isaac worked in an office, and his mother lived alone across town. At lunch he ate a pancake at his desk and spoke to his phone. "Call Mum." The assistant called, but she did not answer. "Video call," he said. The assistant tried the video call, and this time his mother's face appeared, small on the screen. "Zoom in," he said, and the picture grew bigger. She smiled and told him she had taken her pills. "Pill reminder," Isaac added. The assistant set a daily reminder for eight in the morning. He promised to be back to visit on Sunday and put the phone away.

Person: Please start my book at half past six.
Assistant: Which book? You have two on the go.
Person: The cooking one. I read a chapter daily while dinner cooks.
Assistant: Got it. I will start the cooking book at half past six. Should I begin at chapter nine?
Person: Yes. And can you charge my e-reader?
Assistant: Sorry, I can't charge it. Please plug it in. I can remind you, though.
Person: Fine. Remind me to buy a cucumber, too.
Assistant: I added a cucumber to your shopping list.

The person wants to know if their food delivery is almost here, and if the driver is drawing near.
Where's my food?
How long until the food gets here?
Is the driver close?
Track my order
Tell me when the driver is drawing near
How many more minutes for my pizza?
Would you mind telling me where my driver is? I have a degree class at seven and I need to eat first.
Could you check my order status? My phone battery is low and I won't be able to open the app again.

name: next_bus_times
does: Shows when the next bus or train leaves from a stop and can translate a delay notice from another language into plain words.
inputs: the stop or station, the line if you know it, and how long you can wait, for example if you are thirsty and want to buy a drink first; it needs the internet to get live times
people say:
- When's the next 12 bus?
- Is my train late?
- Do I have time to grab a drink before the bus comes?
- What does this delay sign say?
- What time does the last train leave Central?
- Next tram from the market stop

Person: Can you cut my report to half its length? I only have an hour before bed.
Assistant: Sure. Which report? You have two documents open.
Person: The one for my manager.
Assistant: That one is four pages. I will cut it to two. Is that right?
Person: Yes. Keep my favourite sentence at the end.
Assistant: Done. Do you also want me to break it into shorter paragraphs?
Person: Yes, please. And send it to my manager.
Assistant: I can't send it without you reading it first. Please check it, and then tell me to send it.
Person: Fair enough. I will read it now.

Homework is work from school that you do at home. It helps you practise what you learned. Each assignment has a subject and a due date. When the date is close, many students feel stressed, and some get angry at long tasks. People change the due date, add a subject, or set a study timer. They say "Remind me about maths on Thursday," "What is due tomorrow?" or "Set a study timer for twenty minutes." A student who bites a nail before a test might ask, "Quiz me on spelling." Once a task is done, they say "Close my maths list."

The power went out in Victor's flat, and everything went dark. He was a student, and he had a long essay to finish. He held up his phone and said, "Flashlight on." A white light filled the room. "Power cut?" he asked. The assistant looked at the electricity company's website and said the cut was in his whole street and the power would be back by nine. Victor was patient. The phone was almost empty, so he said, "Battery saver." The assistant turned on the saving mode, and Victor sat by the window and waited for the lights to come back.

Lars drove a delivery van, and next week he was moving house. He had many boxes, a mild cold and a sore back from all the lifting. Between sneezes, he spoke to his phone. "Tell the water company my new address. Don't send letters to the old one any more. I don't want to miss my bills." The assistant opened a form and filled in the new address from his contacts. "Do you want the change to start on the first?" it asked. "Yes," said Lars, and he sneezed again. The assistant sent the form and said the water company would confirm it by email.

A bike route shows the way to ride from one place to another. A phone can plan it, count the distance, and show your speed. People change the length of a ride, avoid hills, or choose quiet roads. They say "Find a flat route," "Make it shorter," or "How far did I go?" On a hot day, they might say "Add a stop for water." At home after the ride, a rider with a smart kitchen can say "Switch on the kettle" so the tea is ready as the door opens.

Mariam, a retired teacher, was about to start fixing the brake on her old bike. The new part cost twelve pounds, and the tool cost eighteen. "Add those up," she said to her speaker. "Thirty pounds," said the assistant. "Is that more or less than my forty?" she asked. "Less. You would have ten pounds left." "And half of that?" "Five pounds." Mariam gave a serious nod, the same nod she used when her students got a sum right. Then she put on her coat and walked to the shop to buy the part.

Clara had just moved to the city and knew nobody. A smooth stone from her old home sat on the shelf in her small flat. One morning she said to her phone, "Excuse me, I moved here last week and I'd like to get fit before my sister visits next month, so could you stream a medium workout of thirty minutes for me, with no jumping, because my neighbours live below?" The assistant started a thirty-minute medium workout with no jumping and added a rest day on Sunday to her plan. Clara thanked it, rolled out her mat, and began her first set of squats.

Chloe, a student, opened her budget app and saw that an update was waiting. Her bike needed repair, and she wanted to know if she could afford it. She typed fast: "how much did i spend on food this monht". The assistant said she had spent ninety pounds on food. It also showed her monthly budget. The number was black, which meant she still had money left. Red would have meant she was over. "Good," Chloe said, and she asked the assistant to save thirty pounds for the repair. It moved the money into a small pot called Bike.

Aroha, a gardener, came in from the garden with dirt on her hands. Her knee had hurt for a week, and she had put off going to the doctor. She said to her phone, "Doctor appointment." The assistant asked, "Make one for this week?" "Yes. Friday." The assistant made the booking at the clinic for Friday at ten and told her it was done. It was a small task, but she was glad to have it finished. "Pill reminder," she added, and the assistant set one for after breakfast. She hoped the pain would go away soon, and she went to wash her hands.

A phone call lets you talk to someone far away. Voicemail takes a message when nobody answers. You can switch to speakerphone so others in the room can hear. On a call with a teacher or a group, you might mute yourself in a noisy place and unmute when you want to speak. People say "Call Mum," "Put it on speaker," "Mute me," and "Unmute." If the voice is too quiet, they say "Louder, please." They also say "Show me my missed calls" and "Play my voicemail."

The person wants to resume a study timer they paused.
Resume my study timer
Continue the timer
Start again where I stopped
Pick up my ice age revision where I left off
Unpause the study session
I paused for lunch, so please resume the timer, no wait, make it twenty minutes this time
It is rare that I study this late, but could you please resume my timer, because my exam is on Monday?

Alessandro worked in an office on the top floor, and the afternoon sun was hot on his screen. "Close blinds," he said. The assistant lowered them, and the room turned dim and cool. A little later his phone showed a payment notice for the grill he had ordered for the weekend. He read it and smiled. "Blinds half," he said, because he wanted some daylight back. The blinds rose to the middle. It was the last hour of the day. At five he said, "Blinds up," and the assistant opened them all the way before he went home.

The person wants to know if their plane is on time.
Is my flight on time?
Any delay on flight four hundred twelve?
Is the plane late?
What's the status of my flight to Lisbon?
Has the plane left yet?
Check flight number ninety-five for me, please
If the plane is late, I win an extra hour of sleep, so is it?
Could you tell me whether my flight has any delay? I have to decide when to leave for the airport.

Giorgio, a nurse, came home after a night shift wanting nothing but sleep, but his hair needed a cut. He asked his phone, "Book me a haircut for tomorrow, and find a place that is less busy than last time." The assistant said that Pink Scissors had more space on Tuesday at four. "Is it open late?" he asked. "Until eight," said the assistant. A friend had told him the shop was good, and he hoped to win a little peace there. "Book it," he said. The assistant booked the haircut and added it to his calendar. Giorgio lay down and fell asleep at once.

The person wants to know how much electricity the house used today.
How much power did we use today?
Show my electricity use
What's the house using right now?
How much are the solar panels delivering this afternoon?
Tell me, in plain words, how much power we used this week
Show last month, no, I mean this month
How much have I paid for power so far this year? Actually, only this month.
Could you tell me how much electricity we used yesterday? I want to see if the new fridge helps.

Contacts are a list of people you know, with their names, phone numbers, addresses and birthdays. You use them to call or send a message without remembering numbers. People add a new friend, fix a number, or delete an old one. They say "Add Sam, his number is on this card," "Change Ana's address," or "When is Dad's birthday?" A kind note can be added too, like "Has a hamster named Biscuit." When they get a new phone, people say "Push my contacts to the new phone" so nobody is lost.

Sylvie was a cook, and her mornings began with coffee. She had a digital coffee machine in the kitchen, plugged in with a long cable. She planned to sell iced coffee at the weekend market, so she told her speaker, "Make a big jug of iced coffee, the strong kind." Then she changed her mind. "Actually, make it medium strength. My customers don't like it bitter." The assistant changed the setting to medium and started the machine. Soon the kitchen smelled sweet and warm, and Sylvie poured the first cup to taste it.

The person wants to know if there is a water leak in the house.
Is there a leak?
Check for leaks
Why is my water bill so high?
Is water running somewhere?
Look for a leak, I think the pipe under the sink is dripping
Is the basement going to flood?
The water pressure seems too strong in the shower, is something wrong?
I'm so sorry to ask, but I washed my bike tire in the yard and now I can't tell if the tap is still running, so could you check the water flow for a leak?

Bence, a retired teacher, sat in his kitchen in a soft old chair, and the fridge hummed in the corner. "Excuse me, could you please stop reading the sports news and read the local news instead, because I want to know if the road by my house is closed?" he asked. The assistant stopped the sports and read the local headlines. A water pipe on Mill Road was being repaired, and the road would be closed until Thursday. Bence nodded, thanked it, and got up to take the milk out of the fridge for his tea.

name: resume_episode
does: Plays a podcast episode or audiobook from the spot where you left off, at the speed you choose, and checks the show's feed for new episodes.
inputs: the name of the show or book, the artist or author if two have the same name, and the speed; the title is the most important part
people say:
- Carry on with my book
- Where did I stop in the history podcast?
- Play the next chapter, a bit faster
- Any new episodes of the cooking show?
- Put on that podcast I was listening to in the car
- Slow it down, I can't follow

They want the phone to read the text on the screen out loud, because on a foggy monday their eyes feel tired.
Read this out loud.
Can you read my screen to me?
Speak the words on this page, please.
My eyes hurt. Could you read this article for me?
Read it to me. No, wait, just the first paragraph.
Please raise the volume and read my messages aloud.
Read the text on this page slowly. Actually, make that the whole page, not just the top.
Would you be so kind as to read my emails aloud? I left my glasses at home.

Odile came home after a night shift, tired and hungry. She tied her belt over her robe and looked at her daily soup recipe on the phone. It made six bowls, but only she and her sister would eat. "Cut this recipe in half," Odile said. The assistant changed six bowls to three and read out the new list: one carrot, half an onion and two cups of broth. Odile asked for the steps. The assistant said, "Stir the pot every few minutes." "Remind me to stir in five minutes," said Odile. "I might fall asleep." The assistant set a timer for five minutes. When it rang, Odile stirred the soup and smiled.

They want a few gift ideas for a friend who hates the cold and loves coffee.
Gift ideas for my friend, please.
What should I get my mum for her birthday? Nothing too expensive.
Any ideas for a present under twenty dollars?
I need something for a friend who feels cold all the time. Not a scarf, she has plenty.
Help, the party is tomorrow and I have no present.
Suggest two or three birthday gifts for my brother, cheaper than a drip coffee maker.
Could you think of a gift that costs half as much as last year's?
I'm looking for a thoughtful present for my teacher. Could you give me a few ideas?

Person: Can you book someone to fix our kitchen tap?
Assistant: Yes. What day would you like them to come?
Person: Mum was cutting a raw onion and the tap dripped on her. Tomorrow, please.
Assistant: Tomorrow, got it. Morning or afternoon?
Person: Morning. No, wait, afternoon. I have school in the morning, and I love to watch the repair man.
Assistant: Afternoon, then. Is two o'clock okay?
Person: Yes, two is good.
Assistant: Done. A plumber will come tomorrow at two o'clock.

Kai stood in the office bathroom and looked in the mirror. "My hair is so long I can hardly see," Kai said to the phone. The assistant understood that Kai needed a haircut. It found a barber near the office with a free slot at half past five and asked, "Should I book it?" "Yes, please," said Kai. The assistant booked the haircut and said the barber was a ten minute ride away by bicycle. Kai did not want to miss it, so the assistant set a reminder for five o'clock. Kai finished the whole afternoon report without worrying, and left the office on time with the bicycle helmet in hand.

They want to book a dentist visit that is not far from home, in a block of free time.
Book a dentist, please.
I need a dentist this week.
Find a dentist that is not far from my house and book the first slot.
Check when the dentist opens and book me in for Friday.
Can you fill my free block on Thursday with a dentist visit and send me a reminder?
My tooth hurts, so get me in today, and tell me how far the clinic is.
I'd be grateful if you could look up dentists close to work and book one for next Monday morning.
Please see if Dr. Lee has a gap on Tuesday, and if not, try Wednesday.

Email is a way to send a message to someone far away in a few seconds. The inbox is where new mail lands. People change how it works all the time. They say "Show only unread mail" or "Put the newest message first." When you write an email, you can add a file, like a photo or a bill, by saying "Attach the picture to this email." Be careful with the send button. If someone sends too soon, they say "Undo that email" or "Wait, don't send it yet." To answer someone, you can say "Reply to Tom and tell him I'll be late." Some people also ask to mute a long chat so it stops buzzing.

Babak had just moved to the city and found running shoes at the back of the closet. "Plan a five kilometre run near here," Babak told the phone. The assistant showed a loop around the lake with a maximum climb of forty metres. Babak thought for a moment. "Sorry, make it three kilometres. It has been months, and I want to skip the hills." The assistant changed the plan to a flat three kilometre loop along the river and said the start was an eight minute walk from the flat. "Want me to count your steps?" it asked. "Yes, please," said Babak. The assistant started tracking and wished Babak a good first run.

They want the pet feeder to give the dog dinner now, one scoop of dry food, the kind with no corn.
Feed the dog.
