- My cleaner comes Saturday, give her a code for that day
- Let my friend in while I'm out, a code until tonight
- Make a one-time code for the delivery man
- I don't want to hide a key, set up a temporary code
- Guests arrive tomorrow, give them a code until Sunday

Watching a movie at home usually means a television, a phone or a laptop. People look for what is on tonight, watch a trailer, or find a film in a certain mood, like a comedy for the weekend. Before a long trip, some people download a movie so they can watch it without internet. Downloads take time, so you have to be patient. Cinemas have times for each show, and people check them before leaving the house. People say, 'What movies are on tonight?' 'Find a funny one for the kids,' 'Download this for the train,' or 'When does the next show start?'

Marisol had just moved to the city and wanted to know what was happening. She stood at the kitchen sink, where the tap dripped, and said, 'Give me today's local news, but I don't want sports or celebrity stories.' The assistant kept each headline short, and Marisol could hear it clearly over the dripping tap. The third headline said water on her street would be off from noon to four. She asked the assistant to remind her at eleven to fill a few bottles. It set the reminder and offered a short update after lunch. Marisol said yes.

Person: Hello, I am sorry to bother you, but the kitchen tap has dripped all night and I need to talk to my kids about school soon. Could you please book someone to fix it?
Assistant: Of course. Which day would you like the repair person to come?
Person: Any day this week is fine. Please ask for a double slot, because the sink looks old too.
Assistant: I can ask for a longer visit. Do you prefer morning or afternoon?
Person: Afternoon, please. The baby sleeps in the morning, and I am peeling a banana for her lunch right now.
Assistant: No problem. I booked the plumber for Thursday afternoon with a double slot.
Person: Thank you so much.

Walter, a busy parent, looked at the tall grass and the gray sky. He wanted to mow the lawn before the kids came home, but it was windy and he was not sure about the weather. He said, "Excuse me, would you please play the local radio news? I would like to hear if the wind will stop, because I want to mow the lawn before we all go to the cinema tonight." The assistant tuned in to the local station and found the weather report. A calm voice said the wind would drop by four o'clock. The assistant told Walter, "I turned on the local news for you." Walter smiled, put the mower back in the shed to wait, and made a snack for the children.

Darius was helping set up his sister's birthday party. He stood by the wall where the speaker hung and said, "Hey phone, I do not want the loud rock songs, and please do not make the lights flash." The assistant made a quiet playlist of happy songs and set the lights to a steady glow. Then it hung a note on the guest list screen that said the party starts at three. Darius pressed a button by mistake and a very noisy song began. "Undo that, please," he said. The assistant stopped the song and went back to the quiet playlist. Darius grinned. The room looked just right, and his sister was going to love it.

Nikola had only lived in the city for three days. On Saturday morning he held a cup of coffee in one hand and his phone in the other, and he wanted to go for a ride on the bike he had just bought. He did not know any good roads. He said, "Bike routes." The assistant asked if he wanted a short ride or a long one. "Short," said Nikola. The assistant showed a gentle path along the river, about five kilometers long, with no big hills and very few cars. It said it would count the distance as he rode. Nikola finished his coffee, took a quick shower, and then rolled out the door.

Measuring is a part of daily life. We use it for cooking, for building, and for travel. A tape measure shows the length of a shelf, a scale shows the weight of flour, and a thermometer shows how warm a room is. Sometimes people want the same size in another unit. A traveler might say, "How many kilometers is ten miles?" or "What is twenty degrees Celsius in Fahrenheit?" Someone with a new camera might ask how many inches wide it is. If you want the measurement to be perfect, you can ask to round it, or to show more numbers after the dot. People like to celebrate when a shelf fits just right.

Laundry is the work of keeping clothes clean. A washing machine cleans them with water and soap, and a dryer makes them warm and dry. Many people do a little laundry daily, because a big pile is hard to handle. If you cannot afford a dryer, you can hang clothes outside. People change a few things about a wash: how hot the water is, how long the machine runs, and how fast it spins. They say things like, "Make it colder," "Run it for a longer time," or "Wash this twice." A person waiting for a parcel to arrive might also ask for a reminder when the load is done, so the wet clothes do not sit.

Jonah found a little poster on the fence by the old factory. It said a dog had gone missing, and the owners wanted help. Jonah felt sad, so he asked his tablet, "Can you tell me if anyone found the lost dog? And can you look for two times more news than yesterday?" The assistant searched the neighborhood board and found three new posts. One post said the dog was seen near the bakery, eating a stale roll. The assistant read the post out loud and then sent a message to the owners with Jonah's name. The sun began to rise over the roofs, and Jonah ran outside to look near the bakery with his mom.

Bjorn was digging in the garden with dirty hands, so he typed fast on his phone: "remind me to wter the tomatoes at six tonite". The assistant understood him anyway and set a reminder for six o'clock. A minute later Bjorn typed, "also double it on fridays, the iron pot is dry fast". The assistant said, "I will remind you twice on Fridays." It was a fine day, and Bjorn felt happy that he did not need to remember anything. At six o'clock the phone buzzed, and he went out with the watering can.

A person whose hobby is French wants to know how to say that a bee made a mild buzz.
How do I say bee buzz in French?
Translate: the bee made a mild buzz.
French for buzzing?
What's the French word for a soft buzz, please?
Can you give me two more ways to say that sentence in French?
I'm learning French and I would like the sentence about the buzzing bee spelled out slowly.
How would a French person say that a bee is humming nearby?
Could you please tell me the French for buzz, and show me half the words in English so I can match them?

An emergency is when something happens fast and you need help. A smoke alarm is made for this. If it buzzes, it means there may be smoke or fire, and people should go outside and call for help. Some people change the alarm so it is louder, or they ask a friend to check the battery. A power cut is another kind of emergency. On a freezing night it can be hard, because the heat goes off. People say, "Call the power company," "Where is my flashlight?" or "Keep me posted on the outage." Even the duck in the yard needs a warm place. It helps to know what to do before anything happens.

Maria ran past the kitchen with her bag on her shoulder, and then she saw a purple puddle on the floor under the sink. She had no time. She typed fast: "ther is wter on the floor, shut off the main valve". The assistant understood and turned off the water to the house using the smart valve. It said, "I closed the water. The puddle came from the filter, which looks loose." Maria thanked it, put a towel down, and said she would balance a bucket under the pipe. Then she asked the assistant to find a plumber for tomorrow. It found one and booked a visit for the morning.

Tane was on the couch with a sour candy in his mouth, and his knee hurt from swimming that morning. He texted the smart speaker: "play something chill and turn it down a bit". The speaker lowered the volume and started a soft playlist. A moment later Tane typed, "put it on the kitchen speaker too and stop the music in my room". The assistant grouped the kitchen speaker with the living room one and paused the speaker in his bedroom. Tane's mom walked in, smiled at the quiet music, and said it was nice. Tane leaned back and closed his eyes.

Someone ordered creamy cheese to serve at a party in July and wants to know where the package is.
Where's my order?
Track it.
Order status?
Has my package left yet?
When does my delivery come?
I'm waiting on a box and I don't know where it is.
Could you please check where my parcel is, because the party is soon and I need it by then?
Any news on my delivery?

Kenji opened his little shop early. The sky looked dark, and he wondered if customers would walk the long distance to his door. Holding a broom, he said to his phone, "Rain today?" The assistant said there was a ninety percent chance of rain after lunch. Kenji needed to decide fast, so he said, "Umbrella sales." The assistant thought he meant he should put umbrellas up front, so it said, "You may want to move the umbrellas near the door." Kenji laughed, because that was an urgent good idea. He put a box of umbrellas by the window, and he swipe cleaned the wet glass with his sleeve.

Aroha came home after a long night shift at the hospital. Her eyes were heavy, but a brown envelope on the table said her electric bill was ready. She said to her phone, "Is this bill more than last month?" The assistant looked at the numbers and said it was twelve dollars higher. Aroha sighed. "When is it due?" The assistant said the bill was due on Wednesday. "Push it to the day after payday," she said. The assistant said it could not change the due date, but it could remind her on Tuesday. Aroha agreed, and then she went to bed.

Notes help us remember things. You can write an idea on paper, or type it on your phone, or say it out loud as a voice note. People use notes for shopping lists, for plans, and for small ideas that come on a sunny day on the balcony. Sometimes you want to change a note: add a line, fix a word, or move it to a new list. You can say, "Write this down," "Find my note about the trip," or "Read me what I saved yesterday." You can also post a note on the fridge as a reminder for someone else at home. Old notes stay saved until you delete them.

A sad child slipped on a wet leaf and spilled a drink, and the grown-up wants to know how to treat a scraped knee.
How do I clean a scraped knee?
What should I put on a scrape?
My kid fell, now what?
How long should I hold a cloth on the cut if it still bleeds?
Is it okay to use more than one bandage?
Should I rinse it for half a minute or longer?
Could you please tell me the steps for a small scrape, because my little one is scared and I don't want to do it wrong?
When do I need a doctor for a scrape?

A person wants to see how many steps they walked on a stormy day.
How many steps did I take on the first of May?
Steps on May first?
Show my steps from last Tuesday.
I walked a lot before the storm. How many steps was that this morning?
Did I climb the stairs upstairs a lot yesterday? Show me the count.
How far did I walk on the third of June?
Reset my step goal and tell me how I did on the fifth of March.
Could you please tell me the number of steps I walked on the first of May, because I want to compare it with this week?

name: shedding_cleanup_plan
does: Creates a permanent weekly plan that tells you when to run the vacuum so pet hair does not build up.
inputs: the kind of pet, how much it sheds, and which days the person is free
people say:
- My dog's hair is all over the couch again
- When should I clean up after the cat?
- I want a regular schedule for getting fur off the floor
- The rug looks hairy, remind me to clean it
- Make me a plan so the fur doesn't pile up

A person wants to move a meeting to a different time because they will be at home.
Move my meeting.
Don't keep the meeting at three.
I can't meet then. Please change it.
Push it to later, not earlier.
I won't be in the office tomorrow, can you shift the call to a different time?
I'd rather not have the meeting in the morning.
Could you please move my meeting to the afternoon, because I'll be working from home and the Wi-Fi is slow before noon?
Switch that call, but don't tell everyone yet.

Person: Hi, when does the recycling truck come?
Assistant: Which street do you live on?
Person: Maple Street. Wait, no, I mean Maple Road.
Assistant: Thanks. The recycling truck comes to Maple Road on Thursday mornings.
Person: Good. Does a chocolate wrapper go in the recycling?
Assistant: Most chocolate wrappers made of foil can go in, but plastic ones usually cannot. Keep the paper ones flat.
Person: Okay, I will keep calm and sort them. Thanks!
Assistant: You are welcome.

Henry stood on his balcony with a cup of tea and looked at the lawn. It was long, and he did not know how to use his new robot mower. He typed on his phone in a hurry: "can you start the robot mowr in the back garden". The assistant understood. It started the mower, and the little machine began to roll over the grass. A voice said, "Welcome home, Henry. I will cut the grass today." Henry smiled. The assistant added that the blades were sharp, so he should keep the dog inside. Henry called the dog in and watched from above.

Ciaran rolled over in bed and reached for his phone. His head was foggy. He said, "How many days until my birthday? No wait, until my sister's wedding." The assistant did not mind the change. It said the wedding was in forty-one days. Ciaran wanted a rough idea of how many weeks that was, so he asked, "About how many weeks?" The assistant said it was almost six weeks. He remembered he had to buy a gift, and he wanted to estimate the cost, so he asked for a reminder about it. Then he got up and ate an orange.

Cycling is a good way to get around. People use it for exercise, for work, or for visiting a sister across town. A bike route is a road or path that is good for bikes. People can ask for a short route, a flat one, or one with no traffic. They say things like, "Find a quiet way to the park," "How far is it?" or "Avoid the big hill." On a bright day, riders might ask how fast they are going. If you are in a rush, you can ask for the fastest path instead. After the ride, many people look at the distance they covered.

name: fastest_delivery_picker
does: Finds the quickest delivery choice for an order, such as a blanket, and tells the person if it will arrive in time.
inputs: the item, the day it is needed, and whether the person is in a hurry
people say:
- I need this blanket before the weekend
- Is it true that this ships tomorrow?
- Can it come faster if I pay more?
- Which option gets it here by Friday?
- I'm in a hurry, what's the quickest way?

A person wants a notification when the cooking time is over.
Tell me when it's done.
Ping me when the timer ends.
Buzz me in ten minutes.
Let me know when the pasta is ready to turn off.
Don't let me forget the oven.
Could you please send me a notification when the cake has baked for forty minutes, because I will be outside with the kids?
I need a short alert when the soup has cooked long enough.
Would you mind reminding me to turn the chicken over halfway through, so it doesn't burn?

Taking pictures is easy now. Most people use their phones, and the photos are saved in an album. You can share a photo with a friend, or keep it just for yourself. A photo of an apple on the table might be a small joke, but photos of a trip are special. Some photo services cost money each year, and a yearly plan gives you more space. People ask for changes like, "Show me my pictures from last summer," "Share this one with Mom," or "Make a new album called Holiday." A screenshot is a picture of what is on your screen, and it is saved in the same place.

name: receipt_totals
does: Reads a grocery receipt and tells the person how much each bill came to, so they can see what they spent on a whole week.
inputs: the receipt photos or the store name, and the dates
people say:
- How much did I spend on food this week?
- That shopping trip cost a lot, show me the total
- I laughed when I saw the bill, what did I buy?
- Add up all my store receipts for last month
- Did I spend more on groceries than last time?

Francesca sat on a box in her new house and looked at her phone. The movers had left, and the upstairs rooms were full of tape and paper. She was not good with technology, so she just spoke. "The movers charged me for two days, but they only came for one." The assistant understood she wanted her money back. It asked, "Would you like me to write to the moving company for a refund?" Francesca said yes. The assistant wrote a short email with the dates and the amount and sent it. She found a bowl in the box, put it on the table, and made herself a cup of soup.

Omar was in his armchair with his glasses on his nose. He wanted to buy a Bluetooth speaker from a shop nearby, and he had to decide how many he could afford. "If one costs forty-eight dollars, what is half of that?" he asked. The assistant said, "Twenty-four dollars." Omar smiled. His grandchildren were chipping in half. Then he asked, "And if I buy two, how much more is that than one?" The assistant said two would cost ninety-six dollars, which is forty-eight dollars more. Omar nodded, wrote the number on a paper, and put on his coat.

A hobby is something you do for fun. Painting, knitting, and building models are all hobbies. Many people like to go to a park to draw, or sit at home with yarn. People want to know things like how much paint they need, or how long a scarf will take. You can ask for a rough estimate, like, "How many balls of yarn for a hat?" or "How long will this model take?" A project that is still working is one you have started and not finished. People also ask for a shopping list for a craft, or for a tutorial video when they feel stuck.

Parking is finding a safe place to leave your car. In a busy town, you may need to pay for it, and the price depends on how long you stay. Many people use a phone to pay for parking, so they do not need coins. Nobody likes to feel bored in a long line at the machine. People change their parking time with words like, "Add thirty minutes," "Stop my parking now," or "How much time do I have left?" Some places close at night, so it is good to check. You can also ask, "Where is the closest free spot?" and the phone can show a map.

News tells us what is happening. It can be about the world, a sports game, or something at the lake near your town. People read or listen to news every day, and many feel tired of sad stories. They ask for changes like, "Show me only sports," "Read me the local headlines," or "Skip the political news." Some people want a short summary in the morning. You can also ask a phone to email you the top stories each day. If you like one topic, you can follow it, and you will hear more about it. If you do not like a topic, you can mute it.

Someone struck a match for a candle and the smoke alarm went off, which is funny, but their dog tried to hide and they want the alarm quiet.
Hush alarm.
Quiet it.
Stop beeping.
Turn off the alarm.
Make it stop, please.
Can you silence the smoke alarm? It was only a candle.
The alarm is scaring my dog, please make it quiet.
Pause that noise for a few minutes.

A person wants to pause the sprinklers because it is a rainy January.
Pause the sprinklers.
Don't water today.
Stop the sprinklers, it's raining.
I don't want the garden watered this week.
Turn off the water for the big lawn until it dries out.
Skip the sprinklers in January, they aren't needed.
Please don't run the sprinklers tonight, since the ground is already wet.
Hold off on watering until the weekend.

name: attachment_weight_check
does: Checks how much an email attachment weighs, such as a crispy sharp photo of a speaker, and says if it is too big to send.
inputs: the file or picture, and who it is going to
people say:
- Will this picture send, or is it too big?
- My email says the file is too large, what do I do?
- How big is this video?
- Can I attach all five photos at once?
- Make this file smaller so it fits

name: bulky_pickup_booker
does: Books an extra pickup so the city can take away big things, like old rope, a broken chair, or a mattress.
inputs: what the item is, how many there are, and the street address
people say:
- I have a broken couch to throw away
- Who will take my old mattress?
- There's a pile of junk in the garage, can someone come?
- The bins are too small for all this stuff
- I need an extra pickup for some old rope and boards

Karim stood behind the counter of his shop, wiping the sink. A box of cloth was coming by air, and he needed to know when to open. He said, "When does the flight from Cairo land? Not the one from yesterday, today's one." The assistant checked the schedule and said the plane was due to touch down at ten past four. "I don't want a text, just tell me if it's late," said Karim. The assistant said it would speak only if the flight changed. Karim thanked it and went back to his old rag. Later, a voice told him the flight was twenty minutes late.

name: bed_water_check
does: Looks at the water channel running along the garden beds, tells the person whether it is clear, and can deliver a short burst of water to the dry spots.
inputs: which bed, and how long to water
people say:
- Is the water getting to my carrots?
- The back bed looks dry, give it a drink
- I think something is blocking the little ditch
- Make sure the flowers get water this morning
- Why is the lettuce so thirsty?

Niamh got home after a night shift, and her body felt like lead. She sat on the bed with a glass of water and said to her phone, "I want to sleep until noon, but wake me with an alarm the day after tomorrow at six, because I work the early shift." The assistant set the alarm. Niamh also asked it to turn on the automatic dark mode and keep the phone quiet. Her neighbor knocked to lend her a hand with a package, but Niamh was already half asleep. The assistant sent the neighbor a short note: "Please come back later." Then the room went still.

Tendai was in a rush after school. His glasses were crooked, and he had to pick up a package from the post office before it closed. He texted his phone: "what time does the post office close, can u guess if there will be a line". The assistant said it closes at five and that it was usually busy around four. Tendai asked it to remind him in fifty minutes. The assistant did. He ran the first block, and then he got there with ten minutes to spare. The assistant also said, "Bring your ID." Tendai pulled it out of his pocket and walked inside.

A flight is a trip by plane. Before you go, you check when it leaves, which gate it uses, and if there is any delay. A delay can happen when the runway is wet, or when a storm is near. Many people also check the size of their bag, because airlines have rules, and whether they can lock it. People ask for things like, "When does my flight leave?" or "Is it still on time?" They can say, "Tell me if the gate changes" or "Wake me up two hours early." It helps to know your flight number, because it makes questions quick and clear.

Thabo was texting on the bus, waiting for a red magazine he had ordered. He wrote to his phone, "Track it." The assistant asked which order he meant, and he said, "The magazine." The assistant found it and said the package was out for delivery and would arrive before dinner. Thabo was glad. He added, "Greet my gran when she gets it," because he had sent it to her house. The assistant said it would send a message to his gran with a hello from Thabo as soon as the box arrived. Thabo put his phone away.

Martha was at her desk in the office when she remembered that her brother's birthday was in six days. He got angry when people forgot, so she wanted something nice. She said to her assistant, "I need a gift idea for my brother. He likes food, but I don't understand what to get." The assistant gave a few ideas: a smoked salmon box, a pack of coffee beans, and a cooking class. Martha liked the box. She asked the assistant to order it and write a card with her name. The assistant did, and set a reminder for the day before the birthday to check that it had arrived.

Santiago was bending over his rose bushes when his phone buzzed again. The garden camera had sent a frequent string of alerts. He wiped his hands and said, "What is the camera seeing?" The assistant showed a cat in the corner of the yard. "Is the battery okay?" he asked. It was at ninety-five percent. Santiago stretched his back and said, "Turn down the alerts, and let me know only if it is a person." The assistant changed the setting. Then Santiago said he could smell smoke from the neighbor's grill, and asked the assistant to check the smoke alarm. It was fine.

name: parcel_window_finder
does: Tells the person when a parcel will arrive, like a new engine part in a black box, so they can be home to sign for it.
inputs: the tracking number, and the day they need it, for example to celebrate a birthday
people say:
- When will my box show up?
- I need to be home when the delivery comes
- Will it get here before Saturday's party?
- Did the courier leave something at my door?
- What time will the package arrive?

Thu came in from the garden with dirt on her boots and sat down by the phone. She said, "Excuse me, could you please help me find out the price of a stamp, and where the nearest post office is? I need to mail seeds to my aunt, and my hands are full of soil." The assistant told her a stamp was one dollar and that the closest post office was on Elm Street. It also said the parking lot was full on Saturdays. Thu thanked it, asked it to click on the map for directions, and wrote the address on a seed packet.

name: bake_label_maker
does: Makes a quick label with the name of a loaf or cake, the day it was baked, and how long it stays fresh, even for a cake that will travel on a plane.
inputs: what was baked, the baking date, and where it is going
people say:
- I want to mark this bread so I know when I made it
- How many days is this cake good for?
- Tag the cookies for the bake sale
- I'm taking a cake to my aunt by plane, what should I write on it?
- Put the date on the dough in the freezer

A taxi or ride service takes you from one place to another. You say where you want to start, and a driver comes to a pickup point. The cost depends on how far you go and how busy it is. A new rider may feel unsure, so the app shows the driver's name, the car, and the time of arrival. People change their rides by saying, "Pick me up at the back door," "Change the stop," or "How long until the car gets here?" Some apps warn you when a driver is close, so you can be outside. If you are late, you can ask the driver to wait.

name: room_sound_fill
does: Plays a playlist on the speakers in one room so music floods it with fresh songs, and lets the person skip or change the volume.
inputs: which room, the kind of music, and how loud
people say:
- Put some music on in the kitchen
- Can I have something new in the living room?
- It's too quiet in here
- Play the party list in the garden room
- Skip this one and turn it down a little

It was a snowy morning, and Max was already late. The snow had piled up on the car, and the kids had a dentist visit at nine. "Hey assistant, I don't want to cancel the dentist, but I can't get there by nine with all this snow. Can you move it to ten thirty?" The assistant looked at the dentist's open times. Ten thirty was free, so it moved the visit from nine to ten thirty and sent Max a message to confirm. Max sighed with relief. "And don't change my own haircut on Friday," Max added. The assistant said it would leave the haircut alone. Max zipped up the kids' coats and went outside to dig out the car.

Someone wants to learn which private emails are still unread.
Unread mail?
What's new in my inbox?
Any new emails since this morning?
I've no idea what came in overnight, so show me what I haven't read.
Open my inbox and read me the newest message.
Check my email, and tell me if anything came from my boss.
Show me my unread emails and read the first one out loud.
Could you please look at my inbox and tell me which messages I haven't opened yet, and then read the top one to me?

Matteo does not like gadgets. He stood by the front gate in the cold, holding his phone like a hot potato. His grandson had shown him the heating app, but the buttons were so little that he could not read them. He tried to zoom in, and the screen jumped around. At last he just spoke to it. "Please make the house warmer. A little more, maybe two degrees more than now." The assistant said the living room was at eighteen degrees, and it had raised the heating to twenty. Matteo laughed. "That was easy." "I can lower it at night too," said the assistant. "Yes, half as warm when I sleep," said Matteo. The assistant set the night heat to ten degrees, half of the day setting, and told him it was done.

name: power_use_report
does: Reads out how much electricity the home used, so people can listen to the answer instead of looking at a chart.
inputs: which day or week to look at, and one device if you want, like the tall freezer or the spice grinder
people say:
- How much power did we use yesterday?
- Why is the electric bill so high this month?
- What's eating all the electricity?
- Did the oven use a lot today?
- Show me this week's usage next to last week's

name: battery_saver
does: Makes the phone battery last longer by turning off extras, for example on a stormy night when the power is out in the village, or after a long afternoon of using the phone as a timer while you mow.
inputs: whether to switch it on or off, and the battery level to start at, such as twenty percent
people say:
- My battery is dying and I can't charge it
- Make my phone last until tomorrow
- Turn on low power mode
- How long until my phone is dead?
- Stop wasting battery on things I'm not using

A computer screen is like a room where you do your work, and you want it to feel right. Most computers have a setting for how bright the screen is, and people change it all the time. In a dark room you want it lower, and in a sunny room you want it higher. If the screen goes dark by itself, that is the sleep setting, and you can ask for a longer wait before the computer falls asleep. People say things like "make the screen brighter", "it's too bright for my eyes", or "don't let it go to sleep while I read". A friendly assistant can change these for you. You just say what you want in your own words, and it finds the right setting.

A filter in a heater or a fridge catches dust and bad smells. After a few months it gets full, and then the machine works worse. Think of a bakery: if the vent over the oven is blocked, the whole shop smells burnt, even a little sour. So people change filters, or book someone to fix a problem. They say "the air smells sour", "my fridge is making a noise", or "I need a plumber on Tuesday". When you book a repair, you pick a day and say what is broken, so the repair person knows what to bring. An assistant can remind you when a filter is due, or find a time that suits you, if you tell it what is wrong in plain words.

Someone wants to film a huge October party and then share the clip.
Record this.
Start filming and send it to Mum afterwards.
Film the cake, it's huge, and put the clip in our family chat.
I don't care about the quality, just start recording and share it later.
Begin a video now, and save it in the October folder.
Can you take a video of the kids and post the clip when I'm done?
Please start recording, and when I say stop, send it to my brother.
Would you mind filming the whole party and then sharing the clip with everyone in the group?

Isabel woke up from a deep sleep because her phone buzzed. A guest was coming at nine, and she wanted the alarm off for the front door. Her eyes were still closed. "Turn off the house alarm for the front door," she mumbled. Then she sat up. "No, wait. Not the front door, the back door. The guest comes through the garden." The assistant said it had not changed anything yet, and asked if she meant the back door. "Yes, the back door, until ten." The assistant turned off the alarm for the back door until ten o'clock and left the front door alarm on. Isabel smiled and went to make something warm to drink.

Scores in a sports match change fast, so many people follow them on their phone. A score tracker shows who is ahead, how much time is left, and what happened last. People pick a favorite team and ask for updates. They say "what's the score?", "did we win?", or "tell me when the match ends". They can also switch to a different team or sport if they change their mind. When your team scores in the last minute, the win feels sweet. Some people even lock their phone and still want the news, so they ask a speaker to read the score out loud instead.

name: send_scan_by_email
does: Scans a page on the printer and emails the file to someone, such as a fishing permit, or a form that came out wrong the first time.
inputs: who to send it to, and which page or how many pages
people say:
- Scan this and send it to my sister
- Email a copy of the permit I just put on the glass
- Mail the first two pages to Dr. Patel
- Can you scan the form and send it to the office?
- I need this letter as a file in my inbox

Natasha was juggling a bag, a toddler and a sticky mix of juice and crumbs on her sleeve. The parking meter outside the clinic was running low, and she had only ten minutes left. With one thumb she typed on her phone: "extend my parkng by 30 mins pls". The assistant understood and extended the parking by thirty minutes, using the card she had saved. It said the new end time was two forty. Natasha tried to upload a photo of the receipt to her work expenses, but the toddler grabbed the phone. The assistant said it had saved the receipt, so she could do the upload later. She nodded, picked up the toddler and walked into the clinic.

name: pet_feeder_schedule
does: Sets the times when the automatic feeder fills a pet's bowl, and holds the food back during a lightning storm if the pet is scared.
inputs: which pet (the pretty grey cat or the old dog), the feeding times, and the size of each meal
people say:
- Feed the cat at six every evening
- Give Rex a bigger breakfast
- Stop the feeder until Monday
- Is the dog's bowl empty?
- Make dinner for the cat an hour later

Lorenzo sat at his flat desk with a cold coffee and a long day ahead. His goal was to dig himself out of a mountain of meetings. "Move my two o'clock with Anna to four and tell me when I'm free on Thursday," he said to his phone. The assistant moved the meeting to four o'clock and sent Anna a note about the change. Then it told Lorenzo he was free on Thursday after eleven in the morning, and again from one o'clock on. Lorenzo thought about his report. "Block Thursday at two for me too," he said. The assistant put a block on his calendar called report, and Lorenzo finally drank his cold coffee.

Siobhan came home from the hospital after twelve hours on her feet. A bucket of wet leaves sat by the door, and the grass was long. A few moths fly up from it when the wind moves. "Start the robot mower now," she told the speaker. Then she yawned. "Wait, no. It's too early for the neighbors. Start it at ten instead." The assistant said it had not started yet, and set the mower to start at ten in the morning. It also told her the current weather showed no rain until evening, so the lawn would be dry. Siobhan thanked it and fell asleep on the sofa.

Someone wants to add up numbers, like the days of rain in July.
20 plus 10?
What's 15 and 27 together?
Sum of 8, 12 and 30, please.
Add 45 and 55, then tell me what half of that is.
The ink on my receipt is pale, so can you tell me what 14 plus 26 makes?
I did a quick scan of the bill and see 9, 18 and 21; what do they come to, and is that more than 40?
Could you please work out the total of 130 and 70 for me, and then take away 25?
How much is 6 more than 99, and how much is 6 less?

Person: Can you play soft music for the kids?
Assistant: Sure. Which speaker should I use?
Person: The one inside the kids' room. Start it in an hour.
Assistant: Okay, soft music in an hour on the kids' room speaker. How loud should it be?
Person: Quiet. I want them to sleep until morning.
Assistant: I'll keep it low. Should it stop after a while?
Person: Yes, after thirty minutes. I'd like to play it on all the speakers, but my phone tends to hang when I group them.
Assistant: One speaker is fine. I'll stop the music after thirty minutes.

Person: My watch buzzed and said I used a lot of power. I think it was a false alarm.
Assistant: I can look at your power use. Do you want today or the whole week?
Person: The whole week. And it's freezing in here, but I don't want to waste power.
Assistant: I can turn the heating up by one degree. I can also block the heat to the spare room, so you save power.
Person: Yes, please do both.
Assistant: Done. The heating is up one degree, and the spare room is off. Your power use for the week was normal, so the buzz was probably a false alarm.
Person: Oh good, thank you.

Someone wants to know whether it will rain hard today.
Rain today?
Will it rain hard later?
Do I need an umbrella or not?
Tell me if it's going to pour; I don't want to get wet.
Should I cover the pear tree? I want to save the fruit if rain is coming.
Check if I need a coat, I don't want to carry one if it stays dry.
Could you please tell me whether it will rain this afternoon, because I'd rather not walk to the shop without a jacket?

An appointment is a time you set aside to see someone, like a dentist or a barber. Shops and clinics have opening hours, so you can only book a time when they are open. People often change their mind, so they ask to move the time to another day, or to cancel it. They say "book me a haircut for Friday", "push it back an hour", or "what time do you close?". If the office is up the stairs, people sometimes learn about it only when they arrive, so it helps to ask about the place first. The last appointment of the day is often the hardest to get, so ask early.

Jing had just moved to the city and needed to print a form for her new job. She sat on the floor of her flat, eating a peach, with the printer blinking in front of her. "My printer says the ink is low. I don't want to buy more today, I just want to print the form," she told her phone. The assistant checked the printer. It said the black ink was at five percent, enough for about ten pages, and the current form was only two. It printed both pages. It also offered to remind her to buy ink next week, and Jing said yes. That night she would sleep well, knowing the form was ready.

Irina closed her shop late and drove home half asleep. In the car she clicked her seatbelt and said to her phone, "I'm so tired, and the first thing tomorrow is the delivery at seven." The assistant listened and understood that she needed to get up early. It asked if she wanted an alarm at six thirty. "Yes, please," said Irina. The assistant set the alarm for six thirty and also turned on a sleep reminder for ten tonight. Irina smiled. At home she put the phone beside her bed and fell asleep fast.

A note is a short piece of writing you keep so you do not forget something. People write down ideas, shopping lists, or what a friend told them. Voice notes are the same, but you speak instead of typing. Later, when you want to find an old note, you ask for it by a word you remember, like "the one about the heat bill" or "my note about the sad movie". You can also change a note, add a line, or delete it. People say "make a note", "write this down", or "read my last note". A good note is short and has a clear first line, so it is easy to find.

Person: I'm driving to the hills on Saturday, and I think the nights will be freezing.
Assistant: I can help you pack for that. How many nights will you stay?
Person: Two nights. I also need a present idea for my brother, who loves camping.
Assistant: A warm hat or a small lamp would be nice. Do you want me to put one on your packing list?
Person: Just the lamp. Also, please unlock my car doors so I can load the tent.
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't unlock your car. You can use your key or the car's own app. I can keep a personal packing list on your phone, though.
Person: Okay, that works.
Assistant: Done. It has a sleeping bag, warm socks, a tent and the lamp.

Person: I'm baking for my neighbors the day after tomorrow. Can you make my cake recipe bigger?
Assistant: Yes. How many people is it for now, and how many do you need?
Person: It makes eight. I need twelve. Quickly, please, my kitten is climbing on the counter.
Assistant: Then I'll make everything one and a half times bigger. Do you want the new amounts listed?
Person: Yes, please. And the brown sugar first.
Assistant: Brown sugar goes from one cup to one and a half cups. The recipe still says to fold in the flour last.
Person: Thank you. That's what I needed.

name: move_blinds
does: Opens or closes the blinds or curtains in a room, all the way or part of the way, for example at the main window where the cat sits while you eat.
inputs: which room or window, and how far to open, such as half
people say:
- It's too bright in here
- Open the curtains in the bedroom
- Close the blinds halfway
- I can't see the TV because of the sun
- Let some light into the kitchen

Amira had moved to the city a month ago, and her new friend's birthday was this Saturday afternoon. She had just found parking near a shop and stood on the street with her phone. "Hey, what's a good gift for a friend who likes drawing? I want something I can design myself." The assistant gave her three ideas: a sketchbook, a set of colored pencils, or a card she could design herself. Amira picked the card. Then she asked the assistant to remind her about her friends' birthdays. The assistant set a weekly reminder every Monday, listing the birthdays of the coming week. Amira smiled and walked into the shop.

When you order something online, the shop packs it and a courier brings it to you. Most shops let you see where the package is, sometimes with hourly updates. People change the delivery day, the address, or the size they ordered. They say "send it to my office", "I need a larger size", or "I want to return this". If the box arrives with a crack in the side, or the tent you bought has a hole, you can ask for your money back. Keep the receipt or the order number, because the shop will ask for it.

Olivia was not good with phones. She stood outside the cinema and wanted a taxi home. She did not want to use the app, because the buttons were too small. "I don't want to change channels or open anything," she said to the speaker. "Please just get me a taxi to Elm Street." The assistant asked where she was standing. "Outside the cinema on Park Road." It booked a taxi to pick her up there. When Olivia tried to zoom in on the map by mistake, the assistant said, "Don't worry, the only thing you need to do is wait. The car comes in six minutes." Olivia sat on the bench and waited.

Yusuf, a retired teacher, stood in his kitchen next to a bag of flour as tall as a small mountain. He wanted to bake bread for his grandchildren. "How long do I bake bread at two hundred degrees?" he asked the speaker. The assistant said about thirty-five minutes. "The tap water is icy. Is that okay?" Yusuf asked. The assistant said cold water was fine for this recipe, but warm water would make the dough rise faster. Yusuf asked it to set a timer for thirty-five minutes. Then he stood by the oven and waited, smelling the bread.

Li wanted to print photos of the new baby for each of the cousins. "Print ten photos," he told the printer assistant. Then he looked at his list. "Oh, no, eight, not ten. There are only eight cousins." The assistant said it would print eight copies and started. A woman from next door had helped him build the family album last week, and he wanted the copies to go in it. After six photos, the assistant told him the paper tray was almost empty. Li put in more paper, and the printer finished all eight.

Omar worked at a desk all day, but tonight the family was having a holiday dinner. He said to his phone, "Can you sort my to-do list for the party? I need to buy the cake after school today, when I pick up the kids. My daughter has a loose tooth, so get a plain cake, nothing hard." The assistant added "pick up a plain cake after school today" to his list and sorted the tasks by time. It put the cake first and the decorations last. Omar read the list and felt a little calmer.

The wifi router is the small box that sends the internet around your house. Sometimes the connection is slow, and that is a serious problem when you work from home. A tree outside, or thick walls inside, can block the signal. People move the router to a better place, change the password, or let a guest join. They say "the wifi is slow", "give my friend the password", or "restart the router". When you restart it, it turns off for a minute, then returns to normal. When a guest leaves, you can change the password so only family stays on the network.

Wouter stood in his garden among the tomatoes. A wire fence kept the rabbits away, but the plants were dry. He shuffled over to the shed and held up his phone. "Water the tomatoes for eleven minutes, please, and keep it off the roses. They are too close to the tomatoes." The assistant turned on the sprinkler for the tomato bed for eleven minutes and kept the rose bed off. Wouter nodded. "Good." He sat down with a cup of tea and watched the water.

Colin hated guessing. He was making dinner for friends who traveled from America, and his recipe said 350 degrees, but his oven used Celsius. "I don't want to guess," he told the speaker. "What is 350 Fahrenheit in Celsius?" The assistant said about 177 degrees Celsius, and that most people set the oven to 180. Colin wrote 180 on a sticky note. Then he asked how many kilograms were in two pounds of potatoes, and the assistant said just under one. Colin decided he did not need to go to the public market after all, since the shop on his street sold kilograms.

Shops send updates about your order by text or email. A message might say the order is packed, on the way, or at your door. If you are not at home, the courier may leave a note or use a key box. You can reply with a new time, or ask them to leave the parcel with a neighbor. People say "where is my order?", "send it to my sister instead", or "I want my money back". If the signal is weak where you live, the messages can arrive late, so it helps to check the tracking page too.

Minh wanted the lawn to look nice for a family picnic on the first of May. The grass was getting long. He spoke to the wireless speaker in the hall. "Please start the lawn mower on the first of May at nine in the morning." The assistant said the robot mower was set to start then. It also said the sprinkler could give the grass a drink the evening before, and asked if he wanted that. Minh said yes. The assistant set the sprinkler for the evening of the thirtieth of April. Minh smiled and went to give his grandchildren their breakfast.

Matteo ran down the stairs with his keys in his mouth. A friend was coming for dinner at seven, and his kitchen was messy. "Add 'bake the cake' to my list," he said to his phone, "but don't put it at the top. First I must tidy up." The assistant put "tidy the kitchen" first and "bake the cake" second on the list. Matteo said, "And don't remind me before five." The assistant set the reminders for after five and told him the list was ready. He nodded and hurried out the door.

Baraka was driving to work when his phone rang. It was his sister, calling about her birthday the day after tomorrow. He did not want to look at the screen. "Hey assistant, mute the family group chat until I'm out of the car, and save my sister's new number in my contacts." The assistant asked him to say the number. Baraka said it slowly, and the assistant saved it. "Mark her as a favorite," he added. The assistant did that, and muted the group chat. Baraka kept his eyes on the road.

Someone wants to know how many steps they have walked today.
Steps today?
My step count?
How far have I walked?
Step total, please.
I'm too sleepy to count, so how many steps have I done?
Can you pick up my step count from my watch, please?
Have I reached ten thousand steps? I wore my sandals and walked all day.

Sam was texting in bed when he remembered his cousin's new address. Lena was young, and she had just moved into a house she could barely afford. "Add Lena to my contacts," Sam told his phone. "Her address is two thousand Elm Avenue, and her number is the same as before." The assistant made a new contact card for Lena, put in the address, and copied the old number from Sam's messages. Then it read the card back to him. Sam said it was right and went back to his texting.

A hobby is something you do for fun in your free time, like knitting or painting. Most hobbies need supplies, such as wool, brushes or paper. People often do their hobby in the usual place, like a table by the window. They ask for small changes: a reminder for a weekly class, a list of things to buy, or the bus time to the craft shop. They say "remind me to knit tonight", "put paint on my list", or "when is the next bus to town?". A hobby does not have to be perfect. It should simply be something you like.

name: bill_due_dates
does: Shows which bills are due soon and lists any extra fees, and can invite a family member to see the list too.
inputs: which bill (electricity, water, rent) or all of them, and the time period
people say:
- When is my rent due?
- Do I owe anything this week?
- Which bills are coming up?
- Did the water bill go up?
- Remind me before the power bill is due

Edward sat at his desk on a damp Monday. A friend had tagged him in a photo from a hiking trip, where he sat on a big stone looking silly. "I don't want everyone to see this," Edward told his phone. "Delete the tag, but don't remove the photo. It's my friend's." The assistant took Edward's name off the photo but left the photo on his friend's page. It also told him the photo already had two likes. Edward sighed, thanked it, and went back to his email.

Person: did my parcel arive today?
Assistant: I can check. Which shop sent it, or do you have a tracking number?
Person: The pharmacy on Elm Street. I don't have a number. My tooth is sore and I need the medicine.
Assistant: I see one parcel from that pharmacy. It is out for delivery and should come this afternoon.
Person: Good. Please disconnect the doorbell so it doesn't wake me while I nap.
Assistant: Of course, but then you won't hear the courier. Do you want it off for one hour?
Person: Yes, one hour.
Assistant: Done. The doorbell is off for one hour.

Putri woke up and rubbed her eyes. Today was going to be a long day: her friend the doctor was coming to her party at six. She looked at the empty living room and said, "It's so quiet in here. And the guests will walk in soon." The assistant asked if she wanted music. "Yes, something happy but not too loud." It played a happy playlist on the living room speaker, at low volume. Putri nodded, opened the curtains and started to hang the paper stars.

Person: Excuse me, assistant, could you please set a reminder for me? My grandson says the tyres on my car need air before our long drive on Sunday, and I don't want to forget.
Assistant: Of course. What day should I remind you?
Person: Saturday morning, please.
Assistant: At what time on Saturday morning?
Person: At nine. And can you rank the three nearest petrol stations by price?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't compare prices yet, but I can list the closest stations. Do you want that?
Person: Yes, please. It's funny, my old car never needed so much looking after!
Assistant: Here they are: Maple Road, two minutes away; Station Street, five minutes; High Street, nine. Your reminder is set for Saturday at nine.

name: guest_wifi_access
does: Lets a visitor join the wifi for a few hours, and can answer which devices are connected, which is handy when the whole family comes for a picnic in the garden.
inputs: how many hours the guest can stay online, and a name for the guest network, for example creamy_cafe
people say:
- My cousin needs the wifi password
- Can the guests get online for the evening?
- Who is using the internet right now?
- Make a separate network for visitors
- Turn off the guest wifi tomorrow morning

Someone wants to see how much water their home has used.
Water use today?
How much water have we used this week?
We invited a lot of people over, so how much water did we use?
Tell me if we went over forty-two cubic meters this month.
I'm cleaning the bird cage with the hose, so how much water has it used?
The washing machine is loud and I worry it eats a lot of water. Can you tell me how much we've used since morning?

Chiara came in from the garden with dirty hands. She was lucky to have a printer in the shed. Her seed order had come by email, and she wanted the list on paper. She typed with one thumb: "print my seed list from my emial". The assistant found the email and printed the list. Chiara wanted to join the gardening club too, and the form for that was in the same email. The assistant printed it as well, and Chiara put both pages in her pocket.

A password is a secret that keeps your phone, email and photos private. People change it when they think someone has seen it, or just every few months. A good password has a minimum of twelve letters, numbers or signs, and it is not your birthday or your dog's name. Some people write a password on a slice of paper, but a password manager is safer. At lunch with friends, don't type a password where others can see. People ask their phone for changes with words like "lock my phone after one minute", "make my password longer", or "who can see my photos?"

Margaux was a student, and the wifi at her flat was slow again. Her big brother was streaming a game in the next room, and her paper would not upload. A wheel of cheese sat on her desk, forgotten. She spoke to her phone. "Wifi password." The assistant showed the password for the home network and read it out. Her friend Noor was visiting, so Margaux said, "Email it to Noor." The assistant wrote a short email with the network name and the password and sent it. Then Margaux said, "Pause my brother's laptop for an hour." The assistant paused his connection on the router. The page loaded fast, and Margaux finished her paper before dinner.

name: bedtime_planner
does: Picks a bedtime that fits your wake-up time, reminds you to shower and put your phone away, and shows a weekly sleep chart you can print on paper.
inputs: the time you wake up, the hours of sleep you want, and whether it is still light outside
people say:
- What time should I go to bed if I wake up at six?
- I want eight hours of sleep, when do I start winding down?
- Remind me tonight when it's time to get ready for bed
- I keep going to sleep too late, can you help?
- Tell me how I slept this week

Jomar was a retired teacher, and every evening he liked to read. Tonight his tea was sour because he had forgotten the sugar, but he did not mind. "Remind me to read at eight every night," he told the smart speaker. "But I don't want a loud alarm. My wife is already asleep." The assistant set a reminder for eight with a soft chime. Then Jomar asked, "How many pages a day do I need to finish this book by the end of July?" The assistant worked it out and said about twenty. Jomar liked to carry his e-reader out to the garden, so he asked it to open the book where he had stopped. It did, and he did not have to start again from chapter one.

Gabriela had just moved to the city with her two boys. After a long walk to the new school, her feet were sore, and she had to stand on the bus all the way home. At home she sat down and spoke to her phone. "Cut the boys' screen time in half on school days." The assistant changed the limit from two hours to one hour. Then she said, "Tell me a bedtime story that is a bit shorter than last night's." The assistant chose a story of ten minutes. Tomorrow the class would march in the town parade, so she also asked, "Wake the boys twenty minutes earlier than usual." The assistant moved the alarm, and Gabriela finally felt a little less lost.

Fergus drove a delivery van, and the rainy week had been long. In the evening he sat in the cab with his scarf around his neck and spoke to his phone. "Could you please remind me about my daughter's maths homework at seven tonight? I have a late delivery, and I always forget until she is already asleep." The assistant set a reminder for seven and said it would repeat it ten minutes later if he did not answer. Fergus also asked when the sheet was due. The assistant looked at her school list and said Friday. The forecast said it might snow on Friday, so Fergus asked it to add a note to finish the homework a day early.

Going to the movies starts with a simple question: what is on? An assistant can show you the films near you today, with cinema times and a trailer for each one. People change the day, the cinema or the kind of film by saying things like "show me tomorrow's times", "replace that one with a comedy", or "something safe for the kids". At home, many people watch a trailer first and then say "dim the lamp, we're starting the movie." The point is to find something you want to see, at a time that works, without reading a long list yourself.

Zara was seven, and she noticed that her dad kept coughing. The house felt dusty. She went to the speaker in the living room. "Turn on the air purifier and make it a bit quieter," she said. The assistant started the purifier and lowered the fan speed. Later, Zara was playing in the yard when she saw gray smoke far away to the north. She ran inside and asked, "Close the vents and tell me if the air outside is bad." The assistant closed the vents and said the air was a little smoky today. Her dad smiled and said, "Good thinking, Zara. You helped the whole family."

name: gift_finder
does: Suggests gift ideas for a birthday, from a burger dinner to a blue sweater, and tells you where to buy them.
inputs: who the gift is for, what they like, how much you can spend, and where they live
people say:
- I need a present for my dad
- What should I get my sister for her birthday?
- Any ideas for a gift under twenty dollars?
- My friend turns thirty next week and I have no idea what to buy
- Something nice for a coworker who is leaving

Ximena was ten, and she wanted to chill on the sofa. But her phone kept buzzing. She and her aunt ran a page for the family cat, Mochi, and it had many followers. Every like made a noise, and the page felt too busy. "Stop the like alerts and bring them back in two weeks," Ximena said to her phone. The assistant turned them off and set a note for two weeks later. Then she said, "Post the photo of Mochi tomorrow at noon, and write: down one pound!" The assistant saved the post and scheduled it. Ximena put the phone down and finally had some quiet.

Meal planning means deciding what to eat for the week before you go shopping. It saves time and money, and it ends the "what's for dinner?" stress at six o'clock. People with a busy job often plan on Sunday. They change the plan all the time: "make Tuesday vegetarian", "swap the fish for chicken", "add a packed lunch for Thursday". Fancy dinners are rare, but when friends are invited, people say "plan a dinner for six on Saturday." An assistant can write the plan and the shopping list so you do not have to.

A bill is a request for money for something you used, like electricity, water or the internet. Each one has an amount and a due date. Paying on time keeps the lights on and avoids extra fees. People keep a list of bills and change it often: "move the water bill to the first of the month", "remind me three days before rent is due", "take the phone bill off the list". Some people give each kind a color, and purple might mean rent. The electricity bill goes up with the power every outlet in your home uses, so switching things off helps.

Hodan was late for work, and the flat felt stuffy. She ran past the tall plant by the door, grabbed her bag and called out to the speaker. "Run the air purifier until I'm back, and remind me this Saturday afternoon to change the filter." The assistant started the purifier on high and set the reminder. Her allergies were bad, so she took a dose of her medicine with her coffee on the way out. "Also, cool the bedroom a little," she added from the stairs. The assistant lowered the heat by two degrees, and Hodan ran for the bus.

Layla came home after a rough night shift. The house was cold, and her dog, Biscuit, sat by his empty bowl. She dropped her bag and said, "It's freezing in here." The assistant turned the heat up by three degrees. Layla looked at Biscuit and sighed. "He hasn't had breakfast, and I can barely keep my eyes open." The assistant understood and started the pet feeder with one portion, then turned on the lamp by the couch. When Biscuit was eating, Layla asked it to boost the water fountain to the full setting, because it was almost empty. Then she lay down and slept.

Colin was a gardener, and he had filmed a short video of his roses. The shed was dim, and the phone screen glared. "Dim the screen," he said, and the assistant lowered the brightness. Then he asked it to play the clip again. At the end there was one big flower, red as a star. Colin wanted to show it to his sister. "Send this video to Rosa the day after tomorrow in the morning." The assistant scheduled the message. Colin put the phone in his pocket and went back to his plants, happy that his sister would see the roses.

Ruta was a cook, and her hands were wet from the sink. Her close friend Elena had a birthday on Friday. Ruta grabbed her phone from the shelf next to the washer and typed fast: "remind me to pak elena's cake friday morning". The assistant understood and set a reminder for Friday at nine: pack Elena's cake. Ruta smiled and typed one more line. "any gift ideas for elena, she loves tea". The assistant suggested a tea set, a jar of honey, or a nice mug, and said each one could be ordered today. Ruta chose the tea set and went back to her dishes.

Gustavo owned a small shop, and he worked late. When he left the shop it was already dark, and he was tired. In the car he wanted to hear about the game. "What was the score of the Tigers game? No, sorry, I meant the Lions." The assistant said the Lions had won two to one. Gustavo smiled. "Set an alarm for training at six. No, make it half past six." The assistant set the alarm for six thirty. Before bed, Gustavo asked it to remind him to bring the team shirts to the shop on Monday, and the assistant said it would.

A focus timer helps you work for a short time and then rest. Many people work for twenty-five minutes and take a five-minute break. The break is for your eyes, your back and your head. If your neck is sore, stand up and stretch. Let some air blow in through the window, or sit near a vent. People change the timer often: "make it thirty minutes", "add a longer break", "skip the break today". Others like a routine, so they say "start my morning routine at seven." It is a simple way to get things done without getting tired.

Arjun was running for the train. He wanted to visit his grandmother, but the ticket was expensive, so he had to pick the right day. "Days until Sunday," he panted into his phone. "Three days," said the assistant. The ticket was cheaper on Sunday. Arjun counted on his fingers and nodded. "Her birthday is tomorrow," he said to himself, "so I must buy her a present today." He asked the phone, "Gift shop near me?" The assistant showed a shop two streets away. Arjun jumped on the train, and he planned to buy a scarf there before he left the next day.

Emi, a retired teacher, sat in her cozy chair with a blanket on her knees. She said to the television, "Could you please record the cooking show on the third channel tonight? I will be at choir practice, and I don't want to miss the cake lesson." The assistant said it would record the show at eight and keep it for her. Emi was pleased. Then she asked, "Please track that show, so it records every week." The assistant set up the recording to repeat every Thursday. When Emi came home from choir, the cake lesson was waiting for her.

Wendy ran a flower shop, and she had a call with her supplier at ten. She stood by the shop window and spoke to her phone. "Join my ten o'clock call, and make the volume louder. It was half as loud as yesterday." The assistant joined the call and raised the volume. The supplier's words were still hard to understand, so Wendy said, "Share the order list on the screen, and turn on captions." Now she could read every word. "Sorry I'm late," she told the supplier, and they began to talk about next week's roses.

Many people start the day with coffee or tea. How strong or sweet it is depends on the person. A student might want a strong coffee before an exam, while someone else likes a gentle tea with a little honey. When people ask for changes, they say "make it weaker", "less sugar", "a bit more milk", or "just half a cup". A smart coffee machine can remember your usual drink and make it the same way each morning. Some people pack a flask for the day and ask the machine to fill it before they go.

Tesfaye had a job in the morning and a camping trip right after. The day was sunny, and he was late. He threw his bag in the car and called out to his phone, "Make a packing list for two nights, and add twice as many socks as last time." The assistant made the list. "Flash it on the car screen," said Tesfaye, and the list appeared. Then he asked, "Will it rain less in the hills than here?" The assistant said the hills would be sunny too, with a little cloud in the evening. Tesfaye started the car and drove off.

The person wants to know if a home remedy such as vinegar is safe to use for a small health problem.
Is vinegar safe for a sore throat?
Can I gargle with vinegar?
Vinegar on a bee sting, okay?
Will vinegar hurt my skin?
I have a rash, is it safe to put vinegar water on it?
I plan to visit the clinic before lunch on Sunday, so can I try vinegar on my foot until then?
Is that fine for kids too?
Could you please tell me whether vinegar is safe for someone with a weak stomach?

Person: hey how much is 200 in pounds
Assistant: Which currency are you starting from?
Person: us dollars. im going to london in ten days
Assistant: At today's rate, 200 dollars is about 160 pounds. The rate moves, so it may be a little different in ten days.
Person: ok. is winter a good time to go? i want to climb the hills out west
Assistant: I can only help with prices and rates, so I can't say if it is a good time to go. Sorry about that.
Person: no worries, thanks

A smart speaker is a small speaker that listens for a name, like "hey speaker", and then does what a person asks. It can play music, set timers and answer questions. People change its volume, its voice and the room it plays in. You can say "louder", "a bit quieter" or "play it in the kitchen too". If the speaker cannot hear you, say it again a little closer. When a hungry person asks, "set a timer for ten minutes for the pasta", the speaker counts down and rings when the food is ready.

The person wants a dozen dumplings delivered to the back door and says the driver is welcome to leave them there.
Order a dozen dumplings
Get me a dozen dumplings delivered, please
I'm hungry, can I get dumplings sent over?
Dumplings to the back door, a dozen of them
I need more dumplings than last time, make it a dozen
Send twelve dumplings from the place on Park Street
Could you please order a dozen dumplings and tell the driver to come to the back door, because the front bell is broken?

Ligaya was not good with technology, and her inbox was a mess. She stood in the kitchen next to her dirty apron, which hung on a hook by the door, and spoke to her tablet. "Read email." The assistant read three new messages out loud. The second one was from the power company. "Label it bills," said Ligaya. The assistant added the label bills to that message and told her it was done. Ligaya smiled. For the first time in weeks, she knew where her important mail was, and she did not have to press a single button.

Rizal was not good with technology. He pressed the side button on his phone again and again, but nothing happened. Then he remembered he could just talk. "Move my dentist appointment to Thursday and tell me what else I have that day." The assistant moved the appointment and said he had a lunch with his cousin from the east side at noon. Rizal had tried to change the date on the clinic's website earlier, but he could not find the right page. Now it was done in a few seconds. He laughed and said thank you to the phone.

Wanjiru had just moved to the city, and she did not know the shops yet. She wanted to stretch her money, so she asked her phone for a meal plan. "Plan dinners for the week, but no fish and nothing spicy." The assistant planned five dinners with rice, beans, eggs and vegetables. Wanjiru felt silly, because she had never planned a week of food before. Then she said, "I don't want to buy a whole chicken. Only half a chicken, if the shop sells it." The assistant changed the list and found a small market near her flat that sold chicken by the half.

name: pantry_check
does: Checks what is running low in your kitchen, builds a shopping list, and shows the direction to the closest store, with one click to send the list to your phone.
inputs: the food you have at home, how much you use each week, and your address; a square photo of the fridge helps
people say:
- Are we out of milk?
- What do I need from the shop?
- Make me a shopping list for the week
- Is there any butter left?
- I'm at the store, what was I supposed to get?

A recipe tells you how much of each thing to use for a number of servings. Grandma's cake may serve eight, but tonight you may need only four. Scaling a recipe means making every amount bigger or smaller. People measure in cups and spoons, so a cook says "half the recipe", "double it" or "make it for six". An assistant can do the sums and read out the new amounts. Cooks also use timers, like "wake me in thirty minutes" while the dough rests, so nothing is forgotten.

Li came home after a long night shift and sat down at the kitchen table, very tired. "Book a checkup with Dr. Patel and remind me to take my vitamin at nine," she said to her phone. The assistant found a free time on Tuesday and booked it. The clinic's website asked her to scan her insurance card, so she held the card up to the camera, and the assistant sent it. "Pick the day with the least waiting," she added. The assistant said Tuesday morning was the quietest. Li put her head on her arm and smiled.

The person wants to book a haircut that fits their current plan for the day.
Book me a haircut
Haircut today, but not after five
I need a cut, anything except Monday
Can I get an appointment at the barber? Nothing too early, please.
Find a slot for a trim that totals no more than forty minutes, and not on a Saturday
Please book a trim, and I don't want to wait in a long line
I would like a haircut this week, but please don't book it during my lunch break

Many people let a robot mower cut the lawn while they rest. It goes out on a schedule and drives back to its base when it is done. Grass that is damp after rain is hard to cut, so people say "skip mowing today" or "mow after lunch". Other changes are "make the grass shorter", "cut the edges" and "water the front lawn for ten minutes". A sprinkler can also run on a timer. If a mower breaks soon after you buy it, you can ask the shop for a refund.

name: ride_planner
does: Plans a bike route of the distance you like, finds quiet roads, and cancels the plan if it rains.
inputs: where you start, how far you want to go, how many people ride (a mother with a small child needs an easy route), and the day
people say:
- Plan a ride for Saturday morning
- Where can I bike for about twenty kilometers?
- Find me a flat route, I'm not good with hills
- I want an easy loop near the river
- Cancel tomorrow's ride, it's pouring

News

The person wants to know how much electricity the home has used this week, now that the meter has had time to sync.
Power use?

Francesca had just moved to the city. Her pasta was cooked, and she was packing a lunch for tomorrow when she remembered her bank. "What's my balance?" she asked her phone. The assistant read it out. "Move fifty from savings to checking at half past six," she said, because her rent was due that evening. The assistant scheduled the transfer. The kitchen was sunny, and the screen was hard to read. "Turn up the brightness," said Francesca, and the assistant did. She ate her pasta and felt a little more at home.

name: game_night_helper
does: Keeps score and a turn timer for board games, adds up play money after tax in shop games, and reads the rule when players start a juicy argument.
inputs: the game's name, the players' names, how long each turn lasts, and the time your guests arrive
people say:

- Who is winning?
- Start a two minute timer for Mia's turn
- How do you win at this game?
- Is it okay to trade on the first turn?

The person wants to call their friend Sam on speakerphone while carrying a black bag up the stairs.
Call Sam on speaker
Phone Sam, hands free
Ring Sam

Could you please call Sam and put it on speaker, because I'm carrying things up the stairs?

Haruto had just woken up, and his head was foggy. He reached for his phone. "Book a ride to the station for tomorrow at seven." The assistant booked a car with a pickup on the corner of Maple Street. Then Haruto remembered that his new phone did not have the taxi app. "Install the taxi app," he mumbled, and the assistant did. He also had a flight in ten days. "Book a ride to the airport in ten days, early, because I have to board at nine." The assistant saved the booking. Haruto was glad it was all so easy, and he went to make some tea.

Jomar was a student, and he had to read a book for class. A woman at the library had told him the book was funny, so he was looking forward to it. He sat on a bench in the park and said to his phone, "Open chapter three." The assistant opened chapter three of the e-book. After a page he got hungry for a break. "Bookmark here." The assistant saved the page. Then Jomar said, "Set timer," and the assistant started a twenty-minute reading timer. When it rang, he had finished the whole chapter and was laughing.

Agnieszka was nine, and her grandpa had a bad cough. His medicine was on the kitchen table. "Remind Grandpa to take his pill in an hour," Agnieszka said to the speaker. The assistant set the reminder. Then she asked, "How do we get to the doctor's office?" The assistant showed a route by bus and said the ride took about twenty minutes. Grandpa was cold, so she said, "Keep his electric blanket on low." The assistant turned the blanket on at the lowest setting. Grandpa smiled and said she was the best helper in the house.

Person: Resume please.
Assistant: Do you mean the podcast or the audiobook?
Person: Audiobook. I'm cooking crispy chicken.
Assistant: Okay, playing chapter nine from where you stopped.
Person: Can you split this chapter into two parts?
Assistant: Sorry, I can't split a chapter. I can pause it in ten minutes, if you like.
Person: Yes, pause in ten.
Assistant: Done. I will stop it in ten minutes.

Locks keep a home safe. An old lock uses an iron key, but a smart lock uses a code or your phone. A doorbell camera can upload a short clip to your phone when a person comes to the door. People change who may come in by saying things like "lock the front door", "open the garage", "give Sam a code for Friday" or "who is at the door?" It all works well as long as the battery is charged. If the battery is low, the app tells you, so you can change it before you are locked out.

People follow a sports team to know when it plays and how it is doing. A phone can show live scores, the next match and training times. People change what they follow with words like "follow the Hawks", "tell me the score every ten minutes" or "stop the alerts after nine". When a game is going well, fans want the score often. A coach may say the team is going in the right direction when training goes well. Runners and swimmers use the same tools to see their own times and plan the next session.

Nathan had just moved to the city, and his budget was tight. He wanted to order twelve bread rolls for a party and needed to know the price. "Multiply twelve by four," he said to his phone. "No, wait, twelve by five." The assistant said sixty. "Now divide that by three," said Nathan. "Twenty." He was glad the phone had kept up with his change of mind. He wrote the number in his notes, a safe place where he would not lose it, and then went to order the rolls at the shop around the corner.

News is a short report of what happened today. A headline is the title at the head of a story, and it is short enough to read in the blink of an eye. People pick the topics they care about, like sports, weather or local news. They change the list by saying "show me sports news", "only local news", "read the first three" or "any news since this morning?" News about a cold snap or a storm can matter right away, so many people also turn on alerts for those.

Assistant: Should I raise your bedroom to twenty-one degrees?
Person: yeah. can u split the heat so my room is warmer than the hall
Assistant: I can set your room to twenty-one and the hall to eighteen. Is that okay?

Assistant: Sorry, I can't stop him from changing it, but I can tell you when someone does.

Person: Start the washing machine and tell me when it's done.
Assistant: Sure. Which cycle should I use, cotton or quick wash?
Person: Quick wash, please. The baby will sleep soon and I want the noise to stop by then.
Assistant: A quick wash takes thirty minutes. Do you want me to run the dryer after that?
Person: Yes, and set a reminder to fold the towels. I also spilled cheese sauce on my shirt, so can you scrub it out for me?
Assistant: I can't scrub it myself, sorry. I can remind you to soak the shirt in cold water before the next wash.
Person: Okay, please do that for tonight at seven.

Someone wants the sprinklers to wave back and forth and water the garden, including the sour lemon tree and the seedlings no bigger than a coin.
water the garden
turn on the sprinklers
