run the sprinklers for twenty minutes
i forgot to water the plants again, can you do it now
Could you please switch on the garden sprinklers? We are going away this weekend and I want everything wet first.

A television is for watching shows, news and films. Most people keep it in the living room, but some put a small one on a desk in the kitchen. The remote control lets you change many things. You can change the channel, make the sound louder or quieter, or mute it when the phone rings. Subtitles help when a show is noisy or the actors talk fast. People say turn on the subtitles, or switch to the cooking channel. If a spicy recipe goes by too fast, they say go back ten seconds. With streaming, you can also say pause, skip ahead, or play the next episode.

Ayita was a retired teacher who liked to drive to the market early. On the evening of the twelfth of March, the light in her garage was dim, and she could not read the little tyre gauge. She put her shopping bag down and spoke to her phone. 'Check my tyre pressure,' she said. The phone looked at the car's sensors and told her the front left tyre was a bit low. 'Please notify me tomorrow at eight to put air in it,' said Ayita. The assistant set a reminder for eight in the morning and said it was saved. Ayita smiled, locked the garage and went inside for tea.

name: descale_reminder
does: Tells you when to clean a kettle or coffee machine, with gentle tips such as using a soft toothbrush on the edges, so white scale doesn't build up and snow into your cup.
inputs: which appliance it is, and how often you use it
people say:
- there's white stuff inside my kettle
- my coffee tastes strange lately
- when should I clean the coffee machine
- remind me every month to descale the kettle
- how do I get the crusty bits out of the water tank

Tala did not know much about her phone, but she wanted to write to a new friend in Brazil. She held the phone close and said, 'How do I say good morning in Portuguese?' The assistant answered with the words and said them out loud. Tala wondered if she could spell them right, so she said, 'I don't want the long answer, just show me the letters.' The assistant wrote bom dia on the screen. 'Please double the size so I can read it,' she said. The assistant made the letters bigger. Then Tala asked it to save the words in her notes, and she added her friend as a new contact too.

Thabo sold potatoes and onions from a small shop near the bus stop. It was a bitter cold morning, and his hands were full of boxes. He spoke to the voice assistant on his phone. 'Add Mrs Dlamini to my contacts with the number 555 0142, and clear the old number for Mr Kumar,' he said. The assistant made a new contact for Mrs Dlamini and saved the number. Then it removed the old number from Mr Kumar's page and said both changes were done. Thabo nodded, set the last box of potatoes on the counter and turned the sign on the door to open.

Keoni worked as a cook, and on a windy morning he woke up with a sore throat. He was stirring a pot of soup when he pointed at his phone on the counter and said, 'Remind me to take half a tablet of my medicine at noon, and again at six.' The assistant said it had set two reminders, one at noon for half a tablet and one at six. Keoni asked for something warm to drink too, so he said, 'Set a timer for four minutes, I'm making tea.' The timer started. He tasted the soup, felt a little better, and went on cooking.

Person: Hello dear. I would be so grateful if you could put my photo up for my family, because my sister lives far away and I owe her a picture.
Assistant: Of course. Which photo would you like to post?
Person: The one of the cake on the kitchen shelf.
Assistant: Found it. Should I post it for everyone, or only for your sister?
Person: Only her. Could you also make her pay me a visit?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't make anyone visit. I can send her a message asking if she can come soon.
Person: Yes, please do that.

Kenji got home after a long night shift at the hospital. His motorcycle was parked outside, and his coffee tasted sour because it had been sitting since midnight. He sat down and said to the assistant, 'Read me the guest wifi password.' Then he shook his head. 'No, wait, I mean the main network, not the guest one.' The assistant said the main password out loud, slowly. Kenji typed it into his laptop. 'Also, resume my download from before I left,' he said. The assistant restarted the paused download and told him it had twenty minutes left. Kenji drank his bad coffee and went to bed.

Bills are the payments a home must make each month, like electricity, water and rent. Each one has a due date, and paying late can cost extra. Some people keep paper bills in a jacket pocket and forget them. A perfect way to avoid that is to set a reminder, or to let the bank pay for you on the same day each month. People say remind me to pay the water bill on the fifth, or move the rent date to the first. If an app is locked, they unlock it with a fingerprint to see what is due. They can also ask how much the last electricity bill was.

Someone who cleans their solar panels with vinegar wants to see how much power the house uses and makes, and how often to check.
show my power use
how much electricity did we use today
is it half of what we used last week
Does my power use this week fit under the usual amount?
what did the panels make compared with yesterday
tell me if we use more than double the normal at night
can you check often and warn me if the number jumps
I would like a daily summary of how much power we used, so I can cut the bill by a third.

A restaurant is a place to eat food that someone else cooks. People often book a table before they go, so they don't wait. They can change the time, the day or the number of people. They say things like book a table for four at seven, or make it six people instead. Opening hours matter too, because a kitchen may close early. On a cloudy day, fewer people sit outside, so tables inside fill up first. Some places hide their prices until you ask, but most put the menu online. For takeaway, you say I want to order food to pick up at eight. Many people check the menu on their phone or watch before they leave.

who's at my door

Could you please let me see the camera, because I'm walking back alone and feel a bit nervous?
anyone out front

Naoki was a retired teacher who worried about running out of his heart medicine. On a grey afternoon he picked up his phone and said, 'How long does it take to drive to the pharmacy on Mill Street?' The assistant said about twenty minutes, with a little traffic. 'Is there a quicker way?' asked Naoki. The assistant found a road that was half the distance, but it had works on it, so it said the first route was better. Naoki asked it to guide him by voice. In the car, it said, 'In two hundred metres, turn left. This is your final turn.' He pulled up outside the pharmacy right on time.

Milena was texting her friend when she remembered the cookies. She said to the kitchen speaker, 'Heat the oven to 180 so I can bake.' The speaker said it was heating the oven to 180 degrees. A minute later Milena frowned. 'Sorry, I meant 200, the recipe says hotter.' The speaker changed it to 200 and said it would tell her when it was ready. 'Also put cookies on my calendar for Saturday so I don't forget to bring them,' she said. The speaker added it to her calendar. Soon the oven beeped, and Milena slid the tray in.

Hodan was a retired teacher who found it hard to type on a small screen, so she spoke to her phone a lot. One afternoon she was in the garden when the phone buzzed. She tapped it and said, 'Voicemail.' The assistant played a message from her cousin Ayaan, who asked about Sunday lunch. Hodan smiled. 'Call him,' she said. The assistant rang Ayaan on speaker while she kept weeding. After the call the light on the porch was dim, so she said, 'Alert me at five about the pie.' The assistant set an alert for five, and Hodan went on pulling weeds.

- is it safe to get in the water right now

When you order something online, you pick the item, the size and where it should go. The shop packs it and it travels to your door. Sizes matter a lot for clothes and furniture. A shelf might be a hundred and twenty centimeters wide, so people check that it fits. There is often a maximum weight or size for free delivery. People say ship it to my office instead, or send two instead of one. If something is wrong, they say I want to return this, or swap it for a bigger size. Many shops let you change the delivery day, and people ask for it to come on Friday.

make sure the doors are shut before I go

Measurements tell us how big, heavy, hot or far something is. Different places use different units. In one country a road sign shows miles, in another it shows kilometers. A cook may weigh flour in grams, while an old recipe says ounces. People say how many cups is this, or change it to centimeters. A tv size is shown in inches, so some shoppers ask what that is in centimeters. Athletes train with distance in meters, and a doctor may check a baby's weight in kilograms. Raw chicken must be cooked to a safe heat, and a recipe may give it in Celsius or Fahrenheit, so people ask for the other one.

Person: Lock the front door and open the garage.
Assistant: I can do both. Which garage door do you mean, the big one or the side one?
Person: The big one. I need to get my salad ingredients out of the car.
Assistant: Done. The front door is locked and the big garage door is opening.
Person: Lovely. Do you know who is at the back gate? I heard a knock.
Assistant: I can't see the back gate because there is no camera there. I can show you the front door camera.
Person: No, that's fine. I'll go and look myself.

Neighbours often help each other. If a pet gets lost, people put up a note or type a message on a local group page. Local events, like a street sale or a school fair, are shared the same way. If the noise at night is too loud, a person might knock and ask politely. People say post a note about my lost cat, or remind me about the street party on Saturday. A simple message is best: say what is lost, where, and a phone number. Someone with a bad knee may ask a neighbour to help carry bags. When a pet comes home, people say take the notice down.

how far did I ride

Moshe drove a delivery van, and between jobs he sat in the car park waiting. His phone was slow. 'I don't want to pay for more data,' he said to the assistant. 'Is the wifi at this place working?' The assistant scanned for networks and found one called Depot Guest. The car park was silent, so he asked it to join. The assistant asked for the password. Moshe read it from a sign on the wall, and the phone connected. 'Tell my team I'm online,' he said. The assistant sent a short message to his team group. Moshe opened his map and checked the next stop.

Person: I want to tell everyone about my snowy garden tonight after dinner.
Assistant: That sounds nice. Where would you like to post it, and do you have a photo?
Person: I don't know. I've never smoked a post before, I mean made a post.
Assistant: No problem. I can help. Do you want to post on your family page?
Person: Yes. And I want to celebrate the first snow of the year.
Assistant: Great. Please take a photo, and I will post it tonight at eight with a message about the first snow.
Person: Thank you.

Karim worked at a desk next to a window that looked out at the highway. The air in the office felt dry and heavy, and the room was dim because the clouds were thick. He spoke to the speaker on his desk. 'Turn on the air purifier and speak to me when the air is clean,' he said. The speaker started the purifier on a medium setting. Twenty minutes later it said, 'The air is clean now.' Karim also asked it to switch on the humidifier and raise the light a little. The speaker did both. He took a deep breath and went back to his emails.

Person: Play my happy playlist for the shop this Saturday afternoon.
Assistant: I can do that. Which speaker should I use, the shop floor or the back room?
Person: The shop floor. Make it quiet enough that people can talk.
Assistant: Got it. I'll set it to low volume at one o'clock this Saturday.
Person: Good. The picture on the wall makes me think of home, so I like songs that make you smile and not cry.
Assistant: I'll avoid slow songs. I can't tell which songs make people cry, but I can skip any song you say.
Person: That works.

Person: I'm late. Find a parking spot near the office.
Assistant: Sure. Which office, and how long will you be there?
Person: Park Street. I park there every Monday at nine, and I'm away until noon.
Assistant: There is a lot two minutes away with a free bed of spaces by the side gate. Should I pay for three hours?
Person: Yes, and fill it up every Monday if you can.
Assistant: I can pay for today. I can't pay every Monday automatically, but I can remind you at eight forty-five.
Person: Fine, do that.

Budi was a student who was going to visit his aunt for a short trip. On a rainy evening he put on his black jacket and sat down to study, but then he remembered the hotel. He said to the assistant, 'Find a room for two nights starting Friday.' The assistant looked and found a small hotel near the station. 'Sorry, I mean three nights, not two,' said Budi. The assistant changed it to three nights and asked if he wanted breakfast. 'Yes, please,' he said. The assistant saved the booking details in his notes and told him check-in was after two in the afternoon.

Min-jun drove a taxi, and one morning he had to pick up a friend from the airport. He put a pot of coffee in his bag and sat in the car. He said to his phone, 'When does flight two seven nine land?' The assistant checked and said it would land at ten fifteen, which was twenty minutes away from the time he thought. 'Is it late?' he asked. 'No, it is on time,' the assistant said. 'Tell me when it lands, and when the gate is known,' said Min-jun. The assistant said it would. He finished his coffee and drove toward the airport.

Sunita was a retired teacher who felt scared of making mistakes with money. One quiet morning she spoke carefully to her phone. 'Could you please move two hundred dollars from my savings to my everyday account? I have to pull cash out for the plumber tomorrow, and I would like to have it ready.' The assistant said it had moved two hundred dollars between her own accounts and read out the new balances. Sunita smiled. 'Thank you,' she said. 'And remind me to take my shopping cart to the market at ten.' The assistant set the reminder, and she felt a lot calmer.

Person: Start the robot vacuum.
Assistant: Which room should it clean, the shop floor or the back office?
Person: The shop floor. Actually, no, the back office first, then the shop.
Assistant: Okay, back office first. The wide hallway comes after. Should it also change the filter reminder?
Person: Yes, I think the filter is full of dust from the luggage boxes.
Assistant: I can't change the filter myself, but I can set a reminder for you to do it tonight.
Person: Please do. Thanks.

Irina sat at her office desk. It was a loud afternoon, with phones ringing everywhere, and she had to get to the post office before it closed. She whispered to the assistant on her phone, 'My parcel needs to go out today, and I haven't got time to wait.' The assistant understood. It looked up the post office on Elm Road and said it closed at five thirty. It also found a note saying the queue was short at four. Irina asked it to design a quick route there and back, and it showed a short walk. She grabbed the parcel, left a message for her boss, and walked out toward the old cinema, where the post office was next door.

Mehmet had just woken up, and his eyes were still half shut. The bank was far from his house, so he used his phone. 'What's my balance, and move fifty into my savings,' he said. The assistant read out the balance and said it had moved fifty from his everyday account to his savings. 'Tag that as rent money,' Mehmet added. The assistant put a tag on the move. Then he asked it to read the email from the bank. It said the message was about a new card and had nothing urgent. Mehmet nodded, got up and made breakfast.

Birthdays are days when people say happy birthday and give small gifts. A gift can be a toy, a book or a warm scarf. Some people like to save ideas all year, so they have a minimum worry when the day comes. Cards are sent a few days early so they arrive in time. Like the wind, dates can slip away, so many people ask a phone to remember them. They say remind me of Dad's birthday next week, or give me ideas for a gift for a ten-year-old. They might also say buy a card for Gran, or change the reminder to the day before.

Linh was a retired teacher who lived alone, and she was always careful about her house. On the first of May, her son was coming to stay, and she had to give him a way in. She said to the smart lock, 'Make a new code for my son, and keep it working until Sunday.' The lock created a new code and said it would stop working on Sunday evening. 'Increase the time on the old guest code by one day,' she added. The lock did that. Then she asked it to send the new code to her son as a message, and she put the paper document with the old one in the bin.

A flight has a time when it leaves and a time when it lands. At the airport, a board shows each flight and the gate number. Sometimes a flight is delayed, which means it leaves later than planned. A passenger who waits at home can check the board on their phone. People say when does my flight leave, or is it late. If the gate moves, they ask which gate now. Some people jog through the airport when the gate is far away. A deep breath helps if you worry. At home, people ask what time to leave for the airport, so they arrive about two hours before.

Cooling means keeping a home from getting too hot. A fan moves air around the room, and an air conditioner makes the air itself colder. On an average summer day, many people only need a fan. When the heat is strong, they turn on the air conditioner. People say make it cooler, set it to twenty-two degrees, or turn it off at night. If a room is too cold, they say let it warm up a bit. Many people ask the assistant to turn the cooling on before they get home, for example by Thursday afternoon, so the house is already cool.

Hugo was not good with technology, but his daughter had shown him how to speak to his phone. On Friday morning he had to go to the dentist, and his car was in the garage. He said slowly, 'Please call me a taxi to take me to Baker Street on Friday morning at nine.' The assistant asked for his address, and Hugo told it. It booked a ride and said the car would be at the door at eight forty. Hugo wanted a receipt printed, so he asked for the printer at home to print it, and the assistant sent the page there. He waited inside until the taxi arrived. The driver rounded the corner on time.

Many families make rules for screen time, bedtime and chores. A child may have thirty minutes of tablet time after homework. At bedtime, a parent might read a story or play a quiet one on a speaker. A digital timer can tell the child when time is up. Parents change the rules as kids grow, and they use words like give me ten more minutes, or move bedtime to eight thirty. On school days, someone has to do the school run, and people say remind me to pick up Sam at three, or move the chore list to Saturday. A simple list on the wall helps.

Clara came home after a night shift at the hospital. The flat was cold, and she was afraid the pipes would freeze. A bucket stood under the window to catch a drip. "Please set the heating to nineteen degrees," she said to the thermostat. "And warm the bedroom first, I'm so tired." The assistant answered, "Heating is set to nineteen. The bedroom radiator is on now." Clara sat on the bed near the radiator and listened to it click. Then she said, "Turn it down to eighteen when I fall asleep." The assistant said it would lower the heat at ten o'clock. Clara was asleep before it did.

Dana was nine years old, and the family speaker in the kitchen was her favourite thing. After school she pulled a chair up to the counter. "Make the volume lower and play this song in the living room too," she said. The speaker answered, "Okay, I made it quieter and now it is playing in the living room as well." Soon both speakers played the same song. Her big brother shouted something rude from the stairs about the noise, and Dana laughed. "Make the hall speaker quiet," she said. The speaker set the hall to zero, and Dana danced on her chair.

When a family moves house, the post office needs to know the new address. This is called a change of address, and it makes sure letters find you in your new home. My grandfather forgot to do it, so his letters went to strangers for a month. People say things like "I've moved, send my mail to 4 Pine Road" or "Change where my bills go." They may also say, "Switch my electricity to the new house from Monday." The movers pack the boxes, but a dangerous thing like a can of gas must stay behind. On the first day, neighbours often welcome the new family with a cake.

Rosa had just moved to the city, and the air in her small flat felt heavy. A yellow haze hung over the street. She stretched her arms and asked her phone, "Is the air outside bad today?" The assistant said the air quality number was one hundred and fifty, which was unhealthy for people with weak lungs. Rosa nodded. "Then please turn on the air purifier and tell me when I should change the filter," she said. The assistant switched on the purifier in the bedroom and said the filter had about twenty days left. Rosa kept the windows shut, and by evening the air smelled cleaner.

Smart bulbs let you change a lamp without touching it. A light is for seeing, but also for mood. If you are sick in bed, a bright ceiling light hurts, so you want it low and warm. People say "Make it dimmer," "Turn the lamp to yellow," or "Switch off the bedroom light in five minutes." The bulb counts the minutes and then turns itself off, so you do not have to get up. Some people ask for a different colour for reading and another for the evening. Short words work well too: "brighter," "softer," "off."

Valentina was planning the big family dinner for the holidays. She sat in her armchair with an empty cup of tea and spoke to her tablet. "Remind me on Saturday to buy decorations," she said. Then she shook her head. "No, wait, Sunday. The shops close early on Saturday." The assistant said, "Okay, I changed the reminder to Sunday morning." Valentina smiled. Next she asked it to disconnect from the old speaker in the hall, because it was too loud, and to read a chapter of the story book to her grandchildren. The assistant did both, and the house became quiet and warm.

A voice note is a note you say out loud instead of typing. It is useful when your hands are busy or sore. I like to talk into my phone while I walk a mile to work, and the idea is saved for later. People say "Make a note: buy stamps," "Add milk to my shopping note," or "Find my note about the dentist." When a note is wrong, they say "Change the date in my last note to Friday" or "Delete that note." Old notes can be found by a word you remember, like "find the note with the word garden."

A to-do list is a short list of things you need to do. Tom keeps his on his phone: buy one kilogram of apples, fix the dripping tap, and draw a square on the calendar for Saturday's party. When a task is done, he checks it off and it goes away. People change their lists all day. They say "Add call the bank to my list," "Move laundry to tomorrow," or "Put the dentist at the top." They also say "Tick off the tap," "What's still left today?" and "Remove the apples." A list helps you not to forget.

Bo worked in a cold office, and the only warm thing was the cap on his head. At nine o'clock he spoke to the smart thermostat on the wall. "Set the office to twenty-two degrees," he said. The assistant answered that the building was divided into zones and that his zone was now heating up. Bo asked, "Keep it on for sixty minutes, then lower it a little." The assistant said, "Okay, twenty-two for the next hour, and then twenty." Soon his fingers felt better. Bo took off the cap and went back to his email.

Alessandro ran a small bookshop, and every winter the front room got cold. One Monday morning a student came in shivering. "Turn the heating up to twenty and switch off the heater in the back room," Alessandro said to the shop assistant app on his phone. "Okay, the front is now set to twenty, and the back heater is off," it answered. Then he added, "Label the new thermostat Front Shop." "Done," said the assistant. "The name is saved. Is that correct?" Alessandro checked the screen and nodded. The student sat down with a book, warm at last.

Colin had ten quick minutes before the school run. His daughter Ivy had to practice her violin, and the kitchen was a mess. "Play Ivy's practice playlist and turn the volume down a little," he said to the speaker. The assistant answered right away, "Playing Ivy's practice playlist at a lower volume." Soft violin music filled the room. Ivy tapped her foot and played along with the second song. Colin found her shoes under the table and her bag by the door. When the song ended, he asked the speaker to stop the music, and they walked to school together.

A work meeting is a call where people meet on a screen. Before it starts, someone posts the agenda in the chat, so everyone knows what will be talked about. To join, you open the link in your email and press the join button. People change small things all the time. They say "Mute my microphone," "Share my screen," or "Turn my camera off." Some like a picture behind them, like a butterfly or a blue sky. At the end, people say "Leave the meeting" or "Send me the notes." A good meeting is short and clear.

Dragan was a retired teacher, and on Thursdays he looked after his grandson Luka. The boy dropped his boots by the door, a pair of muddy green ones, and ran to the table. "Excuse me," Dragan said to the assistant on his phone, "could you please set a reminder for four o'clock tomorrow, because Luka has a spelling test and I want to be ready to practise the words with him?" The assistant said, "Reminder set for four o'clock tomorrow: spelling practice with Luka." Dragan thanked it. When the evening came, he was ready with a list of words and a pencil.

Ahmed lay in bed with the blanket over his head. For a fraction of a minute he did not want to move. Then a sudden cold wind rattled the window. "The car is warming up," it said. "It will be ready in ten minutes." Ahmed smiled, closed his eyes for a bit longer, and then got up to find his coat. When he went out, the windscreen was clear.

Tonight after dinner, Freya sat down with her tablet and a cup of tea. She was a retired teacher, and she liked to check her money every week. "Show me how much I spent on food this month," she said. The assistant read out a number. "Is it true that I spent more than last month?" she asked. "Yes, about ten percent more," the assistant said. Freya sighed. Her grandson's drum lessons had cost a lot too. "I'd like to keep my food spending under two hundred next month," she said. The assistant saved the limit and promised to warn her.

When a courier brings a package, you often have to sign for it. Today many people sign by swiping a finger across a small screen. If you are not home, the courier leaves a card, or puts the parcel with a neighbour. People change this all the time. They say "Leave it with my neighbour," "Hold my parcel until Monday," or "Don't ring the bell, the baby is asleep." Some parcels are flat boxes with a shelf inside, and the screws come in a small bag. Letters just go into the mailbox, and you open the door of the box with a small key.

Caleb was driving home with the baby asleep in the back seat. He did not want to look at his phone. "Could you please text my cousin Jo that I'll be twenty minutes late, because the baby just fell asleep in the car and I don't want to wake her by stopping?" he asked quietly. The assistant said, "I'll send Jo a message: running twenty minutes late. Is that okay?" Caleb said yes. The assistant dimmed the screen so the light would not bother the baby. A strong wind pushed the car a little, but she slept on. Jo wrote back with a thumbs up.

Air conditioning takes warm air out of a room and blows in cool air. A fan only moves the air, so the room does not get cooler, but you feel better. People change the temperature or the speed all day. They say "Make it a bit cooler," "Set the air conditioner to twenty-four," or "Turn the fan down, it's too loud." My old unit was hard to use, but the new one can connect to a phone. The manual document has a long list of buttons. Most people just say "Turn on the cooling at five" and come home to a nice room.

A packing list helps you remember what to take when you go camping. It might say: tent, sleeping bag, water, snacks, and a yellow raincoat that fits in your pocket. The weather in the hills can change fast, so people check it before they leave. They say "What's the weather on Saturday up at the lake?" or "Add a torch to my packing list." If the plan changes, they say "Move the trip to next weekend." On the trail, if you will be late, you can text a friend to say where you are, so nobody worries.

Miriam stood at the bus stop with her two small children and a heavy bag. "Don't buy a day ticket, I only need a single one for each of us," she told the assistant on her phone. "Okay, I'll buy three single tickets for the number twelve bus," it said. Miriam wanted to be sure the stop was correct, so she asked, "What is the name of the stop near the museum?" The assistant spelled it out slowly, letter by letter. The tickets appeared on the screen just as the bus came around the corner, and the children cheered.

"Dim the kitchen lights a little, I'm tired," Hassan said. The assistant dimmed them. He looked at the list and liked it. Then he asked it to make a shopping list from the plan and send it to his phone.

Zana was new to the city, and her baby was only three months old. It was late at night, and she could not remember what had happened at the last feeding. Zana held the baby, skin to skin, and whispered thanks. The assistant said it would send a message to her phone if the baby made a sound. Whatever might happen, she felt calmer.

Jonah felt sick and stayed home from school. A parcel was waiting for him at the post office, and he wondered if it was still open. He picked up his phone and typed two words: "Post office?" The assistant told him it closed at five o'clock and was a ten minute walk from his flat. Jonah wrote, "Remind me." The assistant set a reminder for four o'clock that said, pick up the parcel. Then Jonah asked, "How much is the fee?" The assistant said the fee was three euro and that the clerk took coins. Jonah smiled, put a few coins in his pocket, and rested on the sofa until the reminder buzzed.

A booking is a promise to be somewhere at a set time. People make bookings for haircuts, the dentist and the doctor. The shop keeps a list of times, and each time holds only one person. Opening hours tell you when you can come. Sometimes plans change, so people say, "Move my haircut to Friday," or "Cancel my dentist visit." It is true that many clinics close early on Saturday, so ask first. Most waiting rooms have an air purifier, and the chairs are comfortable. If you drive, ask where you can park near the door. If you will be late, say, "I will be ten minutes late," so they can plan.

Aiko was driving home when she remembered the kitchen speaker. Her kids had left it playing a funny song at full volume. She said to her phone, "Turn the kitchen speaker down, but don't stop the music." The assistant lowered the volume to a soft level and kept the song going. Aiko laughed and said, "Search for another funny song, but not the one about the frog." The assistant searched and added a silly song about a cat to the queue. It also said, "The dryer finished a minute ago." "Tell me later, I don't want to hear about it now," said Aiko. The assistant said it would wait, and Aiko turned onto her street smiling.

The news tells you what is happening in the world, in your town, or in sport. A headline is a short line that sums up a story. People change the topic, the place and how many stories they hear. They say, "Read me the local headlines," "Give me sports scores only," or "Skip the weather." On a slow morning you might chill with a cup of tea and hear that a food truck in the park is selling delicious soup. If you want less, say, "Just three stories." If you want more, say, "Tell me more about that one." The news keeps changing, so ask again later for fresh updates.

Person: Can you book a room for my family?
Assistant: Yes. Which city is the hotel in?
Person: Lisbon. We want to arrive early on Thursday.
Assistant: How many nights will you stay?
Person: Three nights. Does the hotel have a good network for my tablet?
Assistant: Most hotels have free wifi. I will check this one. Is there anything else you need?
Person: Can the hotel heat our room before we come?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't do that. I can send the staff a note asking them.
Person: Yes, please. Mum says the breakfast there is healthy.
Assistant: Great. I will book three nights and send the note.

Oscar came home after a night shift, tired but happy. He wanted to make a paper model for his niece's birthday. He said to his phone, "Find a good tutorial for a paper boat." The assistant found one. Then Oscar said, "Wait, I mean a paper plane, not a boat." The assistant changed the search and showed three plane tutorials. He asked it to reduce the video speed to half so he could follow along, and the assistant slowed the video. Then he asked it to write an invitation for the party on Saturday at two. The assistant read it back, and Oscar nodded and fell asleep with a paper plane on his chest.

name: word_translator
does: Translates a single word or short phrase into another language, like the word for a hat or how to say you want to paint a wall.
inputs: the word or phrase, and the language you want
people say:
- How do you say hat in Spanish?
- What is the French word for thank you?
- Translate good morning into German.
- I need the Italian for where is the station.
- What do they call a train in Japanese?

Alejandro was in a hurry. His grandmother, who spoke only Italian, would arrive in ten minutes, and he wanted to read her the recipe from the open book on the table. He held up his phone and said, "Say this in Italian, quick: put the plate in the oven for fifty minutes." The assistant said the sentence out loud and wrote it on the screen. Alejandro said, "Zoom in on the words, I can't read them from here." The assistant made the letters bigger. Alejandro read the line twice, set the plate in the oven, and started a timer for fifty minutes. Just then the doorbell rang, and he was ready.

Edward sat in his car outside his house after a long drive. His mother was inside, and she liked fresh air and light in the living room. He typed fast with his thumbs: "open the livng room curtains". The assistant answered, "Opening the living room curtains now." The curtains slid open, and Edward could see his mother wave from the sofa. He typed again: "and the blinds in the kitchen too". The assistant opened those as well. Edward smiled, locked the car, and walked up the path to see her.

Callum worked as a cook, and he got home late in the evening. It was October, and the grass still needed a trim before the rain. He said to his phone, "Start the robot mower at nine tomorrow morning." Then he stopped and said, "No, wait, make it ten. The neighbours sleep in." The assistant changed the start time to ten and said so. Callum also asked it to keep the mower inside the fence at the back, and the assistant saved that rule. A welcome message appeared on his screen: the mower was ready. Callum put his keys down and went to make some soup.

Person: I want to put something on my calendar.
Assistant: Of course. What is the event?
Person: A pancake party. I will slice fruit for it.
Assistant: Sounds nice. What day is the party?
Person: This Saturday afternoon.
Assistant: What time exactly?
Person: Is it true I can pick any time? Say three o'clock.
Assistant: Yes, any time. I added Pancake party on Saturday at three.
Person: Thank you. I am not good with these things.
Assistant: You did very well.

Nora had just moved to a new city, and her phone was almost full. She said, "I need free space on my phone by the end of the week. It is full of guitar videos." The assistant showed her the biggest files and said the videos used eight gigabytes. Nora chose three old videos and asked it to delete them. Then she said, "Where can I buy a charger? I have to go and feed the neighbour's cat." The assistant said there was a phone shop near her building that sold chargers and was open until six. Nora thanked it, grabbed her keys, and walked out.

Budi knelt in his garden under a grey sky when his phone buzzed. He had far too many unread emails. He said, "Show me only half of them, the newest ones first." The assistant read the five newest emails aloud. One said a package would come on Monday. Budi said, "Tell them I'll be home, and put the rest of the mail off until tomorrow." The assistant sent a short reply and hid the old mail until the next day. Budi wiped his hands and went back to push the wheelbarrow of dry leaves to the compost pile.

Person: I want to order a new iron.
Assistant: Sure. Do you want a small one or a large one?
Person: A small one, please. I only have a few shelves left.
Assistant: Where should I send it?
Person: I drive all day, so nobody is home. Send it to my work.
Assistant: What is the address at work?
Person: Fifteen Mill Road.
Assistant: Thank you. Delivery is on Thursday. Shall I finish the order now?
Person: Yes, please.

A bill tells you how much you owe for things like electricity, water or rent. The body of the bill lists what you used and what it costs. Every bill has a due date, which is the last day to pay without a fee. Many people stay calm by setting a reminder a few days early. You can change the date, the amount or the account you pay from. People say, "Remind me before the rent is due," "Pay the water bill on Friday," or "Get me the total for this month." If the total looks too big, you can ask, "Why is it higher than last month?"

Person: whats the water temprature at the beach today
Assistant: Which beach do you mean?
Person: the one near the pier. we have a beach party tonight and i want to swim
Assistant: The water there is about eighteen degrees. Do you want the tide times too?
Person: yes. and remind me to charge my phone before we go
Assistant: Done. I will remind you at five o'clock. Will you bring sun cream?
Person: yes, and my friends bring cooked fish
Assistant: That sounds like a lovely evening.

Errands are small jobs you do outside the house, like going to the post office or the bank. Each place has opening hours, and many have a long line at lunchtime. People often change the day, the time or the thing they need to pick up. They say, "Remind me to collect the parcel," "Move the bank visit to Tuesday," or "What time does the post office close?" Bring an old letter or receipt if you have one, because the clerk may ask for it. Carry heavy parcels with care so your back does not hurt. Hold the door for the next person, and wait your turn.

name: order_printer_ink
does: Orders new ink for your printer with a discount code if you have one, and sends the shop a polite note asking them to hurry the delivery.
inputs: the printer model, which colour is empty, and a discount code if you have one
people say:
- My printer is out of black ink.
- The text is coming out pale, I think it needs new cartridges.
- I need more cyan for my printer, and fast.
- Can you buy ink for my printer before the weekend?
- The red is all gone, get me a new one.

Navigation shows you how to get from one place to another. It uses a map, your position and the traffic to find a route and tell you how long the drive will take. People change the place they are going, the way they travel, or the roads they want to use. They say, "Take me to the airport," "Avoid the motorway," or "Stay off toll roads." On a long trip at night, roads are often quieter, so the drive may be faster. You can also ask, "Find a cafe on the way," if you want a tasty snack. If you miss a turn, the route changes by itself.

On a phone map, a line shows the way to go. Many maps draw the best route in blue and a slower route in grey, and some show heavy traffic in red or purple. People love to check the map before they leave, because it says how long the drive will take. They can change the end point, add a stop, or pick a different road. They say, "Show me another way," "Add a stop at the petrol station," or "Is the road clear?" In a storm with thunder and lightning, drivers often ask for a safer road. The map then looks for roads with less traffic and fewer hills.

When you book a hotel, you choose a city, the nights you will stay, and how many guests. The hotel keeps a room for you until check-in, which is often in the afternoon. People often change the dates, add a guest, or ask for a late check-out. They say, "Make it three nights instead of two," "Add one more guest," or "Can we check out at noon?" Many hotels run a breakfast in the morning, with fruit, bread and carrot juice. If you arrive early, the staff can keep your bags at the front desk, and you can wait outside in the sun or in the lobby.

Meera woke up in a cold room, and her eyes were still blurry. She picked up her phone, but the words looked like tiny ants. "I can't read anything on this thing," she mumbled. The assistant made the text bigger right away. Her screen seemed to freeze for a second, and then large, clear letters appeared. Meera said, "My eyes are too tired for my notes on the board." The assistant understood that she meant the reminder list she kept on her notes board, and it began to read the notes aloud in a calm voice. Meera lay back on the pillow and listened.

A step counter is a small tool inside most phones. It counts your steps while you walk and shows how far you went and how fast you moved. People use it to reach a daily goal, like eight thousand steps. They change the goal, the route or the length of a walk. They say, "Set my goal to ten thousand steps," "How far did I run today?" or "Undo that last walk." If you like a quiet route, you can ask for a path through the park instead of the busy road. Walking a little more each day is good for your body and your mind.

They want to know, with exact spelling and at normal speed, how to say grill in Spanish.
How do you say grill in Spanish?
Spanish for grill?
What is the Spanish word for a grill?
Translate "grill" into Spanish, please.
I run a food stand and there will be two thousand people at the fair, so what is the Spanish word for grill?
Can you tell me how to spell grill in Spanish, the exact word?
How would a person in Madrid say "I will grill the fish"?
Could you please tell me the Spanish word for grill and say it out loud?

Bence was new to the city and wanted to watch a football match. It was a cloudy afternoon, and he sat at the window with a cup of tea. He said, "When does the home team play next?" The assistant said they played on Saturday at seven. Bence asked, "Is that earlier than last week?" The assistant said yes, it was two hours earlier. He then asked it to make a reminder and show him double the usual news about the team, because he wanted to learn more about them. The assistant listed six stories and read the first one aloud. Bence smiled and finished his tea.

An alarm wakes you up at a set time, and a timer counts down from a set length, like ten minutes. People often use alarms for the morning and timers for cooking. When they need a change, they say, "Wake me at six thirty," "Snooze for five minutes," or "Set a timer for the pasta." You can also say, "Cancel my alarm" or "Make it half an hour later." Pay attention to the sound: a soft sound is gentler in the morning. If the sun is bright when you wake up, you might want your sunglasses by the bed. It is good to check the time before you sleep.

Nathan ran a small shop, and he had to take a box of cakes to a customer across town. He carried the box down the stairs and put it in the van. The streets were busy, so he typed on his phone: "fastest way to the bakry on elm street, skip the motorway". The assistant showed a route that took twelve minutes and avoided the motorway. The route followed a thin road along the river. Nathan put the phone on the dashboard, checked the box one more time, and set off.

Amani, a student, was hosting a small party in her flat. Her friends were patient, but the room felt dull. "It's so quiet in here," she said to her speaker. The assistant started a lively playlist at a medium volume. A while later Amani said, "The floor is so sticky." The assistant understood she wanted to remember cleaning, so it added a note: mop the floor after the party. It also reminded her about the payment she owed for the pizza. Amani laughed, paid by phone, and her friends began to dance.

name: close_blinds_by_time
does: Lowers the blinds a set amount at a set time so the red evening sun stays out of your eyes.
inputs: which room, how far to close them (half, most or all), and the time you hope to have them closed
people say:
- The sun is in my eyes.
- Make the bedroom darker at six.
- Close the shades halfway in the kitchen.
- It's too bright in the lounge.
- Can you pull down the blinds before I get home?

name: start_watch_party
does: Starts a show at the same time for you and your friends and sends each friend an invite.
inputs: the show, who to invite, and the time; friends need the streaming app inside their TV, and you can add a reminder to bring the popcorn bucket
people say:
- Let's watch the last episode with Sam tonight.
- Can my sister watch this with me from her house?
- Start the movie for all of us at eight.
- I want to see the game with my cousins, set it up.
- Get everyone to press play together.

A lawn needs a regular cut so the grass stays short and smooth. A robot mower does this by itself: it moves around the garden, cuts a little, and goes back to its charger. In September the grass grows more slowly, so people cut it less often. People change the days, the height of the cut, and where the sprinklers go. They say, "Mow the lawn on Friday," "Cut the grass shorter," or "Move the sprinkler to the back garden." If it rains, they might say, "Skip the mower today." Edges can be trimmed with a small tool.

Joao was in a hurry to catch the bus. The distance to the stop was long, and his flat felt cold. He said, "Set the heating to twenty-two degrees." Then he stopped at the door and said, "No, twenty. It is too expensive to keep it hot while I'm away." The assistant changed the plan to twenty degrees and told him it would warm the flat again at six, when he came home. Joao also asked it to turn off the bathroom heater. He picked up his bag, thanked the assistant, and ran for the bus.

They want the sprinklers to water the garden now.
Water the garden.
Sprinklers on, please.
Give the plants a drink.
The soil is dry, can you start the sprinklers?
I have a late shift at work today, so could you please water the garden for me before I leave?
Please turn on the sprinklers for ten minutes. I have homework to finish and I can't go outside.
The plants look thirsty, so water them.
Run the sprinklers, the water in the old can has gone stale.

name: find_showtimes
does: Finds cinema showtimes for a film and tells you if there are extra late shows.
inputs: the film's name, the town or the cinema near your gym or the old iron bridge, and the day
people say:
- What time is the new Batman film on tonight?
- Is anything good playing near me on Saturday?
- When can I see the dinosaur movie this weekend?
- Are there any late shows after nine?
- I want to take the kids to the cinema tomorrow, what's on?

name: tv_show_alert
does: Tells you when a show you like is about to come on and switches the TV to that channel, so you have time to get a drink if you are thirsty.
inputs: the show's name (like a cooking show about a chocolate factory), the channel, and how many minutes before it starts
people say:
- Tell me when my cooking show starts.
- I always miss the news at six.
- Switch to channel four when the match begins.
- Remind me before the quiz show tonight.
- Don't let me forget the new episode on Friday.

Seren was new to the city, and her science assignment was due on Friday. The library was silent, so she typed on her phone instead of talking: "when is my scienc homework due". The assistant answered, "Friday at nine in the morning." Her project was about how fast, or at what speed, bean plants grow. Seren typed, "how often should i water a bean plant". The assistant said every two days and added a reminder to her calendar. Seren gave a small smile and went back to her notes.

Person: It's freezing in this empty flat.
Assistant: Do you want me to turn on the heating? Which room?
Person: The living room. The movers left the door open and I keep sneezing.
Assistant: I'm sorry. I turned the heating on in the living room. Should it come on daily at this time?
Person: Just today. Can you also pack my boxes?
Assistant: I can't pack boxes, but I can make a list for you.
Person: OK, put a bottle of water on the list.

Zawadi sat on her bed and texted her assistant. Her birthday was close, and she was planning a party. She wrote, "How many days until my birthday, and dim the lights." The assistant said there were forty-one days left and dimmed the lamp. Zawadi wanted a cake in a big size, so she asked for bakery ideas. The assistant listed three bakeries with delicious chocolate cakes and showed the sizes. Zawadi picked the middle size, smiled, and put her phone down beside her pillow.

Sipho got home after a night shift at the hospital and wanted to paint before sleeping. He said, "Open my painting app and select the big blue brush." The assistant opened the app and chose the big blue brush. Sipho was painting a storm with lightning over the sea. Then he said, "Sorry, I mean the thin brush, the lightning needs thin lines." The assistant changed the brush. Sipho also asked for a timer for one hour so he would not forget to sleep, and then he ate a juicy orange while the paint dried.

Fiona was nervous. Her cousin lived in Sydney, and she wanted to call her, but she did not want to wake her. Fiona was lying on her bed after a shower with her hair still wet. She typed just two words: "Sydney time?" The assistant answered, "It is seven in the morning in Sydney." Fiona thought it over, then wrote, "Call Maya." The assistant started the call. Her cousin picked up and said hello, wide awake. Fiona let out a long breath and smiled.

name: bedtime_wind_down
does: Starts a quiet routine before bed that dims the lights, puts the phone on silent and plays soft sounds instead of talk radio.
inputs: your bedtime, the sound you like, and the brand of your sound machine if you have one
people say:
- Help me get ready for bed.
- I want to wind down this evening.
- It's ten o'clock, time to sleep soon.
- Make my room calm before I go to bed.
- I can't sleep, play something soft.

Water comes into a home through a pipe, and a meter counts how much you use. Some of the pipes run inside the wall, so a leak can stay hidden for days. A water heater, often upstairs or in a cupboard, keeps water warm for showers. A leak sensor can warn you when water is on the floor. People ask for changes like, "Turn the water heater down," "Tell me how much water I used this week," or "Warn me if there's a leak." After a long, hot shower, open the window to let the room breathe. Small changes can save water and money.

Person: Tell me what two pounds is in kilos and what 350 Fahrenheit is in Celsius.
Assistant: Two pounds is about 0.9 kilos, and 350 Fahrenheit is about 177 Celsius.
Person: Good. I'm baking for a party in the shop and I'm in a rush.
Assistant: That sounds simple enough. Do you need anything else?
Person: Yes, change my cups of flour to grams.
Assistant: How many cups of flour do you have?
Person: Four.
Assistant: Four cups of flour is about 500 grams.

Javier was a busy parent, and his daughter's school bake sale was on Saturday. He said, "Print the flyer for the bake sale, but don't use colour ink. It costs too much." The assistant printed ten copies in black and white. Javier looked at one and said it was good enough. Then he said, "Email a copy to the bakery on Main Street." The assistant sent the flyer to the bakery and told him the email was gone. Javier pinned a copy on the fridge and went to get dinner ready.

Writing often starts with a rough draft. You put your ideas down first, and then you fix them. Editing means reading it again to spot mistakes in spelling, words and sentences. A word count tells you how long your text is, which matters for homework or emails. People say, "Check my spelling," "Make this shorter," or "How many words is this?" They also say, "Find a better word for big" when the right word will not come. Many people read their text out loud the night before they send it, because mistakes are easier to hear. A calm second look often makes the text better.

Hui came home after a night shift at the hospital. A box of shoes sat by the door. She slid on a shoe and said, "These pinch my toes." The assistant understood she wanted to send them back and asked, "Do you want me to start a return?" Hui said yes. The assistant made a free return label and put a mark on her calendar: drop the box at the post office on Wednesday. She had bought the shoes for a camping trip, so she also asked for a bigger size. The assistant ordered one. Hui yawned and went to bed.

Chen was a child who loved to walk. After school he asked his tablet, "How many steps did I take today, and how far is the park?" The assistant said he had walked six thousand steps, and the park was one kilometre away. Chen said he wanted to go there tonight. His mum began to worry about the dark, so he asked for the walking route to be shown on the map. The assistant showed a lit path. Chen felt proud that he had found a safe way. He put on his shoes and waved to his mum.

Person: I don't want the heater on in my room.
Assistant: Okay. Which room should be warm instead?
Person: The bathroom. I swam for an hour and I'm cold.
Assistant: Do you want it hot or warm?
Person: Warm, not hot. Dad is cutting the grass, so he will come back soon too.
Assistant: I set the bathroom heater to twenty-four degrees and turned the heater in your room off.
Person: Thank you!

They want the room to be warmer.
Warmer, please.
Turn the heat up a bit.
Two degrees more in here.
It's rainy and my desk corner is freezing.
This cold cuts right through me, can you warm it up?
Make it a little warmer, but not as hot as yesterday.
Could you raise the heating by half a degree?
I'm cold, please give me more heat.
Would you please make the study warmer? I will be sitting at my desk all afternoon.

Camille owned a small shop and was planning a party for the neighbourhood. She said, "Add twenty-five people to the guest list." The assistant added them and asked if she wanted invitations sent. Camille said, "I don't know all their emails. Send the invitation to the ones you have." The assistant sent it to nineteen people. She also asked for music and decorations, and the assistant said it could play a happy playlist. Camille was hungry, so she ate a peach while the assistant finished the list.

name: set_reminder
does: Saves a reminder for a time or place and can update it later, like a note to make the salad before guests come or to bring something warm.
inputs: what to remember, and the time or place
people say:
- remind me to make the salad at five
- don't let me forget my umbrella when I leave work
- ping me tomorrow morning about the dentist
- I need a nudge when I get to the shop to buy milk
- move my five o'clock reminder to six

Giannis was not good with technology, so he talked to his tablet instead of touching it. "Please find me a room near the sea for two nights," he said. The tablet showed a long list of hotels. He tried to scroll with one finger, but the list jumped about and he felt lost. "Never mind, just read them to me," he said. The assistant read the first hotel. It was two kilometers from the sea, and the reviews mentioned weak wifi. "That is too far," said Giannis. "Wait, I said two nights, but my brother is coming too. Make it three nights, and a room for two." The assistant changed the search to three nights and two guests, found a hotel right on the beach, and booked it. Giannis smiled. "Good, that is what I meant."

Rafaela was still sleepy when she sat down in the kitchen with her tea. She stirred in some sugar and looked at the old heater on the wall, which made a strange noise. "Please book someone to fix my heater on Monday," she told the speaker. The speaker found a repair shop and booked a visit for Monday morning. A minute later Rafaela said, "Oh, wait. Not Monday. My grandson comes on Monday and the room will be full of people. Make it Tuesday." The speaker moved the visit and said, "Done. The repairman will come on Tuesday at nine." Rafaela nodded, finished her tea, and went to water the plants.

A cup of coffee or tea is something people like to make just right. What changes most is how strong it is and how sweet. People say "make it stronger," "less sugar," or "just a little milk." A smoothie works the same way: you might peel a banana, add some ice, and ask for it thicker or sweeter. On a cold day a sudden wish for something hot can make you order a big tea. Many cafes now let you pick your drink on the internet before you walk in, so it is ready when you arrive. At home you can also ask a voice assistant to start the kettle and make the water extra hot.

Music is for mood. When there is rain outside, many people lie on the sofa and put on soft songs. A playlist is a list of songs that go together, like cool jazz for the evening or loud songs for a run. People change the volume, skip a track they don't like, or ask for another song by the same artist. They say "turn it down," "next one," "play something calmer," or "play that band again." A speaker or a phone listens, does it, and keeps the music going while you do something else.

Neighbours often help each other. If a cat goes missing, someone puts a note on the lamp post or a message in the street group. When you hear about a lost pet or a street party, you can pass it on. People also use these groups to say that a noise is too loud late at night, for example a wireless speaker in the garden. Most people ask politely: "Could you turn it down after ten?" or "Please keep it quiet, the baby is asleep." If you want to help, you can keep your fingers crossed, send a photo of the lost pet, or ask a voice assistant to share the message with the whole street.

name: next_departure
does: Tells you when the next bus or train leaves a stop, such as the one that will drive you past the library, and can plan the round trip home.
inputs: the stop or station, and where you want to go
people say:
- when is the next bus to the library
- what time does my train go
- how long until the number 12 comes
- is the tram late today
- I need to be home by nine, when should I leave

Harriet was making soup in the kitchen, and the blender was loud. She had just split a big onion and her hands were wet. Her thoughts went to the pool outside, because the water had looked green yesterday. "Pool temperature," she said to her phone. The assistant answered, "The pool is twenty-six degrees." Then Harriet said, "Pump status." The assistant checked the pool pump and said it was working and had cleaned the water for two hours this morning. "Good," said Harriet. She asked it to remind her to buy pool chemicals on Saturday, and the assistant put that on her list. Then she went back to her soup.

Person: I just got off work. Can you set the porch lights for six tonight and remind me to buy a tree?
Assistant: Yes. What time should I remind you about the tree?
Person: Four o'clock. And I want a constant light, not the blinking one.
Assistant: Got it, a steady light at six. Should I keep it on all night?
Person: Until ten, then off. Last year's party photos are in the cloud, right?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't see your cloud photos from here. You can open the photo app to check.
Person: Okay, thanks.
Assistant: Rest well. The tree reminder and the steady porch light are both set.

name: check_saved_passwords
does: Goes through your saved logins and unpacks which ones are weak or used twice, then gives the sum of risky ones and tells you if the whole list is safe.
inputs: which password app or saved list to look at
people say:
- are my passwords safe
- which of my logins are too easy to guess
- do I use the same password twice anywhere
- check if any of my passwords leaked
- how weak are my passwords

name: free_up_storage
does: Shows what is filling a phone and lets you pick what to delete, such as a dirty pile of old screenshots, copies of the same photo and long videos of barbecue smoke.
inputs: the kind of file to look at, like photos, videos or apps
people say:
- my phone says storage is full
- I can't take any more pictures

Thabo sat at his desk with a blank canvas, a brush and a juicy orange. He typed to his phone: "find a video on how to stretch a canvas and set a timer for 20 min". The phone found a short video and started a twenty-minute timer. While the video played, Thabo learned how to pull the cloth tight over the wooden frame. He wanted to paint a portrait of his sister, and the hardest part would be her curly hair. When the timer rang, the assistant said, "Twenty minutes are up." Thabo wiped the orange juice off his fingers and picked up his brush.

It was a cold morning in November, and Mia had just come home from a long night shift. She opened the fridge. There were only a few eggs left and no milk. "Add milk and eggs to my shopping list," she told the kitchen speaker. "But not bread. I don't want bread, we still have some." The speaker added milk and eggs and said, "I did not add bread." Mia also asked for soup ingredients, because she would enjoy a hot bowl after she slept. The speaker added carrots and onions to the list. Mia yawned, thanked it, and went to bed.

Maria was cooking pasta while the kids ran around the kitchen. The speaker was playing songs from an online radio station, and it was very loud. "Make it half as loud," she said. The speaker lowered the volume to half. Then she said, "Set a timer for ten minutes." The speaker set a ten-minute timer. When it rang, the speaker said, "Ten minutes are up," and Maria drained the pasta. "Now stop the music," she said with a smile, "the kids want to hear a story." The speaker stopped the music and the kitchen went quiet.

Alejandro had just moved to a new city. His parents were coming for a vacation and he wanted them to feel safe. In the hall, the smoke alarm began to beep. He said to his phone, "Excuse me, could you please tell me what kind of battery a smoke alarm usually needs and where I can buy one near me, because I am new here, my parents arrive on Friday, and I want the flat to be comfortable and safe for them?" The assistant said most alarms use a nine-volt battery, but he should check the old one to be sure the new one would fit. It then added "9-volt battery" to his shopping list and showed two shops nearby that open early.

A cycling app is a little notebook for your rides. It records the route, the distance, and how fast you went. Some people ride after a morning jog, and the app can sync with a watch so both are saved together. People change what they see: the distance in miles or kilometres, the map with a big zoom, or the speed on each hill. They say things like "how far did I ride today," "show me last week's rides," or "what was my fastest time." Before a ride they might ask for a route that avoids busy roads. After it, they send the map to a friend.

They want to know when the next match begins.
When does the game start?
What time is kickoff tonight?
Is the silver team playing today?

I hope I don't miss the start of the match tonight.
My dad keeps asking if the game is on yet.

Would you mind telling me the starting time of the big game on Saturday?

Noah was at the market, looking at a tiny jar of saffron. It was a pricey spice, and he started to worry about money. He took out his phone and typed fast: "how much have i spnt on food this month". The assistant added up his food payments and answered, "You have spent 340 dollars on food so far this month, and your budget is 400." That did not cheer Noah up much. "Ok, so skip the saffron," he said. The assistant took the saffron off his list and told him there were sixty dollars left for the month. Noah bought a cheaper pepper and went home.

Simon woke up in the middle of the afternoon after a late night. His laptop screen was black. "Restart the computer and open the folder with my bicycle photos," he mumbled to the assistant. The computer restarted, and a minute later the folder opened on the screen. There was also a message on the screen: an invite to his cousin's party on Sunday. "Say yes to the invite," he said, and the assistant sent the reply. Then Simon made some coffee and started to look through the photos.

Walter was in the library, wearing one glove because his hand was cold. He had a stale sandwich in his bag and an essay due soon. The text on the page was tiny. He typed to his phone: "make the text biger and read this page out loud". The phone made the letters bigger and began to read the page into his earphones in a calm voice. "Use a slower voice," Walter whispered, and the phone slowed down. He ate a bite of the sandwich, picked up his pen, and took notes while the page was read to him.

A photo is a small memory you can keep. You take one with a phone, and it goes into an album with the others, like a thick book of pictures you carry in your pocket. People take photos of a cat on the sofa, a meal, or a friend's birthday. Then they change things: they crop a picture, make it brighter, or send it to family. They say "share this with Mum," "make a new album called holiday," or "take a screenshot." Some phones listen for a word like "cheese" and take the picture by voice, which helps when your hands are full or the phone is far away.

Person: I need movers for Saturday.

Person: 14 Willow Road. Sorry, no, it is 41 Willow Road.
Assistant: Got it, 41 Willow Road. How many rooms need to be packed?
Person: Three bedrooms and a long hallway full of boxes. My sister will fly in to help, so maybe we only need two movers.

Person: Yes, please tell the teacher, and write it as 41 Willow Road.
Assistant: Done. I booked two movers for Saturday and sent the new address to the school.

They want to move a meeting to a later time. The direction is always later, and they want a fresh slot.
Push my four o'clock back an hour, but don't cancel it.
Move the team call later today, not to tomorrow.
Can you shift my meeting to the afternoon?
I have to get the groceries home before the ice cream melts, so move my call to five and don't make it any earlier.
Not tomorrow morning, put the dentist after lunch.
Make my meeting later, please, I don't want to rush.
Would you mind finding a different time for Friday's meeting? Not before noon, I wouldn't make it.

Meal planning means deciding what you will eat for the week before you go shopping. It helps you save money and avoid the question of what to cook every night. Some people plan around a low sugar diet, some pack lunches for school, and some want a big dinner after a swim at the pool. A plan might say pasta on Monday, soup on Tuesday, and leftovers on Wednesday. People change it by saying "swap Tuesday and Thursday," "no meat on Friday," or "I want something quick tonight." A good assistant tries to understand what you like and then makes a shopping list for the meals.

Marlene was stopped at a red light when her phone buzzed. She sneezed and then said, "Read my new messages out loud and make the text bigger on the screen." The phone read the first message: it was a booking confirmation from the garage for her car on Thursday. The text on the screen grew bigger, but the voice was very quiet, set at the minimum volume. "Turn it up," she said. The assistant raised the volume and read the next message, and the light turned green.

Dana had just moved to the city and wanted to cook something simple. She had half a loaf of stale bread. "How long do I bake bread pudding at 200 degrees?" she asked the kitchen speaker. Then she changed her mind. "Wait, I meant 180 degrees." The speaker said, "At 180 degrees, bread pudding takes about forty minutes," and it started a timer. Dana switched on the oven light and watched the pudding. The doorbell rang, so she said, "Pause the timer." Five minutes later she came back and said, "Resume the timer." The speaker started it again.

Mehmet worked in a restaurant kitchen and came home tired. The shower water was only lukewarm, and the family-size water heater, which sits in the cellar, seemed to be failing. "Could you please check if the water heater is working, because the shower has been cold since this morning and my wife wants a bath when she gets home?" he asked. The assistant said the heater was on but set too low, at forty degrees. It raised it to fifty-five. Then it said a sensor had found a small leak near the west wall and offered to book a plumber. Mehmet said yes.

A focus timer helps you work without drifting. You pick a time, like twenty-five minutes, and work until it rings. Then you take a short break and pull yourself away from the screen. People use timers to remember an appointment, to cook, or to study. Some timers turn red when the time is nearly up. Routines work the same way: a morning routine might list wake up, wash, breakfast, and leave. People change them by saying "make my break five minutes longer," "start a thirty-minute timer," or "remind me to stand up every hour."

Emre woke up cold in a hotel room he did not know. The window was open, and the floor was chilly. He rubbed his eyes and said to the room tablet, "Check-in time?" The tablet said, "Check-in starts at three, and check-out is at eleven." He did not understand the second part, so he asked, "What does that mean?" The tablet explained that he had to leave the room by eleven. Emre then said, "Late checkout?" and the tablet asked the front desk, which gave him until noon. He smiled and closed the window.

Babies like a plan. They eat, sleep and play at about the same times each day, so parents keep a simple schedule. A feeding might be every three hours, and a nap after lunch. Some parents keep a file of notes on how much the baby ate and slept. A baby monitor lets you hear and see the room when you are in another one. People change the times by saying "move the nap to two," "remind me about the bottle at six," or "turn on the monitor." It is easy to forget things when you are tired, so many parents ask an assistant to remember them. Many babies also have a favorite song to fall asleep to.

A dishwasher is a machine that cleans plates and cups for you. You load it, add soap, pick a program, and let it run. Some programs are quick, and some use more heat for dirty pans. People change the program, the start time, or the strength. They say "start the dishwasher after dinner," "use the short wash," or "stop it for a moment." On a stormy night, some people wait to run it, because a power cut would stop the cycle. The same goes for a washing machine when you have a big pile of laundry. A voice assistant can start either one, if they are connected.

Giulia owned a small flower shop. Tonight her sister would lock up, so Giulia wanted the alarm set. "Turn on the shop camera and the door alarm, but don't record inside the back room," she told the assistant. The assistant turned on the front camera and the door alarm and left the back room camera off. "Is that correct?" it asked. "Yes, that is correct," said Giulia. She added, "And I don't want alerts for the cat at night. I only want to hear about people." The assistant set the camera to send an alert only when it could notice a person. Giulia smiled, waved goodbye, and went home.

Ursula was baking bread and a yogurt cake at the same time, and her kids came into the kitchen to join her. "Set the oven for 180 degrees and give me an hourly reminder about the dough," she said. The oven began to heat up, and the assistant said, "The oven is on. I will remind you every hour." After an hour the speaker said, "Time to check the dough." It had risen well, and the kids pressed it gently with their fingers. Ursula laughed and put the cake in the oven.

A kettle is a good example of a simple kitchen machine. You fill it with water, put it on its base, plug it in, and press a button. It boils the water and clicks off by itself. People use it for tea, soup, or instant noodles. Some kettles let you pick the heat, from warm to boiling. People change that by saying "heat the water to eighty degrees" or "make it boil." If the kettle is new, you may need to dig out the manual to see how. A smart kettle can start when you say "put the kettle on," so the water is ready when you walk in.

Keoni thanked it and decided to send more messages instead.

Can you lock the front door but not the garage? I don't want the garage locked, my son still has to come in," he said slowly to the little speaker. The speaker answered, "I locked the front door. The garage is still open." Daniel breathed out and smiled. It had been easier than he thought.

Lucia spent most of her day in the car. Today she wanted to hear about the train delays on the radio. "Tune in to the news station tomorrow morning at seven," she told the car assistant. The assistant saved the station and said the radio would turn on at seven. Then Lucia added, "Tonight after dinner, play the monthly music show on my favorite station." The assistant set a second reminder for the show. Lucia smiled, because now she would not have to search for either one while driving.

Mathieu was texting on the sofa when he looked in the fridge and found only a lemon. He typed to his phone assistant, "we're out of milk and cereal again lol". The assistant understood and added milk and cereal to the shopping list. "Want me to remind you when you're near the shop?" it asked. "Yes," Mathieu typed. He had a receipt from last week in his pocket and took a photo of it so he would remember the prices. Later he would visit the supermarket on the east side of town, and the phone buzzed with the list when he arrived.

Tamar was texting her friends about dinner. "Can you book a table for four at the noodle place this Saturday afternoon? We just want to chill, nothing fancy," she asked her phone. The phone checked the restaurant and found a table at three o'clock. It booked it and sent the details to her friends. Tamar also asked, "Is the service fast? We only have an hour." The assistant said the reviews call the service fast, and it added that the menu sells water by the liter, which made Tamar laugh.

Clocks tell us what time it is, and time zones tell us that the time is different in other places. When it is noon in London, it is often seven in the morning in New York. Long ago people used a pencil to write down the time on a paper chart; now a phone keeps it. Most phones pick the right time for where you are, but you can add other cities. People ask "what time is it in Tokyo," "is it morning in Sydney," or "set my clock to home time." Even on a trip, your home city can stay as a permanent clock on the screen.

Ahmed was kneeling in his garden with muddy gloves and a sore tooth. He could not decide whether to water the beans. He tapped his phone and said, 'Rain today?' The assistant checked the forecast and said no rain was coming until Thursday, and it would be sunny and warm until then. Ahmed wished to learn more, so he asked, 'Can you give me the weekly forecast for the garden?' The assistant read it out: sun on Monday and Tuesday, clouds on Wednesday, showers on Thursday, then dry again. Ahmed nodded and watered the beans. Then he asked for a reminder in the evening to cover the tomatoes if the wind picked up. The assistant said the reminder was set for seven o'clock. Ahmed pressed a hand to his cheek, smiled, and went back to the roses.

Tamar woke up late and squinted at her phone. 'Show me my new likes,' she mumbled. The assistant opened her notifications and said she had forty new likes and three comments. A huge crowd had come to see her photo from July at the lake. 'Reply to the first comment with a smiley,' she said. Then she changed her mind. 'No wait, not a smiley. Say thank you.' The assistant took away the smiley and posted 'Thank you!' under the comment. Tamar yawned and asked the assistant to mute her notifications until nine. It said they were muted until nine o'clock. She pulled the blanket back over her head.

Ayita woke up early and the whole house was quiet. Her brother had left a note on the kitchen table, but it was written in Spanish. 'Translate this,' she said, holding the phone over the paper. The assistant read the words and said the note meant: the dough is in the fridge, bake it at two hundred degrees for thirty minutes. Ayita opened the fridge. The dough had risen to the top of the bowl. 'Timer thirty minutes,' she said. The assistant started a thirty minute timer. She checked that the oven door was closed and turned the heat on. When the timer rang, the whole kitchen smelled like warm bread.

'Never mind, we'll take the car,' said Mom. Aiko cheered and grabbed her shoes.

Ananya was packing lunches when she remembered her father's check-in. 'Call Dad tomorrow at nine,' she told the assistant. Then she stopped. 'No, make it ten. He sleeps later on Sundays.' She zipped the lunch bags, kissed her kids, and ran out the door.

A podcast app keeps your place. If you stop an episode halfway, it remembers where you left off, so you can pick it up later. People change a few things about it. Some want to go faster, so they say, 'Play at one and a half speed.' Others say, 'Skip back thirty seconds' when they miss a sentence, or 'Next chapter' in an audiobook. You can drag the bar with your finger, but many just ask out loud. Shows you like can sit in your library, like books on a store shelf. You might listen while cooking something crispy in the oven, hands busy, and say, 'Pause,' or 'Go back a bit,' and the app does it.

When you order something online, the shop packs it and a driver brings it to your door. Sizes can be tricky. A shirt in medium might feel strange on you, and then you send it back for a refund or a different size. A heavy parcel, like a box of three umbrellas, may weigh a lot and take longer to arrive. People change their orders by saying, 'Make it a large,' 'Send it to my office instead,' or 'Cancel the second one.' If the box has not come, they ask, 'Where is my order?' and the shop tells them when it will arrive.
