Xiu burned the rice, and the kitchen filled with smoke. She opened a window, then picked up her phone. She was not good with apps, so she typed fast: "ordr my usual from the noodle place". The assistant looked at her past orders and said her usual was two noodle soups and a tea. It asked if that was right. Xiu typed "yes". The assistant placed the order and said it would come in thirty minutes. Xiu sat on the sofa to rest until the doorbell rang, and dinner was saved.

Meera was a student, and money was tight. She was walking to the post office to ship a parcel to her mother when she asked her phone, "Can you find a cheap haircut near campus? I want to pay less than I did last time." The assistant found a top-rated barber that cost half as much as her old salon, about fifteen dollars. It said there was a free slot on Thursday at four. "Book it," said Meera. The assistant booked the slot and added it to her calendar. Meera smiled, dropped off the parcel, and walked home.

Oscar was in a hurry. The pasta would cook for ten minutes, and he wanted to read while he waited. He said to his tablet, "Open my book and tell me how many pages are left in this chapter." The tablet opened the book at his bookmark and said five pages were left, about three minutes of reading. That was less than half the time the pasta needed. Oscar read fast, and his body relaxed for the first time that day. He was happy to finish the chapter before the pasta was done. "Put a bookmark here," he said, and the tablet did.

Someone wants to know which bin to sort an item into.
Which bin does this go in?
Where does a broken toaster go?
Can I recycle this?
I don't know how to sort my trash.
It's bitter cold out and I don't want to drag the wrong bin to the street.
The kitchen is full of cardboard and I have no idea where it goes.
I have a pile of old glass jars, what do I do with them?
Could you please tell me whether a plastic tub that held butter goes in the recycling or the regular trash? I would like to do it properly.

Nimal was driving to the depot when his work call started. He was bored of long meetings, and he had a rule not to look at screens while driving. "Join my nine o'clock meeting," he said to the car assistant, "but don't turn on my camera and don't read me the chat." The assistant joined by audio only, with the camera off. Nimal heard his boss talk about next week's schedule. When the call ended, he asked the assistant to remind him to book his workout for the evening. The assistant said it would, and Nimal drove on.

Roya was studying in her room when the afternoon sun hit her screen. Her fish tank sat in the bright light too. She said, "Lower the blinds on the desk window and open the curtains by the bed." The blinds went down and the curtains slid open. Now the room was calm and the tank was in the shade. Her cat tried to jump onto the desk, so Roya added, "Play some quiet music." The assistant started her personal study playlist. Roya went back to her notes and read for another hour.

Aarav unlocked his car and sat down. He had a long drive ahead and wanted to be safe, so he checked the road first. He typed to the car assistant in a hurry: "put on the trafic news on 94 fm". The assistant tuned the radio to 94 FM, and the traffic report came on. A road was closed on his usual way. Then a local band played a song, and Aarav asked the assistant to keep that station on. It did, and he took a different road to work.

Baraka owned a small shop near the forest road. The air filter in the back was full of dust, and the deep sink was blocked too. He said to his phone, "Find someone to fix my air filter and book them for Tuesday." The phone found a repair man named Lutalo who could come at ten in the morning, and it booked the slot. Baraka then said, "Remind me to lift the boxes off the floor tonight. There are fifty of them." The phone set a reminder for six in the evening, and Baraka went back to serving his customers.

After a long day in the garden, Imran went to bed early. His tie was ready on the chair for the flower market meeting in the morning. He did not want to forget the time, so he said, "Wake me at six, but not with the loud alarm. I don't want to scare the cat." The assistant set an alarm for six with a soft bird sound. Imran also asked it to turn off the electric blanket after an hour, and it did. He fell asleep with the window open and the smell of flowers in the air.

A folder is like a drawer for the files on a computer. It keeps your work in one place so you can find it later. People change how files are sorted: they rename them, move them to another folder, or tag them with a color or a word. When the computer feels slow, people often restart it, because that clears out things that were left running. They say things like "Put this file in my work folder," "Tag this photo as holiday," or "Why is my laptop so slow? Restart it." The battery and the screen brightness are also easy to change when you ask.

Taras woke up and rubbed his eyes. He had not looked at his plans yet. "Good morning," he said to the phone. "Could you please search my calendar for a free hour this afternoon? I need to buy fuel and visit the garage about a new tire, and I don't want to miss any meetings." The phone searched and said he was free between two and three. Taras said, "Put a block there called car." The phone saved it. Then Taras got out of bed and went to make coffee, feeling ready for the day.

Rodrigo moved to the city last month. His phone screen had a crack in it, and his bank account had very little money left. He asked his phone, "Could you please show me how much I spent this month on food and on my hobby? I am new here and I want to understand where my money goes, so I can plan better." The phone added up the numbers. It said he spent three hundred dollars on food and eighty on camera things. Rodrigo sighed, then asked it to set a monthly limit of two hundred and fifty for food.

The news on an assistant gives short headlines about the world, your town or sports. It is for people who want to know what is going on without reading a whole paper. People choose which topics they want, how many headlines to hear, and how often. They say things like "Read me the headlines," "Only sports, please," or "Don't read stories about celebrities." When a freezing storm is coming, many people ask for local news about the roads. Some people like the news in the morning, and others like a short summary at night.

It was a humid afternoon, and Giulia's phone battery was at nineteen percent. She was not good with phone settings. "My phone is nearly dead," she said. "I have a long train ride and no plan." The assistant said it could turn on battery saver and lower the screen brightness. Giulia said yes. It also offered to filter out noisy notifications by turning on do not disturb, and Giulia agreed. Now the phone would last through her ride. She thanked it and put the phone in her bag.

Once a month, Ravi baked bread for his neighbors. It was his monthly baking day, and he had to wait for the dough to rise. He did not want to blink and miss the oven time. He typed fast on his phone: "how lng do i bake the loaf at 200". The assistant said to bake it for thirty-five minutes at two hundred degrees. Ravi asked it to set a timer. Then he took a walk around the block while the bread baked. The timer rang when he got back, and the whole street smelled of fresh bread.

Someone wants the word count of their writing, and they can't wait to know.
Word count?
Count my words.
How long is this essay?
How many words so far?
How many words are in my essay about crispy fried chicken?

Tell me how long my story is.
Could you please tell me how many words I have written today? I need to stay under five hundred.

Assistant: Good morning! How many pancakes do you want to make?
Person: Enough for four. No, six. My cousin is staying to watch a movie with us later.
Assistant: Six it is. Do you want the recipe now?
Person: Yes. And when are they done? Mine always look pale.
Assistant: Cook each side for about two minutes, until golden. Lift the edge with a spatula to check.
Person: Great. Can you also cook them for me?
Assistant: Sorry, I can't cook, but I can set a timer for each side.
Person: Okay, thanks.

Home security means keeping your house safe when you are home and when you are away. Cameras, alarms and motion sensors watch the doors and windows. People change when the alarm is on, who gets a message, and which cameras to look at. They say things like "Turn on the alarm," "Is the front door locked?" or "Show me the back garden." A good idea before a trip is to ask for the total number of open doors and windows. When the house is empty, many people switch the alarm to away mode.

A workout is a plan of exercises, with sets and reps. A rep is doing a move one time, and a set is a group of reps. Rest days give your muscles time to recover. People change how many sets they do, how heavy the weights are, and which days they train. They say things like "Add one more set," "Make today's workout shorter," or "Is tomorrow a rest day?" Many people train with a brother or a friend, even early when it is still dark. If you do not know a move, you can ask an assistant to explain it.

A podcast is a show with many episodes, and an audiobook is a book read aloud in chapters. The player remembers where you left off, so you can go on later. People change the speed, skip ahead, or go back a little. They say things like "Play it faster," "Go back thirty seconds," or "Pick up where I stopped." Some people listen while they clean the carpet, and others listen while they roast vegetables for dinner. A well made show is easy to follow, even at a faster speed.

Kwame was nervous. He had a video interview with a company in Tokyo, and he wanted to look his best. He fixed his tie in the mirror and asked his laptop, "What time is it in Tokyo now, and what time is it here when it is nine in the morning there?" The assistant said it was already evening in Tokyo, and that nine in the morning there would be midnight in Accra. Kwame pointed at his wall clock and laughed. The interview would be very late for him. He asked the assistant to set an alarm for eleven thirty at night, and it did.

Someone wants to know how long to cook something.
how long do i cook rice
cooking time for eggs?
how many minutes for a chicken in the oven
how long shuld i roast potatoes at 200
i want to win the bake-off, how long does the cake need
how long does popcorn take, i need a snack fast
Could you tell me how long to boil pasta? It is for our yearly family dinner and I do not want to ruin it.

Jonah, a grandfather, returned home from the shops on a hot day. The bedroom was freezing because the air conditioning had been on all morning, but the living room was warm. "Turn the air conditioning off in the bedroom and put the fan on in the living room," he said to the speaker. The speaker did both and said it would keep the fan on low. Outside, a van drove past, but inside the house it was quiet and fresh. Jonah sat down with a glass of water and enjoyed the cool air.

Delroy still kept the books for his son's shop. He had a bitter cup of tea beside him and a video call about to start. "Open the invoice from Monday and share my screen with the team," he said to his laptop. The laptop opened the invoice and put it on the shared screen, so everyone could see it. Delroy talked through the numbers, then thanked the team. After the call he said, "Thank you," to the laptop too, and it answered, "You're welcome." Delroy laughed and finished his tea.

Sanne came in from the garden with dirt on her hands. She had been working in the long flower bed all morning. "Book me a dentist appointment on Tuesday at ten," she told her phone. Then she looked out of the window and remembered she had a plant sale on Tuesday. "No, make it Wednesday," she said. The phone changed the booking to Wednesday at ten and asked if it should add it to her calendar. Sanne said yes. "Can you repeat the time?" she asked. The phone said, "Wednesday at ten in the morning."

After his morning jog, Mathieu, a retired teacher, wanted to bake his favorite lemon cake. He took care to ask for a recipe without nuts, because his friend was allergic. "Find me a lemon cake recipe, but I don't want nuts, and I don't want too much sugar," he said. The assistant found a simple recipe with no nuts and a little less sugar. It read the steps slowly, and Mathieu followed along. The cake needed forty minutes in the oven. He set a timer, and soon the kitchen smelled sweet.

Mathieu was nine years old and wanted to make a snack on his own. His jeans still had flour on them from last time. The kitchen door was closed so he would not wake his dad. He typed on the family tablet, in a hurry: "how do i make toast whith no mess". The assistant said to put the bread in the toaster, push the lever down, and wait until it pops up. It reminded him to ask an adult for help with hot things. A train went by outside while he waited, and the toast popped up golden.

people say:
- Tell Mrs Lee her hedge is growing over our fence.
- Write to my boss that I'm sick today.
- Send this photo to my sister.
- Let the school know Sam will be late tomorrow.
- Drop a quick note to the plumber.

name: event_playlist

people say:
- Put some music on for Saturday's barbecue
- We need songs for a two hour dance tonight
- Something calm for dinner, please
- Can you make a party mix for my sister's birthday?
- Play happy songs while we cook outside

name: takeaway_order

- Order me a pasta from Luigi's for lunch
- Can I get a sandwich to go?
- Have dinner ready for collection on my way home
- Is it possible to order food for pickup at half past six?

Many recipes, maps and weather reports use different units, so people often need to change one kind of number into another. In autumn, a traveller may see a forecast in Fahrenheit while at home they think in Celsius. A phone can show the same number in the unit you like. When you ask, you might say "what is that in kilos?" or "show me miles instead of kilometres". The assistant will reply with the new number and the name of the unit. If a shop is closed and you only have an old tape measure in inches, you can ask "how many centimetres is that?" Most people never learn the sums. They ask in their own words, and the answer comes back at once.

A kettle has one job: to heat water fast. Inside it is a small boiler plate that gets hot and brings the water to a boil, and then the kettle clicks off. People change a few things about it. They choose how hot the water should be, because green tea likes cooler water and a sweet hot chocolate likes it nearly boiling. Some smart kettles let you say "heat it to eighty degrees" or "keep it warm for half an hour". Others listen for "start the kettle" or "make it hotter". If the water has gone cool, you can say "boil it again". Most days you say one short thing and wait for the click.

Update my address with the electricity company and cancel the old contract

Sort out my bills for the move

When you buy something in another country, the price is in a different currency. The exchange rate says how much of your money one unit of theirs is worth, and it changes through the day. A traveller might see a scooter for rent at forty euros and want to know the price at home. People ask "how much is that in dollars?" or "what is the rate today?" If the rate drops, the same price costs less at home, which can reduce the cost of a trip. Apps update the numbers fast, but they can differ a little from one to the next. You can also ask for the rate on a certain day, such as last Friday, or ask for the answer rounded to a whole number.

name: fresh_air_cycle

inputs: which room, how long, and how strong the fan should be
people say:

- Freshen up the living room before my guests arrive at eight

Tariq got home from the hospital at eight in the morning, tired but too awake to sleep. He sat on the sofa and said to his phone, "Find me a funny film for tonight and tell me what time it starts at the cinema near me." The assistant looked at the films playing nearby and listed three comedies. It picked the one with the best reviews, said the show was at seven forty, and added the time to his calendar. Tariq smiled. His taste in movies was simple: anything with no hospital in it. He felt like a parking meter running out of coins, but a perfect evening at the cinema sounded like just the thing. "Thanks," he said, and closed his eyes.

- Help me match the sky colour in this photo
- How much paint do I need for a big canvas?
- Make my blue darker without using black

When you book a hotel room, you tell the hotel a few things: the name on the booking, the day you arrive, how many nights you stay and how many guests come. Check-in is usually in the afternoon. Some places near airports offer hourly rooms for a short rest, and some campsites rent out a tent by the night instead of a room. People often change a booking by saying "add one more night", "make it for three guests" or "move it to Saturday". If you want to cancel, you can say "cancel my room" and give the name it was booked under. The hotel will usually send a note to confirm the change.

Iris was ironing her blue shirt with one hand and holding her phone with the other. Her train left in ten minutes, and she still had no shoes on. "Could you please send last night's photo of the cake to my sister Anna, because she asked for it twice and I will forget again if I wait?" she said. The assistant found the picture, a nice one with soft light over the table, and asked if it should go as a message. "Yes, please," said Iris, with a little cough from the steam. The assistant sent the photo to Anna and said it was on its way. Iris put the iron down, found her shoes, and ran for the door.

Rahul pushed his fork into the soil and wiped his hands on his trousers. He wanted some news while he worked, but his hands were too dirty to touch anything. He took out his phone, typed quickly with one thumb: play the local radio newz, and put it back on the bench. The assistant understood the small mistake. It started the local news station on the speaker by the round flower pot. Rahul went on digging and heard that rain was coming in the evening. "Better wash the tools now," he said to himself. He picked up the hose, rinsed the spade, and finished the last bed before the first drops fell.

Ben was already late for work when he heard a drip under the kitchen sink. "Check if there's a leak and turn off the water to the kitchen," he said to his phone as he put on his coat. The assistant looked at the water sensor and said there was a small leak. It shut the kitchen valve right away. It also said the water bill could rise by a few dollars if the drip had gone on all week. Ben said that was good to know and asked it to remind him at six to call a plumber. The assistant set the reminder, and Ben ran out the door.

When you order food to your door, the app asks what you want, where to bring it and when. A sandwich shop nearby cooks it, and a rider brings it to you. The app shows a delivery time that can change if the roads are busy. A tip is a little extra money for the rider, and many people choose how much just before they pay. You can change an order by saying "make it two sandwiches", "leave it at the door" or "give a bigger tip". If the food is late, you can ask "where is my order?" Some people sing along to the radio while they wait, and they are glad when the doorbell finally rings.

They want to join an online meeting with the young interns at quarter to ten.
Join the meeting

Connect me to the team call, the one that starts at nine forty five
I need to be in the call that starts soon, put me in
Open the link for the intern meeting, please
Put my calls in order and join the first one at quarter to ten
Please draw up my calls for today and join the one at quarter to ten
Could you please get me into the morning meeting at quarter to ten, because I promised the interns I would be on time?

Diego was buckling his youngest into the car seat when his phone buzzed. It was the monthly football group chat, and he had six unread messages. "Read me the last one," he said. The assistant read it aloud: practice had moved to half past five on Thursday. "Reply that we'll be there, and mark the chat as read," said Diego. The assistant sent the reply and cleared the little red number. He pulled the belt tight, closed the door and started the car. Six minutes later, stopped at a red light, he asked it to remind him about the boots at four.

Person: I want to go for a bike ride tomorrow. Can you find me a route?
Assistant: Yes. How far would you like to ride?
Person: Not too far. Less than last time.
Assistant: Last time was twenty kilometres. Would ten be all right?
Person: Half of that would be better. My legs are tired.
Assistant: Five kilometres, then. Do you want to start from your house?
Person: Yes. And please go by the river. I like to look at the water.
Assistant: I found a flat route along the river. The path may be frozen early in the morning, so it is better to start after ten. Should I share it with your friend?
Person: Yes, please send it to Hal.

Hodan was stirring a pot of soup with one hand and holding a can of tomatoes in the other when the phone rang and went quiet. She often missed calls on busy evenings. "Look at my missed calls," she said. The assistant said there were two: one from her sister and one from the school. "Call the school back and put it on speaker," said Hodan. The phone rang, and a kind voice said that her son had left his bag in class. Hodan laughed, thanked her and hung up. Then she asked the assistant to play the voicemail from her sister, which was seventeen seconds long and only said hello.

They want a reminder to do their workout.

Could you please send me a message before my evening run, because I always lose track of the time?

Bread dough needs time to rise. You mix flour, water, yeast and salt, then leave the dough somewhere warm, like a sunny balcony in summer or a shelf above the radiator. After an hour it should be twice as big. Bakers organize their day around these times. When they bake, they set the oven to a number such as two hundred degrees and a timer for thirty minutes. People change the heat and the timer by saying "make it hotter", "ten more minutes" or "turn the oven down". If a neighbour downstairs smells the bread, they often come knocking on the door, hoping for a slice.

Oluwaseun had arrived in the city that morning with one bag and a very old map. By evening he stood in the middle of a busy street, wet from the rain and cold in his thin shirt, because he had dressed for a hot day. His phone was at ten percent. He typed fast: get me a taxi to the cental station. The assistant understood the typo, booked a taxi and said the car would be at the corner in four minutes. It showed the driver's name on the screen. When the car came, the heater was on, and Oluwaseun let out a long breath and sat back.

At half past six, the sun was going down and Hugo was cooking rice while his daughter did her homework. "How do you say good morning in Italian?" she called. Hugo did not know, so he asked his phone. The assistant said "buongiorno" in a clear voice. His daughter tried it three times, and it sounded a bit funny, but the assistant was patient and said it slowly each time. Then it spelled the word out letter by letter and showed it on the screen. "Now say good night," she said, and the assistant told them that too. Hugo stirred the rice, smiling, and learned it as well.

Lorenzo sat at the kitchen table, where the smell of garlic filled the room. His mum had lent him her phone, an expensive one, and told him to be careful. He wanted to save his grandmother's number before he forgot it. He typed with both thumbs: save nonna in my contcts, number 555 0142. The assistant made a new contact called Nonna with that number. Then it asked if he wanted her birthday too. "March the ninth," said Lorenzo, and the assistant saved it. He felt his chest rise with pride. He had done a grown-up job all by himself.

name: recipe_scaler

Greta had a cold and a whole list of things to do before lunch. She sat in her car outside the office and lowered her voice so nobody would hear her cough. "Book me a haircut at the salon on Hill Street for Friday at half past four," she said to her phone. The assistant checked the salon's times and said Friday at half past four was free. It booked the haircut and put it in her calendar. Greta thanked it, blew her nose and hurried inside for her meeting. At least one thing on her list was done.

name: workout_sender

people say:

- Email me the sets and reps for chest day
- Pass my routine to my brother
- Can my coach see what I did this morning?

Nathan had been a teacher for forty years, and camping was his favourite hobby now that he was retired. He sat on the porch with his tea and typed quickly on his phone: whats the weahter on top of the hill this weekend. The assistant answered that Saturday would be dry and cool, but the wind would increase on Sunday afternoon, with a chance of rain. Nathan thought for a moment. "Show me the packing list," he said, and the assistant brought up his old list. He added a rain jacket and a spare rope, then went to find his tent in the garage.

Person: Could you please turn up the heating in the kitchen? My back is sore from standing at the stove all day, and it hurts more when the room is cold.
Assistant: Of course. How much warmer would you like it?
Person: Two degrees, I think.
Assistant: Done. The kitchen is now twenty-two degrees.
Person: Thank you. There is also a small leak by the radiator. Can you call a plumber for me?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't phone a plumber. I can show you three plumbers nearby and their numbers.
Person: That would help. My purse is by the door, so I'll call from there.
Assistant: Here they are. I can also remind you to call at nine tomorrow.

A flight has a time to leave, a gate where you wait, and a time to arrive. The board at the airport shows these in white letters on a dark screen. Plans can change, so the board may show a delay, which is just a later time. People follow their flight on a phone by asking "is my flight on time?", "which gate is it?" or "what time does it land?" If a delay is long, a small seed of worry can grow, so it helps to check again every little while. Many people also ask for the time in another city, so a friend knows when to wait at the arrivals door.

Siti ran a small shop, and every night she washed the towels from the front counter. She was sleepy and wanted to go home. "Start dryer," she said to the speaker on the shelf. The assistant started the dryer and said it would finish in forty minutes. Soon a little beep signal sounded, which meant the towels were warm and ready. Siti had learned long ago that short words worked best when she was tired. She folded the towels, turned off the light and locked the door behind her.

A note is a short piece of writing that you keep so you do not forget. It can be a list, an idea, or a few words you said out loud. On a snowy day you might write "buy a sweater for Tom" and be glad you did. People change their notes all the time. They say "add milk to my shopping note", "read me my last note" or "find the note about the trip". Some people know exactly what they wrote, and some only remember one word, so they ask the assistant to search for it. Voice notes are handy when your hands are full, because you only need to talk.

Mei closed the shop and stood at the stop with a heavy bag. "When is the next bus to the market? Not the express, it costs too much," she said to her phone. The assistant looked at the timetable and said that a normal bus would come in six minutes. It also said her travel account had enough money for the ride, so she did not have to spend extra on a ticket. Mei did not want to wait long, and soon the bus came around the corner. She tapped her card, found a seat and watched the street lights go by.

Person: Please print my picture.
Assistant: Which picture? I see three from this week.
Person: The garden one. The fence has fresh paint on it.
Assistant: Got it. Do you want it printed now?
Person: No, print it at midnight, when I'm asleep. The printer smells hot when it runs and I don't like it.
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't start the printer at a set time. I can print it now, or I can remind you at midnight.
Person: Then print it now, and I'll go into the other room. Thank you for being patient with me. I am slow with these things.
Assistant: Not at all. Your picture is coming out now.

Ruth held her phone as if it might bite. Her puppy was asleep upstairs, and she wanted a quiet hour to write letters. She had never used the timer before. "Excuse me, could you please set a timer for twenty five minutes, because I want to work without stopping and then take a short break to see the puppy?" she said slowly. The assistant set a focus timer for twenty five minutes and said it would switch to a five minute break afterwards. Ruth was surprised that it was so easy. She wrote three letters before the soft chime rang, and then she climbed the stairs to find the puppy.

Divya looked at the clock in the hall. Her mum needed to send a parcel, but the house was busy. "The post office closes in half an hour, and the parcel is still on the table," she said to the speaker, hoping it would help. The assistant understood. It said the post office on Park Road was open until five and that it was a quick walk, about ten minutes. It also offered to show the way. Divya jumped up, grabbed the parcel and called to her mum. They put on their shoes and left together, and they got there with plenty of time.

Zoe was packing for the weekend trip and looked out of the window. The sky was grey and heavy. She typed to her phone: "i think this weekend is going to be wet, and we're sleeping outside". The assistant checked the forecast and said it would be rainy on Saturday. It offered to add a tarp and a rain jacket to her packing list, and Zoe said yes. She also asked it to remind her to bring a block of dry firewood. "It might help us build a fire under the tarp," she wrote. The assistant added that to the list as well, and Zoe felt much better about the trip.

Jasmine was at the end of her maths homework, with her phone nearby on the bed and her brother running the vacuum in the hall. The noise made it hard to think. Jasmine checked it with her pencil and saw that it was right. She wrote the answer in the box and asked what 126 divided by 3 was. "Forty two," said the assistant. She smiled, wrote that down too and closed the book.

A to-do list is a place to write down the things you must do, so you do not have to hold them all in your head. Each line is a task, such as "pick up the photo album" or "install new shelves". Many people mark the main task first and the small ones after it. When a job is finished, you check it off, and it feels good to see the line go. People change a list by saying "put this at the top", "remove the last one" or "move the shelves to Saturday". You can also ask "what is left for today?" and the assistant will read what is still open.

Greta was bathing the baby while her son sat on the bathroom floor, frowning at a page of French words. He had a test at school. "I wish I could help him with these," Greta said to the speaker in the hall, "but I never learned French." The assistant understood. It offered to read each word out loud and say what it meant in English. It also offered to quiz her son after the bath. Her son said yes. They did ten words, and he got eight right. It was a monthly test, so there was time to learn the rest. Greta dried the baby and smiled.

An appointment is a time that is kept just for you, like a haircut on Friday or a visit to the dentist. The place has working hours, so you can only book a time when it is open. Before you go, you may want to change something. People say "move my haircut to Saturday", "make it an hour later" or "cancel the dentist". Some people dream of a free morning, and a booking gives them one. The dentist might tell you to eat more lettuce and fewer sweets, but the assistant only needs the day, the time and the name of the place. It will remind you the evening before.

A workout is a plan of exercises, each with sets and reps. A set is a group of the same move, and a rep is one go. Rest days let the body get strong again. People change their plan all the time. They say "add one more set", "make it shorter" or "skip my rest day". If you have a race or a deadline for a goal, you might ask for a harder week. Many people tap the screen to start the timer, but you can also say "start the timer". You may also ask "what is next?" and hear the next move. If your next session is soon, an alert can help you get ready.

A lamp or ceiling light does one simple thing: it makes light. With smart bulbs you can change how bright it is and what colour it shows. Some people like a warm yellow light for the evening and a cool white one for work. A colleague who visits your home might ask you to mix a calm blue for a film night. People say "dim the lights", "make it brighter" or "turn the lamp red". It is good to switch a bulb off before you touch it, because a hot bulb can be dangerous. You can also say "turn off all the lights" when you go to bed, and the whole house goes dark.

Hyun was sitting on the old boat at the lake, watching dark clouds come in. The sky looked stormy, and his phone kept buzzing with messages from his grandchildren. He did not want to be bothered while the wind was rising. "Silence phone," he said. The assistant turned on do not disturb and said it would stay on until the morning. The messages stopped buzzing. Hyun nodded. He shut the little box of fishing hooks, pulled the rope tight and rowed slowly back to the shore as the first raindrops came down.

Person: Move it.
Assistant: Sure. Which event do you want to move?
Person: The dentist.
Assistant: Your dentist visit is on Tuesday at nine. Move it to when?
Person: Next week. Any day.
Assistant: Your calendar is a bit messy on Monday and Thursday. I can calculate the free gaps. Wednesday at ten is open.
Person: My parent comes to visit on Wednesday. Not that day.
Assistant: Then Friday at eleven is free. Shall I move it there?
Person: Yes.
Assistant: Done. Your dentist visit is now on Friday at eleven.

Some clinics and salons like to know a few things before you come. They may ask you to upload a form, or to pack a card, a letter or a list of medicines. It can feel strange to fill in so much just for a short visit, but it saves time at the desk. People change an appointment by saying "move it to Monday", "make it later" or "book my son in as well". The assistant needs the place, the day and the time. If you only say "the usual one", it may ask you to say which one. Opening hours are worth checking first, so you do not arrive at a closed door.

name: celebration_planner
does: Makes a plan for a celebration, like a party for a lost tooth or an indoor picnic on a stormy day, and tags each job with the person who will do it.
inputs: the kind of celebration, the date, and how many guests are coming
people say:
- Help me plan Mia's birthday for next Saturday
- We're hosting twelve people for the holiday, what do we need?

Fergus was ready for a day at the beach. His family would travel to the sea tomorrow, and he wanted to be sure about the weather. He picked up his mum's phone and said, 'Will it be sunny tomorrow at seven?' The assistant said it would be bright and warm, but the water would still be cold early in the morning. 'Do I need sun cream?' asked Fergus. The assistant said yes, and it set a reminder to pack the sun cream tomorrow at seven. Then Fergus asked when the tide would come in. The assistant told him high tide was at ten, and it added that to the reminder too. Fergus put his blue mug in the beach bag for hot chocolate and said thank you. The phone replied, 'Have fun at the beach.' Fergus grinned and ran to find his towel.

Dana woke up with a sleepy head and a rumbling stomach. It was a slow morning, and she wanted to see a film that night. She picked up her phone and mumbled, 'What movies are on tonight?' The assistant listed three films at the cinema near her flat. The main one was a space adventure that started at seven. 'Is there anything funny?' asked Dana. The assistant found a comedy at eight and said it was seventeen minutes shorter than the space film. 'Play me the trailer,' she said, and the phone showed it. Dana laughed twice. 'Increase the volume a little,' she added, and the assistant made the sound louder. Then she asked it to remind her at six to leave, and she wrote the cinema name on a piece of paper by the bed, just in case. Finally she got up and made tea.

When you cook a recipe, the steps tell you what to do and for how long. The oven temperature is one thing people often change. If a roast leg of lamb is cooking too fast, a cook might say, 'Turn the oven down a bit,' or 'Make it cooler.' If the food needs more time, they say, 'Give it ten more minutes' or 'Keep it in longer.' People also change the number of servings: 'Make it for six' or 'Cut the recipe in half.' A calm cook checks the timer and the steps again and again. When the dish is done, the family can celebrate with a good meal. A smart assistant understands all these words and changes the time, the heat or the amount for you.

Rachel was not good with her new phone. She stood at the edge of a shallow puddle outside the station and did not know what to do. Her friend had told her, 'Just ask the assistant.' So she held the phone near her mouth and said, 'Taxi, please.' The assistant asked where she wanted to go. 'Home,' said Rachel. The assistant found a car and said it would arrive in a quarter of an hour at the station door. Rachel said, 'Thank you.' The assistant told her the driver's name and the colour of the car. She waited by the door, and when the car came, she was ready to leave. She smiled. The phone was not so hard after all.

It was a rainy day in October, and Lucy was bored in the back seat of the car. Dad was driving. She took the tablet and said to the assistant, 'My feet are freezing.' The assistant turned up the heat in the back of the car. A minute later Lucy said, 'It's so dark in here.' The assistant switched on the small light above her seat. Then Lucy took a photo of a red bus through the window. 'Upload this to the family album,' she said, and the assistant did it and told her the photo was saved. Lucy asked it to play a song about a bus, and the assistant started a happy tune. Dad laughed. Lucy was not bored anymore. By the time they reached Gran's house, she had sung the whole song twice.

Find me a cheaper way home
Is there a route with no tolls?
Swap this route for one that costs less
Take me a way with half the traffic
That road is pricey, show me another
Which way is the quickest right now?

Could you please look for a road that has fewer cars and does not cost any money?

Chiara came in from the garden, still wearing her muddy coat. She wanted to print her seed list. 'Print my seed list, two copies,' she said to the assistant. A moment later she changed her mind. 'No, wait, make it three copies. My sister wants one.' The assistant stopped and printed three copies on the usual paper. The printer hummed. Then Chiara remembered the old scan of her garden map on the screen. 'Delete the old garden map scan from the printer folder,' she said. The assistant deleted it and told her the folder was now empty. Chiara thanked it, picked up the warm pages, and put them in her basket next to her gloves. It was a good start to a spring day.

Callum owned a small shop, and his dream was a quiet place where people felt calm. Today the screen on his phone was very bright, and it hurt his eyes at the counter. 'This is too bright to read,' he said. The assistant dimmed the screen. Then Callum looked at a note on the counter and said, 'I never remember when my sister's birthday is.' The assistant looked in his contacts and said her birthday was on the ninth of June. It offered a reminder, and Callum said yes. The assistant also said her phone number was still saved if he wanted to call. Callum smiled. Everything was simple when he just talked and the assistant helped. Then a customer came in, and he put the phone away.

A doctor's appointment is a time you book to see the doctor. Many people forget the day, so they ask their phone to remind them. They might say, 'Put my doctor on Saturday at nine,' or 'Move it to Monday.' A reminder can ring the night before, when the room is dim and the day is quiet. People also keep track of medicine doses by asking, 'Remind me to take my pill at eight' or 'Change it to nine.' At the clinic, a friendly nurse will greet you at the desk and check your name. If you cannot go, you can say, 'Cancel my visit,' and pick a new time.

Emi stood in front of the open fridge and frowned. Her grandchildren were coming for dinner, and the shelves were almost empty. She turned to the kitchen speaker and said, 'Put tomatoes on the shopping list, but I don't want the big ones. They are too hard.' The assistant added small tomatoes to the list. 'Also my regular bread,' she said, and the assistant added it. Then it warned her that the milk would go bad in two days, so she should buy a fresh bottle. Emi nodded. 'No fish this week,' she added, and the assistant left it off. When she was ready, the assistant read the list back to her and sent it to her phone. Emi took it to the shop and was home in time to cook.

Chen sat at his desk at lunchtime and looked at a photo his friend sent from Paris. It showed a blue box from a small bakery with a price tag of thirteen euros. 'What is that in dollars?' he asked his phone. The assistant told him it was about fourteen dollars, and said the rate changes a little each day. Chen whistled. 'That is a lot for cake,' he said. Then he asked what the rate had been last week, and the assistant read it out. His phone beeped with a new message from his friend. Chen smiled and wrote back that he would buy her lunch next time. He put the phone down and went back to his spreadsheet.

The shop was loud. A drill whined in the back room, and Daniel could not talk on the phone. He typed in a hurry, 'turn on do not distrub til noon.' The assistant understood and switched on Do Not Disturb until noon. Then Daniel typed, 'brightness to the top.' The assistant raised the screen brightness to its highest level so he could see the screen in the sunny window. A moment later he tried to peel the old plastic cover off the phone, but it kept tearing. He asked the assistant how to peel a screen cover without leaving marks, and it gave him three short steps. Daniel followed them, and the phone looked new. The drill stopped, and the shop was quiet again.

Parking apps help you find a spot and pay for the time you use. You tell the app how long you want to stay, and it starts a countdown. When the time is almost over, it warns you, so you do not get a fine. People change their time all the time. They say, 'Add thirty minutes,' 'Stay another hour,' or 'Stop the parking, I'm leaving.' Drivers also ask, 'Where is a free spot near the park?' A quiet street with a scooter rack may have space when the main road is full. No one wants to burn fuel driving round in circles, so people ask the assistant to find a place close by.

Valentina ran a flower shop, and the lawn behind it was getting long. The morning was foggy, and she could hardly see the garden from the window. Valentina asked if the mower could skip a rainy day, and the assistant said it would stay in its house if the grass was wet. She smiled. The shop was warm, the plan was ready, and the fog would soon clear.

A focus timer helps you work without losing time. You pick a block, like twenty-five minutes, and the timer starts to count down. When it ends, you take a short break. Many people use this routine every day, and they are often excited to see how much they finish. When they want to change it, they say, 'Make it thirty minutes,' 'Shorter breaks, please,' or 'Pause the timer.' Some people reward each break with a coffee and a discount card from a cafe near the office. After four blocks, they take a longer rest. The timer does not do the work for you, but it keeps you honest.

Air conditioning cools a room so it feels comfortable on hot days. In spring, many people use only a fan, but when summer comes they switch on the cooling. Most people have a number they prefer, like twenty-two degrees. They change it with simple words: 'Make it cooler,' 'Drop it two degrees,' 'Too cold, back it off,' or 'Turn the fan to low.' The true goal is not a freezing room but a fresh one. Some units have a timer, so you can say, 'Turn off at midnight.' An assistant understands all these ways of asking and changes the numbers for you.

Roya came home after a long night shift, and her eyes were closing. Her son had a football match on Saturday, and she was afraid she would forget it. She typed in a hurry, 'move dentist apointment to friday at 3.' The assistant moved the visit and said the old time was now free. Then Roya spoke softly and asked it to add the match to her calendar for Saturday at ten. The assistant did it and asked if she wanted a reminder. 'Yes, when I return from my shift on Friday,' she said. The assistant set it for eight in the morning. Roya put the phone down and crawled into bed. She slept until the afternoon.

A dishwasher cleans plates, cups and pots while you do something else. You fill it, add soap and pick a program. When the program ends, it beeps. Wet dishes can be left to dry, or you can pick a hot dry setting. People change how it works with simple words: 'Start a quick wash,' 'Make it longer,' 'Delay it until midnight,' or 'Stop it.' Before a holiday dinner, many families run the dishwasher twice. A smart assistant lets you say these things without touching any buttons, even when your hands are full.

Chioma finished her night shift at the hospital and walked slowly to the car park. She had worked on a special project all night, and her legs were heavy. She got in the car and said to her phone, 'I only have ten minutes left on my parking, and I'm still waiting for my friend.' The assistant understood. It added one hour to her parking time and paid with her saved card. Then she said, 'Start a timer for forty minutes so I don't oversleep.' The assistant started it. Chioma closed her eyes. When the timer rang, she had had a good rest, and the car was still safe in its spot.

Could you please make the lights softer and warmer? I want to read for a long while, and the bright white light is hurting my eyes.

Kofi drove a taxi in the city, and Tuesday was always busy. In the morning he sat in his car under a cloudy sky and asked the assistant, 'What rides do I have today?' The assistant read out four bookings. The first one was a pickup at the station at half past six. 'Tell the passenger I will be there five minutes early,' said Kofi. The assistant sent the message. Then Kofi said, 'Remind me to sweep the back seat before that ride.' The assistant set a reminder for six. He did the sweep with a small brush and checked the mirror. At half past six, a woman with a red suitcase waved at him from the door. Kofi smiled and opened the trunk.

A phone call lets you talk to someone far away. You can say, 'Call Mum' or 'Dial the pizza place.' If you miss a call, the phone shows it, and a rare voicemail may be waiting for you. People change how a call works with short words: 'Put it on speaker,' 'Mute me,' 'Call back the last number,' or 'Play my messages.' Someone calling to order a burger may even hold the phone while the cook talks. Some people stream music through the speaker while they wait on hold. A voice assistant can do all these things without you touching the screen.

Ben was waiting in his taxi for a passenger, and he had a problem. His friend Sam was turning thirty-one on Sunday, and he had no idea what to buy. 'Gift ideas for a man who likes cooking,' he said to the assistant. It gave him three ideas: a good knife, a thin cookbook of quick meals, and a set of spices. Ben liked the cookbook. 'Try the market,' said the assistant. 'A stall near you sells books on Saturdays.' Ben asked it to set a reminder for Saturday morning and to save the date of Sam's birthday for next year. The assistant did both. When his passenger came, Ben put the phone away and started the engine, happy that the gift was sorted.

When you buy something online, a tracking number lets you see where the package is. The shop says when it will arrive, and each day the tracker shows the next step. People often ask, 'Where is my parcel?' or 'When will it come?' If the box is damaged, or a bottle leaked inside, they can ask for a refund. They say, 'Send it back' or 'I want my money back.' A refund can take up to a month to show up. Some people check the tracker every morning. A voice assistant can answer these questions and tell you the new delivery day.

Xiu was driving home when her head began to pound. She pulled over and said to the assistant, 'My head is killing me, and I've run out of pills.' The assistant understood. It said it could find a pharmacy and asked for her location. Xiu allowed it. The nearest pharmacy was two kilometres north, and it was open until nine. 'Take me there,' she said. The assistant started directions and spoke each turn clearly. At the pharmacy, she bought her medicine. The assistant then asked if she wanted a reminder to take the next dose, and she said yes, in four hours. Xiu drank some water and felt calmer. The drive home was slow, but she was safe.

Assistant: Half of 185 is 92.5.
Person: Great. Can you also write the answer on my paper notes?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't write on paper, but I can send the answer to your phone.
Person: Please do.

A baby has a rhythm of feeding times and nap times, and parents write it down to keep track. A baby monitor lets you hear or see a tiny sleeper from another room, even in fog or darkness. If the baby wakes, the monitor sounds an alert. Parents change the plan with simple words: 'Move the nap to two,' 'Feed her in an hour,' or 'Turn the monitor up.' Some say, 'Keep the sound low, she's asleep.' An assistant can set reminders for each feeding and nap so tired parents do not have to remember everything.

He washed his hands and put on a clean shirt.

Time was tight, because the light would fade in an hour. 'How long will that take?' he asked. The assistant said about thirty minutes each way. Tesfaye checked the tyres, which felt firm, and rode off. He enjoyed the quiet path and was home before dark.

Before he went inside, he asked the assistant to remind him to check the tyres again on Friday. It did.

Callum was a retired teacher, and he liked his quiet street. One morning a loud noise came from the field. A cow had wandered onto Mill Road, and the neighbours began to shout. Callum took his phone and said, 'Post in the village group that a cow is loose on Mill Road.' Then he stopped. 'No, I mean Mill Lane, sorry.' The assistant fixed the post and sent it. Soon a farmer answered and said the cow was his. The assistant read the replies to Callum. The farmer thanked him, and the constant barking of the dogs slowly faded as the cow went home. Callum asked if there was a local event this weekend, and the assistant told him about the village fair.

An alarm wakes you at a time you pick, and a timer counts down from a number of minutes. In the kitchen, a timer tells you when the fruit pie is ready. Many alarms are automatic: they ring on weekdays and rest at the weekend. People change them with short words: 'Wake me at six,' 'Snooze ten minutes,' 'Make it ring later,' or 'Cancel tomorrow's alarm.' A watch you wear on your wrist can ring quietly so only you hear it. An assistant can set an alarm, change it, or turn it off when you say so.

Yuki ran a small flower shop and she never slept well. Last night a hot wind blew through her bedroom window, and the baby next door began to cry at three in the morning. By dawn she was tired and cross.

"Hey assistant," she said, rubbing her eyes. "I want to nap this afternoon. Wake me up next Tuesday at noon... no, sorry, I mean today at one. Just a short rest before the shop gets busy."

The assistant said it had set an alarm for one o'clock today and asked if she wanted it to turn on the fan. Yuki said yes. It switched the fan on low and told her the alarm was ready. She smiled, closed the shop sign, and lay down.

"whats on at the cinma tonight near me"

The assistant understood him anyway. It found three films playing at the Grand Cinema, two miles away, and read out the times: 6:15, 7:40 and 9:05. Ishaan asked for the trailer of the middle one. The assistant played it on his phone screen, and he watched with a small smile. Then he asked it to save the 7:40 show to his calendar, and the assistant did.

When you cough in the night and look at the clock, it shows the time where you are. But the sun does not rise everywhere at once. Like a seed that sprouts a little at a time, the morning moves across the world from east to west, so a huge map is split into time zones. Each zone has its own clock. People use the clock for calls, flights and meetings. They ask things like "What time is it in Tokyo?" or "Set my clock to London time." Some say "My phone is an hour off" when they travel, or "Show me two clocks at once." The phone changes by itself when you cross into a new zone.

People count days for all sorts of reasons: a birthday, a holiday, or the day a library book is due. Counting days helps you plan, and it can calm you down if you hate waiting. Even an angry person might feel better knowing there are only nine days left. Some people read a newspaper to check the date and then do the counting in their head. A phone can do it for you. People say "How many days until my birthday?", "How old am I if I was born in 1990?" or "Count the days since we moved." They can also ask for a change, like "Start from tomorrow" or "Count only the weekdays."

Sofia was not good with technology. Her granddaughter had given her a tablet, and she hated how many buttons it had. This morning she was worried because she had to help the girl with homework, and the tablet was pricey, so she did not want to break it.

"Please," she said slowly to the tablet, "tell me what homework Lina has. She has a test next Tuesday at noon."

The assistant opened the school app and read out the list. There was a math sheet due Friday, and a reading task for the test next Tuesday at noon. Sofia asked it to remind her on Monday evening. The assistant said it had set a reminder for Monday at six. Sofia felt a little proud.

Hiroshi was bored in a long Monday meeting, with his phone clipped to his belt and his laptop on mute. He decided to fix something that had bothered him for days.

"Change the password for my email," he whispered to the assistant. "No wait, not the email. The work account."

The assistant asked if he wanted a strong new password. Hiroshi said yes. It made one with letters, numbers and symbols and saved it to his password list. Then it asked if it should lock his phone after one minute, and he said yes.

Just then his boss asked him a question. "Unmute me," said Hiroshi quickly. The assistant turned on his microphone and he began to talk.

An alarm is a sound that wakes you or warns you about something. A kitchen timer is the same idea for cooking: you set it for ten minutes and it rings when the pasta is done. Most phones let you change the time, the sound, and the days the alarm repeats. People say "Wake me at six", "Snooze for five minutes" or "Cancel my alarm." Some ask for a total countdown, like "Count down from forty minutes." On the lock screen you can often see the next alarm and stop it without opening the phone. Sleepy people like this because they only want to tap once.

Jack the gardener was painting the garden fence on a sunny Saturday. His hands were covered in white paint, so he could not touch his phone. He wanted a neat cup of coffee, and he wanted it right now.

"Make me a coffee," he called to the kitchen speaker. "No sugar, and no milk. I don't want anything fancy."

The assistant told the coffee machine to brew one black cup, strong. A minute later it said, "Your coffee is ready." Jack also had a video call with his sister at noon. "Start the zoom call at twelve," he said, and the assistant answered that it would. Then Jack wiped his hands and went to get his drink.

Henry woke up late and his head felt heavy. His phone buzzed on the table, and he could hardly hear it over the noise from the street. He grabbed it and spoke to the assistant.

"Text my wife, tell her I'm working late tonight. Say it's honey chicken for dinner, so she should start the rice."

The assistant read the message back. Henry frowned. "No, change that. Not working late. I mean working from home. And say sorry for the mess."

The assistant fixed the message and sent it: "Hi love, I'm working from home today. I'll make honey chicken, so please start the rice. Sorry for the mess." Henry smiled and finally got out of bed.

A budget is a plan for your money. You write down what comes in each month and what goes out, like rent, food and bills. It helps you save and spend less on things you don't need. Being careful matters most in a cold month, when heating costs more. Many people scan their receipts so the phone can add them up. People say "How much did I spend on food?", "Set my food budget to two hundred" or "Tell me when I've spent half." They also ask for changes such as "Move fifty to savings." The plan is not fixed, so you can change it any time.

It was a foggy morning in July, and Ben, a retired teacher, was making tea when the kettle slipped. A little hot water splashed on his finger. It stung, but he stayed calm.

"Assistant, what do I do for a burn on my finger?" he asked.

The assistant told him to hold it under cool running water for ten minutes.

"Wait, it's not the finger," said Ben. "It's my palm. Does that change anything?"

The assistant said no, the same steps were fine for the palm, but if the skin turned white or blistered badly, he should see a doctor. It also set a ten minute timer. Ben stood at the sink until it rang. "Thank you," he said.

A workout is a plan for moving your body. It is made of exercises, which you repeat in sets and reps. For example, ten push-ups is one set of ten reps. Rest days matter too, because muscles grow when you stop. If you skip rest, tired muscles can lead to dangerous injuries. After a hard weekend in a tent in the hills, you might want an easy day. People say "Start a ten minute workout", "Add one more set" or "Give me a rest day on Wednesday." They also say "Make it easier" or "Do fewer reps." The plan changes as you get stronger.

Writing starts with a draft, which is a first try that does not have to be perfect. Then you edit it: you fix spelling, shorten long sentences, and check the word count. A spell checker will notice if you type tooth as tooht. People who write emails often need to reply fast, but a tall pile of messages can wait until you are ready. Writers ask things like "How many words is this?", "Fix my spelling" or "Read it back to me." They also ask for changes: "Make it shorter", "Make it sound more polite" or "Change the first line." Editing is just making your words clearer.

Do not disturb is a setting that keeps your phone quiet. Calls and messages still arrive, but the phone does not ring or buzz. It is useful at night, in class or in a meeting. You can schedule it so it turns on and off by itself, for example from ten at night until seven in the morning. People say "Turn on do not disturb", "Schedule quiet time for the evening" or "Let my mother's calls through." Imagine working in the soil on a windy day. You may want the phone silent so a buzz does not interrupt you. When the time ends, the phone goes back to normal.

Ananya was new to the city, and her apartment was not perfect. The kitchen tap gave her water that tasted bitter, and the orange juice she made with it was no better. She thought the filter might be old.

"Hey assistant," she said, "my water filter is half used up and the water tastes bitter. Can you find someone to change it?"

The assistant searched nearby repair shops and found a plumber with good reviews, open until six. It asked if she wanted it to ring the shop. Ananya said yes. The assistant called, and the plumber promised to come the next day at ten. It then added the visit to her calendar and set a reminder for nine.

Silvia had just woken up and her cat was already batting a toy across the floor. Her head was still fuzzy, but she had a big day. She grabbed her phone and typed in a hurry.

"set a focus timer for 45 mins and adjst it to silent mode"

The assistant understood. It started a forty five minute focus timer and switched her phone to silent mode, so no sounds would break her work. When she sat down at her desk, the timer was already running. It also asked if she wanted a short break at the end. "Yes, ten minutes," Silvia typed, and the assistant added a ten minute break after the focus time.

First aid means helping someone right away when they get a small injury, before a doctor can see them. For a small cut, you wash your hands, clean the cut and cover it. For a burn, you hold it under cool water. If something gets in your eye, wash it with clean water and don't rub. Pharmacies sell plasters and cold packs, so keep a few in a box at home. Stay away from home remedies like butter on a burn. People say "What do I do for a bee sting?", "How long should I cool a burn?" or "Call an ambulance." They can also ask for a step to be repeated.

Jonah had just finished a long night shift at the hospital. He was tired and wanted to send a quick note to his sister before he slept, but he had to carry a heavy bag home first. On the bus he spoke to his phone.

"Write a short email to Dana. Say I'll visit at quarter to eight on Saturday. Check my spelling."

The assistant wrote the email and read it back. It had found one mistake and fixed it. Jonah liked how fast it was, since his speed with the keyboard was slow when he was so sleepy. He said, "Send it." The assistant sent the email to Dana, and Jonah closed his eyes.

Mei came home from the hospital after a night shift and found the printer jammed. She had a form to send before breakfast, so she typed fast.

"scan this form and email it to my boss, my printr is stuck"

The assistant opened the scanner on her phone, took a picture of the form and made a clean page with a wide margin. Then it emailed it to her boss. Mei also needed new ink. "What's the ink called?" she asked. The assistant read out the cartridge name and spelled it letter by letter, so she could write it down. It said the cartridge cost about twelve dollars at the shop on Main Street. Mei wrote it on her hand and went to sleep.

A phone call is when you talk to someone by phone. If you can't answer, the call becomes a missed call, and the person may leave a message in your voicemail. Missed calls pile up like pictures in an album, so most phones show a list. You can add a number to your contacts to see a name next time. Speakerphone lets other people nearby hear the call, which is handy when your hands are busy. People say "Call my brother", "Put him on speaker" or "Who called me?" They also ask "Add this number to my contacts" or "Play my voicemail."

Ji-woo was an office worker and her days were always busy. On Friday afternoon she was packing her bag when she broke the zipper on her jacket. She sighed and talked to her phone.

"Set an alarm for this Saturday afternoon at three. I need to call the tailor about my zipper before the shop closes."

The assistant replied that the alarm was set for Saturday at three o'clock. Ji-woo thought for a second. "Make it two thirty, so I have time to find the number." The assistant changed the alarm to two thirty and added a note: "Call the tailor." Ji-woo nodded and walked home.

Remy was in a hurry. His dad was sick in bed, and Remy had to hand in his school work before nine. He ran to the kitchen with his bag half open.

"Open my homework list," he said to the tablet. "What is due today?"

The assistant showed three items. There was a science sheet, a poem, and an essay of three hundred words. Remy groaned. "Remind me at lunch to finish the essay," he said, and the assistant set a reminder for twelve thirty. Then Remy asked it to text his teacher that his dad was sick. The assistant wrote and sent the message, and Remy grabbed his coat and ran for the bus.

Money does not last forever, so many families make a plan. First you estimate how much comes in each month, then how much you need for rent, food and bills. Think of all the mouths to feed at home. If your numbers don't match, you may need to spend less on something. People say "Show me my spending this month", "Set aside twenty for savings" or "Estimate what I will spend on groceries." They also say "Spend less on coffee" or "Tell me when I'm close to my limit." A good plan is simple, and you can fix it whenever a bill is bigger than you expected.

Meal planning means deciding what you will eat before you are hungry. You pick meals for the week, make a shopping list, and cook some things early. A smart plan uses leftovers: roast a chicken on Sunday, and use the rest in a sandwich on Monday. A pan with some depth is good for soups and stews. Meal plans help with packed lunches, diets and a tight budget. People say "Plan dinners for five days", "Nothing with nuts" or "Swap Tuesday's pasta for soup." They also ask "What can I cook with potatoes?" and "Make my plan cheaper."

Rania was a gardener, and her tall husband slept badly in small hotel beds. She planned a trip for two and spoke to her phone.

The assistant changed the booking details to three nights with a late check-in at midnight. It asked her to confirm, and Rania said yes. A few seconds later, the room was held for her.

Rania was late for an invitation to her friend's party, and she ran out to her car with her keys in her hand. The seats were cold and she could see her breath.

"It's freezing in here," she said to the car assistant.

The assistant turned on the heat and the seat warmers. Rania looked at the screen. "It's so bright. Can you dim it a bit?" The assistant dimmed the display. Then it told her the tank was only half full, and showed a gas station on the way to the party. Rania smiled and said, "Take me there first, then to Sam's house." The assistant started the route.

Fatou was a gardener who sold plants online. On Wednesday she was in her packing station in the shed, with shallow pots of herbs waiting to ship. But the wifi was so slow that her orders would not load.

"Why is the internet so slow?" she asked the assistant. "It's half as fast as yesterday."

The assistant checked the router and found that six devices were using it. It asked if she wanted to restart it. Fatou said yes. The router restarted, and a minute later the speed was twice as fast. The assistant also offered to pause her smart TV, and she agreed. Fatou loaded her orders and began to ship the plants.

Finding a movie is easy when you know what you want. You pick a film, a cinema, and a time. Start times are listed in order, so the first show is at the top. Many cinemas have middle rows that feel best, and tickets cost more there. To know the price, you multiply the cost of one ticket by the number of people. People say "What's on tonight?", "Show me the trailer" or "Book two seats in the middle." They also ask for changes, like "Make it the later show" or "Make it three tickets." You can order snacks at some cinemas too.

Minh was a retired teacher who loved to bake bread on Sundays. This morning she wanted to try a new loaf with bay leaf and herbs, and she was worried the dough would rise too long.

"Hello assistant," she said politely. "Could you please search for a simple herb bread recipe? I would like one that takes under three hours, because my grandchildren are coming for lunch at one."

The assistant found a recipe and read out the steps. It said the dough needs one hour to rise, then forty minutes in the oven. Minh asked for hourly reminders to check the dough. The assistant said it had set a reminder every hour, and Minh began to mix the flour.

Odile was walking through a museum with her class when she remembered her grandmother's evening pills. She texted her phone assistant: remind Gran to take her blue pill at six, but do not call her, she hates loud phone calls. The assistant set a quiet reminder on Gran's tablet for six o'clock. It said the tablet would show a gentle message and would not ring. Odile also asked for a note when Gran tapped done. Gran loves her little tablet, even though she lives far away from the city, and she tapped the message right on time. At two minutes past six Odile got a text from the assistant: Gran took her pill. Odile smiled, put her phone in her pocket and went back to look at the old paintings with her friends.

A radio is for hearing music, news and talk without looking at a screen. People mostly change two things: the station and the sound. To change the station they say things like 'put on the news', 'find a music station' or 'go back to the last one'. Some listeners like frequent news updates in the morning, and others enjoy a health show that talks about a vitamin or a good breakfast. To change the sound they say 'turn it up', 'a little lower' or 'mute it for now'. A small portable radio has a battery, so people charge it at night and ask 'how much battery is left?' before a trip. If the signal is noisy, they say 'find a clearer station'.

Keeping a lawn neat means cutting the grass, watering it and trimming the edges. A robot mower does the cutting alone and goes back to its base when it is done. People tell it where and when to work: 'mow the back garden at ten', 'skip today, it is raining' or 'cut it a little shorter'. A sprinkler waters the grass early in the morning. If the water goes too far, people say 'point it more to the left' or 'water only the front patch'. For the edges, some people use a garden fork to loosen the soil and a trimmer to make a clean line. When the grass grows fast, they ask for a mow every three days instead of every week.

Lights make a room feel right for what you are doing. A smart bulb can change how bright it is and even its colour, from warm yellow to cool white. People like dim light in the evening and bright light when they work. A smart plug can convert a plain lamp, like an old silver desk lamp, into one you can control with your voice. Common requests are 'make it brighter', 'a little dimmer', 'turn on the hall light' and 'set the lamp to warm'. Many people also ask for the lights to come on before they get home, for example while they are still on the bus.

A fan or an air conditioner keeps a room cool when the day is hot. Too much heat can give a person a headache and make it hard to sleep, so cool air helps. People adjust the temperature, the fan speed and a timer. They say 'make it cooler', 'set it to twenty-two', 'lower the fan, it is too loud' or 'turn it off at midnight'. On a cloudy day a room may stay cool without help. Some people hang a wet towel in front of a fan to make the air feel fresher, and then they say 'a bit stronger, please' or 'switch to the quiet setting'.

A phone call lets you talk to someone who is far away. People use it to call family, check on friends and leave a voicemail when nobody answers. On a train ride the line can get rough, and the sound breaks up, so people say 'call me back' or 'I will try again later'. A farmer out with his horse can still call home from the field. The things people change are the person they call and the sound. They say 'call Mum', 'put it on speaker', 'did anyone call me?' or 'play my voicemail'. If it is too loud, they ask 'turn the call down a little'.

Reading is a calm habit that many people enjoy before bed. A good story can make you dream about faraway places. People keep a bookmark in their book, or ask a phone to save their page, so they can start again where they stopped. They also set a reading time, like twenty minutes each evening. A new book might come in the mailbox, and a person keeps it safe on a shelf. To change things, people say 'remind me to read at nine', 'save my page', 'read to me for ten minutes' or 'go to chapter four'. If the time is too long, they say 'make it shorter tonight'.

A workout is a plan of exercises, such as ten push-ups, then a rest, then ten more. Each group of the same move is called a set, and each single move is a rep. People rest between sets and take a rest day so their body can get strong. They ask for changes like 'make it shorter', 'add one more set', 'skip the jumping' or 'give me an easy day'. Some apps filter workouts so you only see short ones, or ones with no equipment. A person might train every other day for a goal, like running a race in the spring or feeling strong for a friend's birthday.

Moving house means taking everything you own to a new home. People pack boxes room by room, write the room name on each one, and tell the post office and the bank their new address. They also ask the power and water companies to start on the moving day. Dust from old boxes can make you sneeze, so they open the windows. A warm sweater goes in a box marked bedroom. Some movers give a free price before the day. People say 'how much to move a two-room flat?', 'change my address', or 'remind me to turn off the gas on Friday'.

A fan or an air conditioner keeps a room cool when the day is hot. After you bake a cake, the kitchen can feel like an oven, so people turn the cooling on to feel better. They adjust three things: the temperature, the fan speed and a timer. They say 'make it cooler', 'set it to twenty-two', 'lower the fan, it is too loud' or 'switch it off at midnight'. A plain fan only moves the air, while an air conditioner makes the air colder. On a mild day, people open a window instead and say 'turn it off, it's fine now'.

Tomas had moved to the city in December and still did not know where to leave his car. On Saturday he said to his phone: find me a parking spot near the library, I only need it for two hours. The assistant searched and reported that a large car park was three streets away and had twelve free spaces. Tomas asked how much it cost. The assistant said it was fifty cents for each half hour. Tomas said: okay, take me there. The phone showed the way on the map. When he parked, he said: remind me to move the car in one hour and forty-five minutes. The assistant set the reminder and said it would ring at ten to three, so he would not pay for extra time.

Isaac opened his small bakery at six. His hands were covered in flour because he had just mixed a big batch of dough, so he typed to his phone in a hurry: start the cofee machine and heat the middle oven to 200. The assistant turned on the coffee machine and set the middle oven to two hundred degrees. It also told him the oven would be ready in ten minutes. Isaac asked it to write the first item on his list, bread rolls, on the shop screen. The assistant did that too. By the time the first customer walked in, the coffee was hot and the oven was ready.

Meal planning means deciding what to eat for the week before you go shopping. It saves time and money, which helps when money is tight. A person picks dinners, packed lunches and snacks, then makes a shopping list. If a shop sends the wrong box of food, they ask for a refund. Plans change, so people say 'skip fish on Wednesday', 'swap pasta for rice', 'make Friday a pizza night' or 'plan something cheap and quick'. Some people follow a diet, like no meat, and ask 'plan five meals with no meat'.

Andrei came home late from his shop. The street was dark, and a thick fog sat over the road. He told his phone: turn on all four cameras and tell the alarm that the man who mows the lawn will come on Saturday, so do not ring when he opens the gate. The assistant switched on the four cameras and showed a small picture of each one. Then it saved a note for the alarm that a visitor was expected on Saturday. Andrei also asked for his evening playlist to help him relax. The assistant started the playlist and said the doors were locked and the house was safe.
