Can you turn this message into Spanish before Wednesday?
I need it in Spanish by quarter to eight
My guest only speaks Spanish. Could you write the note in her language?
Spanish version, please
Please change the text to Spanish and read it back to me.

Silvia was in a hurry. She had to rise early the next day for a trip, and she still had no jacket. She said to her phone, "Order the navy jacket in size medium. I need it by the first of May." The assistant checked the shop and said, "The jacket is in stock. It can arrive on April 29th. Do you want to order it?" "Yes, and send it to my office," said Silvia. The assistant placed the order and read back the delivery date. Silvia packed her bag and ran out the door.

A note is a short piece of writing you save so that you do not forget it. People write notes about ideas, shopping, or things to tell a friend. Many people say, "Make a note: call the plumber," or "Write down the gate code." They find old notes by saying, "Show me my note about the trip." When their hands are busy, for example when they lift a box on the stairs or stir a hot pot, they use voice notes. They say, "Start a voice note" and just talk. Later they ask, "Read my last note" or "Delete that one."

name: drive_time_check
does: Tells you how long a drive will take right now, with traffic and icy roads in mind, so you can afford to sleep a little longer or leave in time.
inputs: the place you are going, like a berry farm or the office, and when you want to arrive
people say:
- How long will it take to get to the berry farm?
- Is there traffic on my way to work?
- When should I leave to be there at nine?
- Are the roads icy this morning?
- How long is the drive to my mother's?

Ursula, a retired teacher, sat at her kitchen table with a big pile of recipe cards. "Plan my dinners for this week and email the list to my sister," she said. The assistant made a plan: soup on Monday, fish on Tuesday, rice and beans on Wednesday, and a stone fruit crumble on Sunday. Ursula frowned. "Wait, not fish. My sister can't eat it. Put chicken on Tuesday instead." The assistant swapped the fish for chicken and read the new plan back. "That's right now," said Ursula. The assistant then emailed the final plan and the shopping list to her sister. Ursula smiled, put the cards away, and went to make a cup of tea.

A weather forecast tells you what the sky will do, so you can decide what to wear and whether to take an umbrella. Many people forget to check it, so phones can show a short forecast each morning. You can change the place, the day or the unit. You might say, "What's the weather tomorrow?" or "Will it rain this weekend?" Some people want degrees Celsius, and others say, "Switch to Fahrenheit." A farmer may ask for the forecast for each hour of the day, and a child may just ask, "Do I need a coat?" A gardener with pear trees might ask, "Will there be frost tonight?" A good assistant can answer all of these.

Zara was texting her friends when she remembered the news. She turned to her phone and said, "Could you please put on the local radio station with the news? My mum asked me to listen for road closures, because I take the bus to my first day at the new school tomorrow, and I don't want to be late." The assistant found the station and turned up the sound. For a moment Zara heard only music, and then a calm voice read the traffic news. One road near her bus stop was closed. Zara swiped her screen, and the assistant saved the station to her favorites, so she could tune in again the next morning.

Someone wants a taxi to come right to their door, because it is a bitter night and dad can't walk far. They will split the fare with a friend.
Get me a taxi at my door
I need a ride, but not from the corner
Can you send a car to my front door? Please don't make us walk to the corner.
Book a cab to pick me up right here
Dad can't walk far, so don't pick us up at the end of the street
I'd like a taxi to come to the house, not the main road
Please arrange a ride that stops at my gate. I don't want to wait outside in this cold.
Could you call a cab for me? Not one from far away, the nearest one.

Kenji was holding a full tray of cupcakes for his daughter's party when his phone buzzed. It was the school calling. "Put it on speaker," he said to the assistant, "and don't hang up if it goes quiet for a bit. I'm busy with the kitchen." The assistant answered the call on speakerphone. Kenji set the tray on the table and talked while he wiped his hands. The teacher only wanted to say that his daughter had left her coat at school. After the call, Kenji said, "Don't leave a voicemail or send any message, I'll pick it up tomorrow." The assistant did nothing more, and Kenji went back to the cupcakes.

Tomas owned a small shop, and tonight his staff wanted dinner out. It was a puzzle, because nobody agreed on the food. In the past he had called restaurants by hand, which was a manual job he disliked. This time he spoke to the assistant. "Book a table for eight at the Blue Fish for seven o'clock tonight." The assistant checked the restaurant's page and found one free table for eight at half past seven. "Is that fine?" it asked. Tomas said yes. Soon he heard the assistant say that the table was booked, and it added a note to his calendar. He told his staff, and for once everybody was happy.

A taxi or ride app sends a car to a place you choose, called the pickup point. It is for people who don't want to wait on a corner or walk far with heavy bags. You can change the pickup point, the time, or the size of the car. People say, "Pick me up at the front gate," or "Send a bigger car, we have four people." If you have bags of recycling to drop at the centre, you can ask for a car with a big trunk. The app shows the arrival time, so you can understand how long you will wait. Many drivers are proud of their clean cars, and a short note like "Please wait, I'm coming down" is polite.

name: find_calm_shows
does: Finds gentle shows to watch late at night, with no rough scenes, and sets the sound low enough that a whisper would cover it.
inputs: the kind of show or mood you want, such as nature, cooking, or a cartoon about a dog on a leash, and how late it is
people say:
- Find me something relaxing to watch before bed
- Is there anything gentle on TV tonight?
- The kids are asleep, put on something quiet
- I want a nature show, nothing scary
- What's a calm movie I can watch with the sound very low?

Person: Good morning. The light from the window just woke me up. Can you help me move my dentist visit?
Assistant: Of course. Which day would you like to move it to?
Person: Next Tuesday at noon. It's so cold this week that I don't want to go out early.
Assistant: Next Tuesday at noon is free. Should I also tell the dentist's office?
Person: Can you do that for me?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can only change your calendar. I can't contact the office. I can set a reminder for you to call them, if you like.
Person: Yes please, today at three.
Assistant: Done. I moved the visit to next Tuesday at noon, and I set a reminder for three o'clock this afternoon.

name: dry_towel_heat
does: Warms the bathroom radiator for a set time so wet towels dry, then lets the temperature drop again.
inputs: which room, how long to keep it warm, and a heater that is connected to the home network
people say:
- My towels are still wet, can you warm the bathroom?
- Heat the bathroom for an hour
- The bathroom feels damp and cold
- Please dry my towels before lunch
- Turn the towel rail on until I get home

Femke had just moved to the city, and on a cold evening she stood in a shop in her thick coat, holding a basket. Her phone had already helped her translate the signs on the shelves, so now she only needed the numbers. She wanted the cost of three packs of 48 cookies plus 17 loose ones for a party. She typed in a hurry: "whats 48 tmes 3 plus 17". The assistant read the question and answered, "That makes 161." Femke counted the cookies in her head and nodded. "Good," she said. She put the packs in the basket and walked to the till, glad that the numbers were no longer a problem in her new city.

Person: start the vaccum now
Assistant: Which room should the robot vacuum clean? The kitchen, the hall, or the whole floor?
Person: kitchen. a cake fell on the floor and there are crumbs everywhere
Assistant: Starting the kitchen now. It should take about twenty minutes.
Person: can u make the crumbs go away from the table too
Assistant: I'm sorry, the robot vacuum only cleans the floor. It can't reach the table, so a cloth will work better there.
Person: ok thank you
Assistant: You're welcome. I'll tell you when the kitchen is done.

A cycling app keeps a record of your rides: how far you went, how fast, and which road you took. It is for people who want to plan a route or see if they are getting stronger. Many riders turn the ride into a game with weekly goals, and they say, "Set a goal of fifty kilometres this week." You can also change the route before you leave: "Update my route to avoid the big hill," or "Show me a flat way to the park." On a rare day off, a rider may ask, "How far did I ride this month?" The app can answer all of this, so you only need to pedal.

Lengths, weights and temperatures are measured in different units in different places. A recipe from one country may use cups, while your scale shows grams. A unit is just the name of the size, like a metre, a pound or a degree. You don't need a fancy tool to change from one to another. People like to ask in simple words: "How many grams are in a cup of rice?" or "What is seventy degrees Fahrenheit in Celsius?" You can also say, "Show me that in inches," or "I'd like the weight in kilos." The assistant gives the new number and keeps the same amount, only written in the unit you like.

Most homes have a water heater, which keeps water hot for showers and washing. It is for people who want warm water ready when they need it. My grandma loves a quick hot shower in the morning, so she asks the assistant to heat the water earlier. People change the temperature and the time. They say, "Make the water a bit cooler," or "Turn the heater on at six." If the bill is high, they might say, "Show me how much water we used this week." And if there is a puddle under a pipe, people say, "Tell me if there's a leak." Small changes like these save water and money.

A sleepy student on a cold morning wants to see which homework is due soon.
what's due?
homework due tomrrow?
Which assignments are due this week?
Show me my homework deadlines
Can you shift the list so the earliest due date is at the top?
What do I have to hand in soon?
I'm still half asleep. Could you please tell me which homework has to be done first?
Read me my assignments in order of the due date

Rahul was a gardener, and he had planted roses all morning. Before he left to drive to the gym, he looked at his dog's bowl on the porch. "Biscuit's favorite blue bowl is empty again," he said to the home assistant. The assistant understood. It filled the smart water bowl and told Rahul, "Biscuit has fresh water now." Rahul smiled. "Thanks. And he hasn't had his walk," he added. The assistant set a reminder for six o'clock to walk Biscuit after Rahul got home. Rahul grabbed his bag, waved to the dog, and went off to the gym with a calm mind.

Mehmet was grilling beef in the kitchen when the smoke began to fill the room. He texted the home assistant: "it's way too hot in here. make it 3 degrees cooler." The assistant lowered the air conditioner by three degrees and told him it was now 22. Mehmet wiped his face. "Run the fan at double speed too," he typed. The assistant did that and said the fan would stay at double speed for one hour in total. Soon the kitchen was cool and the air was clear. Mehmet sat down with his plate, happy that he did not have to leave the room. Later he asked the assistant to put the fan back on a lower speed.

In August the days are long and hot in many places, so people look at the weather more often. A forecast gives the temperature, the chance of rain and the wind, and it often rounds the numbers, like twenty-nine degrees instead of 29.4. You may notice that the forecast changes during the day. People ask for changes like these: "Show me the forecast for next week," "Tell me when it will rain," or "Give me the weather in the evening." Someone planning a picnic might ask, "Is Saturday a good day for the park?" The assistant looks at the numbers and gives a short, clear answer.

A calendar keeps your plans in one place: lunch with a friend, a meeting, a visit to the dentist, or a Saturday trip to pick apples. It is for knowing what you will do and when you are free. People change a calendar all the time. They say, "Move my meeting to Thursday," "Add dinner at seven," or "Cancel tomorrow's lesson." If a day is too busy, they say, "Don't pack Friday so full." Others want a light week and ask, "What do I have on Monday?" or "Find me a free hour." The assistant checks the days, finds the open time, and makes the change you asked for.

A nurse wants to scale a lemon cake recipe from six servings to three, to brighten a quiet evening, and she can't read the amounts at the bottom of the page.
Halve this recipe
Make it for three people, not six
Can you cut the amounts in half? Don't change the baking time.
Scale the recipe down to three servings
I only need half, so don't give me the full amounts
How much flour for three servings instead of six?
Please rewrite the ingredients for a smaller cake. I don't want leftovers.
Shrink this to half the size

Putri was helping her mum bake cookies. She put the sheet in the oven and then called to the kitchen assistant. She typed quickly: "set a timer for ten minits". The assistant understood and said, "Timer set for ten minutes." Putri sat on the floor and watched the oven light. When the time was up, the timer began to sing a strange little song, and Putri laughed. "That's a funny sound," she said. Her mum took out the sheet, and the cookies smelled warm and sweet. Putri asked the assistant to stop the song, and it did. Then she asked for another timer, five minutes, to let the cookies cool.

Babies eat and sleep in a rhythm, and parents try to keep track of it. A feeding time says when the baby last ate, and a nap time says when the baby should sleep. In autumn the nights get longer, so many babies wake at different times. A digital baby monitor lets a parent hear or see the baby from another room. People ask for changes like these: "Remind me to feed the baby at four," "Tell me if the baby stirs," or "Make the nap an hour earlier." At night a tired parent might just say, "Turn on the monitor." The assistant does it so the parent can rest.

name: night_check_report
does: Checks every door and window sensor at a time you choose and gives a short report of anything left open.
inputs: the time to check, and how you want the report arranged, by room or by floor (for example, the middle floor first)
people say:
- Did I leave anything open?
- Are all the doors shut?
- Check the house before I go to bed
- Is the back window locked?
- Tell me if anything is unlocked before I leave

Person: turn on the lihgt
Assistant: Which light do you mean? The kitchen, the hall, or the bedroom?
Person: the one near the front door. i have to ride to work
Assistant: The hall light is on. Do you want it bright or soft?
Person: bright. Please also turn on the pantry light, I need a vegetable for lunch.
Assistant: Done, both lights are on. Have a safe ride!

Yusuf came home after a night shift at the hospital. He was tired, and he wanted to sit in the hot tub on the patio before sleeping. He put eggs on the stove, and then looked outside. "The water is like ice," he said to the home assistant. The assistant understood. It checked the tub and found the heater was off. It turned the heater on and told him the water would reach thirty-eight degrees in about an hour. Then it wrote a note for him: "Check the main pump filter on Sunday." Yusuf ate his eggs, and when he came back to the patio the water was warm. He slept well that day.

A home security system helps you feel safe when you are out or asleep. A camera watches the door, a motion sensor notices someone moving, and an alarm can sing out loudly if a window opens. The price depends on how many parts you want. People change a few simple things: "Turn the alarm on," "Turn the camera off while I'm home," or "Tell me when someone is at the door." Before a trip they might say, "Arm everything," and when they come back, "Disarm the house." It is perfect for checking the house from far away, if you ask, "Is the front door locked?"

Arthur woke up late on Saturday and saw a poster on his phone showing a dog in a red collar. He rubbed his eyes and typed in a hurry: "find the cinema times for the new dog movie tonigt". The assistant looked and said, "There is a single showing at eight o'clock at the Grand Cinema." Arthur wanted to watch the next film in the series later at home, so he asked, "Continue the series after that." The assistant added the next film to his watch list. Then Arthur asked for a trailer, and the assistant played it. He smiled, got up, and went to find his shoes.

Kitchen appliances make daily jobs easier. An oven bakes, a kettle boils water, a coffee machine brews a cup and a dishwasher cleans plates. You can often tell with your nose when coffee is ready, but a smart machine can also tell you. Some machines can email or message you when a wash is done. People change the settings with simple words: "Make the oven hotter," "Boil the water now," or "Start the dishwasher after dinner." For a difficult stain on a pot, they might ask, "Use the long wash." The assistant sends the order to the machine and says when it is finished.

Kofi was a driver, and he went to bed early because he had a long trip the next day. "Wake me at six," he told the assistant. Then he remembered something. "No, wait. Make it five thirty. My grandma is coming with me, and she likes to leave early." The assistant changed the alarm to five thirty and said so. Kofi also asked it to clear the old alarm for Sunday. "Done," said the assistant. Kofi had a sour taste in his mouth from a long day, so he drank some water, turned off the lamp, and went to sleep. At five thirty the alarm rang, and he got up ready.

Moshe was a cook, and on Friday he was busy planning a party for twenty people. His hands were full of flour, so he spoke to the kitchen assistant in two words: "Guest list." The assistant read out the names it had saved and asked if he wanted anything else. "Sort it," said Moshe. The assistant sorted the guests by name and read the first ten. Then Moshe asked for gentle music to play while he cooked, and the assistant turned on a soft playlist. He also asked it to remind him to buy a plant for each table. The kitchen smelled of bread, and Moshe hummed along.

Person: Is my parcel here yet?
Assistant: You have two parcels coming. Do you mean the books or the lamp?
Person: The lamp. The delivery light on the mailbox was flashing earlier, I think.
Assistant: The lamp is out for delivery and should come by five. The books came yesterday.
Person: Can they leave it inside the mailbox? My last parcel got messy in the rain, and the depth is only half what it needs to be.
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't change what the courier does, and the lamp is too big for the mailbox. I can leave a note asking them to put it under the porch roof.
Person: Yes please. And tell me when they are two stops away.
Assistant: I will. The note is saved.

name: read_label_aloud

- Read me this label
- Is this the cereal or the oatmeal?
- What's on this bottle?
- I can't see the small print. Can you tell me the ingredients?

Keisha was new to the city, and a letter had come with an invoice in a language she was still learning. She held up her phone and said, "Translate this invoice into English and tell me the minimum I have to pay." The assistant opened the page, and it took a moment to load. Then it read the words in plain English. The invoice was for a bike repair, and the minimum payment was twenty dollars by the end of the month. Keisha wrote the date on her hand. "Thank you," she said. She was glad she could understand the letter without asking a neighbor, and she paid it that same evening.

name: gift_idea_finder

people say:

- I need a present for my mum, around thirty dollars
- Any ideas for a gift for a ten-year-old who loves space?
- Help me pick something for my boss's party
- It's her birthday on Saturday and I have nothing. Quick, ideas!

Person: Send my video to Mum.
Assistant: Which video? The one from yesterday in the park, or the new one in the hallway?
Person: The hallway one, where the cat runs. It's my favourite.
Assistant: That video is quite long. Do you want the whole thing or just the first half?

Assistant: Sorry, I can't post on other people's pages. I can send it to your friend privately, if you like.
Person: Fine, do that.
Assistant: Sent to both.

A bill is a paper or message that says how much you owe for things like electricity, water or rent, and the date it is due. It is for making sure you pay on time. A farmer who grows grapes may see the water bill climb in summer, and a student may see a small rent bill each month. People get angry when they miss a date, so they ask for help. They say, "Remind me to pay the electricity on Friday," "Tell me how much the water bill was," or "Move my rent reminder to the first." The assistant keeps the dates and says what is due soon.

Nathan was a grandparent, and he wanted to roast a chicken for his young granddaughter. He did not know how long it needed in the oven. He typed in a hurry: "hwo long for a roast chicken at 200". The assistant answered, "About one hour and twenty minutes for a medium chicken, at two hundred degrees. Check that the juice runs clear." Nathan nodded. "Save that," he said, and the assistant kept the time and the temperature in his recipes. It also set a timer for an hour, so he could look at the chicken. He felt proud of saving the recipe for next time, and he went to peel the potatoes.

name: repeat_weekly_order
does: Repeats a favorite food order each week, such as pizza night for the kids, and writes a note for the driver.
inputs: the usual order, the day and time, the address, and any note for the driver
people say:
- Order the same pizza every Friday
- Make Friday dinner a weekly thing
- Every Thursday the kids want noodles, can you set that up?
- Same order as last time, and again next week
- I'm too tired to cook every Friday, send food then

Weather is how the air feels and moves outside: warm or cold, wet or dry, calm or windy. A wind from the south is often warm in places north of the equator. People look at maps on their phones and zoom in on their town to see the clouds and rain. Dog walkers are among the people who check often, so they can go out between showers. People change what they see with simple words: "Zoom in on my street," "Show me the wind," or "Tell me when the rain stops." The assistant shows the map or reads the answer out loud.

Chioma worked in an office, and her team wanted to buy a new stove for the kitchen because the old one was no longer working. Her boss said he could raise the budget a little. At her desk, Chioma asked the assistant, "Add 450 and 120, and then divide that by two." The assistant answered, "The sum is 570, and half of that is 285." Chioma wrote down 285 as the amount each of the two teams would pay. She sent her boss a short note with the number. He agreed, and they ordered a stove the next day. Chioma thanked the assistant and went back to her work.

Anil, a grandparent, sat in his armchair on a chilly afternoon. He said to the assistant, "Could you please remind me to take a short break every hour? I have a bad back and I sit too long, and the doctor, a kind woman, told me to stand up and walk a little." The assistant set a reminder for every hour from two to eight o'clock. Anil added, "And tell me at four to get ready, because I have to drive to the market." The assistant made that reminder too. When the first one rang, Anil stood up, stretched, and walked to the window. He felt better already.

A washing machine cleans your clothes with water and soap, and a dryer makes them dry. Most machines let you choose a program, often by number, such as a short wash or a long wash. People spend a lot of time on laundry, so they like to change small things. They say, "Wash on a cooler setting," "Make the dryer run for thirty more minutes," or "Tell me when the wash is done." If a shirt has a weird stain, they ask, "What is the best way to clean this?" Folding is the last step, and some people ask for a reminder: "Remind me to take the clothes out."

Zoe was new to the city, and the coffee machine in her flat was a mystery. She held the paper document that came with it, but she could not decide which button did what. She spoke to the assistant: "Make my coffee a bit stronger, and fill only half a cup." The assistant told her which button to press and sent the settings to the machine. A moment later the coffee came out, dark and strong, in half a cup. Zoe tasted it and smiled. Her neighbor downstairs knocked to say hello, and Zoe offered a cup. "Double the strength," the neighbor joked. The assistant, hearing it, asked if she wanted it done.

Sara ran a pepper shop, and on Saturday her shop was full of football fans. She did not have time to look at her phone. She said to the assistant, "Could you please tell me the score of the City match when you get a chance? Customers keep asking, and I would like to tell them, so that they stay and buy something." The assistant checked and said, "City is winning two to one, with ten minutes left." Sara called out the score to the shop, and everybody cheered. Later, she asked the assistant to call her husband and say it was enough for one day. She felt happy as the last fan left.

Omar was a student, studying for an exam, when the lights went out. He had paid the electricity bill the day before, so he knew the problem was somewhere else. He said to the assistant on his phone, "Could you please tell me how long this power cut will last? I have an essay due tonight and my laptop is not charged enough." The assistant checked and said that the power company expected the lights back in two hours. It also put a flashlight on his list as the first item to find. Omar lit a candle, stirred his soup on the gas stove, and used the time to read his notes on paper.

Word count?

Taras was kneeling by the tomatoes when he heard a car on the road. He took out his phone and said, "Is the front door locked? I don't want to walk all the way back to check." The assistant looked at the smart lock and said the door was open. "Please lock it, but don't turn on the alarm," said Taras. "I'm only planning to be in the garden." The assistant locked the door and left the alarm off. Then Taras remembered that his headphones were on the kitchen table. "And please don't open the garage for anyone," he added. The assistant said the garage door was already shut. It was a sunny afternoon, and Taras went back to his tomatoes feeling calm, with the front door locked and the house quiet.

name: hot_water_planner

Tala was late. She drove down the street near the clinic, but every spot was full, and a big truck was parked by the blind corner. "Find me parking near the new library," she said to her phone, "but not the garage, it's too expensive." The assistant found a street spot two minutes away with a small fee and showed her the way. Tala parked, and then asked, "How long can I stay here?" The assistant said the sign allowed two hours and offered to pay from her card. "Yes, pay for one hour," she said. It did, and set a reminder to ring ten minutes before the time ran out. Tala got her bag and ran to the door.

When you shop on a foreign website, the price may be in a different money from yours. An exchange rate tells you how much of your money you need to get one unit of theirs. The rate changes during the day, so the same salty price can cost a little more or a little less tomorrow. People use this to decide how much to spend on a trip or an order. A mother planning a holiday abroad often asks, "What is that in our money?" before she buys anything. People might say, "Show prices in euros," "Use the rate from this morning," or "Tell me how much I will spend in my own currency." The idea is simple: pick the money you understand and let the assistant do the changing.

Person: Can you set a reading time for the kids tonight?
Assistant: Sure. What time should it start?
Person: Seven thirty. Grandpa is coming over to read them a chapter.
Assistant: Okay, a reminder for seven thirty. Which book should I put in the note?
Person: The one about the dragon. Actually, make it eight o'clock, I still have to mow the lawn first.
Assistant: Changed to eight o'clock, with the dragon book. Do you want the reminder to work if your phone is offline?
Person: Yes, please.
Assistant: Done. The reminder is saved on your phone, so it will ring even without internet.

Many phones can read text aloud for people who find small print hard to see, or who just have busy hands. Imagine you are making a roast and your hands are covered in soap and flour, and you want to hear the next step of the recipe. A screen reader speaks the words on the screen, and you can make it faster or slower. Some people find the voice strange at first, but most get used to it quickly. You can also ask for bigger text or a darker screen. People say things like "Read this page to me," "Speak more slowly," "Make the letters bigger," or "Stop reading." These small changes help many people use the same phone in the way that suits them best.

name: dose_reminder
does: Notifies a person when it is time to take medicine and checks that the dose is correct.
inputs: the name of the medicine, how much to take, the times of day, and who it is for, like a child or an uncle
people say:
- Remind me to take my pills at eight and again at night.
- Tell me when it is time for my cough syrup.
- Did I already take today's tablet?
- I keep forgetting my vitamins, can you ping me after breakfast?
- Please nudge my dad to take his heart medicine every morning.

Seren sat down at the kitchen table for the weekly team meeting. The call had started, but the room was so quiet that she could only see people's lips moving. "I can't hear anybody," she said to her tablet. "It's so quiet in here, like I'm sitting in a cave." The assistant turned up the volume. Seren could hear a man talking about the weather report for the delivery trucks. "Still a bit low," she said. The assistant raised it again, and now the voices were clear. Later, when it was her turn to speak, she asked the assistant to turn on her microphone. Seren shared her plans for next month, and the meeting moved on. When it ended, she thanked the assistant and it closed the call.

Ravi ran a small shop that sold phone cases. On Monday morning he had to write to a customer about a refund. He sat at the counter and said, "Help me write a short, polite email. The customer wants a refund for a broken case." The assistant wrote three lines. Ravi read them and said, "Make it sound kinder, and fix the spelling of her name." The assistant did that. "Send it at ten o'clock," said Ravi, "I want it to arrive after she wakes up." The assistant set the email to send at ten. Ravi pressed the button to confirm, and the screen said it was ready. Then he asked for a word count, and the assistant said sixty-two. It was a straight, clear message, and the job was done before the shop opened.

Haruto did not like technology. His power bill had jumped, and his daughter told him to ask the speaker about it. He felt silly, but he said, "Why is my electricity so high?" The assistant said the heavy users were the old fridge and the heater, and that he had used double the power of last month. "Can you start telling me when it is too much?" he asked. The assistant said yes, and started a daily note. Then Haruto asked, "What if I pull the plug on the old fridge in the garage?" The assistant said that could save about half of that cost, but the food inside would spoil. Haruto laughed, kept the fridge, and decided to use the heater only when he needed it.

name: parcel_sound_alert
does: Plays a long, loud tune at the door when the delivery person leaves a parcel, even a heavy sack of corn seed, so you do not miss it.
inputs: which door or mailbox to watch, and whether the tune should be long or short
people say:
- Let me know when my box gets here.
- I'm out in the field, ring me if the delivery guy shows up.
- Tell me when something is in the mailbox.
- Is that my parcel at the gate?
- Make some noise when the courier comes, I can't hear the bell.

A monthly budget is a plan for your money. You write down what comes in, such as your pay, and what goes out, such as rent, food and bills. Some people write their plan on the back of an envelope, and many keep it private and look at it at the end of each week to see what is left. If you spend too much on food, you can move money from another group to put it back. People say things like "Show me what I spent on groceries," "Set my food limit to three hundred," or "Move fifty from fun to bills." Sometimes the bank's words are hard, so you can ask the assistant to translate them into plain words. The point of a budget is to know where your money goes before it is gone.

Mehmet hurried down the hall with a document under his arm and his phone in his hand. "My sister's birthday sneaks up on me every year," he said. The assistant understood and asked for the date. "March ninth," he answered. It added the birthday to her contact and set a yearly reminder. "Also save the number of the new dentist, the one with the pink sign on the door," he said. "The name is Dr. Lund." The assistant saved the name and asked for the number, and Mehmet read it from the card. He had to join a call in two minutes, so he said, "That's all." The assistant told him both contacts were saved, and Mehmet stepped into the room.

name: break_timer
does: Starts a focus timer, rings when it is time for a break, and shows a pale reminder on the screen.
inputs: how many minutes to work, how many minutes to rest, and the days it should run, for example every day until December; if you have several tasks, it can also order them for you
people say:
- I need to focus for half an hour.
- Tell me when to stand up and stretch.
- Give me a break every fifty minutes.
- I keep working too long without moving.
- Set up my study sessions until the exams.

Wanjiru drove a delivery van, and after a rainy day her jacket smelled like a wet dog. At home she told her phone, "My jacket smells terrible and I have a shift at six." The assistant understood and asked if she wanted to use the washing machine. "Yes. Compare the quick wash and the heavy wash for me," she said. The assistant said the quick wash took forty minutes and the heavy one ninety. Wanjiru chose the quick wash with an extra rinse, and the assistant started the machine. "Tell me when it's done," she said. "I'll be inside the garage fixing the van." Forty minutes later, the assistant said the jacket was clean and ready to dry.

Someone wants to book a haircut. They are serious about it and want to fold it in with the rest of their week.
Book a haircut.
Can I get a trim on Friday?
I need to see the barber soon.
Any free slots this week for a cut?
Please find me a haircut, I have a recipe to test on Saturday so the afternoon is better.
Is there a chair free at the salon in fifteen minutes?
Could you check whether Maria has time for me on Thursday?
I would like to make an appointment for a haircut, please, if one is open before the weekend.

Hiroshi sat on the porch with a yellow cup of tea and a bowl of fruit. His grandson had just moved to a new city. "I want to save his new phone number," he told the speaker, "and put his photo on the contact." The assistant asked for the number, and Hiroshi read it slowly. Then he said, "Please download the picture he sent me yesterday." The assistant downloaded it and put it on his grandson's contact card. "Also, he turns thirty-one in July, so remember that," said Hiroshi. The assistant added the date and said it would remind him a week before. Hiroshi smiled and ate a slice of fruit.

Someone wants to change a salty recipe from four servings to more.
Make this recipe for eight people.
Double it.
Scale my soup to six servings.
The recipe in my folder is for four, but ten people are coming, can you fix the amounts?
Cut the salt and everything else in half, I'm only cooking for two.
In ten days I'm hosting dinner for twelve, so what do I need to buy?
I have to borrow a bigger pot, so please tell me how much liquid this makes if I double the people.
Could you please change the cups and spoons so the recipe works for a bigger table?

Person: Hi, I just moved here. Can you tell me when my package comes?
Assistant: Happy to help. Which store did you order from?
Person: A bookshop online. I need an update soon, it's important.
Assistant: I can't see inside that shop's system without a tracking number. Do you have one?
Person: Yes, it ends in 4471.
Assistant: Thanks. Your parcel is two stops away and should arrive today before five.
Person: Can you lower the alert sound? It was twice as loud as I want.
Assistant: I turned the sound down by half.

Person: I'm sorry to bother you, but I have a big report due and I keep losing track of time. Could you set up something so I can focus for a while?
Assistant: Of course. How long would you like to focus?
Person: A quarter of an hour at a time would be best, with a tiny rest in between.
Assistant: Okay, fifteen minutes of work and then a five minute rest. Should I close notifications from your chat apps while you work?
Person: Yes, please close them, that would really help me finish before lunch.
Assistant: Done. I'll start the timer now.

Person: my room is so hot. fix it
Assistant: Sure. Do you want me to turn on the fan or turn down the heating?
Person: not the heating, mom said never touch it. just the fan
Assistant: Okay. What speed? Low, medium or high?
Person: low. I want to sit and play without noise, its already difficult to hear my friends
Assistant: The fan is on low. I can't change the heating schedule, because that needs your mom's code.
Person: fine. I'm getting a snack
Assistant: Enjoy it!

Rhys worked in an office, and a deadline was coming. He needed a shower before his video call, but the bathroom tap was dripping. "Adjust the water heater to forty-five degrees and tell me if there is a leak in the bathroom," he said to his speaker. The assistant set the heater and checked the water meter. "I am sorry, but the meter shows a small leak near the bathroom sink," it said. "Water has been running a little all night." Rhys thanked it and asked it to remind him to call a plumber after work. The assistant added a reminder for six o'clock. Rhys took a quick shower and sat down at his desk just in time.

name: contact_check_in
does: Reminds you to call a person on your contacts list, and pauses your playlist or dims the lights when the call starts.
inputs: the person's name, and how often to remind you, such as daily, weekly or even hourly when someone is unwell
people say:
- Remind me to call Grandma every Sunday.
- I want to check on my brother tomorrow evening.
- Ping me to message Ali before his birthday.
- Don't let me forget to phone my mom this week.
- Nudge me every hour to ask my aunt if she is feeling better.

Someone wants to record a video of the street they visit and hopes it turns out well.
Record a video.
Start filming.
Can you film this street for me?
Film the parade for a minute. No wait, make it two minutes.
Begin recording from the front camera, sorry, I mean the back one.
Hit record, I'm visiting my aunt's street and I want to show the family.
Could you please start a video of the music in the street? I want to remember it.
Please keep the camera steady and record the whole walk.

Someone wants to know where their order is. The little tracking note is hidden somewhere in an old email.
Where's my order?
Track package.
Has my parcel shipped yet?
When will the shoes arrive?
My daughter has a fever and I'm waiting for her medicine, where is that delivery?
Can you look up my last order and tell me what day it comes?
I can't find the tracking number, could you dig it out and tell me where the box is now?

Many families use a tablet for the children, so screen time needs rules. A parent can decide how long a child may watch videos, and the tablet can stop when the time is over. Some families let the kids download only the stories and games that the parents have approved. On school days bedtime comes early, so the screen turns off an hour before. A child who likes to draw can have a drawing app that stays open longer. Parents say things like "Turn off the tablet at eight," "Give her ten more minutes," "Let him download that game," or "Block videos until homework is done." The rules are there to help, and parents can change them whenever the family plans change.

Deepa woke up late, and her head felt heavy. She walked into the kitchen and said to the speaker, "Coffee, please." The assistant started the coffee machine. Deepa worried that the loud beeping would wake her kids upstairs, so she said, "Quieter." The assistant lowered the volume of the machine. "Kettle on," she added, and the assistant turned the kettle on for her tea. Deepa sat down and waited. When the coffee was ready, the machine said so in a soft voice. She smiled, took her cup and a slice of toast, and sat by the window while the house slept.

Somchai was at the beach with friends, and his arms were already getting red. He typed to his phone, "how much sun cream do i need? need more than last time". The assistant said the UV index was high, so he should put cream on again every two hours and use double the amount on his face. Then he asked, "Is the sea warmer than yesterday?" The assistant said the water was two degrees warmer. Somchai also wanted to check the time of the football match later, because his purple team was playing. The assistant looked it up and said it started at eight. He put on more cream and ran off to swim.

The inbox is the place where new email arrives. Unread messages are shown in bold, so you can see what needs an answer. Email programs also score each message, and mail that looks like junk goes to the spam folder. If the text looks too wide to read on a small phone, you can change the width of the page, or ask for a dark screen at night. People say, "Show only unread mail," "Open the last email from Sam," "Attach this photo," "Write a reply saying I'll be late," or "Switch to dark mode." Email is for sending letters quickly, with files attached, and the settings let each person make it easier to read.

name: lawn_mower_helper
does: Tells the robot mower which parts of the lawn to cut, prints a simple map of where it went, and warns you when it got stuck in the wrong place.
inputs: the size of the lawn, the day to mow, and whether the clippings go to recycling or to the compost
people say:
- Mow the front lawn tomorrow morning.
- The robot is stuck by the fence again.
- Why did it cut the flower bed?
- Cut the grass shorter this time.
- Show me where the mower went today.

Lukas was texting his friend about a movie when he remembered his inbox. "check my email and tell me if the restaurant sent the reservation, and write back to say thanks," he typed to the assistant. The assistant found the email: a table for four at seven o'clock on Saturday. It wrote a nice reply, "Thank you, see you on Saturday," and asked Lukas to confirm. "Yes, send it," he said, and the assistant sent it. Then Lukas wanted to talk to his friend about the plan, so he asked the assistant to call her. The phone began to ring.

Person: My phone keeps saying it's full, and I just finished a night shift.
Assistant: I'm sorry. Do you want me to look for big files or old screenshots?
Person: Screenshots. Can you calculate how much space they use?
Assistant: They use about two gigabytes. Should I delete them all?
Person: Not the gray one with the noodle recipe.
Assistant: I can't pick them by what they show. If you tell me the date of that one, I can keep it and move the rest to an album.
Person: It was last Tuesday.
Assistant: Okay, I kept that one and moved the others.

A bookmark helps you remember where you stopped reading. On a phone or a reading device, it saves the page for you, so you can come back to the same chapter later. Some people read a little each day, like a chapter before bed, and some set a time so they do not forget. A book about the ocean may take weeks, while a short story takes an hour. If you want to mix things up, you can keep two books open at once. People say, "Open my book where I stopped," "Add a bookmark here," "Remind me to read at nine," or "Sorry, go back one chapter." A reading list also shows how many pages are left, which makes finishing feel easier.

name: checkup_booker
does: Books a healthy check-up with a doctor, dentist or barber and tells you what to pack, like cards and forms.
inputs: the kind of visit, the day and time you prefer, the place, and for a child's visit the child's height in centimeters if the clinic asks for it
people say:
- I need to see the dentist next week.
- Get me in with Dr. Costa on Tuesday afternoon.
- When is the clinic open on Saturday?
- Can you find a time for my son's check-up after school?
- My knee hurts, I should see someone soon.

Holidays are days when families and friends come together to celebrate. People plan what to cook, who to invite, and how to decorate the house. Some traditions are old, like lighting candles or hanging lights, and others are new. When the plan is ready, everyone feels well prepared. A family might feed a big group, so they make a list of how much food to buy. They might say, "Remind me to buy a gift for Dad," "Put up the lights at six," "Change the dinner to Sunday," or "Add Aunt Rosa to the guest list." Soon the smell of baking tickles your nose, and the whole house feels like a party.

Giorgio was a student, and the lawn behind his rented house was a mess. He told his phone, "Cut the back lawn half as short as the front, I don't want it bare." The assistant sent the robot mower to the back and set a higher blade. Then Giorgio asked it to hold the sprinklers until the grass was cut. "Water it for twenty minutes after, not more," he said. The assistant said it would hold the sprinklers and start them at four. Giorgio went off to study. When he came out, the back lawn looked neat and the water was sprinkling softly. He smiled, took a photo, and sent it to his landlord.

Someone wants to find a cheap movie to watch at the cinema early on Thursday.
What's on at the cinema Thursday morning?
Cheap movie tickets.
Show me films playing early on Thursday.
Cancel the camping plan, we are not putting up the tent in the rain, so what can we watch instead?
Is there a cheaper show before noon on Thursday?
Can you find me a funny movie for early on Thursday, one that doesn't cost much?
I'd like to see what is showing at the cinema, preferably early on Thursday, please.

Tariq woke up with a headache, and his head was full of numbers. His bank account felt empty. "Hey, how much money is left this month?" he asked, still in bed. The assistant said he had two hundred and ten dollars left. "Don't show me the bills, I can't face them yet," said Tariq. "Just tell me if I can still buy groceries." The assistant said yes, if he stayed under fifty a week. He asked it to set that limit and not to send alerts before nine in the morning. The assistant did both. Tariq ironed a shirt for work with a sigh, feeling a little better.

Ada was seventy, and she loved her old kitchen. Her grandson was playing in the yard, and she wanted to bake bread for him. "Turn on the oven to two hundred degrees," she said to the speaker. The assistant did. "Sorry, I meant one hundred and eighty," Ada added. The assistant changed it. Then she said, "Switch on the plug for the kettle." The assistant turned on the smart plug, and soon the kettle was singing. Ada put the dough in the oven and sat down with a cup of tea, waiting for the smell of fresh bread.

Person: Hello. I am going away for the weekend and I want the house to be safe.
Assistant: Good idea. Do you want me to turn on the cameras and the alarm?
Person: Not the alarm. It scares the cat. Just the cameras.
Assistant: Okay. Which cameras? The front door, the back door, or both?
Person: I don't know. Can you explain the difference? I'm not good with these things.
Assistant: The front camera watches the street and the door. The back camera watches the garden. Most people turn on both.
Person: Both, then. I'll look at the clips after my evening meal. It's my favourite part of the day.
Assistant: I'll send you a short clip then.

Tomas had just moved to the city, and his sister was flying in to visit. A wave of heat sat over the town, so he stayed in his flat. "What time does flight two-four-one land?" he asked his phone. The assistant said four thirty. "No, sorry, it's flight two-one-four," he said. The assistant checked again. That flight would land at five ten, twenty minutes late, and the gate had moved to B7. Tomas asked it to tell him if the gate moved again. Then the assistant kindly offered to find the bus from his flat to the airport, and Tomas said yes.

Person: I want to go to bed earlier. Please set an alarm and filter my notifications after ten.
Assistant: Happy to. What time do you want to wake up?
Person: Six thirty. I get frequent headaches when I sleep too little.
Assistant: Alarm set for six thirty. Notifications are filtered from ten at night. Do you want me to track your sleep too?
Person: Yes. And can you tell me why I'm so tired? My bag is a kilogram heavier with the new books, and I walk to class.
Assistant: I can't tell you why you're tired, but I can show how long you slept each night.

Zhen was in the garden with wet hands from cleaning the pond, where the ducks swim. He wanted to thank his neighbor for the leftovers she had left on the gate. "Call Mrs. Park," he said. The assistant asked, "Is this the correct Mrs. Park? You have two." "The one on Pine Street," said Zhen. The assistant dialed her number. After the call, Zhen said, "Text Mei," and the assistant opened a message to his friend, ready for him to speak. Zhen wiped his hands on his trousers and told Mei about the ducks.

Bin day is the day when the trucks come to take away what you put outside. Most towns have a calendar, and the colors tell you what goes where: paper in one bin, plastic and cans in another, and food waste in the compost. An old television can't go in the normal bin; it goes to a special place. Some people climb up to the attic and find more boxes to throw away, then they ask, "Which bin is for this?" Others say, "Remind me about bin day," "Move the reminder to Thursday," or "Tell me what to do with glass." Doing it right means more things get used again.

Someone wants their phone to read the screen aloud because no one is nearby to help.
Read this to me.
Speak the text.
Read it out loud.
Can you read my messages out loud?
Say what is on the screen, please.
Could you please read this letter out loud? The sun on the balcony is so bright and the wind will blow my paper around, so I can't read it myself.
Start the screen reader.

Person: hey just woke up. how far is my ride to the lake
Assistant: Which route? Your usual one, or a new one?
Person: the usual. i hurry to get ther before 8
Assistant: The usual route is 18 kilometers, about 55 minutes at your average speed.
Person: ok. can u book a place for my bike on the train home?
Assistant: I can't book bike places, but I can tell you the train times.
Person: ok thanks. and remind me to bring my book for the train back
Assistant: Reminder set for 7:30.

A recipe is a list of what you need and the steps to follow. It tells you how long to cook each part and what oven temperature to use. A good recipe is like a map: if you follow it, you reach a delicious dish. Cooking times matter. If the oven is too hot, the food burns; if it is too cool, the food stays raw. People say things like "Set the oven to 180," "Start a timer for twenty minutes," "Read me the next step," or "Hold on, I need more time." You also hold the pan with a cloth so you don't burn your hand. An assistant can change the numbers for you when you cook for more or fewer people.

name: clip_share_link
does: Makes a temporary link for a video clip, like the one from last night's grill party, so friends can watch it.
inputs: which clip to share, how many days the link should last, who may watch, and a stop date if you want sharing to end early
people say:
- Send my friends the video from the barbecue.
- Let Grandma watch this clip but only for a few days.
- Share that video, and make the link stop working next week.
- Can everyone in the family see my dance clip?
- I don't want strangers watching my video, can you stop them?

Sigrid was holding a long rope in her hardware shop, and a customer was waiting. The measuring tape only showed inches. "This tape is no help for people who think in meters," she said to her phone. The assistant understood and told her that two meters is about seventy-nine inches. Sigrid cut the rope at the right spot. She coughed from the dust and then said, "Several people ask me this every day. How many grams of nails fit in a spoon?" The assistant said about fifteen grams for a small spoon. Sigrid wrote the number on a card and put it by the counter for the next customer.

Seren was texting a friend on the sofa when the kitchen speaker said the water use at home was high today. Seren remembered that the leak alarm under the bathroom sink had been muted last week because it kept beeping. Seren typed to the assistant, "Please unmute the leak alarm in the bathroom, but don't turn off the water. My favourite show is on and my brother is still in the shower." The assistant unmuted the leak alarm and left the water running. It said the alarm would beep if it felt any wet, and that the sink looked dry for now. Seren sent a thumbs up and went back to the show.

Pooja was scared. The essay about the school camera club was due at nine, and the teacher said it must be under four hundred words. Pooja texted the phone assistant: "how many words is my essay??" The assistant counted and said, "Your essay has four hundred and twelve words. That is twelve over the limit." Pooja asked it to find the longest paragraph, and the assistant read out the first line, the one about the club trip. Pooja cut two long sentences and asked for a new count. This time the assistant said, "Three hundred and ninety-eight words." Pooja was not scared any more and sent the essay with two minutes to spare.

A post on social media is a short message, photo or video that friends and followers can see. People use posts to share news, like the day a big ship comes into the harbour, or just to say hello. Most apps let you change who can see a post, and what happens when a video opens, such as whether it should play by itself. People say things like "make it private," "turn off alerts for this account," or "stop auto play." When someone likes your post, a small alert tells you. If you want the exact time of a post, tap the date under it. And if you do not want any alerts at night, you can ask for quiet hours.

name: sun_time_check
does: Tells a person how long they can stay in the sun before their skin gets sore, and when to paint on more sun cream.
inputs: the person's skin type, the time of day, and the place, like a shady spot by a door or an open beach
people say:
- How long can I stay out in the sun?
- Will I burn if I lie here for an hour?
- When do I need more sun cream?
- My shoulders are already sore, is the sun too strong now?
- Is it safe for the kids to swim at noon?

Person: I'm moving next month. Can you make a list of what I need to clean?
Assistant: Sure. Which rooms should I put on it?
Person: The kitchen and the garden shed. I have half the shed left to do, and the middle shelf is the worst.
Assistant: Okay. Do you want the list sorted by room or by day?
Person: By day, please. Also, I need to tell my band the new address for practice.
Assistant: I can't send messages to your band yet, but I can save the new address in a note that you can copy. Would you like that?
Person: Yes, that helps.
Assistant: Done. The note is saved, and the clean list is sorted by day.

Arash was chopping onions when a message came that his dad was coming for dinner. Arash's dad liked a soft, dim room, but the kitchen lights were harsh. With wet, oniony hands, scrolling through the lamp app was no use. So Arash spoke to the speaker: "Make the kitchen lights half as bright, and use the warmest colour you have." The speaker dimmed the bulbs to half and turned them a soft amber. "Is that the least glare you can do?" Arash asked. "I can go down to ten percent," the speaker said. Arash said that half was fine, and went back to the onions.

Noa grabbed a chocolate bar from the table and ran for the door. "Hey phone, estimate how many steps it is around the park," Noa said. "About two thousand steps for one loop," the assistant answered. "That is ten minutes if you walk fast. Want a timer?" "Yes, ten minutes, and tell me my monthly step total when I'm back." The assistant started the timer. Noa jogged through the gate with the chocolate in a pocket. Ten minutes later the phone buzzed. The loop was done, and the monthly total was about forty thousand steps.

name: beach_water_check
does: Looks at the beach camera and the latest water report and says if green algae is in the sea, and what to do after a swim, like wipe off and rinse.
inputs: the name of the beach and the day
people say:
- Is it okay to swim at Harbour Beach today?
- Is the water clean this morning?
- The sea looks a bit murky, should we stay out?
- Can the kids go in or is there something in the water?
- Any warnings for the bay before we drive there?

name: pet_meal_size
does: Says how many ounces of dry or damp food a pet needs each day, and splits it into meals.
inputs: the kind of pet, its weight (or what the owner thinks it weighs), and what food it eats
people say:
- How much should I feed my dog?
- Is two scoops too much for the cat?
- I think she weighs about ten pounds, how much food is that?
- How much wet food does a puppy need?
- Am I giving my rabbit enough dinner?

Ursula had a family picnic planned on the lawn for Saturday, and the robot mower always started at two. Ursula did not know how to use the mower app, so Ursula picked up the phone and typed fast, in lowercase: "dont let the mower run satuday afternoon". The assistant understood. It blocked out Saturday afternoon on the mower's schedule and said the mower would stay in its station until Sunday. Then Ursula asked about the local weather, and the assistant said it would be dry and warm. Ursula packed the sandwiches and felt much better about the whole thing.

Giorgio texted the garden assistant: "Hello, could you please remind me tonight to wipe the leaves of the big plant in the hall? My brother says the whole thing is covered in dust and I want it to look nice before Gran visits tomorrow, so I would be really thankful." The assistant set a reminder for seven in the evening. It added a short note: use a damp cloth, and hold each leaf gently from below. Giorgio sent back a smiley face. At seven the phone buzzed, and Giorgio went to find a cloth.

Ligaya ran a small bakery shop that was ten years old this week. "Hello, could you please scale my honey cake recipe from eight servings to forty?" Ligaya asked the kitchen assistant. "We are having a party at the shop on Friday and I want to bring a slice for every guest, so I need the right amounts." The assistant multiplied every amount by five and read them out: ten cups of flour, five cups of honey, and thirty eggs. It also said the batter would not fit in the usual bowl. Ligaya found a big clean bucket, mixed the batter in it, and finished the cakes with gold icing.

Clara had just moved to the city with a motorcycle, a single bed and far too many books. "How many boxes do I need for one room and half a kitchen?" Clara asked the phone. "About twelve boxes," the assistant said. "Get twice as many if you have lots of books, because small boxes are better for heavy things." It added a packing list to Clara's notes. Clara then found some old boxes from the neighbour and had to peel off the tape. The assistant put a line on the list: label every box with the room name.

Nandi sat in the garden on a hot afternoon and looked at the tomato plants. "Oh, the tomatoes look so thirsty today," Nandi said to the garden speaker. The speaker understood and started the sprinkler for ten minutes. "I hope that's enough," Nandi said. The speaker answered that the soil would be wet to a good depth, and that the next watering was planned for tomorrow evening. It also wrote today's date in the garden log: the fourth of June. Nandi nodded, pulled the hat down, and watched the water fall.

Hugo owned a small shop and he was getting ready for the winter festival. His hands were full of boxes, so he did not touch his phone. He spoke to the assistant instead: "Turn on the string lights in the yard and remind me to buy candles at four." The assistant switched on the lights, and a moment later the yard glowed gold and white. It said the reminder was set for four o'clock. Because the forecast looked stormy, it also asked if Hugo wanted the lights to turn off by ten. Hugo said yes, and carried the boxes inside.

When you go camping with a dog or a cat, the main thing is to keep its meals the same. Pets like a routine. Feeding times tell the animal when to expect food, so it stays calm in a new place. Many people pack a bowl that can fold flat, and a bottle of water. They might ask, "remind me to feed the dog at six," "move dinner an hour later," or "skip tonight's snack." If a pet eats too fast, people say "make the meal smaller." A few small changes, said in plain words, keep the pet happy and the trip easy.

Noa wanted to stay up late on Saturday night. Mum was out at the toy sale, so Noa asked the bedroom speaker for help. "Set my alarm for eight. No, wait, nine, because it's the weekend." The speaker changed the alarm to nine. "Can you raise the alarm sound a bit? I sleep like a rock." The speaker made the alarm louder. Noa also made the bed neat and asked for a quiet song. The speaker played soft music for twenty minutes and then turned itself off. Noa fell asleep before the last note.

Before a party, most people make a guest list. Then they send invitations, often by email, so everyone knows the day, the time and the place. Some people still like thick paper cards, and they ask a print shop to make them. If the list is long, people upload it to a shared sheet, so friends can add names. When plans change, people say things like "send the guests a new time," "remove Tom from the list," or "add two more seats." The party works best when the list and the invitations match, and the guests know what to bring.

Karim had a long to-do list at work, and it was a mess. "Organize my tasks in order of importance," Karim told the assistant. The assistant sorted them: the report first, then the budget call, then ordering paper. "No wait," Karim said, "by due date instead." The assistant sorted the list again, and this time the budget call came first, because it was due at noon. Karim liked that better. The assistant said it would check off each task as Karim finished it. Karim settled into a steady pace and crossed off three tasks before lunch.

Person: Record a little video of me stirring the soup and send it to my sister.
Assistant: Sure. How long should the video be?
Person: About one minute. And can you post it online for everyone to see?
Assistant: I can send it to your sister. I can't post it online for you, but I can save it so you can post it yourself.
Person: Okay, save it and send it. I would like to learn how to trim it, too.
Assistant: I can trim it to the first minute. Do you want that now?
Person: Yes, please. I want it ready before dinner.
Assistant: Done. The video is sent, saved and trimmed.

Max did not like phones much, but the speaker was easy to use. "I will need somewhere to sleep for three nights in April," Max said, "and my kind sister has no spare bed, and I don't want to bother her." The assistant understood this as a hotel search. It asked which city, and Max said Lisbon. It found three small hotels with free rooms, and one with a fold-out bed that was cheap. It read the names out slowly. Max wrote down the second one on a paper and said that was the one.

Dylan had never moved before, and the phone made everything harder. So Dylan spoke to it: "Find me some movers, but not the expensive ones. I only have a small flat." The assistant looked up three moving companies near Dylan's street and read out the prices. The cheapest one cost about half as much as the biggest company. Dylan asked the assistant to write the name and number of the cheapest one on a note. Then Dylan walked to the shop on the corner and bought a roll of tape and some boxes.

name: battery_hog_finder
does: Searches through the apps on a phone and lists the ones using the most battery, so the phone lasts until the next charge.
inputs: which day or time period to look at
people say:
- Why is my battery dying so fast?
- What is eating all my power?
- My phone was dead by lunch, which app did that?
- Which apps should I close to make the battery last?
- Can you check what used the most charge yesterday?

Tane had a yoga class starting at six, and the dining room was set up for it. The room felt cold and white because the bulbs were on a cool setting. "Make the dining room lights warmer and less bright," Tane told the speaker. "About half as bright as now." The speaker made the lights a warm yellow and cut the brightness by half. Tane asked it to begin a quiet playlist too. The room felt cosy, and the class began on time with the soft light on the mats.

A parent wants to know when the baby's next feed is due (the last one was a creamy flour porridge), following the usual routine.
Next feed?
When does the baby eat next?
What time is the next bottle?
How long until I need to feed the baby?
Hey, baby ate at twelve, so when should the next one be?
Remind me when it's feeding time again.
Is it time to feed her yet? I gave porridge at noon.
Could you please tell me when the baby is due for the next meal, so I can start getting it ready?

Mikko was waiting for a parcel with new headphones. The first message from the shop said it would arrive on the twelfth of March, but that was today and nothing had come. Mikko texted the assistant: "where is my parcel??" The assistant asked Mikko to scan the tracking code from the email. Mikko pointed the phone at it. The assistant read the result: the parcel was at the local post office and would be delivered by six in the evening. Mikko said thanks and asked it to send an alert when the driver was close.

name: scan_and_file
does: Scans a paper page and files it in a folder by year, without anyone having to touch the printer buttons.
inputs: the page on the glass, a friendly name for the file, and the year to file it under
people say:
- Scan this letter and keep it with last year's papers.
- Can you put this bill into the 2023 folder?
- Make a copy of this page on the computer.
- I need to save this form, please scan it.
- Save this receipt as electricity bill.

Rosa mowed the lawn every Sunday, just like her grandma had taught her. This week the robot mower was new, and Rosa asked the garden assistant to start it at ten. "Actually, make that eleven," Rosa said. "The grass will still be wet at ten." The assistant changed the start time to eleven and said the mower would cut for an hour. Rosa also asked it to pack the mower away in its station when the job was done. The assistant said it would go back by itself, and that the lawn would look normal again by lunch.

name: contact_tidy_up
does: Organizes a contact list by joining people who are saved twice, which takes a minute or less, and says sorry if it cannot find a match.
inputs: which contacts to look at, and what to do when two phone numbers are different
people say:
- I have Anna in my phone three times, fix that.
- Clean up my address book.
- Why are there two Davids with the same number?
- Merge my double contacts.
- Can you sort out the duplicates in my contacts?

Someone wants to see gift ideas for an uncle who is turning seventy, who lives in the west and likes a good jacket.
Gift ideas for my uncle?
What should I get him? He's seventy.
Help me find a birthday present.
I need something nice for a seventy year old man.
Any ideas for a gift for someone who loves being outside?
What do you give a man who has everything?
Could you show me a few presents under fifty dollars for an older person?
I am looking for a birthday gift and would be grateful for some ideas, because I never know what to buy.

Moshe sat in the back room, rubbing cold hands. The room felt stuffy and chilly at once, and it was hard to breathe the thick air. "Turn on the heater in the back room and open the vent a little," Moshe said to the smart speaker. The speaker started the heater and opened the vent by a small amount. Then it said the room would be warm in about ten minutes. Moshe asked it to keep the heat on every evening of September. The speaker said it had set that up, and Moshe smiled and picked up a book.

Silvia ordered a pack of sharp pencils and a letter opener for her grandfather. She asked the speaker in the kitchen, "When will my parcel get here?" The speaker looked at the order and said, "The driver will deliver it in an hour." Silvia was very happy. She asked if the speaker could tell her when the doorbell rang, even if she was in the garden. The speaker said yes. In an hour the speaker called out that the driver was at the door, and Silvia ran to get the parcel.

Felix felt worried because the baby had a warm forehead. The phone was not easy for Felix, so Felix just said, "Baby temperature." The assistant did not know how to measure it, but it said, "Use a thermometer. Do you have one?" Felix held the thermometer under the baby's arm. It showed thirty-seven degrees. The assistant said, "That is normal. If the heat goes above thirty-eight, call the doctor." Felix thanked the assistant, put a blanket on the baby, and asked it to remind him to check again in an hour.

Person: I need somewhere to sleep for my friend's wedding. My pension is nothing like my old salary, so nothing too fancy.
Assistant: Of course. Which city, and how many nights?
Person: Porto. Two nights, I think. I'll be tired after the long drive, and I would like to be close to the church.
Assistant: Which dates are you coming?
Person: The tenth to the twelfth of May.
Assistant: Thank you. I can find nearby hotels under a small price. I can't book the room for you, though.
Person: That is fine. Just find me the list, and I will call them.

name: mower_schedule_update
does: Updates the schedule of a robot mower online, and keeps it off the lawn when a toy or a party is in the way.
inputs: the days and times the mower should run, and any day it must stay in its station
people say:
- The kids will be playing on the grass on Saturday, keep the mower in.
- Move the mowing to the evening.
- Don't cut the lawn this week, it's too wet.
- Make the mower start earlier tomorrow.
- Stop the mower, there's a toy on the grass.

The glass of a computer screen is where you see everything: pictures, words and videos. People change how it looks all the time. They might want it to be brighter when they work in a sunny room, or darker at night to rest their eyes. A medium brightness is good for most days. People also change the size of the words. They say "make it brighter," "turn the screen down a bit," or "make the text bigger." Sometimes the screen freezes and people shout at it, but a restart usually helps more. Saying "restart the computer" is a simple way to fix many small problems.

When you order something online, like a water bottle or a pair of shoes, the shop sends you a tracking code. The code shows where the parcel is, and when it should arrive. Every shop has a maximum time it takes to deliver, often five days. If the parcel is late, people continue to wait a day or two and then ask what is wrong. They say "where is my parcel," "change the delivery day," or "send it to my work address." If the item is wrong or broken, people ask for a refund, and the shop sends the money back.

Someone wants to jump to the bottom of the inbox, to measure how old the mail is and find the email with their grade.
go to the bottom of my inbox
show me the oldest emails
scroll to the end
go to teh bottom of my mail, i need an old one
how far back does my inbox go?
find the email from my teacher about my grade
Take me to the very last email in my inbox, please.
I would like to see the oldest messages first, if that's possible.

Wouter worked in a small office, and the morning sun flooded the room, but it was still cold. The heating was set too low, and the room size made it hard to warm. Wouter looked at the wall thermostat and gave up. Instead Wouter said to the assistant, "Warmer, please." The assistant raised the heat by two degrees. Wouter said, "A bit more." The assistant went up one more degree and told Wouter the radiator would take about ten minutes to get hot. Wouter went back to the emails with a warm cup of tea.

Wolfgang sat on the balcony with a cup of tea and watched the street. He suddenly had a good idea for a lesson plan about fancy old maps, and he knew he would forget it by evening. "I'll lose this idea by dinner," Wolfgang said to the phone. The assistant understood. It opened a voice note and said, "I'm listening." Wolfgang spoke for a minute about the maps, the class and the questions. The assistant saved the note with today's date and said it could find it later by saying "my map idea."

Person: going to a dance festival in june, need a place to sleep
Assistant: Sounds fun! Which city, and which nights?
Person: its in Leeds. friday and saturday
Assistant: Thanks. How many people are coming?
Person: me and my mum. she uses a manual wheelchair and it would be hard if there are lots of stairs
Assistant: Got it. I'll look for hotels with a lift and no steps at the door. Do you need a parking space too?
Person: no, we are coming by train. i'll bring oil for her chair, lol
Assistant: Good plan. I'll send you a short list of step-free hotels.

Someone wants to push play on the top video in their list, a clip about using a drill that has two thousand views.
Play the top video.
Play the first one on my list.
Start the drill video.
Can you play the video at the top?
Play that clip about the drill, the one everyone is watching.
Open the most popular video about drills and play it.
Please play the video with two thousand views.
I would like to watch the top clip now, please start it.

Elena lived in a house on a hill with solar panels on the roof, and a friendly neighbour who always asked how much power they made. "How much electricity did my panels make this week?" Elena asked the home assistant. "Forty-two units," it answered. "Actually, I mean this month," Elena said, and the assistant gave the new number: one hundred and sixty units. Elena asked it to search for the best time of day to run the washing machine. The assistant said noon, when the sun was strongest. Elena set a reminder for next Tuesday at noon, and wrote the numbers down for the neighbour.

Felix sat at the kitchen table with a bowl of cereal and a page of homework. "What is seven plus five, and also nine times two?" Felix asked the tablet. The tablet answered right away, "Seven plus five is twelve, and nine times two is eighteen." Felix wrote both numbers on the page. Next Felix asked how the answers came to be, and the tablet explained in simple steps. The tablet also gave a hint for the next problem, but would not just give the answer. Felix finished the page straight away and ate the last of the cereal.

Someone wants a plan for an inside workout that they can post for friends.
Make me a workout I can do inside.
Plan a workout for today, indoors.
I need a quick home workout.
Can you plan something I can do in the living room?
Give me a workout, actually make it a short one.
Workout for twenty minutes please, no wait, thirty.
I want to do arms today, actually legs, and I would like you to write it so I can post it for my friends.
Could you please plan an easy workout I can do inside, because it's raining and I can't go out?

Hiroshi was a gardener, and every morning he walked the same route to the market with a bag of seeds. Today the sun was strong, and the plants in the greenhouse would be thirsty by noon. "The tomatoes will be dry by noon, and I'll be far away," Hiroshi said to the phone. The assistant understood. It set a reminder for noon: water the tomatoes. It also asked if Hiroshi wanted a fast route home. Hiroshi said yes, and the assistant drew a short path on the map. Hiroshi put the phone away and walked on.

Janis had two small children and a lot of bags. "Book me a ride to the station at five," Janis told the phone, "but I don't want a big car, and I can't afford anything fancy." The assistant found a small car for a fair price. Janis added, "Make sure it is a driver with good reviews, someone gentle on the road. The kids get sick." The assistant picked a driver with five stars and a note that said careful driving. It told Janis the car would arrive in seven minutes, and Janis picked up the bags.

A break is a short rest in the middle of work. Many people use a focus timer to work for twenty-five minutes, then stop for five. It helps when you feel tired or when you want to finish a task. Some people set a red light on their desk to show the timer is running. On Saturday, people often change their routine and sleep later. They say "start a focus timer," "remind me to take a break," or "blow the whistle in thirty minutes." A simple routine makes the day easier, and a short rest helps you come back with a clear head.

When you shop online, you pick something, choose a size and pay. Then the shop sends it to your door. Some shops have a minimum order, so you must buy a certain amount to get free delivery. People often buy things for a school project or a gift, and they want the right size. If the thing does not fit, they ask for a return. They say "lock in this size," "change my order to medium," or "send it back." The shop gives you a date for the return, and most shops give you thirty days. It is good to read the rules before you pay.

Ji-woo was cleaning crumbs off the living room carpet while the kids were playing a game. "Whoever wins gets to choose the next song," Ji-woo said. The kids laughed. Ji-woo picked up the phone and typed quickly, all in lowercase: "play that silly song agian". The assistant knew which song the family loved most, the one with the funny animal sounds. It played the song through the living room speaker and turned the volume up a little. The kids danced on the carpet, and the winner cheered, and Ji-woo kept cleaning with a smile.
