Booking a table is a simple way to make sure there is a seat for you when you arrive. The restaurant writes down your name, the day, the time and how many people are coming. Plans change, so people often ask to move things around. They say "make it eight instead of seven" or "we are five now, not four." Some ask the assistant to select a place on the same road as the cinema, or a cool spot with a garden. Opening hours matter too, so people check "are you open on Sunday?" before they leave home. If the answer is no, they ask for another day.

name: voice_note_finder
does: Finds a voice note you recorded before, so you can hear it again, even a large one that runs for many minutes.
inputs: a word from the note, like a name or a thing such as a chair, and roughly when you made it
people say:
- Where is that recording I made about the new chair?
- Play the voice note from last Tuesday.
- I said something into my phone about Dad's birthday, find it.
- What was that idea I recorded in the car?
- Can you dig up my old audio notes about the garden?

Theo was kneeling in the garden with muddy gloves when his phone buzzed. A peach tree at the back fence had dropped fruit all week, and tonight he saw a strange shape near the gate. He had invited his sister for dinner and did not want any surprises.

"Check cameras," he said to the phone.

The assistant opened the live view from the back camera and showed it on the screen. Theo leaned close. It was only a neighbour's cat sitting on the wall, washing its paw.

"Thanks," Theo said, laughing at himself. The assistant asked if he wanted a message whenever the camera saw movement after dark. Theo said yes, and the assistant switched on motion alerts for the garden camera until the morning. Then he went back to his peaches.

Most cars tell you when the fuel is low, but it helps to know how much the tank takes. In many places fuel is sold by the liter, so people ask how many liters are left or how far they can drive. Tyre pressure is another thing to check, because soft tyres use more fuel. People say "pump them up a little" or "what should the pressure be?" On cold mornings the windscreen can be icy, so drivers wipe it clean or turn on the heater. Some cars have a manual gearbox, and the driver changes gears by hand. If you forget where you parked, you can ask the car app to show the spot on a map.

Bread dough needs time to rise, and that time depends on the room. In a cold kitchen it can take two hours, and in a warm one only one. Bakers often put the bowl in a spot near a south window, where the sun keeps it cozy. Many recipes explain that the dough should double in size before baking. People ask for help with this all the time. They say "set a timer for forty minutes" or "remind me to check the dough." Later they change the oven: "make it a bit hotter" or "bake it ten minutes more." A friend who works at a hotel bakery once told me the same rules apply to a big batch.

A lawn stays neat when the grass is cut often. Many people now have a robot mower that drives around by itself, and they tell it when to start and when to rest. Some ask it to mow just a single strip by the fence. They say "mow the front lawn today" or "skip tomorrow, it is raining." A sprinkler waters the grass early in the morning, and people change how long it runs: "water for ten minutes less" or "turn it off." Edges look tidy when they are trimmed by hand. A child may climb on the mower by mistake, so it is wise to pause it when kids are outside. Even the kitchen microwave beeps more quietly than a mower, so some people schedule mowing for midday.

Clocks show what time it is where you are, but the world has many time zones. When it is noon in London, it can already be dark in Tokyo. People use a clock app to know the time somewhere else before they make a call. A mother might ask, "what time is it in Sydney? I want to call my son." Others say "show me New York next to my clock" or "is it too late to ring Berlin?" When you travel, the phone changes its clock by itself, but you can also ask it to set the time by hand, or to wake you an hour earlier. Clocks also change in spring and autumn, so people say "did the clocks go forward?"

Person: Good morning. I am a retired teacher, and I would like to find a quiet trail for a walk this weekend, because my knees do better on flat ground and I need to be home before dark.
Assistant: That sounds lovely. Which area would you like to walk in?
Person: The hills north of town. My friends will join me, so I need a path that is wide enough for three.
Assistant: Do you want a short trail, or something that takes half a day?
Person: Short, please. About two hours. And will it rain? My ear aches when the weather turns.
Assistant: I can show the weather, but I cannot say how your ear will feel. Saturday looks dry in the hills.
Person: Then Saturday it is. Please make a daily weather note for the hills until then.

Many hobbies run on small plans. A person who paints may decide to finish a picture by the end of february, and a knitter may want a scarf done before winter. Models and drawings take many evenings, so people set a little time each day. They ask an assistant to help with that. They say "remind me to paint at seven" or "move my knitting hour to Sunday." Someone who buys blue yarn or a new brush may ask "add them to my list." If a friend wants to see the work, people say "send a photo to Anna" or "forward my drawing to my brother." The hobby stays fun because the plan is easy to change.

Marisa woke up late with a dry mouth and felt thirsty and a little silly. Last night she had left the hot tub cover half open. She stumbled to the kitchen, cracked an egg into a pan, then remembered the water.

"What is the hot tub temperature right now?" she asked her speaker.

"It is thirty-two degrees," the assistant said. "Last night it was thirty-eight."

"Oh no. Heat it back up to thirty-eight, please."

The assistant turned on the heater and said it would take about two hours. Marisa then asked it to remind her to close the cover once she was done. She also asked it to read the pump's weekly clean list, which had three hundred words on it. The assistant read the first part, and Marisa ate her breakfast and listened.

They want to know how far they rode today.
- Distance?
- How far did I go?
- How many kilometres was my ride this morning?
- My legs feel like jelly, how long was that ride?
- Tell me the length of today's ride from the shelf where I left my phone, I mean from the start to the end.
- I am hungry and I need to know if I earned a big lunch, so how far did I cycle?
- Could you please tell me the total distance of my last ride?
- I want to design a longer route next time, so how far did I get today?
- Please show me the miles for my bike ride.

A workout plan is a list of exercises you do on certain days. Each exercise has sets and reps. A set is one round, and reps are the times you do the move in that round. Many people find it hard to start, and a new gym can make you feel scared. A plan helps because you know what to do. People change plans all the time. They say "add one more set" or "make Friday a rest day" or "find me an easy leg workout." If someone is tired or sore, they ask for "fewer reps" or "a lighter day." Rest days matter, too. Muscles grow when you rest. If you get hurt, go to a hospital or a doctor and do not push through it.

They want to spend less time walking by seeing their steps and checking the pace.
- Steps and pace, please.
- How many steps today, and was I quick?
- Show me my distance and tell me how fast I went.
- My shoes feel loose and I think I walked slowly, so what was my pace and how many steps did I take?
- Can you tell me how far I ran and what my average speed was?
- Give me this week's steps, and also tell me which day was my longest.
- I have a task at noon, so could you please tell me how long my run was and how far I went?
- What is my step count, and how does it compare with yesterday?

Person: Hello? I do not know how this works. I want the radio.
Assistant: Hello! I can help. Which station would you like?
Person: The news one. It is so quiet in here, I need some noise.
Assistant: I can play the news station on your speaker. Is it the local news or the world news?
Person: The local news, please. They say the town may earn a prize this year.
Assistant: Playing the local news now. Is the volume fine?
Person: A little louder. The old vent in the kitchen makes a loud sound and the news is raw and hard to hear.
Assistant: I made the volume louder. Tell me if you want it even higher.

Leila got home after a long night shift at the clinic. The air in her flat felt dry and heavy, and she could see dust floating near the mirror in the hall. She dropped her bag by the door and said, "Turn on the air purifier in the bedroom, please."

The assistant switched it on at a soft speed so it would not wake her neighbour's baby through the thin wall.

"Wait, no, I mean the living room one," Leila said. "I will sleep on the sofa today."

The assistant turned off the bedroom purifier and turned on the one in the living room. Then it asked if she wanted the humidifier too. Leila nodded and said yes, and the assistant switched it on. She lay down, and the room hummed quietly.

Tariq had been in the city for only a week, and his new phone already had a serious problem. The battery was almost empty by lunchtime. He sat on a bench in the yard behind his building and said, "Why is my battery so bad?"

The assistant showed him which apps used the most power. A map app had been open all morning.

"Turn on battery saver," Tariq said.

The assistant did, and the screen got a little dimmer. Tariq then asked it to pair his earbuds, which he had bought at the market. The assistant found them and connected them. Last, Tariq asked for the battery level in a number. "Twenty-five percent," the assistant said, and it offered to remind him to charge the phone when he got home.

A pool needs care to stay clean. A pump moves the water through a filter, and most people let it run for a few hours each day. If the water looks messy, with leaves or green spots, people ask for help. They say "turn the pump on now" or "stop the pump, someone is cleaning." Hot tubs have a heater, so people also say "make it warmer" or "keep it at thirty-eight." When they go on a trip, they ask to pause the schedule and resume it when they are back at home. A cover keeps out the dirt and keeps the heat in, so "remind me to put the cover on" is a common request.

Rest days are part of a good fitness plan. Many people feel busy and want to train every day, but muscles need time to heal. A plan might say train on Monday, Wednesday and Friday, and rest on the other days. A tired person might tell the assistant, "skip today's workout" or "move it to tomorrow." If someone starts a run and feels sick, they say "stop the timer" or "end my workout." Others ask for a break in the middle: "pause for a minute." After a long workout, people eat a simple meal, like toast with eggs, and drink water. Some also ask the assistant to remind them to stretch.

They want the score of a match that is on now.
- Score?
- What's the score?
- Who is winning?
- Is it still a draw?
- How did my team do today?
- Could you check the score for me? I left my phone in a small sink of bubbles and I cannot look.
- Tell me what the score is in the football game.
- Can I borrow a minute of your time to hear the latest score from the match?
- Please tell me the result of the game.

A packing list helps you remember what to take on a camping trip. It starts with the big things, like a tent, a sleeping bag and a lamp. Then come small things like socks, a hat and a first aid kit. People like to make a list at home and check each thing off before they leave. They say "add a rain coat" or "take off the extra jacket, it will be warm." Many families cook on a small stove, so they add pots, plates and matches. Some people take a photo of the packed car as a memory. A monthly trip may need a lighter list, so people ask to save the list and use it again.

Freya sat on a box labelled KITCHEN and texted her phone assistant. The new flat had a hard floor and no heater, and the only warm thing was her scarf. She had spent the morning moving boxes up the stairs and now her fingers felt cold.

"brrr, it's like swimming in an icy lake in here," she typed.

The assistant understood and turned the smart heater in the living room up by two degrees. It also said the pizza place nearby had a crispy deal tonight, but she had not asked for that. Freya laughed and typed, "no pizza yet, but thanks."

"Do you want me to remind you at six?" the assistant asked. She typed yes, and a small reminder appeared on the screen.

name: bus_delay_checker
does: Tells you if a bus or train is late and how long the wait will be, even on a stormy day when everything runs slowly.
inputs: the line or route number, and the stop where you are waiting
people say:
- Is the number nine bus late?
- Do you have any idea when the next train comes?
- I have been standing here for twenty minutes, what happened to the bus?
- Is the line to the airport running normally today?
- Will I make my train if I leave in ten minutes?
- Tell me if my tram is delayed. I would hate to pay for a taxi if it is only a short wait.

Abigail stood in the kitchen with a spoon in one hand and her phone in the other. The kids were asking for a film night, and she needed something nice and short. She had only a single free evening this week.

"What films are on at the cinema on the twelfth of March?" she asked.

The assistant listed four films for that day and showed the times. One was a cartoon about a fox that started at five.

"Book two seats for the cartoon," she said, "and a big popcorn if saving some money is possible."

The assistant booked the seats and said the combo deal with popcorn cost less than buying them apart. Abigail said yes, and the assistant sent her the tickets.

Alessandro rolled over, rubbed his eyes and grabbed his phone. The bedroom was grey, and he could not remember if he had paid the water bill. He felt his stomach drop a little. The last one had been very low, so this one should be too, but the due date was close.

"Water bill?" he mumbled.

The assistant said the water bill was one hundred and ten euros and was due on Friday. It had not been paid yet.

"Pay it," said Alessandro.

The assistant asked him to confirm the amount, and he said yes. A moment later it told him the payment was done and a receipt was in his email.

"Thank you," he said, and went to make coffee, feeling much better.

Eleni was unpacking boxes behind the counter of her little shop when the door chime rang. A courier stood there with a big parcel. It was the third one this week. She signed on the screen and then looked at the pile of mail on the desk, with a heap of letters beside a box smelling of fish from the market.

"Track parcel," she said to her phone.

The assistant asked which one. She read the number from a sticker, and the assistant said that parcel had been dropped at the shop an hour ago and was signed for. Then she asked if the total of waiting parcels was right. It said yes: four packages in all. Eleni nodded and cleared the desk for the next one.

A work meeting is easier when everyone knows the plan. The agenda is a short list of what will be talked about, and people send it before the call. To join a call, you click a link or ask your assistant to open it. Some people join from far away, so sound and screen sharing matter. People say "share my screen" or "turn my microphone off" or "make the camera brighter." If a call is running long, they ask to adjust the plan: "move the next item to tomorrow" or "give us five more minutes." Some teams even book a meeting room by the hour, like a pound for each minute, in a joke about how time costs money.

Person: Sun cream.
Assistant: Sure. Do you want me to add it to your shopping list, or are you looking for the weather and UV level?
Person: Shopping list. I own a small shop near the beach and tourists keep asking.
Assistant: Okay. Which kind: for kids, or for adults?
Person: Both, please. And can you convert the temperature of the sea into Fahrenheit? A customer from the US asked me.
Assistant: Today the sea is eighteen degrees Celsius, which is about sixty-four Fahrenheit.
Person: Neat. Also, can you make the swimming flags work from here?
Assistant: I am sorry, I cannot control the beach flags. I can tell you what colour they are today.
Person: That is fine. Thanks.

Person: I want to see more likes on my garden pictures.
Assistant: I cannot make people like your pictures, but I can show how many likes each one has. Do you want that?
Person: Yes. Show me the one with the dream roses first.
Assistant: That post has forty likes. Half of them came yesterday.
Person: Oh, tiny but nice! Post another one tomorrow.
Assistant: Which photo should I post, and at what time?
Person: The tomatoes, at nine in the morning. And no sad face on it, please. My neighbour told me a joke last time and I did not want to cry from laughing.
Assistant: Okay. I will post the tomato photo at nine tomorrow with no sad face.

A calendar keeps your plans in one place. Each event has a day, a start time and an end time, and many have a short note. People use a calendar to see when they are free, and they ask an assistant to add or change things. They say "put dentist on Tuesday at three" or "move my meeting to Thursday." If two events happen at once, the assistant tells them. Some people design their week with colours: blue for work, green for home. A family might share a calendar, with a single page on the fridge at home and the same one on their phones. When a plan is cancelled, people say "delete it" or "take it off."

Person: Quick, how long since the baby ate?
Assistant: Do you mean the last bottle or the last meal?
Person: The bottle. I do not want the long list, just the time.
Assistant: The last bottle was at two o'clock, so about three hours ago.
Person: Good. She is total chaos today. Put her nap on the schedule, please. And she has to wear the warm hat, since it is cold.
Assistant: I can add the nap. What time should it start?
Person: Four. Not five. My son's hamster needs feeding at five.
Assistant: Nap at four, noted. I cannot feed the hamster, but I can remind you at five.
Person: Please do.

They want to find out what is on at the cinema.
- Anything good on?
- What's playing tonight?
- Show me films near me.
- I am so sad and bored, I need a good laugh at the movies.
- There is nothing to do this Thursday, any films showing?
- Could you tell me which films are on at the cinema by the park?
- I want to see something new, what are the new releases?
- If it is not too much trouble, would you please check which movies are showing, as my friends and I need to park nearby and plan the evening?

When you order something online, the shop sends it to your address. You can pick a size, a colour and a day for delivery. Sometimes plans change, and people ask to edit the order. They say "change the size to medium" or "send it to my office instead." If a parcel is left at the gate and not at the door, people say "tell the driver to knock." Some shops let you drop an item off at a shop to return it. If the thing is wrong, people write "sorry, this does not fit" and ask for their money back. An assistant can track the parcel too, and say "it will come tomorrow."

name: packing_helper
does: Keeps a list of moving boxes, what is inside each one, and which room it goes to, so you can find the box with the cool things, like the kettle, fast.
inputs: the box label or number, the things inside, and the room
people say:
- Which box has my plates?
- Where did I put the cables?
- Add the winter coats to box twelve.
- My mom needs the pan, what box is it in?
- Which boxes go to the bedroom?
- Where is the box with the cat's food bowl? The cat needs to be fed.

Ella closed her shop at six and walked to her car. A single light was on in the car park, and the fuel light on her dashboard was glowing. She sat in the driver seat and said, "Hey car, how much fuel do I have?"

The assistant said she had a quarter of a tank, enough for about sixty kilometres.

"Good. Is the tyre pressure okay? I would prefer to know before the long road home."

The assistant checked and told her the front left tyre had less air than the others. It was half a bar low. Ella asked it to find the nearest petrol station with an air pump. The assistant showed one two minutes away on the map and started the directions. She pulled out and kept her mouth closed, listening.

They want to know what homework is due soon.
- Homework due?
- What do I have to hand in this week?
- Tell me which assignments are due on Friday.
- I forgot my diary, can you read out my homework list?
- Is there anything due tomorrow? The weather is stormy and I do not want to go out and find out.
- I need to finish thirty-one pages of reading, which subject was that for?
- Please ask the speaker to tell me what is due before the end of the week.
- Could you please tell me my deadlines for maths and history?

It was a rainy afternoon, and Lars came in from the garden with mud all over his boots. The floor in the hall looked terrible. He had forgotten that guests were coming for tea.

"Start the robot vacuum in the hall," he said, "in twenty minutes."

The assistant set a timer. Then Lars looked at his cleaning schedule on the screen and said, "Pull up the schedule for the week." The assistant showed it. The vacuum usually ran on Monday and Thursday mornings.

Lars took off his boots and asked the assistant to mop the hall on Saturday as well. It added the task. Twenty minutes later the little vacuum hummed to life and rolled across the muddy spots, and Lars sat down with his tea.

Kasia was behind the counter of her flower shop when her phone rang with a call reminder. A meeting with her supplier was about to begin, and she had left the link in her inbox. Her hands were full of ribbon, so she typed fast.

"join the evnt with marek now"

The assistant understood and opened the meeting on her phone. The screen showed her supplier's face. Kasia propped the phone against a vase and carried on with the ribbon.

A few minutes later she said, "play the agenda," and the assistant read it out loud. There was less to discuss than she had feared: prices, one late delivery and a new type of rose. When the call ended, the assistant asked if she wanted notes sent to her email, and she said yes.

Leticia did not like technology, but her daughter had put a smart speaker in the living room. Today she was planning a short trip to a little village by the sea, and she wanted a hotel.

"Um, hello? I want to book a room for three nights," she said slowly.

The assistant asked which dates, and Leticia gave them. It found a small hotel with a free breakfast and read out the price.

"Oh, wait, I made a mistake. Two nights, not three. My husband cannot come for the last one."

The assistant changed the booking to two nights and said the room was for two guests. It asked if she wanted it to boil down the choices by showing only rooms with a sea view. She said yes, thank you, and it did.

Board games are more fun when everyone agrees on the rules. People use a timer to keep each turn short and a score sheet to see who is ahead. At the end of a game, someone counts the points and says who won. Players often ask a smart speaker for help: "set a one minute timer" or "add ten points for Ben." If a player makes a mistake, they say "take two points off" or "start the round again." A game can feel long, and by the middle everyone wants a snack. If you are keeping a receipt from the shop for a new game, you may need it for a return. Puzzles are quieter, and people use a timer to see how fast they finish.

Edward was eight, and he wanted to bake bread with his grandma. She had gone to the shop for butter, so he stood by the oven and asked the speaker, "How long does bread take to bake?"

"About thirty minutes at two hundred degrees," the assistant said.

"Okay. Put the oven on, but not too hot. I do not want it to burn."

The assistant said it could only set the temperature if he asked it to, so he said, "Two hundred." The oven began to get warm. Edward did not want to rush, so he asked for a timer for thirty minutes. When his grandma came home, the kitchen smelled lovely, and they both waited for the warm loaf to come out.

Niamh finished her night shift at seven and wanted a slow walk home to wake up. The morning was chilly, and her feet hurt. She asked her phone, "Start a walk, and track the distance."

The assistant began recording. After ten minutes, Niamh stopped by a bench and said, "Actually, no, I mean a run. A slow one. I need to burn off this coffee."

The assistant changed the activity from walking to running and kept the minutes so far. It asked if she wanted it to notify her at each kilometre. Niamh said yes.

At the first kilometre the watch buzzed, and a calm voice told her the pace. She smiled. Then she remembered a small loan she owed a friend and asked the assistant to remind her about it that evening.

They want to make the text bigger and also see how many words they have written.
- Bigger text and a word count, please.
- Can you zoom in on my page and tell me how many words there are?
- The letters look tiny, and I want to know if I reached five hundred words.
- Increase the font size and show me my word count.
- I am working in a bad light from a bulb that is too dim, can you make the text larger and count my words too?
- Make this bigger, and then check the spelling.
- Please make the writing easier to read and tell me how long my story is. It is taking a bitter long time to finish.
- Larger text, word count, thanks.

Emre had taught history for thirty years, and he loved to eat out. This Friday he wanted a quiet dinner for two. He sat on his sofa with a bar of soap on the table, since he had just washed his hands, and said to the speaker, "Find me an Italian restaurant that is open tonight."

The assistant gave him three names. Emre said, "Not the one on the main street, it is too loud. I do not want to wait outside either."

The assistant took that place off the list and called the second restaurant to ask about a table. It said a table was free at eight. "That is fine," said Emre. The assistant booked it for two and sent him the address.

Shirin was a student with an exam in two weeks, and her group chat would not stop beeping. She was cooking dinner and frying onions in a pan, and the phone sat on the shelf, inside a plastic bag to keep the grease off.

"Read my new messages," she said.

The assistant read three messages. One from Dara said the study group would meet at the library on Sunday.

"Reply, I will be there at ten," said Shirin.

The assistant sent the reply. Then Shirin said, "And remind me in two weeks to send Dara my thanks for the notes." The assistant set the reminder, and Shirin turned back to the glue of onions sticking to the pan and stirred them.

They want a note to be saved without the whole thing being read out.
- Save this note, but do not read it back.
- Just write down my idea, no reply needed.
- Do not make a long note, only the main point.
- I do not want a voice message, please type it.
- My bag is heavy and my hands are full, so jot this down and do not ask me questions.
- When the bus arrives, write down what I say, but no beeping sound.
- Keep it short, and do not send a link to anyone.
- Could you please save this thought for me and not open the notes app until I ask?

Rafaela was nine, and it was her turn to help her mum shop for school things. They were in the living room with the tablet on the table. Her old shoes had a hole in the bottom, and march was only a week away.

"Find me new school shoes," Rafaela told the assistant.

The assistant showed some. She picked a pair and asked, "Do you have these in a size bigger? My feet are growing."

The assistant said they did and that they cost half as much as the shoes in the other shop. Rafaela clapped. Her phone buzzed to say the order could arrive the next day, and she asked it to put the order in. Then she asked for double socks, and the assistant added two packs to the basket.

name: burn_care_guide
does: Tells you the first steps to take for a small burn, and says when it is time to call for help, so you do not need to lift a hand to a pricey doctor for every little thing.
inputs: where the burn is, how big it is, and what caused it
people say:
- I touched the hot pan, what do I do?
- My arm is red after the oven, should I put ice on it?
- How do I treat a burn from boiling water?
- When should a burn go to the doctor?
- My driver friend burnt his hand on the car engine, help.
- Is a blister on my finger serious?

Layla was standing outside the cinema with her friends, and the night was cold. The streets were quiet, and there was only a television playing in a shop window across the road. Her hands felt like ice.

She texted her phone assistant, "my feet are freezing and i dont want to jog home lol."

The assistant understood that she needed a ride. It asked, "Do you want me to book a taxi from here?"

"Yes please."

It found a car three minutes away and showed the driver's name and the plate. It asked if the pickup point was the front door of the cinema, and Layla said yes. The assistant sent a message when the car arrived, and Layla and her friends climbed in, glad of the heater.

Bo was on the sofa with a baby on one knee and a laptop on the other when the phone rang about the family trip. His son wanted to see the sea, and a temporary break from work sounded perfect.

"Find a hotel by the beach for fifteen nights in August," Bo told the assistant, and then he groaned. "No, that is too long. I only have a week."

The assistant said, "I will look for seven nights." It showed a family room that would last the whole week and cost a fair price. Bo asked if breakfast was included, and the assistant said yes, and also that check-in was at three.

Bo asked it to book the room for two adults and one child, and it sent him the details.

They want the phone to read the text on the screen out loud.
- Read this aloud.
- Read it to me.
- Can you speak the words on my screen?
- The letters are blurry today, please read the page.
- I want to hear this article instead of reading it.
- Please read my monthly email, I left my glasses in the vinegar cupboard, where I hide them from the kids.
- Would you please read the text out loud for me? My eyes get tired in the evening, and listening is much easier than looking at a small screen.
- Start reading from the top and go slowly.

The person wants the feeder to add less food to the dog's bowl, because the dog drops half of it on the carpet.
less food
smaller portion tonight
the bowl is too full again
can you cut the dinner amount a bit
put less in the bowl pls, he keeps droping it on the carpet
please halve his breakfast from tomorrow
He is getting round, so could you give him a little less at each meal?
I think she's had enough kibble, give her a lighter scoop
Would you mind making the portions smaller from now on? The vet said he should lose some weight.

name: rain_warning
does: Tells you if it will rain at a time you choose, and it can replace a loud alert with a quiet message.
inputs: the place, the day (like Wednesday) and the time
people say:
- Will it rain on Wednesday afternoon?
- Do I need an umbrella for my walk at six?
- Is it going to pour tonight?
- Should I hang the washing out today?
- Will it be dry for the match on Saturday?

Fatima walked in after her night shift, very tired. She had promised her kids a party for Eid, and yesterday she had forgotten to buy any decorations. She hated to let them down. She dropped her bag on the sofa and said to the kitchen speaker, "Eid ideas." The speaker listed a few: paper lanterns, a banner, and a table with sweets. Fatima nodded and said, "Order lanterns." The assistant found a pack of twelve paper lanterns that could arrive on Friday, put them in her basket and asked her to confirm. She said yes. Then she asked it to make a note on her list about baking sweets with the kids on Thursday. The assistant saved the note and said it would remind her on Thursday morning. Fatima smiled, set an alarm for noon so she could sleep a little, and went to bed.

When you want to watch a film, you can ask an assistant to find one for you. It looks at what is on at the cinema or on your streaming service. People often change the type of film, the time, or the cinema. They might say, "Something funny, not a weak story," or "Show me times after six," or "Only films the whole family can see." If you like animals, you could ask for a movie about a dog. You can also ask to watch the trailer first. If the answer is not right, say "Show me another one" or "Try the cinema near the train station." The assistant then looks again and gives you a new list.

Many homes have a filter in the heating or air system. It catches dust, and when it gets dirty the air does not go through well. Some filters sit in the attic, and others are at the bottom of a unit in the hall. A filter needs to be changed every few months. People ask an assistant to remind them, with words like "Remind me to change the filter in March" or "Move that reminder to next week." If the filter is too old, they may say "Book someone to fix it" or "Find a repair person who can come on Saturday." They can also change the day with "Make it Monday instead" or ask for a cheaper visit.

name: garden_waterer
does: Waters the garden at the time you choose, and it can compare the soil with the rain to decide if it should skip a day.
inputs: the plant or bed (like the round bed by the gate), how many minutes to water, and the water to use (tap water, or cooled water from boiling pasta)
people say:
- Water the tomatoes for ten minutes
- The round bed looks dry
- Is it worth watering if it rained yesterday?
- Give the pots a drink every morning at seven
- Turn the sprinkler off, I'm mowing the lawn

Baraka was not good with phones, but his daughter had put a speaker in the hall. He wanted a haircut before the wedding, and he did not know the number of the barber. He looked at the speaker and said, "My hair is touching my collar and the wedding is on Saturday." The assistant understood. It asked, "Would you like me to book a haircut at Sam's Barbers, the closest shop to you?" Baraka said yes. The assistant checked the opening hours, said the shop was open until five, and booked a slot for Friday at four. Baraka was afraid he would miss it, so he asked for a reminder. The assistant set one for three o'clock. Later he told his wife the speaker had done it all. She was wearing a new skirt for the wedding, and she laughed that his hair would match.

Eleanor owned a little shop on Mill Street. On Sunday it was her sister's birthday, and she wanted to welcome her with a nice gift. She said to her phone, "Find me a gift under twenty pounds, and make it cheaper than the average one you showed me last time." The assistant showed three ideas: a jar of local honey, a scarf and a book. Eleanor said, "Double the honey. She loves it." The assistant changed the order to two jars of honey and added a card, then asked if she wanted it sent to the shop. She said yes. It said the gift would arrive on Friday. Eleanor smiled and asked it to remind her to write the card on Thursday evening.

A weather forecast tells you what the sky will do, so you can plan your day. Most people look at it in the morning and think about what to wear. A forecast can show rain, wind and the temperature outside. People ask for changes, such as "Show me tomorrow instead" or "What about this weekend?" They may want a different place, so they say "What's it like in my mother's town?" If you are on a tight budget for a trip, you might ask, "Will it be dry on Friday so I don't need a taxi?" On a day with an empty calendar, you can say "Tell me when the rain stops" and the assistant will let you know.

The person wants to know how many days are left until a date.
How many days until Friday?
Days left to the deadline?
Count down to Christmas, please.
How long till my report is due on the twelfth?
I want to sit down and plan, so how many days are there before the exam on the ninth?
Actually, not the ninth, I meant the nineteenth.
Could you tell me how many days remain until we move into our cozy new flat on the first of May?
Wait, I said Friday but I meant next Friday, so how many days is that?
How many sleeps until the holiday?

Avi drove a delivery van, and he came home late. His wife and kids were asleep, and the washer was humming in the kitchen. He wanted to watch the game, but he did not want to wake anyone. The TV was in the downstairs room, right under the bedrooms, so he spoke quietly. He picked up the remote and said, "Turn on the sports channel, but don't turn it up loud." The assistant switched on the channel and set the volume low. Avi still worried about the noise, so he said, "Put the subtitles on." The assistant turned the subtitles on. Then he said, "Connect the TV to my headphones." The assistant said it had connected them. Avi sat on the sofa and watched the game in peace.

name: unread_mail_reader
does: Reads out your unread emails one by one, which helps when your eyes hurt or you feel sad about a full inbox.
inputs: the folder (like inbox or work) and how many emails to read, such as a dozen
people say:
- What's new in my mail?
- Read me my messages, my eyes are tired
- Anything from my boss today?
- Do I have any unread emails?
- Tell me the last five emails I got

name: bin_day_reminder
does: Tells you which bin goes out this week, so you never miss the man on the truck and food waste does not sit and attract flies.
inputs: your address, and the colour of the bin, such as the bright blue one
people say:
- Which bin do I put out tonight?
- Is it recycling week?
- When do they pick up the glass?
- Did I miss the bin collection?
- Remind me the evening before the green bin goes out
- Does cardboard go in the blue one?

Knitting is a hobby for slow evenings. You pick a pattern, a colour of wool and the size of the needles. Many people ask an assistant to keep track of their rows, so they do not lose their place. They might say, "Count one more row" or "Go back two rows." If the scarf is too short, they ask, "Make a note that I need ten more rows." To keep the wool safe from the cat, some put the basket on a high shelf and ask the assistant to remind them to tidy up. A good assistant can also find a new pattern. People say, "Show me an easier one" or "Something with a bigger needle."

name: coffee_brewer
does: Makes a cup of coffee at the strength you choose, and tells you the exact time when the last drip falls.
inputs: the size of the cup, how strong you like it, and the time to start; it only needs water in the tank, which is its fuel
people say:
- Make me a strong coffee
- I'd like a small cup, not too bitter
- Get the coffee ready by seven
- Brew two mugs for the guests
- Is the coffee done yet?

When you go camping, you pack a bag with a tent, food and warm clothes. There is no microwave in the hills, so people take a small stove. A packing list helps you remember everything. Many people keep a list on their phone and ask an assistant to change it. They say things like, "Put a torch on the list" or "Delete the heavy book." They also check the weather in the hills, because it can change a lot, and ask for the daily forecast, such as "What will it be like on Saturday morning?" If rain is coming, they say, "Put the rain jacket at the top of my list." On the trip they ask for the trail time and the sunset.

People use units every day: centimetres for a table, kilograms for a bag, degrees for the weather. Sometimes you need to change from one unit to another, because a recipe or a shop uses a different one. If you pack for a trip, a suitcase may have a limit in kilograms, and you may only know pounds. You can ask, "How many kilograms is forty pounds?" or "What is the current temperature in Celsius?" People also say, "Make that in inches" when they want the same number in another unit. Even when there is a cloud outside and it feels cold, a number in the right unit helps you decide what to wear.

The person wants the assistant to restart the wifi router because the connection is slow.
Restart the router.
the wifi's lagging again, fix it
The internet is crawling, can you reboot it?
My video keeps freezing, so turn the wifi off and on.
Please clear the connection and start it again.
Power cycle the modem, thanks.
Can you reset the wifi? The kids can't stream their swim lesson video.
Could you give the router a fresh start? I want a smooth video call.
Would you mind restarting the wifi, please? I have a meeting in ten minutes and I need the picture to stay smooth.

Amani was locking up her shop when she remembered she had left the back door open at home. She had a large article to finish for the local paper, and she was late. She did not stop walking. She typed to her phone, "is the back door lockd at home". The assistant checked the smart lock and said the back door was unlocked. Amani typed, "lock it and message my brother to check the camera". The assistant locked the door and sent a message to her brother, Jabu, asking him to look at the camera. A minute later it told her the door was locked and that Jabu had answered. Amani let out a breath and walked on to her car.

name: clip_trimmer
does: Cuts a video clip so you can remove a dirty or shaky part and keep only a fraction of it.
inputs: the clip, the start time and the end time
people say:
- Cut the first ten seconds off my video
- Make this clip shorter, just the goal
- Keep only the last minute
- The end is boring, chop it
- Save just the bit where she blows out the candles

name: free_time_finder
does: Looks through your calendar for a gap of the length you need and puts an event there, with a reminder so you are ready.
inputs: the length of time, the days to search, and a short name for the event (like buy milk)
people say:
- When am I free on Thursday?
- Find me an hour next week for the dentist
- Squeeze in a short call with Tom tomorrow
- Do I have a gap this afternoon?
- Put a meeting with Anna somewhere quiet in my week

Aroha was in her kitchen, holding a letter with a shiny red stamp. It said a parcel was waiting at the post office, and she had to collect it before Saturday. Her knees were not good that day. She said to the speaker, "I wish somebody could deliver my parcel, because the post office is so far for my legs." The assistant understood she wanted a delivery, not a pick-up. It opened the post office page, found a button for redelivery, and booked it for Thursday morning. Then it read her the details. Aroha thanked it and said, "What a clever thing." She put the letter in the drawer and made a cup of tea.

Oksana was running for the bus, still half dressed for work, with one sleeve of her coat hanging. Her phone showed a missed call from the school, the final one of three. She had no time to tap through her contacts, so she typed, "cal the school back and put it on speaker". The assistant called the school and turned on the speakerphone. A woman said her brother had a fever and needed to go home. Oksana said she would come at noon. The assistant then asked if she wanted to leave a voicemail for her boss. She said yes and told it what to say. It sent the voicemail. Oksana jumped on the bus just as the doors were closing.

Marek, a retired teacher, liked to read a story to his grandson every evening. Tonight a sudden storm had put the power out for a minute, and his clock was wrong. He spoke politely to the speaker, "Could you please set an alarm for six tomorrow morning? I need to be up early because my grandson has a school trip and I promised to make his lunch." The assistant said it had set the alarm for six. It added that it would report the weather in the morning, if he liked. Marek said that would be kind. Before bed, he asked for a ten minute timer for the end of the story, so that he would not read too long. The assistant started the timer. In the morning, the alarm rang, and the speaker said it was going to be dry.

Giulia was leaving for a train station far across the city, and she was late. At the gate, she remembered that a man was coming to mow the lawn at ten. She said, "Please unlock the side gate for twenty minutes at ten, and tell me when the doorbell rings." The assistant said the gate would unlock at ten and lock again after twenty minutes. It also said it would send a message with a picture when somebody pressed the doorbell. Giulia thanked it and ran for the train. At five past ten her phone buzzed with a picture of the gardener at the door. The side gate clicked open, and the gardener walked in.

Abena woke up late on moving day. Her head was still full of a big project at work, and now there were boxes everywhere. She said to the speaker, "How many more boxes do I need? I have twelve, and I think I need double." The assistant said a two-bedroom flat usually needs about thirty, so she needed eighteen more. It offered to order them. Abena said, "Yes, and one roll of tape." The assistant ordered eighteen boxes and tape to arrive at noon. She also asked it to put "eat the cooked rice" on her list so nothing went to waste, and to design a packing plan by room. It made a plan: kitchen first, then the bedrooms, and the books last.

Ciaran was a busy parent, and the baby had been crying since six. He stood outside the back door for some air, and his phone buzzed. It was another notification from a photo app. He said, "Stop alerts from the running group, and change my post about the jog to friends only." The assistant turned off notifications for the group and changed the post so only friends could see it. Ciaran then asked how many people liked the picture. The assistant said six people had liked it and two had left comments. Ciaran smiled, read the comments aloud to the baby, and asked it to switch the alerts back on tomorrow.

Daniel got home from the hospital at eight in the morning. He wanted to watch the video of his niece's school play from last November, but the file was huge. He said to his tablet, "Play my video from November, and make it half the size, I want to send it to my mum." The assistant found the clip and made a smaller copy that took half the space. Daniel said, "Move it to my family folder, please." The assistant did. It said there was no extra room left on the tablet and asked if it should delete old videos. Daniel said no, just send it to his mother. The assistant sent the small copy, and Daniel fell asleep on the sofa while it played.

Ngozi's shop was about one kilometer from her home, and she often used her phone at the till. Today a customer stood too close to her screen. She felt uneasy and typed, "lock my phone and cancle the shared note with the price list". The assistant locked the black screen and said the note was no longer shared with anyone. Then she typed, "change my password for the shop email". The assistant asked if she wanted a new password suggested. She said yes. It gave her a strong one and asked her to save it. Ngozi wrote it on a small card and put it in the locked drawer under the till.

Lights make a room feel different. A bright ceiling light is good for reading, and a soft lamp is better when you want to chill on the sofa. Smart bulbs let you change the brightness and the colour with your voice. People say, "Make it dimmer" or "A bit warmer, please" or "Turn the lamp off in the hall." Some colours match a mood: red for a spicy dinner party, blue for a calm evening. You can also say "Set the lights to the same as last night" and the assistant will use the same colours again. If you have a bridge game with friends, you may say "Make the table lamp brighter."

Oksana was a student with an exam in the morning, and she was not sleepy at all. She sat on the rug in her room, with her books spread around her, trying to dig out a few more facts. At last she looked at the clock. Only five hours were left before the alarm. She said to her phone, "Sleep timer." The assistant asked how long. "Twenty minutes," she said, and it started soft rain sounds that would stop after twenty minutes. Then she said, "Wake me six." The assistant set an alarm for six o'clock. She turned off the light and, listening to the rain, fell asleep before the sounds ended.

Ibrahim was moving to a flat in the north of the city to be near his daughter. His grandson had come to help and was setting up the speaker. Ibrahim was not sure what it could do, so he said, "I don't want the movers on Friday, and I don't want to pay for a whole day." The assistant asked if he wanted a different day. "Monday," he said. It changed the booking to Monday and to half a day. Then Ibrahim asked it to read out the phone number of the gas company, so he could give them his new address. The assistant read it and offered to call. His grandson, who would fly home on Sunday, smiled and said, "See, Grandpa, it is easy."

Mathieu, a retired teacher, wanted a short trip to the sea with his wife. He sat at the table, where a thick curtain kept the afternoon sun away, and said to his tablet, "Find a small hotel by the sea for two nights, and make the price half of the last one we looked at." The assistant found three small hotels. One cost half as much as the last hotel. Mathieu asked for the one with breakfast. The assistant said it had a double room free on Friday and Saturday. Mathieu said to take it, and asked for a late check-in. Then his wife brought a slice of cake. The assistant confirmed the booking and gave him the check-in time.

name: delivery_tracker
does: Shows where your order is and when it will arrive, and points you to the nearest pickup spot if you missed the driver.
inputs: the shop name or order number, and what you ordered, like cat food that should not go stale
people say:
- Where is my package?
- When will my groceries come?
- The driver didn't ring, where's my order?
- Has my parcel left the warehouse yet?
- Is my order late?
- Can I collect it somewhere nearby instead?

Person: Hello. I'm a bit bored at my desk, and I hope you can help. Could you please read me today's headlines, because I want something to talk about at lunch with my colleagues?
Assistant: Of course. Which kind of news would you like: world, local or sports?
Person: Local, please. I want to know if anything is happening on my walk home.
Assistant: Which town do you live in?
Person: Leeds.
Assistant: Here are the top local stories. A new bike lane opens on Monday, the market moves to the square, and a bus strike is planned for Thursday.
Person: Thanks. Can you tell me who will win the match tonight?
Assistant: Sorry, I can't know who will win. I can tell you when it starts and the latest team news.
Person: Okay, just the time then.
Assistant: It starts at eight.

name: note_finder
does: Searches your old notes for a word you remember so you can check what you wrote, even if it is a long note and the part you need is in the middle.
inputs: a word or two from the note, and roughly when you wrote it (like the phone number of your neighbor)
people say:
- What did I write about the garden fence?
- Find the note with my neighbor's number
- Where's that recipe I saved last month?
- I wrote something about a birthday idea, find it
- Look up my shopping note from Sunday

Svetlana drove a bus all day, and she came home to a full kitchen bin. She was not sure what went where. Under the big tree by the gate stood three bins. She asked her phone, "Which bin is for glass, and is it collection day?" The assistant said glass goes in the green bin, and collection was tomorrow at eight. Svetlana had eight old jars and wondered if there was enough room. The assistant said the bin should fit them if she took off the lids. A bird began to tweet in the tree. Svetlana asked, "Remind me at seven to put the bin out." The assistant set the reminder, and she went back inside to rinse the jars.

Siobhan was a grandparent who loved her small lawn. On a hot day she noticed the grass turning brown, and she felt bad. She spoke politely to the garden assistant, "Could you please turn on the sprinklers for the back lawn this evening? The grass looks dry, the heat was bad today, and my grandchildren are coming to play on Saturday." The assistant asked how long it should run. Siobhan said twenty minutes. It turned the sprinklers on at seven. She also asked for a dose of lawn food, and the assistant put a bag of it on her shopping list. Later she watched the red sun go down while the water sprayed across the grass.

Kasia was a cook, and the lunch rush was over. She sat down near the fridge, took out her phone and said politely, "Could you please book me a dentist appointment on Tuesday afternoon? My tooth is sore, and I can only go when the restaurant is quiet." The assistant asked which dentist. "The one on Park Road," she said. It checked and found they were open until five and had a free slot at three. Kasia said to take it, and the assistant booked it and added it to her calendar. She asked it to zoom in on the map so she could see the street, and the assistant did. Then she asked for a reminder to eat something soft that evening. The assistant set the reminder, and Kasia went back to her pans.

The person sees a price in a foreign currency and wants to know what it is in their own money.
In dollars?
What's that in pounds?
How much is forty euros for me?
The rate is never constant, so what is it today?
My phone sensor read the price tag, but what does it cost in my money?
Create a quick list of these three prices in pounds, please.
Could you tell me roughly what this hotel bill is in Canadian dollars?
Is the rate better than yesterday?

Oluwaseun drove a taxi at night, and he came home cold. The house was freezing, and the heating was offline because the router was switched off. He turned the router on and said to the speaker, "Turn the heating up by two degrees, and keep the kitchen warmer than the hall." The assistant said the thermostat was back online and raised the heat by two degrees. It set the kitchen radiator higher than the hall one. While the house warmed up, Oluwaseun began to tidy the shoes by the door. He saw a gap under it, almost an inch wide, and asked the assistant to remind him on Saturday to buy a draught strip. The assistant said it would. He sat down in the warm kitchen with a hot drink.

Somchai was texting his friends on the sofa while he watched his baby sister. She had eaten some apple puree at five, and now it was dark and a little snow was falling. A sudden cry came from the baby monitor. He told the speaker, "Don't turn on the big light, and don't play any music." The assistant understood and turned on the small night lamp in the baby's room, very dim. It also showed the camera on his phone. The baby was only moving in her sleep. Somchai asked the assistant to tell him when it was time for her next feeding. It said the next one was at nine. He went back to his texts.

Translating helps when you meet a word you do not know. You can ask an assistant, "How do you say thank you in Spanish?" or "What does this word mean?" People change the language, and say "Now in French" or "Say it slower." Many learn phrases for a trip, like ordering a soda in a cafe or asking for the bill. Spelling is another need. If you are not sure, you can say "How do you spell that?" If the translation app stops working, people may disconnect from the wifi and connect again, then say "Try that again." Some phrases are funny when translated word by word, so people ask, "What does it really mean?"

Person: Will it be colder than yesterday?
Assistant: Which town do you want the weather for?
Person: Cork. I'm taking my dad out for a walk, and he gets cold easily.
Assistant: In Cork it will be about three degrees colder than yesterday, with a light wind.
Person: Then he needs a coat. Oh, wait, I gave you the wrong day. Undo that, I mean Sunday.
Assistant: Sure. On Sunday it will be about the same as yesterday, a little warmer in the afternoon.
Person: Double check whether it will rain.
Assistant: There is a small chance of rain after four. Maybe go early.
Person: Thank you. We will go in the morning, when the sky is open and clear.

Milena was a cook who liked loud music while she washed up. The kitchen speaker was thin and small, and the sound was weak over the water from the sink. She said, "Turn the music up a bit, and play it on the hall speaker too." The assistant raised the volume by two steps and grouped the two speakers so the song played in both. Then Milena said, "Record this song's name, I want to find it later." The assistant saved the title in her notes. It said it could also record a voice note if she wanted. Milena said no, that was enough. She finished the dishes with the sound filling the house, twice as loud as before.

Person: Good morning. I just woke up and I want to watch my show.
Assistant: Which show would you like?
Person: The detective one. I want the final episode.
Assistant: The detective show has seventeen episodes. The final one is ready on the streaming app. Do you want me to play it?
Person: Yes, but first pause it, I need to make my tea.
Assistant: Sure, I'll start it when you say go.
Person: Can you divide the screen so the news plays at the side?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't divide the screen on this TV. I can switch to the news after the episode.
Person: Okay, that's fine. Go.
Assistant: Playing the final episode now.

Max was a child sitting on his bed with a tablet. His mom was at work and had left money for dinner. He was hungry and typed, "order pizza and lok how long it takes". The assistant asked what kind of pizza. Max typed, "cheese plz". The assistant found a cheese pizza at a nearby shop and said it would cost twelve dollars and arrive in thirty minutes. Max looked at the price and thought it was too high, because his mom had left ten. He typed, "anything cheaper". The assistant found a small cheese pizza for ten dollars. Max typed, "yes order it", and the assistant placed the order. Then it told him to wait by the door.

Person: The bathroom tap has been dripping all night and I can't sleep. I just woke up and it's still going.
Assistant: That sounds annoying. Would you like me to book a plumber? Which day suits you?
Person: Today if possible. I'm cooking chicken tonight, so I need the kitchen free.
Assistant: I'm sorry, the earliest plumber can come tomorrow at nine. Is that all right?
Person: Can you display the other times?
Assistant: Here are the choices: tomorrow at nine, tomorrow at two, or Friday at ten.
Person: Tomorrow at two, please.
Assistant: Booked. They will message you when they are on the way.

Person: It's hot in the house after working outside. Put the fan on.
Assistant: Which fan do you mean? There is one in the living room and one in the hallway.
Person: The hallway one, please. Actually no, the one in the bedroom.
Assistant: There is no fan in the bedroom, but there is an air conditioner. Do you want the fan in the hallway or the air conditioner?
Person: Oh right, my mistake. The air conditioner. Set it to twenty-two degrees.
Assistant: Done. Anything else?
Person: My electric fan is old and noisy. Can you replace it?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't replace it myself, but I can put a new one on your shopping list.
Person: Yes, please do that.
Assistant: It's on your list.

Person: Hi, I'm new in the city and I want to bake bread before work. How long should the dough rise, and what temperature should the oven be?
Assistant: Which kind of bread is it?
Person: A simple white loaf.
Assistant: Let it rise for about an hour, then bake it at two hundred degrees for thirty minutes. Do you want a timer for the rising?
Person: Yes, and make it loud, because my flat is noisy.
Assistant: Done. The timer is set for one hour at a high volume.
Person: Thanks. Which jam would pair well with it, and which shops are open on Sunday?
Assistant: Strawberry or apricot pair well with warm bread. I'm sorry, I can't check shop opening times yet.

Nikhil, a retired teacher, had an urgent problem. His grandchildren were coming for dinner in one hour, and his good blue shirt was still in the washing machine. He grabbed his phone and typed fast, in lowercase: "how much time is left on the washng machine". The assistant checked and said the wash had twenty minutes to go. Nikhil asked it to track the cycle and tell him the moment it ended. A little later the phone chimed, and the assistant said the wash was done. Nikhil moved the shirt to the dryer and asked for a quick fifteen minute setting. The assistant started the dryer. When the doorbell rang, the shirt was warm and dry, and Nikhil was ready.

Sanne owned a small gift shop near the station, and tourists paid with coins and notes from many countries. One afternoon a man held up a vase that cost seventy euros and asked what that was in dollars. Sanne said to her phone, "What is seventy euros in US dollars right now?" The assistant looked up the exchange rate and said it was about seventy-six dollars. Sanne told the man, and he paid with a smile. Later, tired of the constant checking, she asked the assistant to alert her if the euro and dollar rate moved by more than two percent in a day. The assistant said it had set the alert. Sanne dropped a coin into the jar by the till and went back to work.

Most people use music to fill a room, to keep them company while they work, or to help them relax. What they change most is the volume, the song and the playlist. Volume works a little like a car brake: a small push slows things down, and a big push stops everything. So people say "turn it down", "a bit quieter, please" or "pause". To change the song they say "skip this one", "next song" or "play something else". For a playlist they might say "play my morning list" or "shuffle it". If you wish to hear one artist, say "play" and then the name. Even a silly old song is easy to find: just say the words you remember.

An air purifier is a small machine that pulls in the air of a room, cleans it, and sends it back out. People use it when the air smells bad or feels heavy, for example after cooking soup or frying fish, or when someone is sick or has allergies. Most people change only a few things: on or off, the fan speed, and a timer. They say "turn on the purifier", "make the air fresher", "set the fan to low at night" or "run it for two hours". A humidifier is a different machine. It adds a little water to dry air, so people say "make the room less dry". If a cycle ends too soon, they can say "repeat that" and the machine starts again.

A day at the beach needs a little planning. Sun cream protects your skin, and it wears off, so people ask for a reminder to put more on every two hours. The tide is the sea moving in and out twice a day. Swimming can be difficult when the tide is high or the waves are strong, so people ask "when is low tide?" or "is it safe to swim now?" Water temperature tells you how warm the sea is. Some people like to swim in warm water, and others only like to paddle. Many bring a flask of tea for afterwards. A good question to ask is "how warm is the sea today?"

name: line_check
does: Tells you whether a post office, bank or pickup counter is open and how long the line is, so you can stay home on an icy day, and it can send a signal when the line is short.
inputs: the place you want to visit and the time you plan to go; a welcome note with the closing time is shown at the end
people say:
- Is the post office still open?
- How long is the line at the bank right now?
- Can I collect my parcel today or is the counter shut?
- Tell me when the queue at the pickup point gets short.
- I don't want to wait outside in the cold, is it busy at the bank?

Television is for news, shows, films and sport. Most people change only a few things: the channel, the volume and sometimes the subtitles. Subtitles are the little words at the bottom of the screen. They help when the room is noisy, when a show is in another language, or when someone cannot hear well. People say "put the subtitles on", "I can't hear it, what does he mean?" or "turn the words off". To change the channel they say "go to channel five" or "put on the news". For streaming they say "play the next episode". After a camping trip, many families like to sit down and say "find a good film for tonight".

Ingrid was eight, and she wanted to cook pancakes for her mum's birthday. Her half finished puzzle of a lighthouse sat on the table, but the pancakes came first. The recipe was for four people, and Ingrid said to the kitchen speaker, "Make the recipe for two." The speaker gave her half of everything. Then Ingrid remembered. "Wait, no! Three people. Grandpa is coming too." The speaker changed its answer and said three quarters of the cups and spoons in the first list. It told her to use a small bowl and one egg plus a splash of milk. Ingrid measured everything, stirred, and carried the first warm pancake to her mum.

name: order_arrival_time
does: Tells you when your food order will arrive and where it lies on the way, and it says if a delay looks weird, longer than usual.
inputs: the restaurant name or the order number, and what you ordered, like a dozen dumplings
people say:
- Where is my food?
- How much longer until the pizza gets here?
- It's been an hour, has my order even left the restaurant?
- Is the driver close to my street?
- When will my dinner arrive?

A bank account is a safe place for your money, and the balance is how much is in it right now. Most people check their balance on a phone, and some move money between their own accounts, for example from a savings account to the one they spend from. They say "how much do I have?", "move fifty to savings" or "send twenty to my other account". If an account is almost empty, a small alert helps. If a card is lost, people say "freeze my card" so no one can use it. A sharp drop in the balance after a big bill is easy to see in the list of recent payments, and you can ask for that list too.

Fatima, a student, was packing for a weekend hike in the hills when her friends texted that they were leaving in ten minutes. It was urgent. She looked at her half empty bag and said to her phone, "What's the weather in the hills on Saturday, and what should I pack?" The assistant said it would be sunny by day but near freezing at night, with a light wind. It listed warm socks, a hat, a rain jacket and a second water bottle, and it took the cold night into account by adding a thin sleeping bag. Fatima took a deep breath, as if to breathe out the stress, and packed everything in five minutes.

Person: Good morning. I am moving to a smaller flat next month, and my back is not what it used to be, so I would be very grateful if you could help me find a moving company that carries boxes up the stairs.
Assistant: Of course. Which city are you moving in?
Person: Leeds. My flat is on the third floor and there is no lift.
Assistant: Thank you. What day would you like to move?
Person: The twelfth of next month. A low price would be nice, but kind helpers matter more.
Assistant: I can't book a company for you, but I can find movers in Leeds who work on the twelfth and show their prices and reviews. Shall I do that?
Person: Yes, please.

Person: Pool temperature.
Assistant: Which pool do you mean, the one at the front of the shop or the hot tub out the back?
Person: The front one. My aunt had it put in years ago.
Assistant: It is twenty-six degrees right now. Would you like me to change it?
Person: Drop it to twenty-four tonight.
Assistant: Done. I set the heater to twenty-four from this evening.
Person: Thanks.

Wendy, a cook, was writing the menu for her little restaurant. She had typed a line about grilled fish with garlic bulb butter, and she wanted every dish to sound delicious. She was not sure about one word and said to her laptop, "Spell vinaigrette." The assistant spelled it out letter by letter, and Wendy fixed her mistake. Then she said, "Word count." The assistant told her the menu had ninety-four words, which was too many for one small card. Wendy asked it to read the menu back, cut the longest dish name, and save the new version. The assistant did, and the card fit.

A phone is used for calls, messages, photos and maps, and it works only while the battery lasts. People change a few things often. Brightness is how bright the screen is. Outside in the sun the screen is hard to see, so people say "make the screen brighter", and at night they say "dim it". Battery saver makes the phone last longer, so they say "turn on battery saver". Do not disturb is like a small sign on your shirt collar that says you are busy: calls stay quiet until you say "turn off do not disturb". On a new phone you peel off the plastic film first. When storage is full, people say "delete my old photos".

name: wash_cycle_picker
does: Picks the right washing program for a bag of clothes and can choose a quiet cycle for the night.
inputs: what kind of clothes are in the bag, and whether the machine should be quiet; it should understand the care label words, like wool or delicate
people say:
- What setting do I use for wool?
- Wash my gym clothes, but keep it quiet, the baby is sleeping.
- Which cycle is best for towels?
- I have a bag of sheets that need washing tonight.
- How hot can I wash this shirt?

Person: How many days until my tomatoes are ready?
Assistant: When did you plant them?
Person: Seventeen days ago. My neighbour waved me over yesterday and said they often take about seventy days.
Assistant: Then they should be ready in about fifty-three days. Do you want a reminder?
Person: Yes, can you remind me in fifty days?
Assistant: Yes. Should I remind you in the morning?
Person: Morning is fine.

When you order something online, the shop packs it and gives you a tracking number. The tracking page shows where the parcel is and when it should arrive. People ask "where is my order?" or "when will it get here?" If the date changes, a good app will explain why, such as bad weather or a busy week. Sometimes people change the delivery day by saying "deliver it on Friday instead". If the parcel is wrong, they ask for a refund and say "I want my money back" or "send it back". On a phone, turn up the brightness to read the small code on the creamy white label inside the box.

Roya was a student planning a birthday party for her friend, and sixty people were coming. She stood in the hall with a pen and a very long list. First she said to her phone, "How do you spell congratulations?" so the banner would look right. The assistant spelled it out slowly, and she wrote it down. Next she asked it to make a playlist of happy songs for the party, and the assistant made one with forty songs. She also wanted a score sheet for the party game, but the weather news was bad and the party would be indoors. So she asked the assistant to remind her tomorrow to move the tables.

Person: Post my lunch photo.
Assistant: Which photo do you mean, and which account should I use?
Person: The one of the pan of roast potatoes. Delicious, right? Put it on my cooking page, not my work page.
Assistant: Got it. Do you want a caption?
Person: I don't want anything long. Just Sunday lunch.
Assistant: Posted to your cooking page with the caption Sunday lunch.

When you pay with a bank card, the money does not always leave your account at once. Sometimes the payment is only held for a day or two, and then it becomes final. This can confuse people, for example after buying theater tickets. If the bank takes the money twice, people often get angry and ask "why was I charged two times?" or "cancel the second payment". The transfer of money from one bank to another can drag on for a few days too. To check, people say "show my latest payments" or "is the money still pending?" A quick look at the list usually shows what is going on.

Hobbies and crafts give people something calm to do with their hands. An artist may paint, a knitter may make a scarf, and a child may build a model plane. Each hobby has small things people change: the colour, the size, the time it takes. A painter says "mix a darker green". A knitter says "I need a pair of needles in size five" or "how many rows are left?" A model builder asks "how long does the glue need to dry?" or "is it ready to paint?" Many people ask an assistant to set a timer, find a pattern, or order more paint, and they use plain words like "find me a simple pattern".

Ahmed was a grandfather who liked to read the news on his computer. One morning he sat down with his coffee, which was bitter, and a slice of toast. He opened a long article, but the screen was so dark that the words were hard to see. He said, "It's like reading in a cave in here." The assistant understood that he meant the screen was too dim. It turned up the brightness and asked, "Is that better?" Ahmed said it was better. Then he said the letters were still small, so the assistant made the text bigger. Ahmed smiled, ate his toast and read the whole article.

Food delivery lets you order a meal from a restaurant and have it brought to your door. You choose the dishes, give your address, and the app shows a time. People often add a special request, like no onions or extra sauce, and a tip for the driver. If the food is late, the app may warn you that the delay is longer than first said. A doctor on a night shift or a tired parent might say "order the same thing as last time" or "get dinner here in thirty minutes". To change an order, people say "make that two" or "add a tip of three dollars". It is easy when you use plain words.

They want to know how many days are left until a day on the calendar, such as a gold wedding anniversary, so no one has to cry about forgetting.
- days till christmas
- how many days are left untill my birthday
- How long until Friday?
- Count the days to our trip on June third.
- I can't read the calendar without my glasses, so how many days until the anniversary?
- Could you please tell me how many days remain before my sister's party?
- How far away is the end of the school year, in days?
- I would be grateful if you could work out how many days are left until the first of next month.

Valentina was a cook, and she looked after her grandmother on weekends. One evening, after she dropped a pot on the kitchen floor, she realised she was running late. She said to her smart speaker, "Remind my grandmother to take her pills at eight and call her at nine." The assistant said it would do both. It added that it would count the pills in the weekly list and tell her if one day was missing. Valentina had also looked at a medical alert bracelet, but it was expensive, so she asked the assistant to find cheaper ones. The assistant showed three, and Valentina saved the best one for later.

Bo was a gardener with a lemon tree and a very long list of friends. His neighbour had just given him a jar of lemon jam, so he wanted to add her to his phone. He said, "Add Maria Costa, phone 555 0142, and her birthday is the ninth of May." The assistant made the new contact. Then Bo frowned. "Sorry, her name is Marta, not Maria." The assistant fixed the name and kept the number and the birthday. Bo also asked it to remind him a week before the birthday so he could bring flowers and celebrate with her. The assistant set the reminder, and Bo went back to his lemon tree.

Callum woke up late and stared at the clock. He had a meeting across town in an hour. He rubbed his eyes and said to his phone, "How long does it take to drive to the office, and send the route to my car?" The assistant looked at the traffic website and said the drive would take thirty-five minutes, a little longer than usual because of road work. It sent the route to his car screen. Callum grabbed a piece of stale bread from the kitchen, put on his shoes and ran out the door. In the car, the route was already waiting for him, with the first turn shown on the screen.

Siti woke up at three in the morning to a quiet house. Her baby had been fussy with gas the night before, and she was not sure if the little one was still asleep. She whispered to her phone, "Start monitor." The assistant turned on the baby camera and showed a small, sleeping face. Siti sighed in relief. Then she asked, "Nap time?" The assistant told her the baby had last napped at noon and would probably want another nap at two. Siti asked it to skip the loud morning alarm and set a soft one instead. It was a simple fix, and she went back to bed.

They want help remembering a birthday and choosing a great gift for it.
- Gift ideas for my mum
- When is my gram's birthday, and what should I get her?
- I forgot last year, so remind me a week before Dad's birthday and suggest a present.
- What's a great present for a ten year old who likes drawing?
- Find me a card and remind me to post it
- Could you please remind me of my brother's birthday and suggest something under thirty dollars?
- Do I have any birthdays this month, and what could I give each person?
- I would love your help finding a gift for my teacher and a card to go with it.

Notes are a place to write down ideas before they fall out of your head. People use them for shopping lists, plans, a funny joke they want to remember, or a thought that came to them at night. Each note is an item in a list, and you can name it, change it or put it in a folder. Voice notes let you speak instead of type. People say "write this down", "make a note: call the dentist", "add milk to my shopping note" or "read me my last note". To find an old one they say "find the note about the garden". If a note is no longer needed, they say "delete that note".

Henry was a student, and he burned his finger on a hot pan while making dinner. It hurt, and he did not know what to do. He asked his phone, "What should I do for a small burn?" The assistant said to hold the finger under cool running water for ten minutes and not to use ice. Henry did that. The pain began to ease. Then he asked, "What is the price of burn cream at the shop?" The assistant found two kinds and said they cost a few dollars each. Henry put one on his personal shopping list and asked the assistant to remind him in ten days to check the burn again.

Kwame did not like phones much, and he talked to his assistant slowly. His daughter had ordered him a new skirt for his wife, and he was waiting for the delivery. He said, "Is there a parcel for me today, and what time does the post office shut?" The assistant checked and said the parcel was out for delivery and would come before six. The post office closed at five-thirty. It said that the maximum waiting time at the counter was usually ten minutes. Kwame thanked the assistant and sat on the porch to wait. When the van came, he smiled, signed his name, and carried the box inside.

Sunita had just moved to the city, and she wanted to send her mother some pictures of her new flat. She stood in the chilly bathroom and said to her phone, "Take a photo of the bathroom, and tomorrow morning remind me to take more." The assistant took a photo and set the reminder. Then Sunita said, "Create an album called New Home." The assistant made the album and put the photo in it. Later she asked it to share the album with her mother.
